title: feat(join): a hidden-vetting join asks the community for its challenge itself
body:
## What

A community that hides its vetters (PCS ZKP) accepts a join's proof only over a challenge it issued itself (`vtc/vetting/pcs-challenge/0.1`). Until now the join failed when no challenge was stored, telling the person to press `m` on the application and join again. Now the join asks for the challenge itself, waits a bounded time for it, and carries on.

## How

- **Asking.** `launch_join_sequence` gets a new gate after the answers and trust-registry gates: `challenge_step(application, hears_replies, fresh)` decides `Ask` or `Proceed`. On `Ask`, `ask_challenge` sends the request with a bounded send (`ASK_TIMEOUT`, R1.2) and records it as a `QueryKind::PcsChallenge` query. The launch then parks in `state.join.challenge_wait`.
- **Waiting.** This reuses the pattern for waiting on requirements. The join flow returns `JoinExit::AwaitChallenge(AwaitingChallenge)`, and the runtime loop (the only loop with an inbound arm) holds it. Resumption happens in one of two ways:
  - When the answer arrives, `challenge_resume_for` picks it out and the loop re-enters with `JoinEntry::Challenge { awaiting, outcome }`. That entry does **not** reset `state.join`, so the persona, invitation, approved answers and registry choice the person made are all kept. The launch is taken up again where it parked.
  - When `CHALLENGE_WAIT` (15s, the same as `REQUIREMENTS_WAIT`) passes with no answer, the loop re-enters with an `Unanswered` outcome.
  - `JoinCancel` while parked forgets the query.
- **Matching.** A new `CommunityAnswer::Challenge { query, community }` is emitted by `inbound::challenge_issued` alongside its existing notice. Matching is on the request's **document id**, so a challenge asked for from the Vetting page (`m`) does not resume the join.
- **Errors (R6.4).** Each failure ends in a "Nothing was sent — join again" sentence that names which of these happened:
  - the request could not be sent (our mediator; the send timeout is worded separately)
  - the community refused (with its code and note)
  - the answer could not be read (contract mismatch, "not a refusal")
  - no answer came within 15s (the service may be offline or unreachable)
- **Loops that can't hear replies (State A).** The join does not ask. If no challenge is stored, the refusal now says that this screen cannot hear the community's answer, and that starting the join again once messaging is running will ask for the challenge itself. The old "press m" advice was wrong there. In practice State A has no persona, and so no application.
- **Existing refusals kept.** The no-attestation and proof-build-error sentences are unchanged. No-attestation is now checked first, so a join with nothing to prove says so without asking for a challenge.

## Single-use semantics (from vtc-service `vetting/pcs_challenge.rs` + `pcs.rs::decide`)

The community keeps **one open challenge per applicant DID** and replaces it whenever it is asked again. A challenge expires after **15 minutes**. It is **consumed on any submission carrying a proof**: the row is removed before the expiry and match checks, so a refused proof spends it too.

So:

- **Every hidden launch that can hear the answer asks for a fresh challenge**, even when one is stored. A stored one may have been replaced, may have expired, or may already be spent, and this client cannot tell. One round trip at join time costs less than sending a proof the community will certainly refuse. The stored challenge is dropped once the new request is sent, because the community has replaced it by then.
- **After a submit that carried a proof**, `Application::hidden_submission_sent()` clears `hidden_challenge` and `hidden_submission`. This is saved together with the pending membership. A submit that failed at our mediator keeps the challenge, since nothing reached the community.

## Tests

- `join_flow::vetting_tests`:
  - `a_hidden_launch_asks_for_its_challenge_rather_than_failing`: no challenge → ask; a stored challenge → still ask; a fresh one → proceed; can't hear replies → proceed.
  - `only_a_hidden_launch_with_an_attestation_asks`
  - `only_the_awaited_challenge_resumes_the_launch`: matching by document id and community; refused and unreadable outcomes are worded distinctly.
  - `a_hidden_join_with_no_attestation_says_so_before_the_challenge`
  - `a_challenge_that_did_not_come_stops_the_join_and_says_why`
  - `a_hidden_join_without_its_proof_stops_and_says_why`: adjusted to the new State-A wording.
- `openvtc-core` `vetting::tests::a_challenge_is_answered_to_its_question_and_spent_by_the_submit_it_binds`: an issued challenge is stored and answered under its query id; a proof-carrying submit spends it, and one with no proof does not.

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`, `cargo test -p openvtc --features dev-overrides` and `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` all pass locally.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): the send is under `ASK_TIMEOUT` and the wait under `CHALLENGE_WAIT`
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the stored challenge is cleared only after the request is sent, and only after a proof-carrying submit returned Ok
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no automatic retry; the person joins again
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a, no new loop
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no wire change; `CommunityAnswer` is in-process only
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): no proof means no submit, as before
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): a crash while parked leaves the old challenge cleared (or kept, if the send had not completed) and nothing submitted; the next join asks again
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: feat(vetting): a vetter can give an optional reason and note when declining
body:
## What
`vetting/decline/0.1` carries an optional reason `code` and an optional `message` (1–500 characters). `VettingBook::decline` already passed them through, but the TUI always sent `None, None` and the confirm page had no way to give either.

**Vetter: "Decline this request?"**
- **Reason** (←/→): starts at *no reason given*, then cycles through:
  - could not establish who you are (`couldNotVerify`)
  - your document did not match your card or you (`documentMismatch`)
  - the match code could not be confirmed with you (`livenessFailed`)
  - the vetter prefers not to vouch for you (`notComfortable`)
  - another reason (`other`)
- **Note:** optional free text. More than 500 characters is refused with the count; an empty note sends none.
- **What the page says:** a reason is never required, and whatever you choose goes to the applicant only. The community isn't told you declined, or why.
- **Keys:** `y`/Enter declines and `n`/Esc keeps the request while the cursor is on Reason. On Note, `y` and `n` are typed as text, and Enter declines.

**Applicant:** the request row shows what they were given, e.g. `declined — your document did not match your card or you · they wrote: "…"`. With neither, it still reads `declined`.

The vetter journey's footer now reads `x: decline (a reason is optional)`.

## Tests
- **Core:** new `a_declines_reason_and_note_reach_the_applicant` sends a code and a note through the real exchange and checks both arrive in the applicant's `RequestState::Declined`.
- **Keys:** `y`/`n` and ←/→ act on Reason, while on Note `n` is typed rather than taken as "keep it".
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p openvtc -p openvtc-core`: all pass.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

## 🤖 New release * `vti-common`: 0.37.2 -> 0.37.3 (✓ API compatible changes) * `cnm-cli`: 0.27.1 -> 0.27.2
Changelog

## `vti-common`

## [0.37.3](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-common-v0.37.2...vti-common-v0.37.3) — 2026-10-05 ### Fixed - **vtc**: Working in the admin console counts toward the idle timeout ([#1953](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1953)) The console signed out operators who were using it. The idle timeout (`auth.admin_idle_timeout`, 900s) is measured from `Session::last_seen`, and only a cookie-authenticated request through the `AuthClaims` extractor advanced it. Most of what the console sends is now a signed Trust Task document to `/v1/trust-tasks`, which authenticates by its proof and reads no session, so a busy operator stopped producing activity. Fifteen minutes after the last cookie-borne call the renewal was refused and the session-deadline watcher showed Login. Counting every signed document would be wrong the other way: the action badge, counts and banners post signed reads on timers, and an unattended tab would never time out. Only the console can tell input from a poll, so: - The console notes real input (pointerdown, keydown, wheel, touchstart) and sends `X-VTC-User-Activity` on a document posted within 60s of some (`admin-ui/src/lib/user-activity.ts`). Timers in an idle tab send none. - The route records activity only for a document that ran successfully, was verified as a known signer, and whose principal (the signer, or the administrator its console key acts for) owns the session the cookie names (`vti_common::auth::touch_cookie_session_for`, which authenticates the cookie exactly as the extractors do). A document signed by one identity cannot keep another's session alive, and a refused one counts for nothing. Renewals and timer-driven reads still never count, so the daemon still decides when an operator who walked away is signed out.

title: fix(vtc): working in the admin console counts toward the idle timeout
body:
## Problem

The admin console signed operators out while they were using it.

The idle timeout (`auth.admin_idle_timeout`, default 900s) is measured from `Session::last_seen`, and only a cookie-authenticated request through the `AuthClaims` extractor advanced it. Most of what the console sends is now a signed Trust Task document to `POST /v1/trust-tasks`, which authenticates by its proof and reads no session. So a busy operator produced no activity. Fifteen minutes after the last cookie-borne call, the renewal was refused for inactivity and the session-deadline watcher (#1905) showed Login.

Counting every signed document would be wrong the other way. The action badge, community counts and banners post signed reads on timers, so an unattended tab would never time out. Only the console can tell input from a poll.

## Change

- **Console** (`admin-ui/src/lib/user-activity.ts`): notes real input (`pointerdown`, `keydown`, `wheel`, `touchstart`; not mouse movement) and sends `X-VTC-User-Activity: 1` on a signed document posted within 60s of input. Timers in an idle tab send nothing. Tracking starts in `watchSession`.
- **Route** (`routes/trust_tasks.rs`): records activity only when all of these hold:
  - the header is present;
  - the document ran successfully;
  - it was verified as a known signer;
  - its principal owns the session named by the cookie. The principal is the signer, or the administrator its console key acts for: `Admission::verified_principal`, the same mapping the per-signer rate limit uses.
- **`vti_common::auth::touch_cookie_session_for`** (new, additive): authenticates the session cookie exactly as the extractors do (signature, session state, `jti` pin), requires the session's DID to equal the principal, then calls `touch_last_seen`. Best-effort, like the extractor's touch.

Invariants preserved:
- Renewals never count.
- Bearer callers never touch.
- A document signed by one identity can't keep another identity's session alive.
- A refused document counts for nothing.

Anyone able to send the header already holds the session and could just click. The header only lets the console report activity the server could not otherwise see.

The VTI spec has no idle-timeout requirement, so there is nothing to cite or record as a divergence.

## Tests

- `vti-common`: own-DID touch; another identity's session is untouched; no cookie or a forged cookie does nothing.
- `vtc-service` unit: `verified_principal` is known only after verification and maps a console key to its admin.
- `vtc-service` it (`session_idle_timeout`), through the real router:
  - a console-key document with the header advances the admin's `last_seen`;
  - one without the header does not;
  - a document signed by another admin does not;
  - a refused document does not.
- Console (vitest): the header is sent within the window, and is absent before any input or after the window.

Run locally:
- `cargo nextest run -p vti-common -p vtc-service`: 3482/3488 passed. The 6 failures were the admin-UI embed tests, which fail under `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1`; re-run with the UI built, all 11 pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- admin-ui `vitest run`: 793 passed. `tsc -b --noEmit`: clean.

title: feat(join): review what the community will receive, and word the invitation page for vetting in hand
body:
## What
The Join step of the applicant journey: before a request goes out, the person sees exactly what the community will receive. The invitation page also stops misdescribing what happens when you hold vetting.

### Review and send
The last page before sending (#439's trust-registry page, retitled " Review and send ") now opens with a review. The publication question follows it.

```
What first-vtc will receive
  Your identity    did:webvh:…:march-issue
  Invitation       none
  Vetting          PCS ZKP  a zero-knowledge proof built from 2 vetter attestations
                   it learns that enough vetters vouched for you — not who they were
  Your face sends  name.legal  Alice Example
  How it decides   meeting its vetting requirements admits you automatically
```

**What each line shows:**
- **Your identity:** the persona's DID, or "a new persona — its DID is made when you send".
- **Invitation:** the issuer, plus a note when the invitation was issued to another of your personas and a proof will link the two.
- **Vetting:**
  - **Named:** "N named statement(s) — it sees who vouched for you", with one line per statement: vetter, method, the claims they checked, and validity.
  - **Hidden:** the PCS ZKP badge, the attestation count, and what the community does and doesn't learn.
  - **None:** "none".
- **Your face sends:** the approved answers.
- **How it decides:**
  - Read from the admission rule of the criterion the application names.
  - With neither an invitation nor vetting, it says the request goes to moderators.

Everything comes from the same records `run_join_sequence` builds the request from (`join_review`).

### Invitation page
When the persona joining holds vetting for this community, it goes with the request whether or not an invitation is chosen. The page used to say joining without one meant "The community reviews and approves the request manually", which wasn't true. Now:
- **Title:** "Also present an invitation?"
- **New line under the prompt:** "Your 2 vetting statements go with this request either way. An invitation is optional on top of them." For PCS ZKP, it names the proof instead.
- **The without row:** "Join without one — with your 2 vetting statements only", followed by the community's actual admission rule.
- **Without vetting held,** the page is unchanged.

`VettingInHand` is filled in `open_invitation_choice` from the same application lookup the join uses. The "how it decides" wording is shared between the two pages (`vetting_decision`).

## Tests
- `the_review_says_what_the_community_receives_and_who_it_learns_vouched`, covering named and hidden. The review comes before the publication question.
- `a_bare_join_reviews_as_a_new_persona_with_nothing_to_present`
- `with_vetting_in_hand_the_invitation_is_optional_on_top`, a rendered page test that also checks the plain open-request wording is unchanged.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p openvtc`: all pass.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.
author: stormer78

body:
feat(join): review what the community will receive before sending, and word the invitation page for vetting in hand (#440)

The last page before a join request goes out now reviews what it carries:
the DID the community admits (or that a new one is made), the invitation and
whether a proof links it to this DID, the vetting — named statements with who
vouched and what they checked, or a PCS ZKP proof that names no vetter — what
the face sends, and how the community decides. The trust-registry question
follows it. Everything is read from the records the join builds from.

The invitation page no longer promises a manual review to someone holding
vetting: their statements go with the request either way, so the page asks
whether to also present an invitation, and the without-row says the vetting
alone decides it, under the community's own admission rule.

title: feat: an applicant can consent to trust-registry publication when joining
body:
## Why

A VTC publishes a member in its trust registry only if that member consented. Consent is `registryConsent` on `vtc/join-requests/submit` (0.2 and 0.3). It defaults to `false`, and the VTC copies it onto the member record (`publish_consent`). Approving the request does not consent for the applicant, and the registry sync skips any member without consent.

openvtc hard-coded `registry_consent: false` in `build_join_submit_document`, so nobody who joined through openvtc could ever be published.

## What

**Core (`openvtc-core/src/join.rs`)**
- `JoinPresentation` gains `registry_consent: bool`, and the submit sends it as given.
- `From<Value>` sets it to `false`, so any caller that does not ask keeps today's behaviour.
- Breaking for struct literals; noted in the CHANGELOG.

**TUI join flow**
- New `JoinPage::RegistryConsent` page, shown on every join as the last step before the request goes out (after any requested-attribute answers).
- It is gated in `launch_join_sequence`, which every launch path goes through: identity, invitation, context, vetting and answers.
- The page says what publishing means: a public record that the identity you join with is a member. It also says that leaving the box unticked is a complete answer, that the community may still decline to publish, and that openvtc can't change the answer after joining.
- The box starts unticked. Only Space toggles it, and no letter key answers yes. Enter answers either way, and Esc cancels.
- The answer belongs to the community it was given for (`RegistryChoice::consent_for`) and is `take()`n by the one submit that sends it. A retry, or a second join from the same open flow, asks again.
- The success page shows a `Registry:` row with the answer that was sent.
- The CLI has no separate join entry point. `--invitation` only pre-loads an invitation for the TUI flow, so it goes through the same page.

**Tests**
- `the_applicants_registry_consent_reaches_the_wire_as_given` covers `true` and `false` on submit 0.2 and 0.3. It asserts three things:
  - the raw JSON member `payload.registryConsent` carries the value;
  - no snake_case `registry_consent` member is present;
  - the generated `trust_tasks_rs::specs::vtc::join_requests::submit::{v0_2,v0_3}::Payload` reads back `Some(value)`.
- `an_unasked_presentation_does_not_consent` covers the `From<Value>` default.
- `join_lifecycle_e2e.rs` sends `true` in the approval scenario and `false` in the rejection scenario. It asserts both the wire member and the VTC's parsed value.
- Unit tests for the page cover its wording, unticked on open, and the keys. Tests for the state handler cover the page opening and parking the launch, a previous yes not pre-ticking the next question, and `consent_for` / `answered_for` semantics.

**Docs**
- `docs/design/multi-community-support.md` gains R-B-6a, and the §3 note now gives the wire name.
- CHANGELOG: Breaking and Added entries.

## Out of scope: changing consent after joining

A member has no way to change consent afterwards. `vtc/members/update` is administrator-only, and no member-signed Trust Task exists for it. A new task has to be specified in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf first. Until then, leaving and rejoining with the other answer is the only route: self-remove tombstones the member row by default, which clears `publish_consent`, and re-admission writes a fresh row with the new request's answer.

## Checks run locally (as CI runs them)

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace`
- `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`
- `cargo test -p openvtc --features dev-overrides`
- `cargo check -p openvtc-core --no-default-features --features arbitrary`
- `cargo test -p openvtc-core --features arbitrary --lib`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`
- `cargo bench --workspace --no-run`
- `cargo test -p openvtc-core --test join_lifecycle_e2e -- --include-ignored` (3/3)

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new clients
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the answer is in-memory UI state, taken by the submit; nothing new is persisted
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): untouched
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): untouched
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no new type; an existing camelCase member now carries the user's value, checked against the generated spec payloads
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): an absent answer sends `false`
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): the success row says "consented" / "not consented", not "published"
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): dying before the submit sends nothing, and the next join asks again
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: feat(vetting): applicant and vetter journeys — the whole process, where you are, and why
body:
## What
Applying for vetting and vetting someone are each now a **journey page**. The page shows the whole process, marks where you are, explains each step as you reach it, and offers only the action the current step needs. It takes the full width of the screen (the menu steps aside), so the process no longer jumps between full-screen and menu-panel layouts.

```
Applying to first-vtc as alice                          PCS ZKP
✓ Requirements ─ ✓ Face ─ ● Vetters ─ ○ Sessions ─ ○ Statements ─ ○ Join
                 Work                               0 of 2
What's happening — Vetters
  A vetter is a member the community has named to vouch for people. …
Your part now
  r  ask a vetter with the ticket link they gave you
  v  find a vetter in the community's directory
Esc: back to your applications (nothing is lost)   x: abandon this application
✓ done   ● yours now   … waiting on someone else   ○ to come
```

**Steps:**
- **Applicant:** Requirements → Face → Vetters → Sessions → Statements → Join
- **Vetter:** Request → Session → Match code → Card → Check → Sign

## How it works
- **`openvtc_core::vetting::journey`:** the pure model. `applicant_journey(&Application)` and `vetter_journey(&DeskEntry)` mark each step done, current, waiting on someone else, or still to come, with progress such as "1 of 2" or the match code.
  - It's built on `Application::next_step`, so the journey and the existing "next:" hints agree.
  - At most one step is current.
  - Every step has `explain(hidden)` text that teaches what the step is for. Where it matters, named and PCS ZKP communities get different text, e.g. who the community learns vouched for you.
- **`ui::journey`:** the step strip, the "What's happening" box and the legend, shared by both sides so they look alike.
- **`components::vetting_journey`:** the page itself. It wraps the Vetting page's existing views (face picker, ask-a-vetter, card page, attest form, confirms) rather than replacing them: an open form is drawn under the strip. With nothing open, it shows "Your part now", plus the applicant's vetters and match codes or the vetter's view of the card.
- **Keys:** with a journey open, only steps already reached take their keys, plus `m`, `x`/decline and Esc. Esc returns to the list with nothing lost. A key for a step not yet reached does nothing.
- **Opening a journey:**
  - Enter on an application, or on a desk request. `c` and `a` still go straight to the card or attest form.
  - Starting an application from the join page (`focus_application`).
  - Opening a vetting Inbox entry (`focus_vetting_target`).
- **Keeping it current:** `sync_journey` rebuilds the open journey on every sync, so a session opening or a statement arriving moves it on by itself. A journey whose application or request has gone closes.

## Not in this PR (next)
- The Join step still hands off to the existing join flow. A "what the community will receive" review screen, including whether the vetting is a named statement or a PCS ZKP proof, comes next.
- Rewording the invitation (VIC) page for an applicant who holds vetting statements.

## Tests
- **Core:** a new application starts at Requirements; then Face, then Vetters, with details; every step explains itself, and hidden mode says vetters stay hidden.
- **Integration (`vetting/tests.rs`):** both journeys follow a real request→session exchange. The vetter is on the match code and waiting for the card.
- **UI:** the strip marks and progress; the applicant page (process, explainer, step key, way out); the vetter page (the match code with what to do); journey keys gated by the steps reached.
- `cargo clippy -p openvtc -p openvtc-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo test -p openvtc -p openvtc-core`: all pass.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

title: fix(vetting): attest on the session's method, and allow resending an unrecorded withdrawal
body:
## Problems (vetter side)
1. **The attest form ignored the session's method.** `StartAttest` opened `AttestForm::default()`, so Method was always "in person". After a video-call session, the vetter was one Enter away from signing a statement that misstates how the person was checked.
2. **A refused or unrecorded withdrawal got stuck.** `ArmWithdraw` refused any statement with a withdrawal attached ("That statement is already withdrawn"), including one the community refused (`WithdrawalRefused`, which is only logged) or never recorded. The row read "withdrawal sent — not yet recorded" indefinitely, with no way forward. Yet `VettingBook::withdrawal` explicitly allows sending again until the withdrawal is recorded ("withdrawal converges").

## Fix
1. `StartAttest` reads the desk entry's `DeskState::CardReceived { session }` and opens the form on `session.method`.
2. `IssuedRow` gains `withdrawal_recorded`. `w` is refused only once the community has recorded the withdrawal. While one is pending, the hint reads "w: send the withdrawal again".

## Tests
- New: `an_unrecorded_withdrawal_can_be_sent_again`, covering the hint for none, pending and recorded.
- The method default is a direct lookup in the dispatch path, which needs a live `ActionCtx`. It isn't unit-tested.
- `cargo test -p openvtc`: 817 passed. clippy: clean.

title: fix(inbox): a vetting task opens where its step is taken
body:
## Problem
The inbox tasks raised for vetting were mapped to `TaskKind::Informational("Unknown")` with an empty DID:
- **Vetter side:** "Vetting Request (Inbound)" and "Vetting Card Received".
- **Applicant side:** "Vetting Session (Send Card)".

Opening one showed only its type and task id, with "d: dismiss  Esc: back". So the one notification telling someone it's their turn led nowhere. They had to go to Vetting, switch to the right tab (the desk isn't the default), and find the row themselves.

## Fix
- A new `TaskKind::Vetting(VettingTarget)`, with two targets:
  - `Card { application_id, session_id }`
  - `Desk { request_id }`

  Both are read from the fields the tasks already carry.
- **Enter on one** (`OpenDetail`) calls the new `vetting_actions::focus_vetting_target` instead of building a detail view:
  - **Card:** opens Vetting → Applications on that application, straight into the card page for that session.
  - **Desk:** opens Vetting → desk → Requests with the request selected, or says "That request is no longer on your desk."
- The row is labelled `✓ VET`, with the applicant's or vetter's DID underneath.

## Tests
- New: `a_vetting_task_opens_where_its_step_is_taken`, covering the card target, the desk target and the "gone" message.
- `cargo test -p openvtc`: 817 passed. clippy: clean.

Part of the applicant/vetter flow work. The planned journey pages will become the target these open.

title: fix(join): carry on as the persona just made, and stop naming keys that are gone
body:
## Problem
1. **Wrong persona after making one.** On the vetting join page, choosing "a new persona" opens the create-persona overlay. When it closes, `show_vetting` rebuilds the page and `take_route` resumes. But `vetting_view` picks which persona the page opens on by its own rules: one with a satisfied application, else the first application's persona, else the first by name. With other personas present, the resumed route could start or continue an application as **a different persona** from the one just made.
2. **Stale keys.** The "Applying needs a persona" refusal told the holder to "Press n to create one here, or join anyway (j)". Neither key is bound on that page any more.

## Fix
1. `JoinState::minted_persona` is set when `mint_persona_inline` persists a persona. `vetting_view` takes a new `prefer: Option<PersonaId>`, which `show_vetting` fills from it, so the page reopens on the persona just made. Making it was the decision about who applies.
2. The refusal now reads "Set Apply as to "a new persona" with ←/→, then press Enter to make one."

## Tests
- New: `the_page_reopens_on_the_persona_just_made`. It uses two personas, and the preferred one wins over the page's default pick.
- `cargo test -p openvtc`: 817 passed. clippy: clean.

title: fix(join): a hidden-vetting join with no proof stops instead of submitting nothing
body:
## Problem
When a community hides its vetters (PCS ZKP), the join sends a zero-knowledge proof in `extensions.hiddenVetting` in place of the named vetting statements. In `run_join_sequence`:
- **If `prepare_hidden_submission` failed,** the error was logged as an *info* line and the join was **submitted anyway**, with neither the proof nor any statements. The community decided on no vetting, while the holder believed they had presented theirs.
- **`Ok(false)` (hidden parameters, but no attestation has arrived)** submitted the same empty join, with no message at all.
- **With no community challenge yet,** the join showed "Waiting…" and returned without `fail()`. The progress page never completed, nothing resumed it, and the listener and any persona minted for this join were left behind.

## Fix
A new function, `hidden_proof_refusal`, returns `None` when the proof is built, or `Some(sentence)` otherwise. The caller fails the join with that sentence and runs the same cleanup as every other failed step: remove the listener and roll back a just-minted persona. The three sentences:
- **No challenge:** "…none has arrived yet. Nothing was sent. In Vetting, press m on this application to ask for it, then join again." (`m` is what calls `ask_for_challenge`.)
- **No attestation:** "…no vetter's attestation has reached this application yet, so there is nothing to prove. Nothing was sent."
- **The proof fails:** "The zero-knowledge proof of your vetting could not be built (…). Nothing was sent — joining without it would present no vetting at all."

I also corrected `prepare_hidden_submission`'s doc comment, which said hidden vetting applies to no application today.

## Tests
- New: `a_hidden_join_without_its_proof_stops_and_says_why`, covering the no-challenge and no-attestation refusals. The proof-error path needs real PCS keys to trigger and is covered by the same branch.
- `cargo test -p openvtc`: 817 passed. clippy: clean.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)
The join could ask for the challenge itself rather than sending the holder to press `m`. That fits better into the planned applicant journey, where "get the community's challenge" becomes a visible step.

Under a community that hides its vetters, the join sends a PCS zero-knowledge
proof in place of the named statements. When that proof could not be built,
the failure was logged as an info line and the join was submitted anyway,
carrying no vetting at all: the community decided on nothing while the holder
believed they had presented their vetting. With no attestation yet the same
happened silently, and with no community challenge the join stopped without
being marked failed, leaving its listener and any new persona behind.

All three now fail the join with what to do (press m for the challenge, wait
for an attestation, or the proof error), and clean up as every other failed
step does.

title: feat: show PQC signing and PCS ZKP vetting, and say what each credential is
body:
## What
Two cryptographic properties are now visible wherever they matter. Each is drawn as a filled badge, and its meaning is explained once per page:

| Badge | Meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `PQC-SIGNED` | Signed with a post-quantum key (ML-DSA) as well as a classical one | **Credential:** its proof set has an `mldsa*`/`slhdsa*` proof. **Community:** a credential it issued you has one, or, before joining, its DID document lists an ML-DSA-44 key under `assertionMethod` |
| `PCS ZKP` | The community proves vetting with a PCS zero-knowledge proof. It learns that enough vetters vouched, not who they were | The community's stored vetting requirements (`org.openvtc.hidden-vetting`), read with the same `hidden::read_mode` an application adopts |

**Where they appear:**
- **My Credentials:** a badge on each PQC-signed row, plus a "Signature" line in the detail view that also says "classical only" when it isn't.
- **Communities:** both badges on the community's header line, with a legend.
- **Vetting → Applications:** a badge on the row, and a "Vetters" line: hidden, named, or not known until the requirements arrive.
- **Vetting desk:** a badge on the row, and a "You are" line: hidden (counted in a zero-knowledge proof) or named (your signed statement, with your DID, goes to the community).
- **Join page:** a new "How it protects you" block. It always states both properties, including when they're absent ("named — the community sees which vetters vouched for you", "classical keys only").

**Credentials list:** each row now shows what the credential is (Membership, Role: vetter, a statement), which of your personas it was issued to, and a readable validity. Before, every row showed the issuer and two raw timestamps, so four first-vtc rows looked identical.

## How
- **`openvtc_core::proof_check`:** new `signed_post_quantum(&Value)` and `publishes_post_quantum_key(&Document)`. The second handles relative `#key` references, which webvh documents use.
- **`VettingBook`:**
  - `KnownCriterion::hidden_vetting()` / `VettingBook::hidden_vetting(community)`.
  - A new `KnownCommunity::post_quantum_key: Option<bool>`, `serde(default)` so older configs load, recorded from the DID document the join flow already resolves in `learn_over_http`. No extra network call.
- **UI:** a new `ui::badges` module with one definition per badge. Credential rows get `post_quantum` and `subject_label`, filled in one pass (`finish_credential_rows`) so no list misses them.

## Not covered
- A community reached only over DIDComm, never resolved here, shows "Signing: not checked" on the join page until its DID document is read.
- PQC is shown from the proofs as held. Credentials are verified with `proof_check::verify_signed` on receipt, which fails a set if any proof fails.

## Tests
- **Core:** a PQ proof in a set is recognised, a classical-only one isn't, and a document's ML-DSA signing key counts while an auth-only one doesn't. A stored criterion knows whether its vetters are hidden.
- **UI:**
  - A credential row shows its kind, persona, validity and badge, with the legend once.
  - The join page states both properties when present and when absent.
- `cargo test -p openvtc -p openvtc-core`: all pass. clippy: clean.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

title: fix(vetting): a card with no face says so, and f chooses one from the card
body:
## Problem
An applicant tried to send their card to a vetter and got:

> Could not preview the card: VTA Error: persona disclosure preview failed: not found: … persona did:webvh:… has no profile bound, so there is nothing to disclose

A vetting application's persona wears no face until the holder presses `f` on the application and picks one. Nothing enforces that before the card step. On the card page:
- The raw VTA refusal named a DID and no action to take.
- `f` didn't work on that page.
- The face picker only opened when the page was in list mode. So `f` from the holder-grant retry page produced only a status line, and with no faces at all the picker (and its "Make a face" row) never opened.

## Fix
- **`preview_refusal`:** "has no profile bound" now reads "This application has no face yet, so there is no card to show. Press f to choose the face vetters see — you come back here once it is worn."
- **`f` on the card page** sends `ChooseFace` for the card's own application, not the list's selected row. The card is remembered in a new field, `VettingState::card_after_face`.
- **The `Faces` outcome opens the picker** from the list, the card page or the holder-grant retry. It also opens with an empty face list, whose only row makes a face.
- **Returning to the card:** wearing a face (`FaceWorn`), making one (create, which also wears it), or pressing Esc in the picker returns to the card it was opened from. From the list, everything behaves as before.
- **Card page hint:** now reads "Enter: preview  f: choose the face  Esc: not now".

## Tests
- New: `a_card_with_no_face_worn_says_to_choose_one`, `vetting_card_chooses_the_face_on_f`, `a_face_chosen_from_the_card_returns_to_the_card`, `backing_out_of_the_picker_returns_where_it_came_from`.
- `cargo test -p openvtc`: 816 passed. clippy: clean.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

Part of the wider applicant/vetter flow work. This is the smallest piece that removes the dead end.

title: perf: raise TEE keys/sign throughput (vsock storage, fewer round trips, multi-core REST)
body:
## Summary

Load tests of the VTA in a Nitro Enclave found that `keys/sign` throughput is capped by serial sections, not by hardware. This PR removes them in seven independent commits, so each can be kept or dropped on its own. Together they take a c6g.xlarge appliance (1-vCPU enclave) from about 80 to about 195 keys/sign per second, and let bigger enclaves use their CPUs: a c6g.4xlarge with a 2-vCPU enclave reaches about 345, and with a 4-vCPU enclave about 380 to 400.

Only one commit depends on another: the one-write framing changes code added by the storage pool. The rest apply on their own.

## Commits

| # | Commit | What | Risk for review |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `fix(vti-common): pool the enclave's vsock storage connections` | All enclave storage went through one connection behind one mutex. Now a pool of up to 8. Also fixes a stale-response bug: a cancelled request could leave its response for the next caller. | Low; enclave builds only |
| 2 | `fix(vta-enclave): log to stderr only while vsock logging is down` | Every log line was also written synchronously to the enclave console, which nobody can read in production. | Low; enclave builds only. CI does not build the `vsock-log` feature, so this is checked by hand only |
| 3 | `perf(vti-common): send each vsock storage request in one write` | Length and payload went out as two packets. Depends on 1. | Low |
| 4 | `perf(vta-service): read the caller's ACL entry once per keys/sign` | Both sign gates read the same ACL row. Both gates still run, in the same order. | Low; authorization code, so worth a careful look |
| 5 | `perf(vta-service): reuse the context record for the keys/sign custody check` | The context row was read for the policy and again for the custody base path. Adds `effective_context_policy_and_record` (vta-support) and `derive_record_key_in_context` (key custody). | Medium; adds a second entry point to key custody. It falls back to reading the context when the record does not match |
| 6 | `perf(vta-service): serve REST on one worker per CPU` | REST ran on a current-thread runtime, so the VTA used at most one CPU. Now multi-threaded with more than one CPU; unchanged with one. | High; affects every deployment. Handlers now run in parallel, not only interleaved at awaits, so existing non-atomic read-modify-writes become likelier to race |
| 7 | `perf(vta-enclave): serve REST on vsock directly, without the inbound socat` | socat forked per inbound connection, and new connections timed out under load. The VTA now binds vsock itself when the entrypoint sets `VTA_REST_VSOCK_PORT`. | High; changes the enclave entrypoint (part of the image measurement) and the boot path: the parent's connections are refused until the VTA binds |

Commits 4 and 5 take a sign from 10 storage operations to 8.

## Results

`keys/sign/0.1` over REST through a load balancer, EdDSA over 32 bytes, from 50 agents in 5 contexts, open-loop stepped rates of 4 minutes each. "Healthy" means no errors and p95 under 150 ms. Approximate saturation in keys/sign per second:

| Build | c6g.xlarge, 1-vCPU enclave | c6g.4xlarge, 2-vCPU enclave | c6g.4xlarge, 4-vCPU enclave |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` before this PR | about 79 (healthy at 70) | not measured | not measured |
| + 1 | about 97 (healthy at 85) | not measured | not measured |
| + 1, 2 | about 165 (healthy at 160) | about 235 to 245 (see note) | not measured |
| + 1 to 5 | about 195 (healthy at 160, p95 63 ms) | about 287 (p95 30 ms at 235, 4 errors) | not measured |
| + 1 to 7 (this PR) | about 195 (healthy at 160, p95 59 ms) | about 345 (p95 114 ms at 320, 13 errors) | about 380 to 400 (p95 41 ms at 320, 7 errors; 309 ms at 400) |

Below saturation the latency gain is larger than the ceiling gain: on c6g.4xlarge with a 2-vCPU enclave at 235/s, p95 was 600 ms with commits 1 and 2, 30 ms with 1 to 5, and 12 ms with all seven.

The "+ 1 to 5" and "+ 1 to 7" rows are this branch exactly, built and run as they are. Note: the c6g.4xlarge figures for "+ 1, 2" and the 600 ms baseline come from builds with extra timing and counter logging, which is not part of this PR. While investigating, each change was also measured one at a time; those runs found commit 6 worth nothing on a 1-vCPU enclave (it keeps one thread there) and commit 7 worth no throughput but removing connect-timeout errors (7 → 0 at 320/s on a 4-vCPU enclave).

## How the bottlenecks were found

- Storage round trips were serial (commit 1), and console logging serialised every request on the stderr lock (commit 2).
- With those fixed, a 2-vCPU enclave sat half idle at its ceiling. The parent answered each storage request in about 33 µs, yet the round trip measured inside the enclave grew from 0.4 ms to about 4 ms under load. The time was the reply waiting for the single REST thread to poll it (commit 6). More storage connections (32 instead of 8) did not help, which ruled out the pool.
- Each sign made 10 storage round trips, 4 of them repeats or reads of data that almost never changes (commits 4 and 5 remove 2; the audit-key cache below would remove the other 2).
- Inbound socat cost little CPU (about 0.2 core) but caused connection timeouts while forking (commit 7).

## Not in this PR (follow-ups)

- **Audit key cache.** Every audited operation reads the active audit key from storage twice (the marker, then the key). Caching it in `AuditKeyStore` saves both, but a cache per store instance misses a rotation through another instance (the VTC builds several on one keyspace), and it breaks `vti_apv_022_a_waiver_that_cannot_be_audited_is_refused`, which simulates an audit outage by deleting the active marker. Needs a design that keeps VTI-APV-022 (a cache per keyspace that fails closed, or a different fault injection agreed for the test).

It is worth doing. It takes a sign from 8 storage operations to 6, and measured against this PR without it:

| Shape | This PR (no cache) | This PR's changes + audit-key cache |
|---|---|---|
| c6g.xlarge, 1-vCPU enclave | about 195 (healthy at 160) | about 220 (p95 193 ms at 220, 0 errors) |
| c6g.4xlarge, 2-vCPU enclave, commits 1 to 5 only | about 287 (p95 30 ms at 235, 4 errors) | about 300 (p95 15 ms at 235, 0 errors) |
| c6g.4xlarge, 4-vCPU enclave | about 380 to 400 (p95 309 ms at 400, 169 errors) | about 475 to 480 (p95 44 to 49 ms at 400, 22 to 43 errors) |

The cache runs used builds with the extra timing and counter logging, which cost some throughput (with a 2-vCPU enclave, all seven commits reached about 345 without that logging against about 310 with it and with the cache), so the cache figures are more likely low than high.

- **Audit chain lock.** Each audited operation holds the chain lock across one storage insert. With a 4-vCPU enclave, releasing the lock before the insert made 400/s fully healthy and cut p95 at 480/s from 374 to 111 ms. That prototype is not crash-safe (a failed insert leaves a gap in the chain), so it needs a design, not this PR.
- **Parent proxy inbound cap.** `MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTIONS = 256` in `deploy/nitro/enclave-proxy/src/channels.rs`. With commit 7, the remaining errors past about 400/s are this cap rejecting load-balancer connections.
- **Replies in one write.** The parent proxy still writes each storage reply as two packets.
- **Overload has no back-pressure.** Past saturation, health checks fail and the appliance restarts instead of shedding load.
- **Restart with a large audit log.** The first audited write after a restart reloads the chain head by scanning the whole audit keyspace over vsock. This will be reported separately.
- **CI does not build `vsock-log`.**

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`, workspace doctests, and the vtc-service audit tests

title: vta-sdk: keep a trust-task rejection's code and details instead of flattening to Protocol(String)
body:
## Problem
`vta-sdk` turns most trust-task rejections into `VtaError::Protocol(format!("trust task failed [{code}]: {message}"))` (`vta-sdk/src/client/mod.rs`, the rejection mapping before `seal_vault_secret`). The payload's `details` is read only for `unsupportedType` / `unsupportedVersion`. For every other code it is dropped, and the code itself survives only inside a sentence.

As a result, callers:
- can't act on data the VTA already sends, and
- have to string-match the code out of the message to tell rejections apart. That's the drift a typed error is meant to prevent.

## Concrete case
`persona/profile/delete` refuses a bound face with `persona/profile/delete:bound` and `details.personaDids` (`vta-service/src/trust_tasks/persona.rs`, `handle_profile_delete`).

OpenVTC needs those DIDs. A face can be worn by a persona the client can't see from its own memberships, for example another client sharing the VTA or a `pnm` binding. OpenVTC's prompt should say *who* wears the face before it offers to take the face off them.

Because the SDK drops `details`, OpenVTC (OpenVTC/openvtc#430) currently:
- matches `delete:bound]` in the error string, and
- parses the count from "N persona(s) are bound to this profile".

So it can only say "worn by N personas", not which ones. The same applies to the `versionConflict` rejections, whose `details.currentVersion` is also lost.

## Proposal
Add a variant that keeps the rejection as data, for example:

```rust
VtaError::Rejected { code: String, message: String, details: Option<serde_json::Value> }
```

Keep `Display` producing today's `trust task failed [{code}]: {message}` text, so log and error output doesn't change. The existing special cases (`permissionDenied`, `transportUnavailable`, `unavailable`, `unsupportedType`/`unsupportedVersion`) stay as they are.

Possibly add helpers such as `VtaError::rejection_code()` / `rejection_details()`, so callers can match on `code.rsplit_once(':')` for the local part without parsing strings.

## Acceptance
- A `persona/profile/delete:bound` rejection exposes `details.personaDids` to the caller.
- A `…:versionConflict` rejection exposes `details.currentVersion`.
- The `Display` output of existing errors is unchanged.

Once this ships, OpenVTC's `openvtc_core::persona::profile::worn_by` string-match can be replaced with a typed read, and the prompt can name the DIDs.

title: fix(identity): a face worn outside this account's communities is asked about again
body:
## Problem
Deleting a face failed with a dead-end error:

> persona profile delete failed: … trust task failed [persona/profile/delete:bound]: 1 persona(s) are bound to this profile

The delete prompt decides whether to send `unbind` from OpenVTC's binding map. That map is built only from this account's community memberships (`PersonaReadJob::targets`). The VTA counts bindings in every context, so a persona wearing the face anywhere else was invisible to OpenVTC. Examples are another OpenVTC profile sharing the same VTA, or a binding made with `pnm`. In that case the delete went out without `unbind`, the VTA refused it, and nothing on screen offered a way forward.

## Fix
- `openvtc_core::persona::profile::delete` now returns `Deleted::{Done, Worn(n)}`. A `delete:bound` refusal to a delete sent without `unbind` comes back as `Worn(n)` instead of an error. The count is read from the refusal message, because the SDK's `Protocol(String)` drops the payload's `details` (`personaDids`).
- A new `PersonaOutcome::ProfileWorn` re-arms the same delete confirmation with `unbind: true`. Its status line says how many personas outside your communities wear the face and that `y` takes it off them.
- It never retries with `unbind` on the holder's behalf. That would take the face off personas the holder was never told about.

## Follow-up (SDK)
`vta-sdk` turns trust-task rejections into `trust task failed [{code}]: {message}` and drops `details`. Keeping `details` would let this prompt name the persona DIDs instead of only counting them.

## Tests
- `a_bound_refusal_reads_as_worn_with_its_count` (core) checks the message parsing, including a non-bound refusal.
- `a_face_worn_elsewhere_is_asked_about_again_not_failed` checks the re-arm, the status line, and that `y` sends `unbind`.
- `cargo test -p openvtc -p openvtc-core`: all pass. clippy: clean.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

title: fix(identity): s shows one value while values are hidden
body:
## Problem
On **My Identity → Your attributes**, with values hidden (the default, "values hidden — v to show"), pressing `s` ("show one") did nothing. The selected row kept reading "(hidden)".

## Cause
With values hidden, the listing is fetched without values. `RevealValue` only fetched a value when `is_withheld_sensitive` was true, and that requires values to have been requested. Every other case lifted the mask over the in-memory value, but no value was in memory. `value_line` then drew "(hidden)" as before.

## Fix
`RevealValue` now fetches the one value (`pool::reveal`) whenever the row has none in memory and isn't stale. That covers both the withheld-sensitive case and the values-hidden case. A value already in memory is still only unmasked, with no round-trip, and a second `s` still hides it.

## Tests
- New: `a_reveal_while_values_are_hidden_fetches_the_one_value`.
- `a_reveal_names_one_fact_and_toggles_off`: its fixture now holds values. The test's premise is "the value is already in memory", and the old fixture had none; it only passed because of the bug.
- `cargo test -p openvtc`: 810 passed. clippy: clean.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

title: fix(identity): a face editor drops references to attributes the pool no longer holds
body:
## Problem
Editing a face that references an attribute no longer in the pool fails on every save:

> persona profile write failed: … validation error: profile references 1 attribute(s) the pool does not hold: 01M44…

The header said "2 ticked", but only one box was ticked. The missing attribute had no row, so it couldn't be unticked and the face could not be fixed from the editor. This happens when two clients share one VTA (and so one attribute pool) and one of them deletes an attribute another's face still uses.

## Fix
- When the editor opens, `live_refs` is split against the pool listing. References to attributes the pool no longer holds are left out of `ticked` and counted in a new `ProfileForm::dropped` field.
- This is only done against a pool that has loaded and read cleanly (`loaded && load_error.is_none()`), so an unreachable VTA never makes every reference look missing.
- The editor shows an orange line, "N attribute(s) this face showed are no longer in your pool — saving removes them from the face", so the change is stated before the save.

## Tests
- New: `the_editor_drops_references_to_attributes_the_pool_no_longer_holds` covers the clean-read case, the failed-read case and the not-yet-loaded case.
- `cargo test -p openvtc`: 810 passed. `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets`: clean.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

title: fix(join): the cursor can reach Send an open request
body:
## Problem
On the vetting page for a community that vets the people who join, moving the cursor down from **Apply as** took the selection marker away from every row. **Send an open request** could never be highlighted or taken.

## Cause
`KnownVetting::rows()` built the row list from the cursor position: the nested "Apply as" row was only listed while the cursor was on or inside the vetting route. Moving down from it set `row = 3`, the list rebuilt without "Apply as" (3 rows), and index 3 was past the end. Pressing ↓ again wrapped back to the vetting route, and pressing ↑ went back to "Apply as".

## Fix
- `rows()` always includes `ApplyAs`, so each index names the same row no matter where the cursor is.
- A new `KnownVetting::shows()` hides "Apply as" when drawing unless the vetting route is selected. The page looks the same as before.
- A new `KnownVetting::step()` replaces the inline modulo arithmetic. Moving ↓ from the vetting route opens "Apply as". Moving ↑ from below lands on the route itself, never on a hidden row.
- Removed `nested_rows`, `row_is_vetting` and `row_count`, which nothing used any more.

## Tests
- New: `the_cursor_reaches_every_way_in_and_never_rests_on_a_hidden_row` walks the cursor both ways and checks it never rests on a hidden row.
- `cargo test -p openvtc`: 809 passed. `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets`: clean.
- Not yet checked by hand in the TUI.

title: vti-common-v0.37.2
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: A community serves governance/capability/* — members list its capability modules, administrators enable them, and the trust registry follows ([#1948](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1948))

* feat(vtc): a community serves governance/capability/* — members list its capability modules, administrators enable them, and the trust registry follows

  OpenVTC's Capabilities panel sends a signed governance/capability/list/0.1
  to the community's VTC DID over DIDComm or TSP, and the VTC answered
  unsupportedType: it only ever relayed git-trust writes outward. The VTC is
  the source of truth for which capability modules a community has enabled;
  its Trust Registry is a projection, whose own enable/disable are admin-only
  and only switch which record families it accepts.

  "Capability module" (a pluggable governance capability, git-trust first) is
  kept apart from ACL capabilities throughout: crate::capability_modules,
  trust_tasks::capability_module_tasks, AuditEvent::CapabilityModuleChanged.

  list/enable/disable 0.1 are served on the document spine (DISPATCHED_URIS),
  so DIDComm, TSP and HTTPS route them and discovery lists them; every reply,
  refusals included, is signed, addressed to the requester and threaded.

  - list answers members and administrators (an application entry and unknown
    DIDs get permissionDenied), filters on status as the registry does (absent
    means enabled), and answers the generated #response that
    trust-tasks-capability-client's parse_capability_reply reads. Admins
    holding vtc.config.admin also see each decision's projection in ext.
  - enable/disable need vtc.config.admin (VTI-ACL-030) and a step-up bound to
    the document (VTI-APV-015) — the destructive class. They do not park for
    consent: VTI-APV-018–020 / VTI-VTC-022 ask that of authority-conferring
    acts, and a module confers no ACL authority. config.authority defaults to
    the VTC DID and may name nothing else; any other config member is
    configInvalid rather than silently ignored. Declared codes
    unknownCapability, alreadyEnabled, configInvalid, notEnabled are emitted.

  The decision (version, config, enabledAt/By, generation, projection status)
  is persisted in the community keyspace first and audited; the new
  capability_modules::Projector then sends governance/capability/enable|
  disable as the registry's admin via TrustRegistryClient::
  project_capability_module (TSP > DIDComm selection, schema-checked payload).
  alreadyEnabled/notEnabled are success. Transient failures back off 5 s to
  1 h with jitter; a refusal is marked failed, audited once
  (projectionFailed), warned, and still retried at the cap so fixing the
  registry converges. Results are recorded only against the generation sent;
  no lock is held across the round trip.

  The git-trust manifest is a pinned copy of the registry's; enablement does
  not yet gate [hooks.git-trust] or the git-ns projection.

title: VTC: messaging/message/status reply lost on the 12-minute token-refresh reconnect, bounced as unsupportedType
body:
## What we see

A running VTC logs this pair every **12 minutes**, exactly (:05:20, :17:20, :29:20, :41:20, :53:20):

```
WARN vtc_service::messaging: enveloped Trust Task refused — trust-task-error returned task="https://trusttasks.org/spec/messaging/message/status/0.1#response" thid=… status=422 code=unsupportedType
WARN vtc_service::messaging: received unhandled problem-report — not replying (a reply would loop) from="did:webvh:…:mediator" code=e.p.delivery.refused comment=Message not accepted for delivery
```

It isn't a security problem and no delivery is lost, but it's a real defect and fills the logs with noise.

## Diagnosis so far (not yet confirmed)

1. `affinidi-messaging-delivery`'s `outbox_drain_loop` (every 10s, `vtc-service/src/messaging.rs`) calls `DidCommTransport::outbox_status` → `trust_tasks().message_status()`, which waits for the mediator's reply over the websocket (`send_message(…, wait_for_response = true)`).
2. affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.33.0 refreshes the access token and **reconnects the websocket at 80% of the token's TTL** (`websocket.rs`, `refresh_after_secs`). A 15-minute token gives the 12-minute cadence. The reconnect calls `fail_pending_requests()`, which drops the waiter.
3. The mediator's reply (threaded correctly, `thid` = envelope id, checked against mediator 0.37 `trust_tasks.rs`) then arrives with no waiter. It goes to the VTC's general inbound router, which has no handler for a `#response` and answers with a `422 trust-task-error`.
4. The mediator won't deliver that error (`e.p.delivery.refused`) and sends the VTC a problem-report. The VTC correctly doesn't reply, so it stops there.

The SDK treats the failed `message_status` as "receipts unavailable" and falls back to the outbox listing for that round, so the push itself still settles.

## Open questions

- **Why every cycle?** A ~300µs query on a 10s poll should rarely overlap the reconnect, yet it hit 5/5. Something makes them coincide. Candidates: the refresh's HTTP `refresh()` call is awaited inside the websocket task's `select!` while a query is queued, or the reply is held and flushed after the reconnect.
- **Why is the outbox ever non-empty?** `outbox_status` sends nothing for an empty hop-id list, so a query every cycle means the VTC holds an outbox entry that keeps being polled. Check the outbox keyspace for a member push that never settles.
- Do pushes in flight across a reconnect ever escalate to a second transport (a duplicate delivery to the member) because their receipt was lost?

## Likely fixes

- **SDK (affinidi-tdk-rs):** keep reply registrations alive across a self-initiated token-refresh reconnect, or re-issue the query instead of failing it, so the late reply reaches its waiter.
- **VTC (this repo):** the inbound Trust Task router should never answer an unsolicited `#response` with an error. Drop it with a debug log, the same rule as for problem-reports. Check whether vta-service's router has the same behaviour.
- Consider logging the proactive refresh/reconnect at INFO so this pattern can be read from the logs.

title: Should a VTC's identifier be required to be "public", or may a restricted community be "directed"?
body:
The spec says, in three places that a VTC's identifier can only truthfully be declared `public` ("a community that cannot be found cannot be joined"). This is likely too strong due to the following reasons:

1. __Restricted communities are contemplated.__ The VTC definition says a VTC may be "a family … a company … a nation state." A family community's identifier is likely not something public so that anyone can find it.
2. __Joining is by invitation, not only discovery.__ A prospect joins via a VIC (verifiable invitation credential), which contains the community's identifier. The prospect does not "find" the community — they are invited. So "cannot be found, cannot be joined" does not justify `public`.
3. __"Findable" and "public" are being conflated.__ Resolvability (can the DID document be fetched?) and correlation scope (how widely is the identifier intended to be correlated?) are different properties. A community's identifier must be resolvable by whoever verifies its members' credentials — at minimum, its members — which is `directed`, not `public`


Proposed: a VTC's identifier is `directed` at minimum (its members must be able to find it) and `public` if the community is open to outsiders; never `pairwise` (a community has more than one member). This matches the witness case, which is already "directed at minimum."

Decision: is `public` a hard requirement (every VTC discoverable by anyone, for third-party verification) or a choice (a restricted community may be `directed`)? If a choice, the three places in the spec - (`verifiable_trust_community.md`, `body.md` VMC section ~383, and the Correlation Scope section) - have to be updated; if a requirement, the "family to nation state" range needs reconciling.

title: feat(vtc): a community serves governance/capability/* — members list its capability modules, administrators enable them, and the trust registry follows
body:
## Problem

OpenVTC's per-community **Capabilities** panel sends a signed
`governance/capability/list/0.1` Trust Task — enveloped over DIDComm or TSP — to
the community's **VTC DID**. vtc-service did not serve `governance/capability/*`
at all: the envelope handler reached `dispatch_trust_task_core`, found no arm,
and answered `unsupportedType`. The only capability traffic the VTC had was the
*outbound* git-trust hook relay to its Trust Registry (#681).

Settled architecture: **the VTC is the source of truth for which capability
modules a community has enabled; the Trust Registry is a projection.** The
registry's own `governance/capability/enable|disable` are admin-only (its
`admin_dids`, i.e. the VTC) and only switch which record families
(`git-trust/grant|revoke`) it accepts.

Also: an answered `join-requests/status` poll logged nothing at INFO (only the
re-delivery paths warned), which made a stuck-join investigation read as "no
polls arrived".

## Design

**Naming.** "Capability" already means an ACL capability on an administrator's
entry (#1924/#1927). The new concept is a *capability module* throughout:
`crate::capability_modules`, `trust_tasks::capability_module_tasks`, audit event
`CapabilityModuleChanged`, log text "capability module". The ACL capability that
gates enabling one is `vtc.config.admin`.

**Served tasks** (`trust_tasks/capability_module_tasks.rs`). `list`, `enable`,
`disable` 0.1, wire types from `trust_tasks_rs::specs::governance::capability`
(generated `Payload` / `Response`, `error_codes`), added to `DISPATCHED_URIS`,
so DIDComm, TSP and HTTPS all route them and discovery lists them. Every reply —
refusals included — goes through the spine: signed (`sign_response`), addressed
to the requester and threaded (`respond_with` / `reject_with`, SPEC §4.9).

**State** (`capability_modules/mod.rs`). One row, `capability-modules/state`, in
the `community` keyspace (beside profile/branding; backed up with them): per
module `version`, `enabled`, `config`, `enabledAt`/`enabledBy`,
`disabledAt`/`disabledBy`/`disableReason`, a `generation`, and the registry
`projection` (`pending|applied|failed`, attempts, lastError, nextAttemptAt,
appliedAt). Available modules: `git-trust` 0.1. Its manifest is parsed into the
generated `CapabilityManifest`; no shared crate publishes it, so it is a
member-for-member copy of the registry's (`git_trust.rs`), pinned by
`the_git_trust_manifest_is_the_registrys`.

**`list`** — any member (live ACL entry) or administrator (incl. a console key's
admin); an `application` entry (bridge / external signer — not a membership) and
DIDs with no entry get `permissionDenied`; unsigned REST gets `proofRequired`.
`status` absent ⇒ `enabled`, `available` ⇒ not enabled, `all` ⇒ both — the
registry's `handle_list` filter. Entry shape `{manifest, enabled, enabledAt?}`,
validated against the generated `#response`, parsed in tests with
`trust_tasks_capability_client::parse_capability_reply` (incl. a request built
by the client's own `build_list_document`). Administrators holding
`vtc.config.admin` also get `ext["org.openvtc"].projection`.

**`enable` / `disable`** — `vtc.config.admin` (VTI-ACL-030, via
`capable_signer`; suspended / expired entries refused as elsewhere), then every
check that decides the outcome (declared codes `unknownCapability`,
`alreadyEnabled`, `configInvalid`, `notEnabled`), then a **step-up bound to the
document** (`acl::bound_step_up`, VTI-APV-015) — the VTC's form of the
`destructive` class (vtc-capability-modules.md §4.1; the enable spec asks the
same of disable). Not parked in the action list: second-party consent is what
VTI-APV-018–020 / VTI-VTC-022 require of authority-conferring/-reducing acts,
and enabling a module confers no ACL authority, so single-administrator mode has
nothing to waive. `config.authority` defaults to the VTC DID; any other
authority, or any other config member (e.g. `grantOnRole`, which lives in
`[hooks.git-trust]` and nothing here would read), is `configInvalid` (R3.2).
Companion modules (`delegate`) are not supported yet. Refused without an audit
writer rather than made unaudited.

**Projection.** The handler persists, audits (`CapabilityModuleChanged{enabled|
disabled}`), wakes the projector and answers with `projection.status: pending`;
it never calls the registry. `capability_modules::Projector` (spawned in
`server.rs` when a registry client exists, supervised like the hook relay) sends
`governance/capability/enable|disable` through the new
`TrustRegistryClient::project_capability_module` — on
`MessagingRegistryClient` that is the existing signed round trip with the
registry client's TSP > DIDComm selection (REST has no governance surface →
permanent refusal), payload checked against the published schema before it
leaves. `alreadyEnabled` / `notEnabled` (extended codes, or the registry's
current `taskFailed` + `already_enabled:` / `not_enabled:` prefix) are success.
Transient failures back off 5 s·2ⁿ to 1 h with jitter; permanent ones mark
`failed`, write `CapabilityModuleChanged{projectionFailed}` once on the
transition, warn, and retry at the cap — fixing the registry side converges
without re-sending. A result is recorded only against the generation it was
sent for. No lock is held across the round trip (state lock covers local store
ops only).

**Not in this PR.** Enablement does not yet gate the VTC's own git-trust
machinery (`[hooks.git-trust]` relay, git-ns projection) or discovery; a module
the VTC holds no decision for is never projected (so a registry enabled by hand
is never disabled behind the operator's back).

**`join-requests/status` logging** (second commit). `answer` now logs one INFO
line per answered poll: request id, applicant DID, status, whether it was the
id-less form, whether a resend was asked, `credentialsDelivered`, and the resend
decision. No PII beyond the DID the join logs already carry.

## Files

- `vtc-service/src/capability_modules/mod.rs` — new: definitions, state, plan/commit, audit, projector.
- `vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/capability_module_tasks.rs` — new: the three handlers + tests.
- `vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs` — module, dispatch arm, `DISPATCHED_URIS`, `DISPATCHED_WITHOUT_PROOF` (list's proof is RECOMMENDED).
- `vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/member_tasks.rs` — `acting_party` / `Actor` made `pub(super)`.
- `vtc-service/src/registry/{client,messaging,mod}.rs` — `project_capability_module`, `CapabilityModuleChange`, mock, reply classification + test.
- `vtc-service/src/server.rs` — projector spawn.
- `vti-common/src/audit/{event,mod}.rs` — `AuditEvent::CapabilityModuleChanged` (enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so additive).
- `vtc-service/admin-ui/src/plugins/audit.tsx` — label for the new event.
- `vtc-service/src/routes/join_requests/status.rs` — the INFO line.
- `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/03-vtc/trust-registry.md` — flow + operator docs.

## Tests

Run locally on macOS (Rust stable):

- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` — **2842 passed**, 0 failed (incl. discovery, `dispatcher_routes_every_dispatched_uri`, `the_dispatched_set_declares_the_proofs…`, conformance/error-code census, size census).
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client` — **5362 passed**.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --doc` — passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.

New tests (`trust_tasks::capability_module_tasks::tests`, `capability_modules::tests`, `registry::messaging::tests`):
- member list on REST/DIDComm/TSP: signed, issuer = VTC, recipient = member, threadId = request id, parses with `parse_capability_reply`; no projection ext for members
- the client's own `build_list_document`, signed, is answered on its thread
- non-member refused `permissionDenied` (signed, threaded refusal); `application` entry refused
- status filter: absent/enabled/available/all before and after enable; bad status → `malformedRequest`
- admin listing carries the projection status
- VTI-ACL-030: moderator / member / stranger refused enable and disable `permissionDenied`, nothing written, nothing projected
- VTI-APV-015: enable without a bound step-up is refused and writes nothing
- enable persists (authority defaulted to VTC DID), handler never calls the registry, projector sends it, status → applied, not re-sent; audit `enabled`, `projected`
- projection failure: transient → pending + backoff; permanent → failed + one `projectionFailed` audit row; then converges
- declared refusals: unknownCapability (slug, version), configInvalid (foreign authority, unknown member), notEnabled, alreadyEnabled
- disable keeps the row, audits the reason, projects only the current generation
- manifest is schema-valid and equal to the registry's; backoff bounded; registry reply classification (extended + legacy idempotent codes)

## Spec / open questions

- **`list` access is host policy, not spec.** `governance/capability/list/0.1`
  declares no access rule ("hosts MAY restrict `available`/`all` listings to
  community members or operators while leaving `enabled` open"). This VTC
  restricts *every* listing to members + administrators. Its proof is only
  RECOMMENDED, so the list URI is in `DISPATCHED_WITHOUT_PROOF` with the reason
  (an unsigned REST caller is refused `proofRequired`; DIDComm/TSP always
  require one at the spine).
- **No access error code declared for `list`** — refusals use the standard
  `permissionDenied`.
- **Which ACL capability gates enable/disable** is not stated anywhere;
  `vtc.config.admin` was chosen (the community's configuration). A dedicated
  capability would need an `acl/_shared` change upstream.
- **Consent class.** Implemented as bound step-up only (see Design). If
  reviewers want N-of-M consent instead, it needs a new `Act`, an action-list
  kind and a pinned summary template (also mirrored in the console).
- **The git-trust manifest has no shared source**; the copy is pinned by test
  against the registry's literal. The list spec's own example adds
  `lifecycleHooks`; the registry's manifest does not, and this follows the
  registry.
- **The registry emits `taskFailed` + message prefix** rather than the declared
  `governance/capability/enable:alreadyEnabled` / `disable:notEnabled`; both are
  accepted here.

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide.md §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no new client; the registry round trip's existing 60 s reply window bounds it.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — the state lock is released before `project_capability_module` and re-taken to record the result.
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — the VTC is the source of truth; the projection is a resumable pending record keyed by generation, and the registry answers convergently.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — 5 s·2ⁿ capped at 1 h with jitter; enable/disable are convergent at the registry.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — a failed pass is logged and the loop continues; panics restart under the supervisor.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a (no acks/deletes added).
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — generated spec types only; replies validated against the published `#response`; stored state is camelCase + `deny_unknown_fields`; consumer is `trust-tasks-capability-client` (OpenVTC), tested.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — absent `status` ⇒ `enabled`; unknown future status ⇒ `enabled`; no registry ⇒ decision held, projection pending with the reason.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — "acknowledged" only on a registry answer; failures in projection status, audit row and warn log.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — before the state write: nothing happened, the spine released the id; after it: the projector re-drives on the next boot/pass.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — none.

## Repo checklist (CONTRIBUTING.md)

- [x] `cargo check` passes for the entire workspace
- [x] `cargo test` passes (see Tests)
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` clean
- [x] New public functions have `///` doc comments

- [x] Conforms to the VTI specification; cites VTI-ACL-030, VTI-APV-015, VTI-APV-018–020/VTI-VTC-022 (why not consent)
- [x] No divergence to record
- [x] PR title is a conventional commit
- [x] No `version = ` edits
- [x] Commits are signed off (DCO)
