title: feat(vtc): a community serves governance/capability/* — members list its capability modules, administrators enable them, and the trust registry follows (#1948)
body:
feat(vtc): a community serves governance/capability/* — members list its capability modules, administrators enable them, and the trust registry follows (#1948)

* feat(vtc): a community serves governance/capability/* — members list its capability modules, administrators enable them, and the trust registry follows

OpenVTC's Capabilities panel sends a signed governance/capability/list/0.1
to the community's VTC DID over DIDComm or TSP, and the VTC answered
unsupportedType: it only ever relayed git-trust writes outward. The VTC is
the source of truth for which capability modules a community has enabled;
its Trust Registry is a projection, whose own enable/disable are admin-only
and only switch which record families it accepts.

"Capability module" (a pluggable governance capability, git-trust first) is
kept apart from ACL capabilities throughout: crate::capability_modules,
trust_tasks::capability_module_tasks, AuditEvent::CapabilityModuleChanged.

list/enable/disable 0.1 are served on the document spine (DISPATCHED_URIS),
so DIDComm, TSP and HTTPS route them and discovery lists them; every reply,
refusals included, is signed, addressed to the requester and threaded.

- list answers members and administrators (an application entry and unknown
  DIDs get permissionDenied), filters on status as the registry does (absent
  means enabled), and answers the generated #response that
  trust-tasks-capability-client's parse_capability_reply reads. Admins
  holding vtc.config.admin also see each decision's projection in ext.
- enable/disable need vtc.config.admin (VTI-ACL-030) and a step-up bound to
  the document (VTI-APV-015) — the destructive class. They do not park for
  consent: VTI-APV-018–020 / VTI-VTC-022 ask that of authority-conferring
  acts, and a module confers no ACL authority. config.authority defaults to
  the VTC DID and may name nothing else; any other config member is
  configInvalid rather than silently ignored. Declared codes
  unknownCapability, alreadyEnabled, configInvalid, notEnabled are emitted.

The decision (version, config, enabledAt/By, generation, projection status)
is persisted in the community keyspace first and audited; the new
capability_modules::Projector then sends governance/capability/enable|
disable as the registry's admin via TrustRegistryClient::
project_capability_module (TSP > DIDComm selection, schema-checked payload).
alreadyEnabled/notEnabled are success. Transient failures back off 5 s to
1 h with jitter; a refusal is marked failed, audited once
(projectionFailed), warned, and still retried at the cap so fixing the
registry converges. Results are recorded only against the generation sent;
no lock is held across the round trip.

The git-trust manifest is a pinned copy of the registry's; enablement does
not yet gate [hooks.git-trust] or the git-ns projection.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): every answered join-requests/status poll is logged at info

An answered status poll logged nothing — only the credential re-delivery
paths warned — so a stuck join whose applicant was polling steadily looked
in the logs exactly like one whose polls never arrived. One info line per
answered poll now names the request id, the applicant DID, the status,
whether the poll was id-less, whether a resend was asked, whether
credentials were delivered, and the resend decision. Nothing beyond the DID
the join logs already carry.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: cnm-cli-v0.27.1
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: A cooling-off suspends its subject, and single-administrator mode can remove now (VTI-APV-019, VTI-APV-022) ([#1944](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1944))

* feat(vtc): a cooling-off suspends its subject, and single-administrator mode can remove now (VTI-APV-019, VTI-APV-022)

  Removing another unrestricted administrator when nobody else can consent
  waits out a cooling-off (acl.removal_cooling_off, default 24 h). Until now
  the subject kept full authority for that whole window, and in
  single-administrator mode there was no way past it.

  Suspension (vtc-action-list.md §8.2). From the moment a cooling-off
  reduction is raised until it lands or is cancelled, the subject's entry
  authorizes nothing. The suspension is set on the entry wherever it is read
  (acl::storage::get_acl_entry / list_acl_entries), and VtcAclEntry::can,
  can_any and can_approve answer false for it, so every gate refuses without a
  per-handler check. The signed administrative door (resolve_admin_claims,
  console keys included), the git-ns door (acting_as), require_capability and
  ACL reads refuse with a message naming the action and when it lands. The
  subject can still sign in, read the action list (callerRole: subject) and
  cancel a request of its own; its event stream carries only actions and the
  mode banner. It approves and decides nothing, acknowledges nothing, and is no
  role assigner for the attrition guard; raising a cooling-off checks the guard
  as though the subject were already gone, and only one cooling-off runs on a
  subject at a time. Its sessions are revoked at suspension, as any reduction's
  are. The row is never changed, so cancelling restores it exactly. A
  suspended subject cannot raise a counter-removal, so the first to act wins
  outright; refuse_if_reduced_first stays as a backstop.

  The suspension is derived from the open action and kept beside the entry as
  a marker (suspended:<did> in the ACL keyspace). admin_actions::save writes
  it before an action that suspends and lifts it after one that no longer does
  (R2.1), so a crash can only over-restrict, and reconcile_suspensions settles
  either half at start (before serving), on every sweep, and after a restore.

  Remove now (vtc-action-list.md §8.5, single-administrator mode only). No new
  task: a reduction's payload carries ext["org.openvtc"].immediate =
  {confirm, actionId?}. confirm must be the subject's DID (or the action id
  being landed), checked before any gesture; the gesture is bound to the
  payload digest, which includes `immediate`, so a gesture for the delayed
  removal is never spent on the immediate one or the reverse (VTI-APV-015).
  Sending the same operation with `immediate` naming an open cooling-off lands
  it now. Refused without the mode (naming the cooling-off and that the mode
  is host-set), on a mismatched confirmation, without the gesture, and by the
  attrition guard. Audited Critical as SingleAdminMode reductionImmediate
  before the write, then AuthorityReducedUnopposed, and the subject is told.
  The landed cooling-off closes landedAfterCoolingOff with ext landedNow; a
  reduction that never waited enters the history with the same marker.

- **vtc**: A subject may relabel its own entry; single-administrator mode is one person under many identifiers (VTI-ACL-052, VTI-APV-022) ([#1941](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1941))

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#54 and #55 (both merged).

  VTI-ACL-052 item 2 — a subject may change its own entry's label and
  nothing else, on every door that writes it (acl/update 0.1 and 0.2,
  acl/grant re-stating the same entry, vtc/members/update). No step-up: the
  label confers no authority (VTI-ACL-001). The change is audited as a
  MemberUpdated row naming the old and new label and `labelSetBySubject`,
  and the entry carries `label_set_by_subject` (serde-default false,
  cleared when anyone else sets the label), shown to other parties as
  `ext["org.openvtc"].labelSetBySubject` on acl/list and acl/show 0.2 — an
  ext member, so the published response schemas are untouched. A request
  that changes the label and anything else is refused whole. A subject's
  own write never re-affirms a delegation under review.

  VTI-ACL-052 item 3 (as widened by #55) — in single-administrator mode a
  subject whose entry has unrestricted act scope (granting::is_unrestricted:
  a community-admin acting everywhere with its full ceiling) may modify its
  own entry on acl/update/0.2 and acl/change-role/0.2. It takes the
  subject's step-up bound to the operation (VTI-APV-015) and a Critical
  SingleAdminMode{event: selfEditWaived} row written before the write
  (acl::single_admin::authorize_self_edit), and is refused if it would leave
  no live unrestricted entry (narrowing, demoting or shortening the life of
  the only one). Ending the subject's vtc.roles.assign is attrition-checked
  like any removal. Every other self-edit is refused as before, and the
  refusals now say what the subject may do instead.

  VTI-APV-022 ([#55](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/55)) — single-administrator mode waives second-party consent
  whether or not other administrators' entries exist: one person may hold
  an administrator entry per device, and the node cannot tell one person's
  identifiers from two people's. gesture_then_consent_for and the session
  door's require() no longer test for an empty approver set; git-ns rule 7
  is waived the same way (others_eligible is gone). A reduction of another
  administrator (VTI-APV-019) is not parked for a third party's consent in
  the mode: it takes the unopposed path — step-up, notice to the subject,
  Critical row — and keeps its cooling-off, which now lands in the mode even
  with a third administrator present (recheck_cooling_off and the sweeper's
  invalidation skip the "a third party can now consent" check).

title: fix(capabilities): wait on a request's thread before sending it
body:
## Problem

**1. A fast reply was lost to the send that asked for it.** Pressing `c` (Capabilities) on an Active community showed *"no reply within 30s — the community's governance host may be offline"*. The VTC had in fact answered in about 300µs, with a signed `trust-task-error` (`unsupportedType`). A retry showed the right text, *"this community does not offer capability management"*.

The view armed `pending_thid` only when the spawned send's outcome was applied (`CapabilityOutcome::apply`). The reply comes in on the inbound channel and the outcome on the dispatch channel, so a fast reply could be applied first. `apply_capability_replies` then saw `pending_thid == None` and dropped the reply without a log line, and the 30 s sweep failed the view. The Repos panel had the same pattern for every git-ns send (`ReposOutcome::apply` armed `view.pending`, and `link.poll` for polls).

**2. A refusal was reported as a replay of itself.** A `trust-task-error` is offered to the capability view first. `community_reply_proven` verifies it **and records it** in `seen_documents`. It then falls through to the git-ns arm and to the join refusal arm. There `community_document` checked it again, found it already recorded, and logged `WARN unverified community refusal ignored reason=it was already acted on (replay)`. This also broke real join refusals. A genuine join refusal also passes the capability arm first, so it hit the same check, and the pending join was **never marked Rejected**. The new join test fails that way without this fix.

**3. Members are offered capability enable/disable.** Enabling and disabling capabilities is for VTC administrators only. A member who tried got the refusal as a bare code.

## Fix

**Bug 1: wait on the thread before the send starts** (`capability_actions.rs`, `repos_actions.rs`, `mod.rs`)
- The request document is built on the loop thread (`CapabilityJob::prepare` and, for repos, `git_ns::build` in `Loop::send`). Its `correlation_thread` (the doc id) is the `threadId` the reply carries. The view or link-poll slot is armed with it and `sent_at` **before** `spawn_dispatch`. The job only signs and sends; signing never changes the id. The persona secret is already resolved on the loop, as before.
- A send that succeeds reports nothing. A send that fails clears the wait and shows the error, but **only if the view is still waiting on that request's thread**. A late failure for an older request no longer ends a newer request's wait (or a different community's).
- `openvtc-core`: `git_ns::build` (unsigned; `build_signed` now wraps it). `capabilities` re-exports `correlation_thread` and adds a `RequestDocument` alias. `send_capability_document` threads and returns `correlation_thread(doc)` instead of the bare `doc.id`, which is the same value for every document we build. The shared crate is unchanged; replies are still classified with `parse_capability_reply`.
- A capability or git-ns reply that matches nothing pending is now logged. It is `warn` for a listing, toggle or git-ns answer. For a refusal it is `debug`, because every `trust-task-error` is offered to both views, whatever it refuses, so a refusal that is not ours is routine. The default filter (`openvtc=debug`) still records it.

**Bug 2: a refusal is checked once per pass** (`message_dispatch.rs`, join `trust-task-error` arm)
- If the refusal was already proven and recorded earlier in the same `process_inbound_message` pass (`reply_proven == Some(true)`), the join arm skips the second `community_document` check:
  - If the refusal's `thid` matches a pending join of ours, it goes to `handle_join_trust_task_error` as before. It is already recorded, so it is not committed again.
  - Otherwise it is let go with a debug line. Before, it went on to the misleading "trust-task-error did not match a pending request id" warning.
- Replay protection across messages is unchanged. A refusal not proven earlier in the pass goes through `community_document` exactly as before, and the same refusal delivered again is still refused (tested).

**Bug 3: enable/disable is for administrators, and a refusal says so** (`capability_actions::toggle_refusal`, `capabilities_panel.rs`)
- **Decision: keep `e`, explain the refusal.** The client cannot tell beforehand whether the persona is an administrator of the VTC:
  - Administration is the VTC's own ACL (an `admin` role there), which a member cannot read.
  - The role VAC a member holds names the roles it was issued with (normally `member`), not the current ACL. A later promotion or demotion is not reflected in it.
  - The community profile carries nothing about the viewer's role.

  Hiding `e` on that basis would sometimes hide it from real administrators. Instead, a `permissionDenied` (or `forbidden`) refusal of a toggle now reads *"only the community's administrators can enable or disable capabilities"*. Other refusals keep their code and message. The footer hint is now `e enable/disable (administrators)`.

## Tests

- Capabilities (`capability_actions.rs` tests):
  - `a_reply_that_overtakes_the_send_is_still_matched`: the `unsupportedType` refusal lands before the send's outcome, still produces "does not offer capability management", and the outcome does not re-arm the view.
  - `a_toggle_reply_that_overtakes_the_send_is_still_matched`
  - `a_late_failure_for_a_superseded_request_keeps_the_current_wait`
  - `another_communitys_request_does_not_touch_the_view`
  - `a_member_refused_a_toggle_is_told_it_is_for_administrators`
  - `another_toggle_refusal_keeps_its_code`
  - The existing tests were updated to the arm-then-outcome flow.
- Repos (`repos_actions.rs` tests):
  - `a_reply_that_overtakes_the_send_is_still_matched`
  - `a_poll_answer_that_overtakes_the_send_is_still_matched`
  - `a_late_failure_for_a_superseded_request_keeps_the_current_wait`
  - `a_failed_poll_frees_its_slot`
  - The existing outcome tests were updated.
- Dispatcher (`message_dispatch.rs` tests): both tests run a signed refusal through the real off-loop check and capture `WARN` output.
  - `a_capability_refusal_is_not_reported_as_its_own_replay`: the refusal reaches the capability view, no replay or "refusal ignored" warning is logged, and redelivering it is still refused.
  - `a_join_refusal_still_rejects_the_pending_join`: `permissionDenied` on our submit marks the join Rejected.
  - With the Bug 2 fix disabled, both tests fail.

### Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test --workspace`: all passed (openvtc bin 808, openvtc-core 887, plus integration suites; 0 failed). The `openvtc-vetting-pcs` `wire_fixture` test, which is known to be flaky under the parallel run, passed this time.
- Not exercised against a live VTC; the race is covered by the unit tests above.

### Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new clients
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the wait is armed before the send, but it is display state that a failure clears and the reply window bounds; nothing is persisted
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): unchanged
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): a failed link poll frees its slot and is retried on the next tick, as before
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no wire change; the envelope `thid` is `correlation_thread(doc)`, which equals `doc.id` for every document we send
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): dropped replies are now logged; the administrator refusal is worded from the refusal code, not guessed
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): the only persisted mutation touched is the replay record, which is still committed once per document
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

the join arm now skips the second check. If the refusal matches no
pending join of ours, the arm lets it go with a debug line. Replay
protection across messages is unchanged: the same refusal delivered
again is still refused.

Enabling and disabling capabilities is for administrators only. The VTC
refuses anyone else with `permissionDenied`. The client cannot know in
advance whether the persona is an administrator. That is the VTC's ACL,
which a member cannot read, and a role VAC lists the roles it was issued
with, not the current ACL. So `e` stays available, but that refusal now
reads "only the community's administrators can enable or disable
capabilities", and the hint says `e enable/disable (administrators)`.

title: feat(vtc): a suspended subject's git rights are withdrawn from the registry and the forge until its cooling-off closes (VTI-APV-019)
body:
**Stacks on #1944 and must merge after it.** Until #1944 merges this PR's diff against `main` includes #1944's commits. The changes here are `a323cf3f`, `0a90c11b` and `faedf826`. Once #1944 lands I'll rebase onto `main`.

## What and why

#1944 suspends the subject of a removal cooling-off. The VTC refuses everything the subject signs, but #1944 left one gap (its follow-up note): the **git-ns projection still published the subject's git rights**. Its Trust Registry records stayed up, including the implied `git.commit.sign`, so the community's commit check kept passing its commits. Its forge roles also stayed in every `desiredRoles`. Both lasted until the removal landed.

With this PR, a suspended holder is **projected as holding nothing** (`vtc-action-list.md` §8.2, VTI-APV-019):

- its registry records are withdrawn: explicit rights, the implied `git.commit.sign` of `own`/`maintain`/`ns.admin`, and any role-derived grant this projection owns;
- its linked accounts leave every repository's `desiredRoles`, so the bridge takes off the roles it gave. This works the same way as an unlinked account (git-namespaces.md, *Linking*);
- a repository created during the suspension gives it no role, and a drift revert never sends one back;
- **the pull-request gate counts none of its rights and not its role** (`faedf826`). It reads rights through `ProjectionView::effective_on`, so a suspended owner or maintainer is not always allowed, its reopen is no override, and its VTC role counts toward no `roles` level. It is still a member until the removal lands, so a `members` level still admits it. Membership is not authority.

**Nothing is deleted.** The rights stay recorded on the entry. Cancelling republishes, from the stored rights, exactly what they still give. When the removal lands, the rights go with the entry and nothing already withdrawn is withdrawn again.

## Design: reconcile, not events

The projector already re-derives everything on every pass: the registry diff against the mirror, and role projection by digest. So the cheapest crash-safe design is to make the projection's **input** a pure function of the stored rights and the suspension markers. No event path is involved.

- **`projection::ProjectionView`** is the stored records with every row of a subject holding a `suspended:<did>` marker left out. It is a **separate type from `Snapshot`**. It lends out row slices and the (unfiltered) namespace and repository records, but never a `Snapshot` or a `RightsSet`. Every write path loads its own `Snapshot` and writes with `put_rights`, so none of them can be given the view and persist the filtered rows. `Snapshot::load` is unchanged, as #1944's note asked.
- These consumers now read the view: registry `reconcile`, `bridge::project_roles`, `desired_roles_now` (drift revert), `desired_roles_for_repo` (repo create), `withdrawal_pending` (which has to agree with reconcile), and `projection/show`'s `pendingChanges`. `verify` and `role_mapped` are unchanged. Role-derived tuples are filtered in `desired_with`, not in `role_mapped`, because unbind's hand-back to the hook relay still reads `role_mapped`.
- **R2.1:** the marker is the only state. A crash after the marker and before the withdrawal, or after the lift and before the republish, converges on the next pass, including the first pass after a start. #1944 already orders marker → record → lift.
- **Landing race:** an `executing` action is still open, so the marker is held through the effect and lifted only after the record closes. A pass between the effect and the lift finds the rows already gone, so it withdraws nothing twice and republishes nothing.
- **R1.1:** role changes go through the existing `git_ns_jobs` queue and `dispatch_due` (`send_v0_4`, 0.4/0.5 only, retried until the bridge answers). Nothing is sent inline, and nothing is treated as delivered on a bare send `Ok`.

## Audit

`GitNsOperation` rows with target = the subject and detail = `{actionId, rights: <count>}` (plus `landsAt` on the first):

- `gitNs.projection.withheld`: a suspension now withholds a holder of git rights;
- `gitNs.projection.restored`: the suspension ended with rights still recorded (cancelled, or a demotion that keeps them), so they are republished;
- `gitNs.projection.released`: it ended with nothing left (the removal landed).

**Severity: normal (Info).** These rows record a mechanical consequence that only *removes* what is published. They bypass no control. The decision behind them is already audited at its own severity: the action's `raised`/`completed`/`cancelled` rows, and `AuthorityReducedUnopposed`/`SingleAdminMode` at `Critical` for an unopposed landing. A second high-severity row per suspension would only add noise. The projector writes these rows before its audit tail runs, so the row wakes the same pass. The order is audit first, then the record of what was audited: a crash between the two can give a duplicate row, never a missing one. The count only, never which rights, and never a grant's `reason`.

## Not done / follow-ups

- Grants that the v0.1 `[hooks.git-trust]` relay publishes **outside** every bound namespace are not the projection's, so they are not withheld. This is documented.
- Withdrawal takes effect on the next projector tick (`git_ns.tick_seconds`), not synchronously with raising the cooling-off.

## Boot ordering

`reconcile_suspensions` now runs **before** the git-ns projector is spawned (`server.rs`), so the projector's first pass never reads a marker the action list does not hold. #1944 already put it on the startup path. It is bounded local-store work: one pass over the action list and the markers, with no network and no wait on another task. So the startup path still reaches its shutdown select (mediator-connection invariant 1).

## Docs

- `docs/03-vtc/git-namespaces.md`: new *While its holder is suspended* section.
- `docs/05-design-notes/vtc-action-list.md`: §8.2 bullet and an as-built row.
- `docs/03-vtc/admin-access.md`: the cooling-off bullet.
- Console: the cooling-off card now says the subject's git rights are withdrawn.

## Tests

Unit tests in `vtc-service/src/git_ns/tests/suspension.rs`. They use the real projector pass (`Projector::run_once`), `reconcile`, `project_roles`/`dispatch_due`, the `FakeBridge`, and `MockRegistryClient`:

- `suspension_withdraws_projected_git_rights_without_deleting_them`
- `suspended_subjects_commit_signing_right_is_not_published`
- `cancelled_cooling_off_republishes_exactly_what_was_withdrawn`
- `bridge_receives_role_withdrawal_on_suspension_and_reprojection_on_cancel`: a queued `projectRoles` job without the subject's account, then one with it back at `git.repo.maintain`
- `landing_after_suspension_removes_rights_once`
- `reconcile_converges_projection_after_crash_between_marker_and_withdraw`: also covers a registry failure on the first pass
- `write_paths_never_persist_the_projection_view`

I disabled the filter in `ProjectionView::of` to check these tests: all 7 fail without it.

Pull-request gate tests (`git_ns/tests/pr_gate.rs`): `pr_gate_ignores_a_suspended_holders_rights`, `pr_gate_ignores_a_suspended_holders_role`, `pr_gate_counts_the_rights_again_after_cancel`. If the gate reads an unfiltered view, all three fail.

Integration tests (`tests/it/cooling_off_suspension.rs`) over a **real** cooling-off (`vtc/members/admin-remove` between two admins) on the signed spine:

- `cooling_off_withdraws_the_subjects_git_projection_and_cancel_restores_it`
- `landed_cooling_off_leaves_nothing_to_withdraw_twice`

Results (local, macOS, RAM disk):

- `TMPDIR=/Volumes/RAMDisk VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1 cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client -p cnm-cli --no-fail-fast`: 2946 run, 2940 passed, 6 failed, 1 skipped. All 6 are the ones the skip flag is known to fail: the four `admin_ui::tests` and `routing_modes::path_mode_admin_{bare_prefix,trailing_slash}_serves_admin_spa`.
- `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1 cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1 cargo check --workspace --all-targets`: clean.
- admin-ui (after `npm ci`, `package-lock.json` unchanged): `npx vitest run` → 65 files, 788 tests passed; `npm run lint` → exit 0.

title: fix(join): an id-less poll's answer resolves the join that never got a reply
body:
## Problem

A member joined a VTC. The VTC approved the join and lists them as a member, but OpenVTC still shows the join as **Pending** with "no response from the community yet".

#226 added the recovery for this: when we hold only our own placeholder id, the status poll leaves the request id out and the community answers with its own. But `handle_join_status_response` correlates strictly by `requestId`. The answer carries the community's id, which matches nothing we hold, so it is dropped with `status-response did not match a pending request id — ignoring`. The #226 commit message says the handler "already calls `confirm_request_id`". It never has (checked with `git log -L`).

## Fix

- `Account::membership_awaiting_request_id`: finds the Pending membership for the VTC that still holds our placeholder. If several personas are waiting, the reply's `to` decides, and an ambiguous reply resolves nothing.
- `handle_join_status_response`: falls back to that membership when no record matches by id, then adopts the community's id with `confirm_request_id`. The adopted id is persisted whatever the status says.
- A `pending` answer now stamps acknowledgement, because the VTC knows the request, so the "no response" warning clears.

For an approved join, recovery then runs on the existing path. `approved_at` is stamped, and the next poll after the grace period carries `resendCredentials`. The VTC re-sends, because it counts delivery by the member's reciprocal VMC, which this client never sent. The credential is matched to the record by VTC and persona, so it activates the membership. This requires a vtc-service that includes VTI #1900, which answers an id-less poll for an already-approved request.

## Tests

- `an_id_less_poll_answer_resolves_the_join_that_never_got_a_reply`: the field scenario.
- `an_id_less_poll_answer_still_pending_acknowledges_and_adopts`
- `an_id_less_poll_answer_goes_to_the_persona_it_was_sent_to`
- `status_response_with_mismatched_request_id_is_ignored` now holds a confirmed id, which is the case it was always about.

`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` is clean. `openvtc-core` passes all 887 tests. `openvtc-vetting-pcs`'s `wire_fixture` failed once during the parallel workspace run (fixture `NotFound`). It passes on its own, both with and without this change, so it looks flaky and is unrelated.

#226 made a join with no reply pollable: when we hold only our own
placeholder, the poll omits the request id and the community answers
from the authenticated applicant. Its commit said nothing else was

It never did. The handler correlates strictly by `requestId`, the
answer carries the community's id, and the record holds the
placeholder. The answer was dropped with "status-response did not
match a pending request id", so the join stayed Pending for good.
That happened even when the community had already admitted the
member, which is the case seen in the field.

When no record matches by id, the answer now goes to the join that is
still waiting for one (Pending, `request_id_confirmed == false`) and
adopts the id. If several personas are waiting on the same community,
the reply's recipient (`to`) decides, and an ambiguous reply resolves
nothing. An `approved` answer then flows through the existing path:
`approved_at` is stamped, a later poll carries `resendCredentials`,
and the re-sent credential activates the membership. A `pending`
answer now stamps acknowledgement too, because the VTC knows the
request.

The mismatched-id test now holds a confirmed id, which is the case it
was always about. Three tests cover the stuck join, a still-pending
answer, and persona disambiguation.

title: feat(repos): manage checkouts and commit signing from the Repos panel
body:
## Summary

A developer can now see and manage their community's repositories and commit signing from the Repos panel. did-git-sign still does the signing behind it.

- **What's on this machine.** Each repository shows its local state: not cloned, signed, not signing, or signing as another identity. A repository's screen adds an *On this machine* section with:
  - the checkout's path, branch, ahead/behind and changed files;
  - whether commits there are signed as this persona;
  - whether `HEAD` is signed and carries the `Signed-by-DID:` claim `verify-trust` checks.
- **One key per action:**

  | Key | Action |
  |---|---|
  | `c` | Clone into `<workspace>/<forge>/<owner>/<repo>`, set did-git-sign up if needed, and make the checkout sign |
  | `e` / `E` | Make a checkout sign as you (`did-git-sign enable --profile`) / stop it |
  | `u` | Adopt an existing checkout, once its `origin` proves to be the repo |
  | `s` / `S` | Set up or repair did-git-sign (re-prove the credential, rewrite an outdated hook) / remove the identity and revoke its credential |
  | `w` | Workspace directory and HTTPS/SSH |
  | `p` | Copy a checkout's path |

- **A narrowed credential, not the account's.** openvtc mints a `did:key` for did-git-sign and grants it `admin` of the persona's own context, narrowed to `key-export`. The previous (removed) wizard copied openvtc's account admin credential, which can reach every persona. Before anything is stored, the grant is proven: the new credential exports the key, and it must be the key the persona's DID document publishes. If the proof fails, the grant is revoked. Personas whose keys sit in the account's top context are refused. No `did-git-sign init` or `pnm` step is needed.
- **The signing row no longer depends on the directory openvtc was started in.** It now reports:
  - the persona's did-git-sign profile and keyring credential;
  - whether the `did-git-sign` binary git runs is on `PATH` (≥ 0.14);
  - did-git-sign's own commit-msg hook.

### Commits
1. `chore(deps)!`: `vta-sdk` 0.63, `trust-tasks-rs` 0.27, `affinidi-tdk` 0.23, `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.33, `did-git-sign` 0.15.1. 0.15.1 is the signer on VGI `main`; 0.16.0 changed only vgi-bridge and vgi-core. `cargo tree -d` shows no duplicate vta, trust-tasks or affinidi crate. Two code changes came with it:
   - the join submit body now carries `criterion` natively;
   - the tests that answer as a pre-0.3 community derive the dropped `manifest/0.2` response type themselves.
2. `feat(core)`: `git_workspace` and `git_signing`.
   - `git_workspace`: locating, inspecting and cloning checkouts. Resources are parsed strictly before reaching a command line or path, and every git call passes `--`.
   - `git_signing`: grant, prove, install, status, enable/disable, remove.
3. `feat(repos)`: the panel. It adds two dispatch domains, `GitWorkspace` and `GitWorkspaceProbe`, so local work never waits on a `git-ns` send. A probe runs on open, when the view lands, after each change, and every 20 s. Only explicit probes read the keyring.

### Worth knowing
- **The VTA releases a private key only over DIDComm or TSP, never REST.** So did-git-sign signs through the VTA's mediator. The e2e (`git_signing_e2e`) runs against `MockVta::start_with_transports()`, which needed the `transport-harness` dev feature.
- **Proving the grant connects as a fresh `did:key`, so the VTA's mediator must admit unknown DIDs.** did-git-sign's own `init` and every later signature already depend on this.
- **Wipe now removes did-git-sign's identity for every persona** in the profile, not only the detected default. It has no VTA session, so it logs each granted credential with the `pnm acl delete` that revokes it.
- **Not covered here:**
  - A private HTTPS clone needs a git credential helper; openvtc never prompts.
  - The `did-git-sign` binary is installed separately; the panel says how.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test --workspace`: 884 core + 796 TUI pass. New tests cover:
  - resource parsing and injection refusal, remote matching, status parsing;
  - a real local clone read back;
  - profile naming, grant shape, checkout signing classification;
  - reducer, outcomes, key map and rendering.
- [x] `cargo test --workspace -- --ignored`: all MockVta / mediator suites pass. This includes the new `git_signing_e2e`, which checks that:
  - the grant exports Alice's key and is refused Bob's;
  - revocation works, and revoking twice is a no-op;
  - openvtc's own DID is never revoked;
  - a mismatched key is refused and leaves no grant;
  - the top context is refused.
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`
- [ ] Manual run against a live VTA + forge: set up, clone, commit, and check that `verify-trust` passes

## Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). VTA calls are wrapped in a 30 s timeout. `git clone` is bounded at 15 min, and `did-git-sign enable`/`disable` at 30 s.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1). The grant is proven before the keyring and profile are written, and a failed write revokes the grant.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). There are no retries; a failed step reports and stops.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). The probe is periodic and stateless, and a failed probe is simply superseded.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6). The previous credential is revoked only after the new one is stored.
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*). None are new; the ACL grant uses the SDK builder.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*). There is no VTA backend or session → no setup. Top-context personas are refused.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*). Clone errors tell credentials, SSH, not-found and network apart (R6.4). A panicked job clears its busy marker and says so.
- [ ] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1). **Deviation:** if openvtc dies between the ACL grant and storing the credential, an orphaned grant remains. It is narrowed to one persona's `key-export`, and its private key was never written anywhere, so it cannot be used. It shows up in `pnm acl list` labelled `did-git-sign · … (openvtc)`.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers

origin, branch, ahead/behind, changes, the signing settings in effect and
whether HEAD is signed with a Signed-by-DID claim. `clone_repo` never
prompts (HTTPS without a terminal fails, SSH runs in batch mode unless the
member set core.sshCommand), is bounded (R1.2), and says why it failed in
words that tell auth from not-found from network (R6.4). A resource comes
from the community, so it is parsed strictly before it reaches a command
line or a path, and every git call passes `--`.

git_signing — did-git-sign set up for a persona without `did-git-sign init`
or a pnm grant. openvtc mints a did:key and grants it, through its admin
session, admin of the persona's own context narrowed to `key-export`;
did-git-sign never holds the account credential. The grant is proven
before anything is stored (the credential connects, exports the key, and
the key must be the one the persona publishes) and revoked if the proof
fails. The identity is then stored as a named profile with the library's
own calls (keyring, allowed_signers, profiles.json, include file). Per
repository, the did-git-sign binary's `enable --profile` / `disable` run
in the checkout — git needs that binary on PATH to sign at all. The
library calls that read the process cwd or print are not used.

The e2e runs against MockVta with its mediator: the VTA releases a private
key only over DIDComm/TSP, never REST, so the signer is proven the way
did-git-sign signs.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(repos): manage checkouts and commit signing from the Repos panel

Each repository a community governs now shows what is on this machine —
not cloned, signed, not signing, or signing as another identity — and a
repository's screen shows its checkout: path, branch, ahead/behind,
changes, whether a commit there is signed as this persona, and whether
HEAD carries the Signed-by-DID claim verify-trust checks.

One key each, with did-git-sign doing the signing behind it:
  c  clone into <workspace>/<forge>/<owner>/<repo>, set did-git-sign up
     if needed, and make the checkout sign
  e  make a checkout sign as you (did-git-sign enable --profile); E stops
  u  adopt an existing checkout once its origin proves to be the repo
  s  set did-git-sign up, or repair it (re-prove the credential, rewrite
     an outdated hook); S removes the identity and revokes its credential
  w  workspace directory and HTTPS/SSH;  p copies a checkout's path

Local work runs in two new dispatch domains so it never waits on, or
holds up, a git-ns send: GitWorkspace for changes and GitWorkspaceProbe
for reads. A probe runs on open, when the community's answer names the
repositories, after every change, and every 20 s while the view is open,
so a commit made in a terminal shows without a refresh; only an explicit
probe reads the keyring.

The signing row no longer depends on the directory openvtc was started in
or looks for the repo-local .did-git-sign.json did-git-sign stopped
writing in 0.14: it reports the persona's profile and credential, the
did-git-sign binary git runs, and did-git-sign's own commit-msg hook.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(repos): keep the workspace tests path-separator neutral

The Windows runner joins with `\`, and has no /dev/null for an empty
global git config.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(settings): a wipe removes every persona's did-git-sign identity

It uninstalled only the default identity the settings panel detected.
With per-persona profiles that left every other persona's credential in
the keyring, still able to sign, for a profile that no longer exists. A
wipe has no VTA session, so each credential openvtc granted is logged
with the `pnm acl delete` that revokes it.

title: feat(vtc): a cooling-off suspends its subject, and single-administrator mode can remove now (VTI-APV-019, VTI-APV-022)
body:
## What and why

In single-administrator mode (and in any two-administrator community), removing another unrestricted administrator waits out a 24 h cooling-off — and until now the subject kept **full authority** for that whole window, free to do damage. This PR:

1. **Suspends the subject of every cooling-off** (mode on or off) from the moment it is raised until it lands or is cancelled: the entry authorizes nothing, while the row is kept so cancelling restores it exactly.
2. **Adds "remove now" in single-administrator mode only**: a reduction (or an open cooling-off) can land at once, behind a typed confirmation (the subject's DID, or the action id) and a passkey gesture bound to the *immediate* variant.

The specification asks of such a removal only re-authentication, notice to the subject and a highest-severity audit (VTI-APV-019); the cooling-off and the suspension are this VTC's own design (`vtc-action-list.md` §8.2), so no specification change is needed. No new Trust Task URI: the request rides `ext["org.openvtc"].immediate` on the existing reduction payloads.

### Suspension (§8.2)

- **One chokepoint.** The suspension is set on `VtcAclEntry` wherever it is read (`get_acl_entry`, `list_acl_entries`, paginated); `can`, `can_any`, `can_approve` answer `false`. On top, the signed administrative door (`resolve_admin_claims`, console keys included), the git-ns door (`acting_as`), `require_capability` and ACL reads refuse with a message naming the action and when it lands.
- **What the subject may still do:** sign in, read the action list (`callerRole: subject`), cancel a request of its own. Event stream: `actions` + `singleAdminMode` only. No act, approval, queue decision, acknowledgement or git-ns operation.
- **Sessions** are revoked at suspension, matching how reductions bind (`routes::acl`).
- **Crash-safe (R2.1):** derived from the open action and kept beside the entry as `suspended:<did>` in the ACL keyspace. `admin_actions::save` writes the marker *before* an action that suspends and lifts it *after* one that no longer does; `reconcile_suspensions` repairs either half at start (before serving), every sweep, and after a restore.
- **Attrition:** a suspended entry is no role assigner; raising a cooling-off checks the guard as if the subject were gone; one cooling-off per subject.
- **First to act wins — by suspension:** the subject's counter-removal is refused at the door. `refuse_if_reduced_first` stays as a backstop. A suspended requester's own open actions are invalidated (§4.4).

### Remove now / Land now (§8.5)

- `ext["org.openvtc"].immediate = {"confirm": "<subject DID or action id>", "actionId": "<optional>"}` on `acl/revoke`, downward `acl/change-role`, narrowing `acl/update`/`acl/grant`, `vtc/members/admin-remove` (all via `gate_reduction`). Malformed → refused, never read as the delayed path.
- Confirmation checked before any gesture; gesture bound to the payload digest including `immediate`, so delayed/immediate gestures are not interchangeable (VTI-APV-015).
- Re-sending the same operation with `immediate` (optionally naming the action) lands an open cooling-off now; a different operation can't borrow an action id.
- Refused without the mode (naming the cooling-off and that the mode is host-set), on a wrong confirmation, without the gesture, and by the attrition guard.
- Audited `Critical` as `SingleAdminMode { event: reductionImmediate }` *before* the write (resource = landed action), then `AuthorityReducedUnopposed`; the subject gets the authority-reduced notice. History: `landedAfterCoolingOff` + `ext.landedNow`.

### Surfaces

- **Console:** ACL list chip "suspended — removal lands T"; **Remove now** beside Revoke (single-admin mode, other unrestricted admins) and **Land now** on an open cooling-off, each behind a typed-confirmation dialog then the passkey; cooling-off card states the subject is suspended; landed-now banner.
- **cnm:** `cnm access revoke <did> --now [--action <id>] [--confirm <did|id>]` (prompts on a TTY); `cnm actions show` / `cnm access list` show suspension and landed-now. `vtc-client` gains `acl_revoke_now` (additive).

## Design notes / docs changed

- `docs/05-design-notes/vtc-action-list.md`: as-built table + deviations, **§8.2** (suspension, first-to-act-by-suspension), **§8.5** (remove now / land now).
- `docs/03-vtc/admin-access.md` (§2.1a, §3.4, cheat sheet), `admin-access-infographic.html`, `bootstrap-runbook.md`, `non-interactive-setup.md`, `vtc-admin-roles.md`.

## Tests

New `vtc-service/tests/it/cooling_off_suspension.rs` (all over the signed Trust Task spine REST/DIDComm/TSP share): `cooling_off_suspends_subject_until_it_lands`, `cancelled_cooling_off_restores_subject`, `suspended_subject_cannot_act_approve_or_counter_remove`, `suspension_survives_restart`, `suspension_never_leaves_no_live_unrestricted_entry`, `single_admin_remove_now_lands_at_once_with_bound_step_up_and_confirmation`, `remove_now_refused_when_mode_off`, `remove_now_refused_on_wrong_confirmation`, `remove_now_gesture_not_spendable_on_delayed_removal_and_vice_versa`, `land_now_on_open_cooling_off`. Unit: `a_suspended_entry_authorizes_nothing`, cnm `remove_now_needs_the_subject_or_the_action_typed_back`. `vti_apv_019_the_first_of_two_administrators_to_act_wins` updated to the suspension semantics. Console vitest: `lib/immediate.test.ts`, `acl.test.ts` (revokeAclNow), `AclForm.test.tsx` (suspended chip, Remove now gating), `Actions.test.tsx` (suspended subject, Land now gating + payload, landed-now).

Results (local, macOS, RAM disk):

- `TMPDIR=/Volumes/RAMDisk VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1 cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client -p cnm-cli --no-fail-fast` → 2934 run: 2928 passed, 6 failed, 1 skipped. The 6 are the four `admin_ui::tests` the skip flag is documented to fail plus `routing_modes::path_mode_admin_{bare_prefix,trailing_slash}_serves_admin_spa` (also need the baked SPA); re-run **with** the admin UI built, all 11 admin-ui/routing tests pass.
- admin-ui: `npx vitest run` → 65 files, 788 tests passed; `npm run lint` clean. `package-lock.json` unchanged.
- `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1 cargo clippy -p vtc-service -p cnm-cli -p vtc-client --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` clean.

## Known limitation (follow-up)

The VTC refuses every git-ns operation a suspended subject signs, but the **forge / Trust Registry projection** of its git rights is not withdrawn during the cooling-off (re-projecting needs the projector to filter suspended holders and re-run on suspend/restore, without the read-modify-write paths that share `Snapshot::load` dropping their rows). Rights are withdrawn when the removal lands, as before.

title: fix(vtc): a console key grants the vetter role as its administrator (VTI-ACL-030)
body:
`vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1` took its actor from the bare proof signer,
so a grant made from the admin console — which signs with its own did:key,
acting for the administrator who delegated it — was refused as "<console
key> does not hold vtc.vetting.manage", even for a community-admin.

The handler now resolves its actor through `capable_signer`, as every other
administrative task does: the signer's own entry, or the delegating
administrator's for a console key, held to vtc.vetting.manage at execution
time. The other handlers that resolve the bare signer act for members, where
the signer is the actor.

Tests: a console key acting for a community-admin grants the role; one with
no delegation, and one acting for an administrator without
vtc.vetting.manage, grant nothing.

title: feat(vgi-bridge): setup command writes a runnable VTA-mode folder and service file
body:
## Why

Setting up a bridge meant root paths (`/etc`, `/var/lib`, `/run/secrets`), Docker assumed, and hand-copied values: `trust_registry_did`, `mediator_did`, a 40-hex verify-trust commit, a random master key. `vgi-bridge setup` writes one complete, runnable folder in VTA mode (BRIDGE.md §2a) instead, and needs no root.

```sh
vgi-bridge setup --vtc <VTC DID> --vta <VTA DID> --dir ~/vgi-bridge \
  --public-url https://bridge.example.org/ --owner acme \
  [--forge github|forgejo] [--user-account] [--service systemd|launchd|docker|none] [--yes] [--force]
```

## What it does

1. **Finds** the Trust Registry (the `TrustRegistry` referral) and the mediator (`TSPTransport`, else `DIDCommMessaging`) in the VTC's DID document and prints them. `--registry` / `--mediator` override them. The referral reader moves to `vgi-core` (`registry_referral`, plus `messaging_mediator`), so `vgi repo init` and setup now share one copy.
2. **Asks** for `--public-url` (https, or http to loopback only) and `--owner`. With `--yes` it asks nothing and fails on a missing value instead.
3. **Pins** `[verify_trust]` to `v{CARGO_PKG_VERSION}` and that tag's commit, looked up with an unauthenticated GitHub API call that follows annotated tags. If the lookup fails, it writes a commented TODO with the `gh api` command that fills the value in. It also fetches `web-flow.gpg` into `<dir>/web-flow.asc`.
4. **Provisions the VTA credential** the same way `did-git-sign init` does. It mints an ephemeral setup `did:key` and prints both `pnm` grants: `contexts create … --admin-handoff` for a new context, and `acl create … --handoff` for an existing one. Then it runs `provision_client` with `ProvisionAsk::vta_admin_rotated` over TSP/DIDComm, which rolls the setup key over to a long-term admin scoped to the context. The result goes to `<dir>/vta-credential.json` with mode 0600, in the format `credential_file` reads. `--credential <file>` skips provisioning. A credential left in the folder by an earlier run is reused. A VTC's DID document does not name its VTA, so `--vta` is required unless a credential is given.
5. **Writes `bridge.toml`** with absolute paths only and checks it with `BridgeConfig::parse` and then `load`. It never overwrites an existing file without `--force`. If the VTA's mediator differs from the VTC's, it also writes `[vta] mediator_did`.
6. **Writes a service file**: a systemd `--user` unit, a launchd agent, a Compose file (the folder mounted at its own path, read-only, with `data/` writable; it runs as the folder's owner, and a comment covers the uid-10001 alternative), or none. Logs go to `<dir>/bridge.log`.
7. **Mints and checks the DID.** If the context has no DID, it mints a `did:webvh` with TSP and DIDComm services on the VTA's hosting server (`--webvh-server` picks one when the VTA has several). Then it runs the existing `vta::setup` checks. It finishes by printing the DID, the `[git_ns] bridges = { "<host>" = "<DID>" }` line plus "restart the VTC", the HTTPS/tunnel note, and the `<public_url>/github/<host>/<owner>/register` next step.

`--self-contained` keeps the master-key mode: the key lives in the folder and the `did:peer` comes from `init`.

## Docs

- `BRIDGE.md` §2 is rewritten as: install, then setup, then start the service, then the VTC line, then register the App.
- §2a keeps the concepts and points to setup.
- The manual, self-contained and container steps move to a new §8 and use home-folder paths.
- `SETUP-GITHUB-VTC.md` §2 is rewritten the same way.
- `bridge.example.toml` comments now point to setup.

This PR leaves the packaging lines alone (publish flags, install paragraphs, the crate README); `feat/publish-vgi-bridge` changes those.

## Tests

Unit tests cover:
- config rendering in VTA, self-contained and Forgejo modes, checked by the real parser (absolute paths, no root paths, escaping)
- the https rule
- folder-path safety
- systemd, launchd, compose and none rendering
- discovery from sample DID documents
- refusal to overwrite
- credential 0600 and read-back
- the grant commands and the summary
- tag resolution and the web-flow fetch against wiremock

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test -p vgi-bridge` all pass. A smoke run of `--self-contained --service systemd` against the live GitHub API produced a folder that loads. The VTA provisioning and minting path has not been run against a live VTA.

  an ephemeral setup did:key, the two `pnm` grant commands (new or existing

  ProvisionAsk::vta_admin_rotated over TSP/DIDComm; written 0600 in the
  credential_file format (or --credential, or reused from an earlier run);
- writes bridge.toml with absolute paths, checked by the bridge's own
  parser, never over an existing one without --force;
- writes a systemd --user unit, a launchd agent, a Compose file (folder
  mounted at its own path, run as the folder's owner) or nothing;
- mints the bridge's did:webvh into the context when it has none, runs the
  `vta setup` checks, and prints the DID, the VTC's `[git_ns] bridges`

title: feat: publish vgi-bridge to crates.io and attach bridge binaries to releases
body:
Makes `vgi-bridge` installable the same ways as the other tools: from crates.io, as a release binary, or as a container.

## crates.io
- `crates/vgi-bridge/Cargo.toml`: `publish = false` becomes `publish.workspace = true`. The description, readme, keywords, categories and license (from the workspace) were already set.
- **No other crate had to change.** Everything vgi-bridge depends on is already published: `vgi-core`, `vgi-forge`, `vgi-forge-github`, `vgi-forge-forgejo` and `verify-trust` are workspace path deps that carry versions, and every other dependency (including the `trust-tasks-git-ns` alias) is a registry crate. There are no git deps or `[patch]` sections.
- `publish.yml`: `vgi-bridge` is now last in the publish loop, because it depends on both adapters, verify-trust and vgi-core, and nothing depends on it. The comment calling it an unpublished service is gone. A crate in the loop that has **never** been published (the sparse index returns 404) now stops with a clear instruction to publish it by hand first, not an opaque auth error. Crates earlier in the loop still upload before it stops. The `package` job already runs `cargo package --workspace`, so it now verifies vgi-bridge too.

## Release binaries
`release.yml` now runs one matrix leg per (binary, target):
- `verify-trust`: the same four targets, and asset names are unchanged (`verify-trust-<target>.tar.gz`), so the action's download-by-name still works.
- `vgi-bridge`: `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-apple-darwin` and `x86_64-apple-darwin`. Each produces `vgi-bridge-<target>.tar.gz` plus a `.sha256` and gets the same build-provenance attestation. The tarball also contains the bridge README and `bridge.example.toml`.
- **No Windows bridge build.** On Windows, `check_owner_only` and the 0600 file modes in `seal.rs` / `main.rs` do nothing, so the binary would accept a master key anyone can read.
- The hardening is unchanged: SHA-pinned actions, no cache, and attestation only on tags. Only the release job can write. Artifact names are now `<bin>-<target>` so legs don't collide.

`bridge-image.yml` is unchanged.

## Docs
- The bridge README has a new **Install** section, and `docs/BRIDGE.md` has a new unnumbered **Installing** section before §1. Both cover `cargo install`, the release binary with `gh attestation verify`, and Docker.
- The root README table row is updated.
- I did not touch the §2 deployment text, to avoid conflicting with `feat/bridge-setup-command`.

## Maintainer action needed on crates.io
crates.io Trusted Publishing **cannot create a crate**. A Trusted Publisher can only be configured on a crate that already exists, and crates.io has no PyPI-style "pending publisher" (RFC 3691 lists it as possible future work). `publish.yml`'s own comment already says the same. The name `vgi-bridge` is currently free on crates.io (the index returns 404). So for the first release that includes this change:
1. Push the tag as usual. `publish.yml` publishes the seven existing crates, then stops at vgi-bridge with the instruction.
2. From that tag, run `cargo publish -p vgi-bridge --locked` once by hand, using a crates.io API token with the `publish-new` scope. Revoke the token afterwards.
3. On crates.io, go to vgi-bridge, then Settings, then Trusted Publishing, and add: repository `OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure`, workflow `publish.yml`, environment `crates-io`.
4. Re-run the workflow (or not; later tags publish it normally).

Alternatively, publish 0.15.1 by hand from `main` once this PR merges, then configure Trusted Publishing before the next tag.

## Checks
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test -p vgi-bridge --locked`: all pass
- `cargo package -p vgi-bridge --locked`: builds from the tarball
- `actionlint`: no findings in publish.yml or release.yml. Its only finding is an existing shellcheck warning in ci.yml.

title: feat(vtc): a subject may relabel its own entry; single-administrator mode is one person under many identifiers (VTI-ACL-052, VTI-APV-022)
body:
Implements **trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#54** (VTI-ACL-052: a subject may change its own label; a single-administrator exception) and **trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#55** (VTI-APV-022: single-administrator mode is one person under as many identifiers as they hold; VTI-ACL-052 item 3 widened to any unrestricted entry). Both spec PRs are merged.

## VTI-ACL-052 item 2: your own label
- A subject may change **only** the label of its own entry, on every door that writes it: `acl/update/0.1`, `acl/update/0.2`, `acl/grant` re-stating the same entry, and `vtc/members/update`. Over REST, DIDComm and TSP (one spine). No step-up.
- If the same request changes anything else, the whole request is refused.
- Audited: a `MemberUpdated` row with the old and new label and a `labelSetBySubject` change.
- `VtcAclEntry::label_set_by_subject` (serde default `false`). It is set when the subject writes its own label, cleared when anyone else sets it, and kept by writes that leave the label alone.
- Shown to other parties as `ext["org.openvtc"].labelSetBySubject` on `acl/list` and `acl/show` 0.2. That is an `ext` member, so no published response schema changes. The conformance tests (`conform::<…Response>`, `assert_conforms`) still pass.
- A subject's own write never clears a delegation review on its entry. Only another administrator can re-affirm one.

## VTI-ACL-052 item 3: unrestricted entries in single-administrator mode
- When the mode is on and the subject's entry is unrestricted (`granting::is_unrestricted`), the subject may change its own entry on `acl/update/0.2` and `acl/change-role/0.2`.
- This holds even when other unrestricted entries exist (#55).
- Authorization: the subject's step-up, bound to the operation (VTI-APV-015).
- Audit: a `Critical` `SingleAdminMode { event: selfEditWaived, requirement: VTI-ACL-052 }` row, written before the change (`acl::single_admin::authorize_self_edit`).
- Refused if the change would leave no live unrestricted entry: narrowing or demoting the only one, or bringing its expiry forward.
- Removing the subject's own `vtc.roles.assign` goes through the attrition check, as any removal does.
- `acl/change-role/0.1` and `vtc/members/update` still refuse a subject's own role move. The refusal names the doors that carry item 3.
- Every refusal now says what is allowed: the label always; in single-administrator mode, the rest with a step-up.

## VTI-APV-022 (#55): consent is waived beside other administrators
- `gesture_then_consent_for` and the session door's `require()` no longer check for an empty approver set.
- git-ns rule 7 is waived the same way. `others_eligible` is removed.
- Reductions (VTI-APV-019) in the mode are never parked for a third party's consent. They take the unopposed path: step-up, a notice to the subject, a `Critical` row, and the cooling-off.
- The cooling-off now lands even when a third administrator exists. `recheck_cooling_off` and the sweeper's invalidation skip their "a third party can now consent" check in the mode. Without this fix, the action would have been cancelled at landing.
- Tests that asserted "another eligible party brings consent back" now assert the new rule. They are named after VTI-APV-022.

## Console
- **Your own row** is tagged *you*. Its label is editable inline. **Edit** is offered only when the mode is on and your entry is unrestricted; saving then asks for the bound step-up. Otherwise **Edit** is disabled, with the reason as a tooltip and as inline text. **Revoke** is disabled, with the reason.
- **Self-set labels** carry a *self-set* tag, and the name book shows them as "(self-set)" everywhere else in the console.
- **Single-admin wording**: the banner, the dashboard, the *consent waived* and cooling-off text match the new rule.
- **Parked actions** list who can approve them. The VTC now sends `ext.org.openvtc.approvers` on open actions; an older VTC sends only the count, which is still shown.
- **Summary fields read as words**: `expiresAt` is shown as "Expires at", `{"scope":"ceiling"}` as "the role's full set of capabilities", and listed grants as `cap at resource`. An empty value is shown as "—".
- **Roles form layout**: a new `.checkbox` / `.checkbox-text` / `.cap-row` layout. The cause of the bug: the capability picker reused `.row-actions` (`justify-content: flex-end`, which right-aligned it), and the approve toggle sat in a column `.field`. The Roles page's ceiling picker used an undefined `.checkbox` class, so it now gets the same layout. `.row-actions` and `.field` are unchanged, so no other form changes.

## Docs
- `docs/03-vtc/admin-access.md`: a new §1.4a; §2.1a, §3.3 and §3.4 rewritten.
- `admin-access-infographic.html`, `bootstrap-runbook.md`, `non-interactive-setup.md`, `git-namespaces.md` (the section anchor is renamed and its links updated) and the setup TOML example.
- `vtc-action-list.md` §8.5, `vtc-admin-roles.md` and the root `CLAUDE.md`.
- The setup wizard prompt and warning, CLI help, `config.rs` docs and the `cnm` notices.

## Decided differently / notes
- **"Unrestricted act scope"** at a VTC means `granting::is_unrestricted`: a `community-admin` with act `all` and its full ceiling, the same test VTI-ACL-033 uses. Every administrative role at a VTC acts with act `all`, so a moderator's `act: all` does not count.
- **Self-label audit**: recorded as `MemberUpdated` field changes. A dedicated field on `AclChangeData` would have been a breaking change to the published `vti-common`. The only `vti-common` change here is a doc comment listing `selfEditWaived`.
- **No `!`**: `vtc-service` is `publish = false`, and the published crates changed (`vti-common`, `cnm-cli`) only in a doc comment and in message strings.
- A rewrite of your own entry that changes nothing is still refused, not treated as a label change. This keeps `vti_ops_050_granting_yourself_the_admin_role_is_refused`.
- A self-edit does not revoke the subject's own sessions, even when it narrows the entry: the subject asked for the change from the session it is using.

## Tests run locally (macOS, `TMPDIR` on a RAM disk)
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client -p cnm-cli --no-fail-fast`: 2922 passed, 1 skipped.
- `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1 cargo clippy -p vtc-service -p cnm-cli -p vti-common --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `admin-ui`: `npx vitest run` gives 778 passed (64 files). `npm run lint` (wire check plus `tsc`) is clean.
- New tests:
  - `tests/it/acl_self_edit.rs`: `vti_acl_052_subject_may_relabel_own_entry`, `…_on_every_door`, `…_a_label_set_by_another_is_not_self_set`, `vti_acl_052_label_with_other_field_refused`, `vti_acl_052_single_admin_unrestricted_may_edit_self_with_step_up`, `…_self_edit_refused_without_step_up`, `…_refused_when_it_leaves_no_unrestricted_entry`, `…_refused_when_mode_off`, `…_refused_when_subject_not_unrestricted`, `vti_apv_022_consent_is_waived_beside_other_administrators`, `vti_apv_022_a_reduction_cools_off_instead_of_waiting_for_consent`.
  - `trust_tasks::acl_tasks`: per-transport (REST, DIDComm, TSP) relabel and bound-gesture tests.
  - vitest: own-entry, self-set, layout, readable-field and who-can-approve tests.
- The full workspace suite is left to CI.

body:
feat(vtc): a subject may relabel its own entry; single-administrator mode is one person under many identifiers (VTI-ACL-052, VTI-APV-022) (#1941)

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#54 and #55 (both merged).

VTI-ACL-052 item 2 — a subject may change its own entry's label and
nothing else, on every door that writes it (acl/update 0.1 and 0.2,
acl/grant re-stating the same entry, vtc/members/update). No step-up: the
label confers no authority (VTI-ACL-001). The change is audited as a
MemberUpdated row naming the old and new label and `labelSetBySubject`,
and the entry carries `label_set_by_subject` (serde-default false,
cleared when anyone else sets the label), shown to other parties as
`ext["org.openvtc"].labelSetBySubject` on acl/list and acl/show 0.2 — an
ext member, so the published response schemas are untouched. A request
that changes the label and anything else is refused whole. A subject's
own write never re-affirms a delegation under review.

VTI-ACL-052 item 3 (as widened by #55) — in single-administrator mode a
subject whose entry has unrestricted act scope (granting::is_unrestricted:
a community-admin acting everywhere with its full ceiling) may modify its
own entry on acl/update/0.2 and acl/change-role/0.2. It takes the
subject's step-up bound to the operation (VTI-APV-015) and a Critical
SingleAdminMode{event: selfEditWaived} row written before the write
(acl::single_admin::authorize_self_edit), and is refused if it would leave
no live unrestricted entry (narrowing, demoting or shortening the life of
the only one). Ending the subject's vtc.roles.assign is attrition-checked
like any removal. Every other self-edit is refused as before, and the
refusals now say what the subject may do instead.

VTI-APV-022 (#55) — single-administrator mode waives second-party consent
whether or not other administrators' entries exist: one person may hold
an administrator entry per device, and the node cannot tell one person's
identifiers from two people's. gesture_then_consent_for and the session
door's require() no longer test for an empty approver set; git-ns rule 7
is waived the same way (others_eligible is gone). A reduction of another
administrator (VTI-APV-019) is not parked for a third party's consent in
the mode: it takes the unopposed path — step-up, notice to the subject,
Critical row — and keeps its cooling-off, which now lands in the mode even
with a third administrator present (recheck_cooling_off and the sweeper's
invalidation skip the "a third party can now consent" check).

Console: your own row is tagged "you"; its label is editable inline;
Edit is offered only in single-administrator mode while your entry is
unrestricted (and asks for the bound step-up on save), otherwise disabled
with the reason; Revoke is disabled with the reason. Self-set labels show
a "self-set" tag and the name book appends "(self-set)". A parked action
shows who can approve it (new ext.org.openvtc.approvers on open actions),
and summary fields read as words (humanised field names; authority scopes
and capability sets instead of raw JSON). The roles form's capability
rows and approve toggle use a new .checkbox layout: box left-aligned on
the line of its text, text wrapping, the "confers authority" pill inline
(the picker had borrowed .row-actions, whose flex-end right-aligned it,
and the toggle sat in a column .field). The role-ceiling picker on the
Roles page, which used an undefined .checkbox class, gets the same layout.

Docs: admin-access.md (§1.4a new, §2.1a, §3.3, §3.4), the infographic,
bootstrap-runbook, non-interactive-setup, git-namespaces, the setup TOML
example, vtc-action-list §8.5, vtc-admin-roles and CLAUDE.md; setup wizard
and CLI help text and cnm's notices follow the new rule.

title: vta-service-v0.53.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: Trust-tasks 0.27 — cooling-off actions, the reduction-pending notice, offline-write records, and approver-device approvals ([#1922](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1922))

trust-tasks-rs 0.27.1 (trust-tasks-tf #719) specifies what the action list's
  A2 phase had to express by workaround. This adopts it.

  - trust-tasks-rs and its sibling crates move to 0.27.1, in lockstep with the
    TDK release built on it: affinidi-tdk 0.23, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.33,
    affinidi-messaging-test-mediator 0.18 (mediator 0.37), and
    affinidi-messaging-mediator-{admin,tui} 0.8. The graph holds one
    trust-tasks-rs (and one trust-tasks-proof), so the mediator `MediatorAcl` is
    one type and no bridge is needed. 0.27.0's typed git-ns
    `ActivityItem.source` needed no change: the VTC builds that response from
    JSON, and its wire is unchanged.
  - `vtc/admin/actions/{list,show,cancel,acknowledge}/0.2` are served beside 0.1.
    At 0.2 a cooling-off (VTI-APV-019) is category `coolingOff` with `landsAt`
    and `cancellableBy: requester`, no threshold, expiry or approvers remaining,
    closes `landedAfterCoolingOff`, and its subject sees it as `callerRole:
    subject` in `all` and `history`, never `waitingForMe`. 0.1 keeps answering
    as before (`ext["org.openvtc"].coolingOff`, `thresholdMet`). A parked
    operation's next step expects show/0.2. vtc-client, cnm and the console use
    0.2; cnm and the console count down to `landsAt`.
  - A reduction parked for its cooling-off sends the subject
    `vtc/members/authority-reduction-pending-notice/0.1` (durable push). The
    landing still sends the authority-reduced notice (`unopposed`); a cancelled
    one reduces and sends nothing more. Landing never waits on delivery.
  - An operator's offline write (VTI-VTC-023), the emergency bootstrap
    included, is raised with `typeUri` the record type
    `vtc/operator/offline-write/0.1` and the record `{command, dids, host, at}`
    as payload, replacing the URN placeholder and four per-command templates
    with one pinned template. The emergency marker now records the recovery DID
    and the administrators it wiped. A document of the record type answers
    `unsupportedType`; the manifest census lists it as embedded-only.
  - The console approves with the admin's approver device through the plugin's
    `approveDecision` (vta-browser-plugin #293): the device signs a
    decision-purpose statement over the per-approver salted wire digest, and
    the wallet signs `task-consent/decision/0.2` carrying it as `approverSigned`
    evidence. Precedence: approver device, passkey, wallet signature alone,
    then the `cnm consent approve` guidance.
  - A crash between a `policy/upsert` revision write and its effect marker was
    reconciled `failed` although the revision existed, because the upsert moves
    no state pin (CLAUDE.md R2.1). An executing action's revision is now stored
    under an id derived from the action and execution
    (`admin_actions::policy_revision_id`), so the row is its own evidence.
