Note: VTI-ACL-054 – 058 (hand-off markers) are a different mechanism and are not implemented here. Backup restore. backup/finalize-import with confirm: true is previewed, then parked (Act::RestoreBackup) for the holders of vtc.backup.restore; approvers see the payload without its password, and the staged bundle is kept alive for the action's lifetime. Console. auth/whoami returns the caller's live capabilities (the published member) and ext["org.openvtc"].{adminRole, approves}; navigation and action buttons render per capability; a Roles page lists, defines and deletes roles through the action list; the new action kinds have pinned summary templates. - **vtc**: Single-administrator mode, set at install, for communities with one administrator (VTI-APV-022) ([#1925](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1925)) A community run by one person has nobody to give second-party consent (VTI-APV-014, -018 - 020). Without this, its administrator could add a colleague or change an authority rule only through the offline break-glass. VTI-APV-022 lets a node run in single-administrator mode instead. This implements it at the VTC. - Config: `[acl] single_admin_mode` (default false). Host configuration only (item 1). It is read at start, kept out of the runtime registry, and refused by name by `config/patch` and `vtc/config/import`, with the host-side fix in the refusal. It is written to config.toml only when on. - Setup: `vtc setup --single-admin` (interactive and `--from`), `single_admin_mode = true` in the setup TOML, and an interactive "Run as a single-administrator community?" (default No). Setup warns when it is chosen beside `co_admin_did`, because the mode has no effect while that administrator is eligible. - Gate: where the approver set is empty and the mode is on, the consent gate neither refuses nor parks. The requester's operation-bound step-up (VTI-APV-015) stands in for the consent. Spending it writes a Critical `SingleAdminMode{consentWaived}` audit row naming the requirement, task, kind and digest. The row is written before the write, and a failure to audit refuses the operation. Once the write lands, the operation enters the action history marked `ext.org.openvtc.consentWaived`. A non-empty approver set parks exactly as before (item 2). - Reductions (VTI-APV-019) are unchanged and keep their cooling-off. Removing the subject at once would let one credential first remove the only other eligible party and then act on the waiver (vtc-action-list.md section 8.5). - Boot (item 4): Critical `inEffect` at every start with the mode on, and `enabled`/`disabled` when the value differs from the last start (stored in the install keyspace). A start that cannot audit does not proceed. - Visibility (item 3): `vtc/admin/actions/list` carries `ext.org.openvtc.singleAdminMode`. The console shows a permanent, non-dismissable banner on every page and a dashboard tile, and marks waived operations in Actions. `cnm actions list` prints a notice and marks waived operations. - Docs: admin-access section 2.1a, bootstrap runbook, non-interactive setup and example TOML, vtc-action-list section 8.5, vtc-admin-roles section 7, the infographic, and CLAUDE.md. Adds the `AuditEvent::SingleAdminMode` variant to vti-common. The enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so this is additive. - **vtc**: Trust-tasks 0.27 — cooling-off actions, the reduction-pending notice, offline-write records, and approver-device approvals ([#1922](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1922)) trust-tasks-rs 0.27.1 (trust-tasks-tf #719) specifies what the action list's A2 phase had to express by workaround. This adopts it. - trust-tasks-rs and its sibling crates move to 0.27.1, in lockstep with the TDK release built on it: affinidi-tdk 0.23, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.33, affinidi-messaging-test-mediator 0.18 (mediator 0.37), and affinidi-messaging-mediator-{admin,tui} 0.8. The graph holds one trust-tasks-rs (and one trust-tasks-proof), so the mediator `MediatorAcl` is one type and no bridge is needed. 0.27.0's typed git-ns `ActivityItem.source` needed no change: the VTC builds that response from JSON, and its wire is unchanged. - `vtc/admin/actions/{list,show,cancel,acknowledge}/0.2` are served beside 0.1. At 0.2 a cooling-off (VTI-APV-019) is category `coolingOff` with `landsAt` and `cancellableBy: requester`, no threshold, expiry or approvers remaining, closes `landedAfterCoolingOff`, and its subject sees it as `callerRole: subject` in `all` and `history`, never `waitingForMe`. 0.1 keeps answering as before (`ext["org.openvtc"].coolingOff`, `thresholdMet`). A parked operation's next step expects show/0.2. vtc-client, cnm and the console use 0.2; cnm and the console count down to `landsAt`. - A reduction parked for its cooling-off sends the subject `vtc/members/authority-reduction-pending-notice/0.1` (durable push). The landing still sends the authority-reduced notice (`unopposed`); a cancelled one reduces and sends nothing more. Landing never waits on delivery. - An operator's offline write (VTI-VTC-023), the emergency bootstrap included, is raised with `typeUri` the record type `vtc/operator/offline-write/0.1` and the record `{command, dids, host, at}` as payload, replacing the URN placeholder and four per-command templates with one pinned template. The emergency marker now records the recovery DID and the administrators it wiped. A document of the record type answers `unsupportedType`; the manifest census lists it as embedded-only. - The console approves with the admin's approver device through the plugin's `approveDecision` (vta-browser-plugin #293): the device signs a decision-purpose statement over the per-approver salted wire digest, and the wallet signs `task-consent/decision/0.2` carrying it as `approverSigned` evidence. Precedence: approver device, passkey, wallet signature alone, then the `cnm consent approve` guidance. - A crash between a `policy/upsert` revision write and its effect marker was reconciled `failed` although the revision existed, because the upsert moves no state pin (CLAUDE.md R2.1). An executing action's revision is now stored under an id derived from the action and execution (`admin_actions::policy_revision_id`), so the row is its own evidence. - **vtc**: Administration is role-based — capabilities, built-in roles and explicit act scope (VTI-ACL-030 – 037, VTI-APV-018) ([#1924](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1924)) Phase C1 of docs/05-design-notes/vtc-admin-roles.md. A VTC ACL entry no longer reads "admin with an empty context list" as unrestricted: it carries explicit administrative authority beside its community role. Model (vtc-service/src/acl/capability.rs, entry.rs) - VtcAclEntry gains adminRole (seven built-ins: community-admin, moderator, vetting-lead, repo-manager, credential-officer, auditor, approver; custom roles are a C2 placeholder), act all|none, capabilities ceiling|none|listed with resource qualifiers (git-ns, git-repo, policy, criterion) and additive grants, approve and approveCapabilities. Absent means none. - A typed registry of 20 capabilities with authority-conferring flags. The effective set is ceiling ∩ listed (plus additive), and every gate asks one question: entry.can(capability, resource). No authority list is tested with is_empty(). Gates (§4) - Every require_super_admin / is_super_admin / "any admin" gate is replaced by the specific capability. Reads need any administrative role; writes need their capability. Console sign-in admits every administrative role. git-ns community-admin standing is git.ns.admin unqualified. - vtc/members/update refuses a move to or from a community role that implies an administrative role (moderator, issuer, admin) with adminRoleForbidden; acl/change-role carries the bound gesture for it. Consent (VTI-APV-018, -019, -009) - APV-014 generalises to any authority-conferring capability: approvers are holders of the same capability at a covering qualifier who may approve it; the requester (and, for a reduction, the subject) is excluded. A2's after_reduction, agreements, cooling-off, record_effect and notices are kept; actions record the capabilities at stake. An expiry put on or brought forward is a reduction of everything the entry holds. The last holder of vtc.roles.assign is never removed. Granting bounds (§6.3; VTI-ACL-031, -033, -042, -050, -053, -071) - A granter must hold each capability and vtc.roles.assign at a qualifier at least as wide, may confer approve only within its own, never past its own expiry, never to itself. delegatedBy is recorded. A departed or narrowed granter's grants go under review and are withdrawn after the action lifetime unless re-affirmed (review listing + sweeper, not an action-list item). Wire - acl/{grant,update,show,list,revoke,change-role}/0.2 are served with the generated trust_tasks_rs types beside 0.1, mapped per acl/_shared/0.2 CONVENTIONS §8; an entry 0.1 cannot express is refused at 0.1. Six 0.2 summary templates are pinned (Rust and console). Migration (§9) - At boot, before anything is authorized, every ACL row in the pre-role shape is rewritten in place with the same mapping a backup import uses. All rows are mapped before any is written, and each is one put, so a refusal or a crash leaves no half-migrated row. A second boot is a no-op. The run is audited once (new AuditEvent::AclMigrated, Critical: counts plus the context-scoped admins left with no administrative role), and those losses are raised as an acknowledge item for the remaining community-admins (VTI-VTC-023; new pinned template, urn:openvtc:vtc:operator:acl-migration). A row that cannot be mapped refuses the boot, naming the DID and the offline fix (vtc acl remove, which now removes an undecodable row, then vtc acl add). It is never dropped. - Backup import maps legacy rows: unrestricted admin -> community-admin, context-scoped admin -> no administrative role (listed for re-grant in the import report), moderator / issuer -> the matching role, custom -> none. - Install bootstrap and the co-admin are community-admins; offline `vtc acl add --role admin` writes a community-admin, and gains --admin-role and --capability cap[@resource]; --contexts is refused. Clients - vtc-client gains the 0.2 calls; cnm access list/show/grant/update use 0.2 with --admin-role / --capability / --approve. - The console's Access control shows each entry's administrative role and capabilities, adds and edits with role and capability narrowing, and no longer calls a least-privilege entry "all" ([#746](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/746)). - **cnm**: Setup onboards the personal VTA the way pnm does — self-minted key, grant, rotate ([#1923](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1923)) `cnm setup` used to require a sealed bundle from an administrator before cnm could touch the personal VTA. It now follows pnm's admin cold start: mint an ephemeral did:key, park it, print the grant routes (`vta import-did`, `admin_did` in setup.toml, `pnm acl create`), and on `cnm setup continue [] [--vta-did ] [--vta-url ]` authenticate, which rotates to a fresh did:key over `acl/swap-key` and removes the temp DID's entry. A continue before the grant prints the routes and stays resumable. Non-interactive mode mirrors pnm ([#1753](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1753)): `cnm setup --name [--overwrite]` and `continue --vta-did` each print one `{slug, admin_did, state}` line. Alternatives in the wizard: - "Bootstrap from your existing pnm session" when a pnm profile on this machine ($PNM_HOME honoured) is bound to the same VTA DID. pnm's config and session store are read only; pnm's key authenticates in memory once, over REST (so no mediator socket is taken from a running pnm), to grant cnm's own freshly minted key, which then rotates as above. The grant is an unrestricted admin: cnm creates a top-level context per community on the personal VTA, which the VTA gates on super-admin. - "I have a sealed bundle from an admin" — unchanged, digest pinned. Communities now get an admin identity each, so one operator's communities share no key. `cnm community add [--vtc-did] [--vta-did] [--slug] [--overwrite]` mints a did:key for that community, parks it in `pending_communities` (not selectable by --community or as default until confirmed), and prints the VTC grant routes: `co_admin_did` in vtc setup, `vtc acl add` offline, or an existing admin's `cnm access grant` / console, noting the second-administrator approval an online unrestricted grant waits for. `cnm community continue [--vtc-did] [--vta-did]` confirms with a DI-signed authenticate to the VTC (VTC audience) before promoting the profile. The VTC has no key-rotation task (no acl/swap-key; a successor admin entry is itself an unrestricted grant needing a second admin's consent, VTI-APV-014), so the minted key is kept rather than a rotation invented. Reusing another community's key takes `--reuse-identity ` (or an explicit, warned choice in the wizard). `cnm community list` shows each community's identity and the pending ones; `delete` drops a pending one. Holding a community identity as a persona on the personal VTA is a follow-up. - **vtc**: Consent-gated operations wait in an action list and complete on the N-th approval (VTI-APV-017) ([#1918](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1918)) A VTC operation that needs other administrators' approval -- an unrestricted grant (VTI-APV-014), a reduction of another unrestricted admin (VTI-APV-019), a lowered consent threshold (VTI-APV-020), an authority-policy change (VTI-VTC-022) -- is no longer refused with `auth:consent_required` and re-sent. Phase A1 of docs/05-design-notes/vtc-action-list.md. Once every other check passes and the requester's operation-bound step-up is spent (VTI-APV-015), the operation is parked as an action in the new `admin_actions` keyspace (excluded from backup: it binds the ACL as it stood on this host). The record keeps the requester's signed document verbatim, the payload, requester, step-up evidence, approver set, threshold, one challenge per approver, a state pin and its lifetime. The requester is answered `trust-task-next-step/0.1` (202, continuation `proceed`, expecting `vtc/admin/actions/show/0.1` with the action id) and never sends it again. Approvers decide with `task-consent/decision/0.1` or `/0.2`, signed by their own DID (a delegated console

title: Single-administrator mode is one person, under as many identifiers as they hold (VTI-APV-022, VTI-ACL-052)
body:
VTI-APV-022 waived consent only where no eligible party but the requester
existed (item 2). It counted entries, and entries are not people: one person
holding an administrator entry per device was asked to approve their own
requests from another of their own devices, which is the multi-step ceremony
the mode exists to remove, with no second mind behind any step of it.

The node cannot tell one person's identifiers from two people's, so the mode
no longer tries. In single-administrator mode consent is waived whether or
not other administrators' entries exist; the mode SHOULD be enabled only
where every administrator is the same person (new item 2), and stays what it
was otherwise: host-only, a gesture bound to each operation, reported to
every administrator in every session — so a second person who does exist
sees it — and audited at the highest severity.

VTI-ACL-052's single-administrator exception follows: any holder of
unrestricted act scope may edit its own entry in the mode, not only the sole
holder, still refused where the edit would leave no unrestricted entry.
VTI-APV-019's removal conditions (re-authentication, notice, highest
severity) already apply wherever the mode waives a consent.
author: stormer78

title: A subject may relabel its own entry, and a sole administrator in single-administrator mode may edit its own (VTI-ACL-052)
body:
VTI-ACL-052 forbade every self-edit but rotation, which also forbade two
edits it was never aimed at:

- The label. It is on no axis of authority (VTI-ACL-001), so a subject that
  relabels itself gains nothing a bound could have withheld. The remaining
  risk is a misleading self-description; the change is audited and SHOULD be
  shown to others as self-set.
- A community run by one person. Its sole holder of unrestricted act scope
  already holds every axis, so an edit to its own entry cannot widen
  anything, and there is nobody else to make the edit for it. In
  single-administrator mode (VTI-APV-022) that subject may edit its own
  entry under the mode's conditions: a re-authentication bound to the
  operation (VTI-APV-015), the highest audit severity, and never an edit
  that leaves the node without an unrestricted entry.

The rationale for VTI-ACL-052 / VTI-ACL-053 says why neither exception
reopens the bypass the pair closes.

title: fix(did-git-sign): init finds persona DIDs across the context and its sub-contexts
body:
## Problem

`did-git-sign init --profile bob --vta-did <VTA> --context openvtc-bob` showed:

```
openvtc-bob — OpenVTC BOB (no DID)
openvtc-bob/qme5theer1qr — did:webvh:Qme5…:first-vtc (no DID)
```

Then it listed DIDs in the exact chosen context, found none, and offered to create a new did:webvh. That DID has no git rights in any community.

## Where openvtc puts persona DIDs

Read from openvtc `origin/main`:

- **Every persona has a sub-context of its own** under the account's top context: `<top>/<slug>` (`openvtc-core/src/config/context_path.rs` `build_sub_context_id`/`child_path`).
  - A **standalone persona** (`create_persona.rs`, `auto_context`) takes its slug from the persona label.
  - A **persona minted while joining a community** (`join_flow.rs`) takes its slug from the community's display name. When the community has no name, the slug comes from the VTC DID's SCID instead (`fallback_token`, e.g. `openvtc-bob/qme5theer1qr`).
- The persona's keys and DID are created in that sub-context (`community_context::ensure_context`, then `create_persona_keys` / `create_did_via_server(context_id)`).
- `create_did_webvh` is called with `set_primary: false`, so **no context ever has a primary DID**.
- The top context (`config.account.top_context_id`, e.g. `openvtc-bob`) holds no persona DID itself.

## What the VTA does (VTI `origin/main`)

- `vta/webvh/dids/list` (`operations/did_webvh/lifecycle.rs`) filters `contextId` by **exact** match.
- With **no** filter, it returns every DID whose context passes `auth.has_context_access`. That check is segment-aware: an admin of a parent context covers the whole subtree (`vti-common` `ActScope::covers`).
- `keys/list` (`operations/keys.rs`) also filters `contextId` exactly, with the same subtree-aware visibility check.

So did-git-sign makes one unfiltered `dids/list` call and selects the subtree itself. That costs one round trip in total, not one per context.

## Changes

- **Finding the DID.** `init` matches the chosen context and everything under it, segment by segment: `ctx` and `ctx/…` match, `ctx-other` does not.
  - Context labels show how many DIDs are in each subtree (`2 DIDs`, `no DIDs`). The primary DID is still shown, after the count, when one is pinned.
  - The DID picker shows each DID's name, through `names::inline`, and the context it lives in.
  - When there is exactly one DID, `init` uses it and says which one.
- **Creating a DID (changes the default 0.12.1 introduced).** `init` offers to create a DID only when the whole subtree has none. The prompt is: "No DID found in <ctx> or its sub-contexts. A new DID has no git rights in any community until granted. Create one?", and the default answer is **No**. Under `--yes` it never creates one. It stops instead, and says to point `--context` at the context holding the persona, or to run `pnm did-mgmt dids create --context …`.
- **Key picker.**
  - Keys are listed from the chosen DID's own context, not the selected context.
  - Only the DID's own `assertionMethod` Ed25519 keys are offered. Which keys count is decided by `vgi_core::ed25519_signing_keys_from_doc`, the same rule the verifier uses.
  - Each key is shown with the `DID#key-N` it signs as.
  - The old `resolve_did_key_fragment` fell back to `#key-0` when it could not match a key. That fallback is gone: a DID with no matching key now fails with a clear error.
- **Grant command.** `pnm contexts create` fails for a context that already exists, so `init` now prints both commands:
  - If `<ctx>` does not exist yet: `pnm contexts create … --admin-did <setup> --admin-expires 1h --admin-handoff`
  - If it already exists: `pnm acl create --did <setup> --role admin --contexts <ctx> --expires 1h --handoff`

  Both sets of flags were checked against the local `pnm … --help`.
- README Setup and RUNBOOK §3 are updated to match.

No version bump; the release commit does that.

## Tests

New unit tests in `main.rs`:

- subtree matching (`ctx`, `ctx/x`, `ctx/a/b`, `ctx-other`, `ctxby/x`, child vs parent)
- collecting and ordering DIDs across a subtree
- context and DID labels
- `--yes` refuses to create without prompting, the prompt defaults to No, and declining refuses
- the key filter: assertion keys only, relative and embedded methods, bare and multicodec `publicKey`, X25519 excluded
- the grant command text for both paths

Checks run: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p did-git-sign --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test -p did-git-sign` (93 + 7 + 2 + 2 passing).

title: feat(vetting): held statements get a tab of their own
body:
The Vetting page counts held statements on its checklist, but none could be opened, so an applicant had no way to see what a vetter actually signed. This adds a **Vetting** tab to My Credentials, beside Membership. It's useful for the 5 Oct demo: after a session, the applicant can open the statement they just received.

The change is client-only, with no protocol, VTA or VTC change.

## Behaviour

- **List.** One row per held statement, across every application (`VettingBook::applications[*].statements`). Each row names the vetter (contact alias, then verified agent name, then DID, as on the other tabs), then the method and community, e.g. `in person · Kernel Developers`, then the validity window.
- **Detail.** The usual headline (`Vetting statement · valid`), issued by, about and valid lines, followed by what the vetter signed:
  - `For`: the community, labelled the way the Membership tab labels it;
  - `Method`;
  - `Declared`: the relationship they declared;
  - `Relied on`: the documents they relied on, when any;
  - `Verified`: the claims they verified;
  - `Received`.

  Then the ID and the raw credential. `c` copies the JSON.
- **No removal.** A statement belongs to its application, so `d` does nothing on this tab, as on Membership. The detail footer now leaves out `d: remove` on both tabs rather than advertising a key that does nothing.
- **Status is the window only.** Whether a vetter has withdrawn a statement is the community's to record (design §9.6). The tab claims nothing about revocation (R6.3).
- **Persistence.** Applications keep their statements after the join, so members see theirs too.

## Code

- `CredentialsState::active_list()` replaces the per-tab `match` that was repeated in five places across the panel and key handler. `CredentialTab::allows_local_removal()` replaces the `!= Membership` check.
- `VrcSummary` gains two display fields: `note` (shown after the name in the list) and `facts` (labelled lines in the detail view). Existing constructors set them empty, so the other tabs render exactly as before.
- `collect_vetting_statements` in `state_handler/main_page/mod.rs` builds the rows. Every peer-supplied string goes through `sanitize_display`.
- The design doc's §12.3 as-built note and the CHANGELOG are updated.

## Testing

- `a_held_statement_is_listed_with_what_the_vetter_signed`: the row's issuer, subject, status, note and each fact.
- `an_application_without_statements_lists_none`.
- `credential_detail_d_does_nothing_on_the_vetting_tab`.
- `switch_tab_cycles_and_resets_index` now covers Membership → Vetting → Received.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass. `cargo test -p openvtc` passes (786).

**Not checked in a running TUI.** The rendering path is shared with the existing tabs, but nobody has looked at the new tab on screen yet.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no network code
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): no network code
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): read-only view
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): none touched
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): none touched
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no wire types changed
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): status is the validity window and says nothing about revocation
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): no mutations
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: ci(release): at most two semver checks at once in the Release PR job
body:
#1938 measured 91 GB free on / at the start of the run that then died the
same way (runner lost 13 minutes into "Checking API compatibility", "The
operation was canceled" with no newer push), so the disk was never the
cause: memory is. release-plz semver-checks every changed crate in a pool of
`available_parallelism` workers with no setting for it, and the release
pending since #1918 touches eleven crates, so four cold dependency builds
the size of vta-service's run at once.

release-plz runs `cargo-semver-checks` from PATH, so put a gate ahead of
the real binary that admits two checks at a time (two flock slots), and log
what it admits next to a 30 s memory sample. Reverts #1938's SDK deletion
and halved build jobs, which addressed neither.

title: feat(vtc/git-ns): PR-open gate — close pull requests from openers the policy does not allow
body:
Builds on `git-ns/bridge/event/0.4` and `git-ns/bridge/job/0.5` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#723), published in trust-tasks-rs 0.27.3. The workspace floor is raised to `trust-tasks-rs = { version = "0.27.3", … }`. The sibling `trust-tasks-*` crates stay at `"0.27"`, and `Cargo.lock` moves only trust-tasks-rs, from 0.27.1 to 0.27.3.

## What

The VTC side of the pull-request gate. A community can now restrict who may open a pull request on the repositories it governs. The bridge reports each pull request opened or reopened (`git-ns/bridge/event/0.4` `pullRequestOpened`). The VTC checks the author against the community's pull-request policy. When the author is not allowed, the VTC queues a `closePullRequest` job (`git-ns/bridge/job/0.5`), and the bridge posts the community's message on the pull request and closes it (result steps `comment`, then `close`).

**This is hygiene, not the merge gate.** The required commit-trust check is still what keeps untrusted commits out. The gate fails open: if the VTC or bridge is down, if the bridge lacks job 0.5, or if a setting can't be read, the pull request stays open.

## Behaviour (event 0.4, request step 6)

- The VTC serves `git-ns/bridge/event/0.4` beside 0.1–0.3, so 0.4 is listed in `trust-task-discovery`. Older payloads are read as 0.4, and every 0.3 event kind works unchanged.
- A pull request is ignored unless its repository is recorded `active` in a bridge-mode namespace. It is also ignored when the level in force is `anyone`.
- The author's account is matched by forge + id, never by login, through account links to a member. These are **always allowed**:
  - an owner or maintainer of the repository, explicit or implied (a namespace admin included);
  - the bridge's own app account (`<slug>[bot]`);
  - a login in `pr_exempt`.
- Per level, the linked holder must be:
  - `members`: a current member;
  - `committers`: a holder of `git.commit.sign`, explicit or implied (namespace-wide grants included);
  - `maintainers`: `maintain` or higher;
  - `{"roles": [...]}`: a member whose ACL role is listed.
- An account linked to nobody is allowed only under `anyone`.
- **Reopen:** a reopen by an owner, a maintainer or the bridge is an override and is never closed again. A reopen by anyone else re-checks the author exactly as an opening does.
- The message is rendered from the template using only `{author}` (login), `{repo}` (owner/name), `{community}` and `{join_hint}`. No DID, membership state, role or reason goes into it. A value that doesn't look like a login is not rendered. The message is capped at 16384 characters.

## Settings (`gitNamespace` policy `settings`)

| key | default |
|---|---|
| `pr_open` | `"anyone"` (no behaviour change) |
| `pr_open_overrides` | `{}`: `{"github.com/acme[/repo]": level}`; the repository's entry wins over the namespace's, which wins over `pr_open` |
| `pr_exempt` | `["dependabot[bot]"]` |
| `pr_close_message` | built-in Markdown template |
| `pr_join_hint` | derived from the community profile (public URL if set) |

An unreadable value is logged and falls back to that key's default (for `pr_open`, `anyone`). The shipped `git_ns.rego` sets the defaults and documents the keys.

## Job 0.4 vs 0.5

- Discovery now records `takesV0_5` beside `takesV0_4`.
- A bridge that lists 0.5 is sent **every** job as 0.5: 0.5 is a superset with the same meaning, and accepting 0.4 is only a SHOULD for such a bridge.
- A bridge that lists only 0.4 keeps getting 0.4 and never gets a `closePullRequest`.
- When the bridge is known to lack 0.5, the event handler queues nothing; it reads only the cached discovery answer, because it holds the store lock while the bridge waits for its acknowledgement. When the answer is unknown, the dispatcher asks the bridge and cancels the job.
- In both cases, the namespace's administrators get one `gitNs.pullRequest.gateUnenforced` activity row plus a log warning. They are told again only after the bridge has taken 0.5 and then lost it.

## Records

- Only closes are recorded:
  - the `closePullRequest` job, which shows in `activity/list` as `gitNs.job.closePullRequest`;
  - on a `succeeded` result with `close` applied, the audit row `gitNs.pullRequest.closed`, with detail `{number, author (login), level}`.
- A pull request that was allowed leaves no record.
- `closePullRequest` jobs are left out of `git-ns/bridge/job/list/0.1`, because that spec's `JobKind` enum doesn't include the new kind (a spec gap in #723 — the list should be bumped with job 0.5).

## Not done

The configured level isn't shown on the namespace card or in `cnm git view --admin`: the namespace rows in `namespace/list/0.1` are `additionalProperties: false`. The docs say so.

## Tests

- Unit tests (`git_ns::pr_gate`): the decision table (each level, exempt, unlinked, owner/maintainer/bridge always allowed, reopen override vs re-check), settings parsing/validation/defaults/overrides, and message rendering (placeholders, one-pass substitution, login sanitising, length cap).
- Policy tests: the default gate is `anyone`, and settings are read from Rego.
- Integration tests (`git_ns::tests::pr_gate`): from the signed 0.4 event through dispatch to the 0.5 job, the result, and the audit row; the per-repo override; inactive repository and default policy (nothing happens); a bridge without 0.5 (no close and one notice, other jobs still sent as 0.4); every job sent as 0.5 to a 0.5 bridge; 0.3 event kinds under 0.4.

* feat(vtc/git-ns): PR-open gate — close pull requests from openers the policy does not allow

The VTC side of git-ns/bridge/event 0.4 (pullRequestOpened) and
git-ns/bridge/job 0.5 (closePullRequest), trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#723,
published in trust-tasks-rs 0.27.3 (now the workspace floor).

- bridge/event 0.4 is served (and so listed in trust-task-discovery) beside
  0.1-0.3, which are read as 0.4; every earlier event kind is unchanged.

  namespace, the author (matched by forge + id through account links) is
  checked against the gitNamespace policy's new settings: pr_open

  {number, author login, level}. bridge/job/list 0.1 omits closePullRequest

* docs(claude): git-ns jobs go as 0.5 to bridges that list it (send_versioned)

* fix(vtc): dispatch a Trust Task through a boxed router, not one 1.1 MiB poll frame

dispatch_typed was an async fn holding the whole routing match, so its
unoptimised poll frame carried every arm's handler future and temporaries —
measured at ~1.13 MiB (aarch64 debug) — under whichever handler ran. A
git-ns test thread needed ~2.08 MiB in all, and on Linux with vetting-pcs
git_ns::tests::reproject_is_an_owners_for_their_repository_only_and_refused_without_a_bridge
overflowed the 2 MiB test stack (the second time: #1907 grew the join path
and boxing three arms put it off).

dispatch_typed is now a plain fn returning the chosen arm's future, boxed
where it is chosen, so its frame is popped before any handler is polled.
The same test now passes with a 1.15 MiB stack (was 2.08 MiB). Routing is
unchanged: the same 70 arms, in the same order.

trust-tasks-rs 0.27.4 (trust-tasks-tf #727) publishes bridge/job/list 0.2,

title: ci(release): the Release PR job fits eleven parallel semver checks
body:
release-plz runs the semver check for every changed crate in a pool of
`available_parallelism` workers (4 on ubuntu-latest), and each check builds
the crate's dependency tree twice, the crates.io baseline into a target dir
of its own. The pending release touches eleven crates, so four cold builds
run at once at cargo's default -j4. Since 2026-10-03 the job has died 11-20
minutes into "Checking API compatibility" on every push (exit 143, once
"The runner has received a shutdown signal"), with the 12 GiB swap in place,
and the Release PR has stayed stale since #1918.

Halve the build jobs per check, delete the ~20 GB of preinstalled Android,
.NET and GHC SDKs the job never uses (as ci.yml does), and sample memory and
disk every 30 s into a log printed after the run, so a recurrence names the
exhausted resource.

title: feat(vtc/git-ns): single-administrator mode waives git self-grant separation of duties
body:
A community in single-administrator mode (VTI-APV-022, #1925) has one
administrator. Fixed rule 7 of git-ns/right/grant/0.3 still refused every
elevated self-grant, so `cnm git adopt <repo> --owner <own DID>` failed with
git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed. Break-glass left records nobody could ever ratify.

Single-administrator mode now reaches rule 7. It uses the same discipline as
the consent waiver (`git_ns::single_admin`):

- Only where nobody else is eligible. `others_eligible` reuses
  `admin_consent::approvers_for` over the namespace's `git.ns.admin`. That
  covers the break-glass deciders and any approve scope reaching them. It also
  counts any other member whose git rights could make this grant (rules 1 and
  2). One eligible party, or the mode off, and the refusal stands.
- Every path the rule covers: right/grant, repo/create (implied repo.create
  naming self as owner), repo/adopt naming self, namespace/reseat to self, and
  drift/resolve adopt for one's own account. The rules accept a `Waivable`
  token only for that exact actor, right and resource. Rules 1, 2 and 5, the
  granter-covers floor, the consent-class gate and policy all still apply.
- Requires the requester's operation-bound step-up. This is the break-glass
  mechanism (`bound_step_up`), bound to the document actually signed (for an
  adoption, the drift/resolve document).
- Writes a Critical `SingleAdminMode { event: selfGrantWaived }` audit row
  before the write. It names the rule, task, digest, git-ns action, right and
  resource. If the audit write fails, the operation is refused and nothing is
  recorded.
- Marks the result. The record carries `singleAdmin { at, task }`, which is
  never published. The answer carries `ext.org.openvtc.selfGrantWaived`.
  git-ns/view 0.4/0.5 lists waived records under the same ext member. The ACL
  resource grant shows `selfGrantWaived: true`. A `gitNs.right.selfGrantWaived`
  activity item is written.
- Counts for invariants. Waived records count toward the last-owner and
  last-admin invariants, unlike unratified break-glass.

cnm: `git grant|create|adopt|reseat|drift resolve` now sign and go through
the step-up flow `git break-glass` uses. They print a note before the gesture
and a "Single-administrator waiver applied" note after.

vti-common: `SingleAdminModeData` gains optional `right` and `resource`
fields and derives Default. The struct has not been released yet (it was added
in #1925, after vti-common 0.36.0), so this is not breaking against crates.io.
vtc-client adds additive type-URI constants and `self_grant_waived`.

Spec: rule 7 is a MUST naming break-glass as the only way. This is host
configuration, not policy, but it diverges from the rule's text until the git-ns
spec admits VTI-APV-022. The divergence is documented. The upstream change and
the Appendix F entry are not in this PR.

Docs: git-namespaces (separation of duties), admin-access §2.1a and §3.3,
vtc-action-list §8.5, bootstrap runbook, CLAUDE.md.

## Security reasoning

- The waiver never widens past VTI-APV-022 item 2. The eligibility test is the consent gate's own (`approvers_for`), plus anyone whose git rights could make the grant. That makes it stricter than #1925's set. As soon as a second administrator, or an owner who could grant, exists, rule 7 applies again.
- Rules 1, 2 and 5 still run, so nothing is granted that the actor could not grant to someone else. The `Waivable` token covers exactly one (actor, right, resource) and only `single_admin::waivable` can build one.
- The step-up is the break-glass gesture, bound by digest to the signed document and spent before the write. A console key alone cannot satisfy it.
- No waived write can land without its Critical audit row, because the row is written first and an audit failure refuses the operation. The mode itself stays host configuration only.

## Tests

- `git_ns::tests::single_admin` (10): sole admin adopt waived with step-up + Critical row ordered before the grant + record/answer/view/ACL markers + activity item; second admin present refused; repo owner who could grant present refused; mode off refused; audit failure refuses (gesture spent, nothing recorded); waived record counts for last-owner (`git-ns:lastOwner` on self-revoke); grant, repo/create (implied), reseat (also last-admin) and drift adopt each waived.
- `rules` unit tests: the waiver lifts rule 7 only for its exact grant, and rules 2 and 5 still bind; waived vs unratified break-glass invariant counting.
- vti-common round trip for `selfGrantWaived`; cnm note tests, including terminal-escape safety.

## Checks run

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, and the `vetting-pcs` clippy all pass.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 2739/2740 passed. The one failure, `action_list_a2::vti_apv_019_the_first_of_two_administrators_to_act_wins` (a reduction race test this PR doesn't touch), passes when re-run alone.
- `cargo nextest run -p vti-common -p cnm-cli`: 740/740 passed. Doctests pass. Admin UI `npm run lint` and vitest (752) pass. `check-authz-context-types.sh` OK.

## Not in this PR

- Upstream dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf change to rule 7, and the VTI spec Appendix F divergence entry.
- The console still pre-blocks self-grants client-side (`isSelfGrant`). Only the activity label and audit description were added there.

title: feat(vtc/git-ns): single-administrator mode waives git self-grant separation of duties (#1936)
body:
feat(vtc/git-ns): single-administrator mode waives git self-grant separation of duties (#1936)

* feat(vtc/git-ns): single-administrator mode waives git self-grant separation of duties

A community in single-administrator mode (VTI-APV-022, #1925) has one
administrator. Fixed rule 7 of git-ns/right/grant/0.3 still refused every
elevated self-grant, so `cnm git adopt <repo> --owner <own DID>` failed with
git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed. Break-glass left records nobody could ever ratify.

Single-administrator mode now reaches rule 7. It uses the same discipline as
the consent waiver (`git_ns::single_admin`):

- Only where nobody else is eligible. `others_eligible` reuses
  `admin_consent::approvers_for` over the namespace's `git.ns.admin`. That
  covers the break-glass deciders and any approve scope reaching them. It also
  counts any other member whose git rights could make this grant (rules 1 and
  2). One eligible party, or the mode off, and the refusal stands.
- Every path the rule covers: right/grant, repo/create (implied repo.create
  naming self as owner), repo/adopt naming self, namespace/reseat to self, and
  drift/resolve adopt for one's own account. The rules accept a `Waivable`
  token only for that exact actor, right and resource. Rules 1, 2 and 5, the
  granter-covers floor, the consent-class gate and policy all still apply.
- Requires the requester's operation-bound step-up. This is the break-glass
  mechanism (`bound_step_up`), bound to the document actually signed (for an
  adoption, the drift/resolve document).
- Writes a Critical `SingleAdminMode { event: selfGrantWaived }` audit row
  before the write. It names the rule, task, digest, git-ns action, right and
  resource. If the audit write fails, the operation is refused and nothing is
  recorded.
- Marks the result. The record carries `singleAdmin { at, task }`, which is
  never published. The answer carries `ext.org.openvtc.selfGrantWaived`.
  git-ns/view 0.4/0.5 lists waived records under the same ext member. The ACL
  resource grant shows `selfGrantWaived: true`. A `gitNs.right.selfGrantWaived`
  activity item is written.
- Counts for invariants. Waived records count toward the last-owner and
  last-admin invariants, unlike unratified break-glass.

cnm: `git grant|create|adopt|reseat|drift resolve` now sign and go through
the step-up flow `git break-glass` uses. They print a note before the gesture
and a "Single-administrator waiver applied" note after.

vti-common: `SingleAdminModeData` gains optional `right` and `resource`
fields and derives Default. The struct has not been released yet (it was added
in #1925, after vti-common 0.36.0), so this is not breaking against crates.io.
vtc-client adds additive type-URI constants and `self_grant_waived`.

Spec: rule 7 is a MUST naming break-glass as the only way. This is host
configuration, not policy, but it diverges from the rule's text until the git-ns
spec admits VTI-APV-022. The divergence is documented. The upstream change and
the Appendix F entry are not in this PR.

Docs: git-namespaces (separation of duties), admin-access §2.1a and §3.3,
vtc-action-list §8.5, bootstrap runbook, CLAUDE.md.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-console): single-administrator mode lets the console send git self-grants for the VTC to waive

The console blocked every elevated git self-grant client-side (`isSelfGrant`),
so a lone administrator on a node in single-administrator mode (VTI-APV-022)
could not use the waiver the VTC now applies (`git_ns::single_admin`).

With the mode on (read from `ext.org.openvtc.singleAdminMode` on the shell's
action-list read, `useSingleAdminMode`), the grant, reseat, adopt, create and
drift-adopt forms no longer block a self-grant. They show "Single-administrator
mode: this self-grant will be waived, recorded as a critical audit event, and
needs your passkey", build the task, and let the VTC decide. The sign dialog
repeats the notice and uses the same bound step-up flow as break-glass (refused
until the passkey gesture, then the identical document is resent). A
`git-ns:selfGrantNotAllowed` refusal under the mode explains that somebody else
could make the grant. An accepted answer that carries
`ext.org.openvtc.selfGrantWaived` says so in the toast. `adoptStanding` offers a
self-adopt under the mode and keeps every other check.

Records made under the waiver are listed by `git-ns/view` under
`ext.org.openvtc.selfGrantWaived`. The drift read already makes that view call,
so its answer now carries them. The repository's people tables and the member
page's git rights flag each one "self-granted (single-admin)".

With the mode off nothing changes: the client-side block and the break-glass
offer stay as they were.

The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.27.3` → `0.27.4` | patch |

| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.27.3` → `0.27.4` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.27.3` → `0.27.4` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.23.4` → `0.23.5` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.5.5`) | `0.5.4` → `0.5.5` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.5.4` → `0.5.5` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vtc): live admin console — a hint-only event stream over HTTPS (binding 0.3 streamed responses)
body:
UX2: the admin console is told *when* to re-read, over one live channel per session, instead of polling every read on a timer. It implements `vtc/admin/events/subscribe/0.1` and `vtc/admin/events/event/0.1` (trust-tasks-rs 0.27.2 generated types), carried as an **HTTPS binding 0.3 §2.1 streamed response** on the existing `POST /v1/trust-tasks` door. No new route.

### Wire
- The signed subscribe goes with `Accept: text/event-stream, application/json;q=0.5`. The door runs the whole spine first, so any refusal is the ordinary JSON `trust-task-error` and **opens no stream**. Only a success answers `200 text/event-stream` (`Cache-Control: no-store`), and the signed `#response` is its first event.
- Each event carries one complete document on one `data:` line, with no `event:` field. The SSE `id` is the resume token, and heartbeats are `: heartbeat` comments.
- After the `#response` the stream carries only hints and heartbeats, never a `trust-task-error`. It ends without a reason.
- Resumption is in-band only, through `since`. `Last-Event-ID` is a cross-check: if it disagrees with `since`, the subscribe is refused `malformedRequest`. An unknown, foreign or expired `since` opens with `resumed: false`, never an error.

### The hints-only rule
A hint carries `topic`, `at`, `resumeToken`, and `count` on actions, acknowledgements and joinRequests. It never carries a record, an id or a DID. The integration tests assert the shape of every hint the VTC sends. The console reacts only by invalidating the react-query keys of that topic's own signed read.

### VTC (`src/admin_events`, `trust_tasks/event_tasks.rs`)
- **Bus:** a broadcast fed from the storage seams: action save/delete, join-request store/delete, member store/delete, ACL store/delete, config overrides and the community profile.
- **Effective topics:** requested ∩ readable. A topic is readable exactly when the community would answer its read: one gate table (`admin_events::read_capability`) that the `members/list`, `join-requests/list` and `config/export` handlers gate on too. Today `config` needs `vtc.config.admin` (as `config/export` does) and every other topic goes to any administrator. Standing is re-checked on every ACL change, before every hint and once per heartbeat. If the readable topics shrink, the stream ends.
- **Hint suppression:** a per-recipient digest means a change the caller's read would not show sends no hint. Hints are limited to one per topic per second.
- **Stream end:** the stream also ends when the client goes, at shutdown, when the signer's ACL entry, the console-key delegation or the document's `expiresAt` lapses, after an hour, or when a write stalls for 2× the heartbeat.
- **Caps:** 5 concurrent streams per administrator and 256 in all, then `tooManyStreams` (retryable). The defaults are 25 s heartbeat and 10 min / 4096 changes of resume history. All are documented.
- **Freshness and replay:** the subscribe has a 5-minute `issuedAt` window. Its response is never recorded for redelivery, so a replayed subscribe gets `204` and opens nothing.
- **Signing:** hints are signed with the VTC key. No lock is held across an await (R1.3).

### Console
- One subscription per session, read with streaming `fetch`. It reconnects with a freshly signed subscribe carrying `since`, with exponential backoff and jitter, using `retry:` as the floor. It stops for the session on `streamUnavailable`, `notAdministrator`, `permissionDenied` or `unsupportedType`.
- Hints invalidate:
  - the Actions badge and page;
  - the acknowledgement and single-admin banners;
  - the Join requests badge, page and tile;
  - the Members page and tile;
  - the config screens.
- A **Live / Polling** indicator shows Live only while bytes keep arriving, and goes offline after 2× heartbeat of silence (R6.2). Going offline triggers an immediate re-read.
- Badge and tile polls run every 5 minutes while live and every 60 s otherwise.

### cnm
`cnm actions watch [--topic …] [--json]` prints the hints on a terminal. It works over HTTPS only.

### Censuses
- subscribe is in `DISPATCHED_URIS` and has a conformance witness.
- notAdministrator, streamUnavailable and tooManyStreams have error-code witnesses.
- The console manifest lists subscribe as sent and event as received.
- The OpenAPI document and `wire.ts` are regenerated.
- The trust-tasks-rs floor is raised to 0.27.2.

### Open points
- **Consumer rule 1's bearer cross-check (SHOULD).** The `/v1/trust-tasks` door authenticates by the document's proof alone and reads no bearer token, so the caller is always the proven issuer. That meets the SHOULD's intent: the stream is never opened on a session the proof did not establish.
- **`singleAdminMode` never changes while the process runs.** It is boot configuration, and a restart ends every stream and resumes with `resumed: false`.
- **Rebased onto #1931.** The `joinRequests` hint's count is `vtc/join-requests/list`'s own `totalEstimate` (pending filter, `limit: 1`) — the same read the console's badge and tile make. A request referred for review also raises its join-review queue item, which moves the `actions` topic through the action list's save seam. The console's badge and tile polls (now `limit: 1` reads) keep the live/offline intervals, and hints invalidate their keys.

### What CI must prove
- `Test (workspace)`, `Test (VTC)`. This includes the new `tests/it/admin_events.rs`, which covers: the response first then a hint on an action change, capability filtering, shrink ending the stream, refusals as JSON, replay → 204, unknown and foreign `since`, resume, the heartbeat, credential expiry and the stream cap. It also includes the census, conformance and manifest tests, and `openapi_snapshot`.
- The `Test (VTC admin UI)` job: lint and `wire:check`, plus vitest, including `live-events.test.ts` with a mocked stream.
- `clippy -D warnings`, workspace and `vetting-pcs`, plus fmt.

Run locally:
- After the rebase onto #1931: targeted integration filter (admin_events, action_list, trust_task_manifest, openapi, join_requests, community_verbs, members_crud, admin_config) 236/236. Before it, the full `--test it` run was 986/988; the 2 failures are `routing_modes` tests that fail only because `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD` was set.
- vtc-service lib tests filtered to `admin_events`, `admin_actions`, `trust_tasks`, census, conformance and join: 351 passed. The full lib suite was not run locally.
- `cnm-cli`: 120/120 passed.
- vitest: 761/761 passed.
- `npm run lint`, both clippy configurations and fmt: clean.

title: feat(vgi-bridge): PR-open gate — report pull requests (event 0.4) and close them on the VTC's order (job 0.5)
body:
The bridge side of the PR-open gate (spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#723, released in trust-tasks-rs 0.27.3).

## Commits
1. **chore(deps)!: take vta-sdk 0.63 and trust-tasks 0.26.3.** No source changes. One `trust-tasks-rs` node (0.26.3) and one copy of every affinidi / vta crate.
2. **feat(vgi-bridge): PR-open gate**
   - **Event 0.4 `pullRequestOpened`.** Sent for GitHub `pull_request` `opened`/`reopened` on managed repositories. It carries author, actor, draft and fromFork, and never the title, body, branches or diff. The bridge-posted check on the same delivery is unchanged. It is only sent under `event_version = "0.4"`, which is opt-in: the spec forbids sending 0.4 to a VTC that has not listed it in a discovery answer, and this bridge does not send discovery requests. The default stays 0.3.
   - **Job 0.5 `closePullRequest`.** The bridge takes job 0.4 and 0.5 and lists both in discovery. It posts the comment, then closes the PR, idempotently:
     - already closed or merged: `unchanged`, no comment;
     - reopened after `issuedAt` by anyone but the App: `unchanged`;
     - the App's own comment with `<!-- vgi-bridge job:<jobId> -->` already there: the comment step is `unchanged`.
     Forgejo answers `notCapable`.
   - **GitHub App permission.** `pull_requests: write`, the one permission that covers both commenting and closing. Existing installs keep working. Without write, the comment step is `forbidden` and `missingPermissions` lists `pull_requests:write`.
   - **Docs.** BRIDGE.md §3/§6d/§7, RUNBOOK §8f/§8k/§8m, SETUP-GITHUB-VTC, bridge.example.toml.

## Two trust-tasks-rs copies, contained
vta-sdk 0.63 (the latest) and trql-client 0.22 still declare `trust-tasks-rs ^0.26`. So the generated payload types come from `trust-tasks-git-ns`, which is trust-tasks-rs 0.27.3 under another name, used by `vgi-bridge/src/wire.rs` only and meeting the rest as JSON. Everything vta-sdk, trql-client and verify-trust share stays on 0.26.3. Once a vta-sdk and a trql-client on 0.27 are published, the alias collapses into `trust-tasks-rs`.

## Checks
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` (775 passed) and `cargo +1.95.0 check --workspace` all pass. New tests: `crates/vgi-bridge/tests/pr_gate.rs` (17), webhook translation in vgi-forge-github, and discovery, kind and config unit tests.

body:
feat(vgi-bridge): PR-open gate — report pull requests (event 0.4) and close them on the VTC's order (job 0.5) (#133)

* chore(deps)!: take vta-sdk 0.63 and trust-tasks 0.26.3

vta-sdk 0.63 (VTI #1910) is a major only for the VTC join-criteria types
(VTI #1907, Keyring VTI-13), which this workspace does not name, so no
source changes follow. It stays on the TDK 0.22 line and declares
`trust-tasks-rs ^0.26.2`, so that floor and trust-tasks-proof's move with
it; `cargo update` resolves both to 0.26.3. OpenVTC takes 0.63, and
did-git-sign on ^0.62 would put a second vta-sdk in its graph.

`cargo tree -i trust-tasks-rs` is one node (0.26.3) and `cargo tree -d`
shows one copy of every affinidi / trust-tasks / vta crate.

vta-sdk 0.63.0 is not the trust-tasks 0.27 release: VTI main took 0.27
(VTI #1922) after it was cut, and trql-client 0.22 still declares ^0.26.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vgi-bridge): PR-open gate — report pull requests (event 0.4) and close them on the VTC's order (job 0.5)

A community can limit who may open pull requests on its governed
repositories (the VTC's `pr_open` policy). The bridge reports and the VTC
decides (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#723, trust-tasks-rs 0.27.3).

Event 0.4 (`pullRequestOpened`). A verified GitHub `pull_request`
`opened`/`reopened` on a managed repository is reported with its number,
author (`pull_request.user`), actor (`sender`), draft and fromFork (head
repository not the base, or gone) — never title, body, branches or diff.
Other actions, unmanaged and foreign repositories and `.vgi` are not
reported; each delivery once, under its own dedup key, so the bridge-posted
check the same delivery prompts is unaffected. `event_version = "0.4"` is
opt-in: event 0.4 forbids sending it to a VTC that has not listed it in a
discovery answer to this bridge, and the bridge does not ask discovery (0.3
was made the default because it had no such rule). Below 0.4 no pull
request is reported, and one still queued is dropped rather than sent under
an older type.

Job 0.5 (`closePullRequest`). The bridge takes job 0.4 and 0.5 and lists
both in its discovery answer; a 0.4 job naming the new kind is
malformedRequest. Steps `comment` then `close`: already closed or merged ->
both unchanged, no comment; reopened after the job's issuedAt by anyone but
the App -> both unchanged (issuedAt is now kept in the job ledger); else the
message verbatim plus a hidden `<!-- vgi-bridge job:<jobId> -->` marker,
skipped when the App's own comment with that marker is already there, then
PATCH state=closed. Errors map to notFound, forbidden, notCapable,
rateLimited, forgeError; a forbidden re-reads the installation so
missingPermissions is current. Forgejo answers notCapable.

vgi-forge gains `ForgeEventKind::PullRequestOpened`, `PullRequest` /
`PullRequestState` / `Reopen`, and four defaulted `Forge` calls
(`pull_request`, `has_own_comment`, `comment_on_pull_request`,
`close_pull_request`, default Unsupported). vgi-forge-github implements
them, and maps GitHub's 422 "permissions requested are not granted" on a
token request to Forbidden (it was NotFound for repository-scoped tokens).

The App manifest asks for `pull_requests: write` (was read): commenting on
a pull request needs Issues or Pull requests write and closing one needs
Pull requests write, so that single permission covers both. The
bridge-posted check still needs only read; an existing installation keeps
working, reports `pull_requests:write` missing, and its closePullRequest
jobs fail `forbidden`.

The payload types come from `trust-tasks-git-ns` (trust-tasks-rs 0.27.3
under another name) while everything vta-sdk, trql-client and verify-trust
share stays on the single 0.26 line: no published vta-sdk or trql-client
takes 0.27 yet. They meet only as JSON; the alias collapses when they do.

Docs: BRIDGE.md §3 (permissions, upgrade), §6d (the gate), §7 (event
versions); RUNBOOK §8f, §8k, new §8m; SETUP-GITHUB-VTC; bridge.example.toml.

title: docs(git-ns): single-administrator mode may waive the self-grant rule
body:
## What

Fixed rule 7 (separation of duties) of `git-ns/right/grant` 0.3 names break-glass as "the one way" an actor records an elevated right for themselves. A community run by one person has nobody to make its administrator's elevated grants and nobody to ratify a break-glass. Under the rule, that administrator cannot own a repository they create or adopt, or reseat a namespace to themselves, except through break-glass records that are never ratified.

This PR adds a narrowly scoped exception, **The single-administrator waiver**, as a new section of `git-ns/right/grant` 0.3:

- A VTC that its **host operator** has configured for single-administrator operation **MAY** waive rule 7 for one operation. It may do so only when **no other party is eligible** to make the grant. That means no other holder of covering grant authority (rules 1 and 2), and no other administrator who could ratify or revoke the break-glass. Single-administrator operation is a host-level setting outside community policy (the VTI specification's VTI-APV-022). Community policy still cannot waive the rule.
- When the VTC waives the rule, it **MUST**:
  - require an operation-bound step-up,
  - record a highest-severity audit event before the record is written, and refuse with nothing recorded if it cannot,
  - keep a mark with the record, and mark the response in its payload `ext`. The member name is left to the VTC.
- The record counts toward the last-owner and last-admin invariants (rules 3 and 4).
- If any other eligible party exists, rule 7 applies unchanged.

`repo/create` 0.3, `namespace/reseat` 0.3 and `drift/resolve` 0.3 now refer to the waiver at the step where they apply rule 7. `repo/adopt` is covered through grant 0.3's "Tasks the rule binds" table, which already lists it. Its own 0.2 prose does not restate rule 7, so it is unchanged.

## Why in place

All four specs are `status: draft`. SPEC §5.2 and §5.3 allow a draft's prose to change without a version bump. The change has no wire effect: every affected response already carries the open `ext` member, and `RightRecord` is unchanged.

## Context

Implementation: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1936. Its `docs/03-vtc/git-namespaces.md` records this as a divergence until the spec admits it.

## Checks

`npm run validate`, `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all` (no diff), TS/Go/Dart bindings builds (no diff), `npm run check-bindings`, `cargo test --workspace` (1449 passed), `npm run build`. All pass.

title: feat(git-ns): bridge event 0.4 pullRequestOpened and job 0.5 closePullRequest
body:
## What

A VTC community can restrict who may open pull requests on its governed repositories. The bridge reports each pull request opened or reopened to the VTC, and the VTC, when the opener is not allowed, sends the bridge a job to comment with a templated message and close the PR.

Two new spec versions, each carrying its predecessor forward unchanged otherwise:

- **`git-ns/bridge/event/0.4`** = `0.3` + the `pullRequestOpened` `ForgeEvent` variant
- **`git-ns/bridge/job/0.5`** = `0.4` + the `closePullRequest` kind

Both still pin `git-ns/_shared/0.3`.

### New event variant (`event.type = "pullRequestOpened"`)

```jsonc
{
  "type": "pullRequestOpened",        // required, const
  "forgeId": "812736451",             // required, _shared ForgeId (the repository's)
  "resource": "github.com/acme/widgets", // required, _shared RepoResource
  "number": 42,                       // required, integer >= 1
  "action": "opened",                 // required, "opened" | "reopened"
  "author": { "forge": "github.com", "id": "5550123", "login": "eve-dev" }, // required, _shared ForgeAccount
  "actor":  { "forge": "github.com", "id": "5550123", "login": "eve-dev" }, // required, _shared ForgeAccount
  "draft": false,                     // optional boolean
  "fromFork": true                    // optional boolean
}
```

### New job kind (`kind = "closePullRequest"`)

```jsonc
{
  "jobId": "job_01J9C4M7QX",
  "namespace": "ns_01J8Z6Q4M2",
  "kind": "closePullRequest",
  "repo": "github.com/acme/widgets",  // required for this kind
  "number": 42,                       // new: integer >= 1
  "message": "markdown..."            // new: string, 1..16384
}
```

The schema adds `dependentRequired` (`number` → `repo`, `message`; `message` → `number`); which kind may carry them stays the kind table's rule, as for every other member.

## Semantics written down

- **Policy** (event 0.4 Definitions): levels anyone / members / committers / maintainers / named VTC roles, configured at the VTC. Repository owners and maintainers (by record or implication, so namespace admins too) and the bridge's own forge account are always allowed.
- **Reopen**: a reopen by an owner, maintainer or the bridge is an override, and the VTC does not close the PR again. A reopen by anyone else is checked again, exactly as an opening is.
- **Hygiene, not the merge gate**: the required commit-trust check stays the security control. If the VTC or bridge is down, the PR simply stays open.
- **Idempotent close** (job 0.5 Request step 7): steps `comment` then `close`. Already closed (merged included) → `succeeded`, both `unchanged`, no comment. Reopened after the job's `issuedAt` by someone other than the bridge → `unchanged` (don't defeat an override). The bridge MUST be able to tell whether it already commented for the `jobId` (a durable record, or a hidden marker on its own comment), so a retry never posts twice. Error codes reuse `git-ns/bridge/result` 0.1's vocabulary: `notFound`, `forbidden`, `notCapable`, `rateLimited`, `forgeError`.
- **Version negotiation via `trust-task-discovery`**: a VTC sends job 0.5 only to a bridge that lists it. A bridge still on 0.4 is unaffected and keeps getting 0.4 jobs, but has no PR gate, and the VTC tells its operator. A bridge sends event 0.4 only to a VTC that lists it, and otherwise sends 0.3 with no PR events.

## Why `git-ns/bridge/result` is not bumped

`result/0.1` does not enumerate job kinds. Its `steps[].step` is an open lowerCamelCase pattern, and `error.code` is open ("a bridge MAY use others"), so `comment`/`close` and the reused codes already validate. The per-kind handling is documented in job 0.5 instead.

## Recipe

`npm run validate`, codegen + `cargo fmt`, TS/Go/Dart bindings, `npm run check-bindings` (all agree), `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features "validate,git-ns" --test conformance` for both new modules (8 tests each, including `rejects_invalid_examples`), and `npm run build`: all green. No versions or changelogs touched.

feat(git-ns): bridge event 0.4 pullRequestOpened and job 0.5 closePullRequest (#723)

A VTC community can restrict who may open pull requests on its governed
repositories. The bridge reports each pull request opened or reopened
(git-ns/bridge/event 0.4, new pullRequestOpened variant); when the VTC's
pull-request policy does not allow the author, it sends the bridge a
closePullRequest job (git-ns/bridge/job 0.5), which posts the community's
message as a comment and closes the pull request, idempotently.

Owners, maintainers and the bridge are always allowed; a reopen by an
owner or maintainer is an override. The gate is hygiene, not the merge
gate: the required commit-trust check remains the security control.

Regenerated Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings.

title: feat(vtc): break-glass ratification, join review and vetting review live in the action list; lists count and filter before paging
body:
## What

Implements step 3 of `vtc-action-list.md` §8.4: the three queues in §8.2's *Existing queues* table become action-list items of category `queue`. Also makes two listings count and filter before paging (no wire change).

### Part A: queue items

| Kind | Raised when | Deciders | Approve | Decline |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gitNs.breakGlass.review` | a break-glass is recorded unratified | `git.ns.admin` at its namespace, never its subject | `right_ratify` | `right_revoke` |
| `member.join.review` | a join is referred for review | `vtc.join.decide` | `decide_inner` `approved` | `decide_inner` `rejected` |
| `vetting.withdrawal.review` | a withdrawn statement leaves a current member `needsReview` (one item per member) | `vtc.vetting.manage`, never the member | keep (recorded) | `admin_remove_inner` as the decider (its own rules) |

- **No wire task changes.** Each item's `typeUri` is a record type (`urn:openvtc:vtc:…`, never dispatched, like a grants review). Decisions are `task-consent/decision` signed by the decider's own DID, and each answer runs the existing operation, so audit, notices and invariants stay as they were. That includes break-glass: the Critical row, the notice, and the rule that an unratified record never counts toward last-owner or last-admin.
- **Summary templates are pinned** in `summary.rs` and `action-summary.ts`, with shared vectors.
- **Queue semantics** (`admin_actions/queues.rs`):
  - Deciders hold the capability (`admin_consent::may_decide`); approve authority is not enough.
  - Threshold 1, and it does not appear on the wire.
  - No expiry and no cancel. The person who broke the glass cannot withdraw it.
  - Queue items are excluded from the action-list limits.
  - A refused decision leaves the item open. An interrupted one is settled from the record.
- **Closing by any route.** Hooks in `decide_inner`, `right_ratify` and `right_revoke` close the item at once and name the decider. Anything else closes at the next read (`queues::settle`).
- **Crash-safe raising (R2.1).** Items are raised when the record is written, and the minute sweeper raises any that are missing (`queues::reconcile`). Holders who gain the capability later get a slot at the next sweep.
- **Single-admin mode changes nothing.** A queue item is a decision, not a consent, so a sole holder decides it. A break-glass is still never self-ratified.
- **Console:**
  - Actions cards show per-kind buttons: Ratify/Revoke, Approve/Reject, Keep member/Start removal.
  - Queue items show no threshold, no expiry and no Cancel.
  - Closed items say how they were decided.
  - Deciding on the Join requests page refreshes the Actions badge.

### Part B: listings count and filter before paging

- `vtc/join-requests/list/0.1` (status) and `vtc/members/list/0.1` (role, live ACL entry) now filter before paging. The cursor walks only matching rows, which fixes the empty-page-with-`nextCursor` bug. Both fill `totalEstimate` with an exact count; at VTC scale the page is already cut from the in-memory keyspace.
- Console:
  - The Join requests badge, both dashboard tiles and the ceremonies count each make one `limit: 1` read using `totalEstimate`.
  - The Join requests page shows the total.
  - The "Awaiting a vetting decision" tile now reads `more` and the pending total from it.
  - The list-limit census is unchanged and passes.

Docs: `admin-access.md` §3.2a and quick reference, `website-and-admin.md`, `git-namespaces.md`, `vtc-action-list.md` §8.2 status and §10, `CLAUDE.md` (git-ns invariants).

## Tested locally (targeted)

- `admin_actions::queue_tests` (join and vetting raise, approve, reject, keep, start-removal, refused removal, closing by another route, sweeper re-raise, limits; filter-before-page and `totalEstimate` for both listings)
- `git_ns::tests::break_glass_queue` (raise, deciders, invariants kept, ratify and revoke via the action list, closing by direct ratify and revoke, never lapses, no cancel, sweeper re-raise and new-holder slot)
- `tests/it/action_list_queues.rs` (wire conformance of `queue` actions at list 0.1 and 0.2, decide through the spine, `totalEstimate` over the door)
- A broader targeted nextest run over admin_actions / git_ns / acl / join / members / vetting / action_list / admin_roles / single_admin / console_list_limits / openapi / census / conformance: 928 passed
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `-p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`
- admin-ui `npm run lint` and full `vitest` (752 passed)

## What CI must prove

- `Test (workspace)` and `Test (VTC)` full suites are green. In particular nothing else depends on the old post-page filtering or on an absent `totalEstimate`, and the response-conformance gate accepts `queue` actions everywhere they are rendered.
- Clippy across the workspace and the reduced `vtc-service` feature sets, MSRV, and the admin-ui build (vite, embedded by `build.rs`).
- The `no_rebuild` step, the openapi snapshot and census tests are unaffected (no route or schema changed).

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.27.2
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: Live admin console events — a hint-only subscription ([#721](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/721))

Adds vtc/admin/events/subscribe/0.1 and vtc/admin/events/event/0.1, and
  the HTTPS binding 0.3 that carries them.

  A console opens one live channel per session with a signed subscribe
  naming the topics it renders (actions, acknowledgements, joinRequests,
  members, singleAdminMode, config). The community answers with the
  #response as the first document on a stream, then sends event documents
  that are hints only: a topic, a time, a resume token, and for the badge
  topics the caller's count. A hint MUST NOT carry record data, record
  identifiers or personal data; the console re-fetches through the
  existing signed reads, so authorization stays on every read and the
  stream can neither leak a record nor grant a read. Each topic is sent
  only to a caller who could perform its read, checked per hint; a
  shrinking topic set ends the stream rather than silently narrowing it.
  Resumption is in-band (`since`), an unknown token is never an error,
  and the console must show live/offline from a signal that can go false
  (heartbeat interval in the response). Polling stays the fallback.

  HTTPS binding 0.2 said it defined no streaming variant, so 0.3 adds
  §2.1 streamed responses: Accept: text/event-stream on the ordinary
  POST; refusals stay JSON and never open a stream; the #response is the
  first SSE event; one complete document per single data: line, no
  event: field; SSE id carries the task's resume token; heartbeats are
  SSE comments; resumption is in-band only, with Last-Event-ID a
  cross-check (mismatch is malformedRequest); either side may close, a
  close is not cancellation, no error is sent after the #response, and a
  stream ends no later than the bearer credential that opened it. Native
  EventSource reconnection (a bodiless GET) is deliberately not offered:
  every (re)connection is a freshly signed request. Registered in
  website/assets/bindings.js. No framework change was needed.

- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

title: feat(vtc): live admin console events — a hint-only subscription
body:
## What

- **`vtc/admin/events/subscribe/0.1`**: an administrator's console opens **one live channel per session** with a signed subscribe (console key) naming the topics it renders: `actions | acknowledgements | joinRequests | members | singleAdminMode | config` (minItems 1), plus an optional opaque `since` resume token. The `#response` (effective `topics`, `heartbeatSeconds`, `resumed`, `resumeToken`) is the first document on a stream. Event documents follow it.
- **`vtc/admin/events/event/0.1`**: the hint. It carries `{topic, at, count?, resumeToken}`, with `count` only on `actions`, `acknowledgements` and `joinRequests`. It has no response. Its proof is RECOMMENDED: SPEC §4.7.2 defaults to SHOULD over HTTPS and §7.3 item 8 forbids declaring less, but a console still accepts an unsigned hint, since a hint grants nothing. A hint **MUST NOT** carry record data, record identifiers or personal data.
- **`vtc/admin/events/_shared/0.1/topic.schema.json`**: holds `Topic` and `ResumeToken`, which both tasks use.
- **HTTPS binding 0.3** (`bindings/https/0.3`, registered in `website/assets/bindings.js`): adds §2.1 *Streamed responses*. 0.2 stated explicitly that it defined no streaming variant, so this needed a binding change. It is a MINOR change and additive.

## Design

- **Hints only.** The console reacts to a hint by re-fetching through the existing signed reads, so authorization stays on every read. The stream can neither leak a record nor grant a read.
- **Per-topic authorization.** Each topic is bound to one read. A community sends a topic's hints only to a caller who could perform that read, and checks this for every hint. If the caller's readable topics shrink, the community ends the stream rather than silently narrowing it, and the console's re-subscribe reports the new set.
- **No latched status.** The console shows live only while bytes keep arriving within 2 × `heartbeatSeconds`. When they stop, it shows offline at once and falls back to polling.
- **Resumption.** `since` is in-band. An unknown or foreign token is never an error: the community answers `resumed: false` and the console re-reads every topic, so a token cannot be used as an oracle.

## The binding addition (§2.1)

- The client sends the ordinary `POST /trust-tasks` with `Accept: text/event-stream, application/json;q=0.5`.
- Refusals stay JSON under the §4 status mapping. A stream is never opened to carry an error.
- On success the server answers `200` with `text/event-stream`, and the `#response` is the first event.
- Each event carries one complete document on a single `data:` line, with no `event:` field.
- The SSE `id` carries the task's resume token. Comments are heartbeats, and 2 × the interval with nothing received means the stream is dead.
- Resumption is in-band only. `Last-Event-ID` is a cross-check, and a mismatch is `malformedRequest`.
- Either side may close at any time. A close is not cancellation, no `trust-task-error` is sent after the `#response`, and a stream ends no later than the bearer credential that opened it.
- The lifecycle and security-profile sections gain the matching rows.
- Native `EventSource` reconnection (a bodiless `GET` with no `Authorization`) is deliberately not offered. Every connection and reconnection is a freshly signed request, so the client reads the stream with a streaming `fetch`.

No framework change was needed. `messaging/monitor/subscribe` + `event` already establish the pattern of a `#response` followed by separate fire-and-forget documents on a live connection.

## Checks

- `npm run validate` and `npm run build` pass.
- All four bindings were regenerated, and `npm run check-bindings` reports that all agree.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --no-default-features --features vtc,validate --test conformance` passes (399), including the 8 new tests.
- `--lib` passes (126) when `acl` is added to the feature set. The lib unit tests reference the `acl` family (`UNIT_TEST_FAMILIES`), so `--features vtc,validate --lib` alone does not compile, and that is not caused by this change.

A console opens one live channel per session with a signed subscribe
naming the topics it renders (actions, acknowledgements, joinRequests,
members, singleAdminMode, config). The community answers with the
#response as the first document on a stream, then sends event documents
that are hints only: a topic, a time, a resume token, and for the badge
