title: fix(vtc)!: removing an administrator, lowering the consent threshold and changing authority policy take a second party (VTI-APV-019, VTI-APV-020, VTI-VTC-022) (#1917)
body:
fix(vtc)!: removing an administrator, lowering the consent threshold and changing authority policy take a second party (VTI-APV-019, VTI-APV-020, VTI-VTC-022) (#1917)

* fix(vtc)!: removing an administrator, lowering the consent threshold and changing authority policy take a second party (VTI-APV-019, VTI-APV-020, VTI-VTC-022)

One unrestricted administrator could undo VTI-APV-014 alone: remove every
other administrator one at a time, lower the consent threshold back to 1, and
rewrite the policy that decides authority (vtc-action-list.md §8.1, holes 1-3).
These are the stop-gaps of §7b, built on the consent machinery that already
exists. Each is replaced by its action-list rule once that lands.

1. Removals and demotions of an administrator take the requester's
   operation-bound step-up (VTI-APV-019). acl/revoke (removal and scope
   reduction), a downward acl/change-role, an acl/update or acl/grant rewrite
   that takes authority from a live admin (narrowed scopes, an expiry brought
   forward), and vtc/members/admin-remove of an admin all go through
   bound_step_up::redeem_or_request. When the subject is another live
   unrestricted admin they also take consent through admin_consent, from the
   unrestricted admins other than BOTH the requester and the subject (approver
   set `unrestricted-admins-except-subject`; the subject's decision is refused
   as notAnApprover). Where that set is empty (two unrestricted admins), the
   step-up suffices, and once the write lands it is audited as the new
   `AuthorityReducedUnopposed` event at AuditSeverity::Critical; a removal also
   sends the subject the signed removal notice. The attrition guards
   (check_attrition, lock_admin_set, last-admin) are unchanged and still run;
   attrition is also asked before the gesture so a stranded removal never asks
   for one. Removing an expired or non-admin entry is unchanged.
   vtc/members/update can no longer demote an admin (it has no operation to
   bind a gesture to) and names acl/change-role instead.

2. Lowering acl.unrestricted_admin_consent_threshold, by config/patch or an
   applied vtc/config/import, takes the requester's step-up and consent at the
   threshold as it stands (VTI-APV-020), pinned to that value. Raising it, or
   leaving it unchanged, stays immediate; the meetable check is unchanged.

3. policy/upsert/0.2 and policy/activate/0.1 require an unrestricted admin
   (require_super_admin), not any admin. For the purposes that decide authority
   (roleChange, removal, join, crossCommunityRoles, gitNamespace —
   PolicyPurpose::decides_authority) they also take the step-up and consent of
   another unrestricted admin (VTI-VTC-022). The upload and activation checks
   run before the gate, so a module that would be refused asks nobody.

4. vtc/members/admin-remove applies acl/revoke's scope-cover check
   (caller_covers_target, VTI-ACL-050): an entry the actor cannot see answers
   as not found, one it does not fully cover is refused.

admin_consent is generalised over an `Act` (GrantUnrestricted,
ReduceUnrestricted, LowerThreshold, ChangeAuthorityPolicy) that decides the
approvers, the refusal wording, what the approvers are shown and the state the
consent is pinned to. require and gesture_then_consent keep their signatures
and are Act::GrantUnrestricted, so APV-014 is unchanged. TaskError gains a
StepUp variant so a gate deep in an operation refuses with the ceremony inline.

Breaking: these verbs now refuse without a gesture (and consent) where they
used to succeed; vti-common's AuditEvent gains a variant (it is
#[non_exhaustive]).

Known gap: an unopposed demotion or narrowing has no specified notice to send
(member-removal-notice covers removal only); the subject is told only through a
re-minted role credential where they are a member.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc)!: the console answers the new gates on removal, demotion, policy and threshold changes (VTI-APV-019, VTI-APV-020, VTI-VTC-022)

The daemon now refuses these verbs without the requester's bound passkey gesture, and where a second party is needed with auth:consent_required. The console sent them through plain postSignedTrustTask, so an operator would have seen a raw refusal.

Each now goes through postSignedWithStepUp + explainConsent, as grant and promotion already did:
- acl/revoke (lib/acl.ts revokeAcl, now taking a ConfirmGesture; plugins/acl.tsx passes the confirm dialog's).
- acl/change-role (lib/acl.ts changeAclRole), which now explains consent itself, so a demotion of an unrestricted admin is explained as a promotion was.
- vtc/members/admin-remove (new lib/member-removal.ts adminRemoveMember; plugins/members.tsx).
- policy/upsert and policy/activate (lib/policies-api.ts; plugins/ceremonies.tsx).
- config/patch (saveConfig, moved from lib/api.ts to lib/config-api.ts because the step-up path sends through lib/api.ts; plugins/SessionTimeoutCard.tsx).

Tests: lib/acl.test.ts covers revoke and demotion through the gesture and the consent explanation. New lib/gated-writes.test.ts covers admin-remove, policy upload and activation, and a threshold-lowering config patch.
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: Bind re-authentication factors independently, hold consent-gated operations, and close the routes around second-party consent (VTI-APV-016 – 021, VTI-ACL-035 – 037, VTI-VTC-022 – 023)
body:
Requirements for role-based administration at a community, the approval action list, and approver-device step-up.

**Approvals (03b):** VTI-APV-015 clarified (which signatures count as a re-authentication factor); new VTI-APV-016 (factor binding anchors), -017 (operations held pending consent are re-evaluated at execution), -018 (authority-conferring capabilities generalise VTI-APV-014), -019 (removing authority takes a third party's consent, or loud audit when none exists), -020 (lowering a threshold takes consent at the old threshold), -021 (approval-fatigue bounds).

**Access control (03a):** VTI-ACL-035 – 037 resource-qualified capabilities (never naming a trust context; conferring nothing without a live entry; delegation-bounded) — the resolution F.5 already proposes for community resource rights.

**VTC (11):** VTI-VTC-022 policy may only refuse; VTI-VTC-023 operator writes surfaced to administrators and acknowledged.

**Appendix C.3** proposes the community capability registry and roles; **F.5a** records three observed divergences these requirements close.

Companion: trust-tasks registry PR (wire shapes) and VTI design notes (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1914).

title: Bind re-authentication factors independently, hold consent-gated operations, and close the routes around second-party consent (VTI-APV-016 – 021, VTI-ACL-035 – 037, VTI-VTC-022 – 023) (#51)
body:
Bind re-authentication factors independently, hold consent-gated operations, and close the routes around second-party consent (VTI-APV-016 – 021, VTI-ACL-035 – 037, VTI-VTC-022 – 023) (#51)

- VTI-APV-015: a signature satisfies an operation-bound re-authentication only
  from a key bound as a factor under VTI-APV-016, distinct from the caller's
  signing keys and held behind user verification.
- VTI-APV-016 (new): a re-authentication factor is bound only on evidence
  independent of the subject's signing keys (an out-of-band token, an existing
  factor, another administrator's re-authenticated authority, or host access),
  with proof of possession, audited.
- VTI-APV-017 (new): an operation held pending consent and executed when it
  completes is re-evaluated at execution, executed at most once, never after
  expiry.
- VTI-APV-018 (new): granting an authority-conferring capability takes another
  party's consent; VTI-APV-014 is its instance for unrestricted act scope.
- VTI-APV-019 (new): removing another subject's unrestricted or
  authority-conferring authority takes consent from a party other than the
  requester and the subject, or, with none, re-authentication, notice and a
  highest-severity audit row.
- VTI-APV-020 (new): lowering or removing a consent requirement takes consent
  at the requirement as it stood.
- VTI-APV-021 (new): bound pending requests per requester and alert on bursts.
- VTI-ACL-035 – 037 (new): resource-qualified capabilities, never naming a
  trust context, conferring nothing without a live entry, delegation-bounded.
- VTI-VTC-022 (new): community policy may only refuse; VTI-VTC-023 (new):
  access control written outside the operation surface is surfaced to every
  remaining administrator and acknowledged.
- Appendix C.3: proposed community capability registry and roles.
- Appendix F.5a: three observed divergences at one community node (unchecked
  removal of administrators, consent-free threshold lowering, policy open to
  context-scoped administrators).

title: fix(vtc-console): error text wraps inside its box
body: Error toasts overflowed their box when the message carried a long DID (e.g. the step-up refusal naming a `did:webvh`). Root cause: the message is a flex item with `min-width: auto`, so it couldn't shrink below its longest unbroken token, and a DID has no break opportunity. Fix: `min-width: 0` + `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on `.toast-message`, and `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on the other error surfaces (`.card.error`, `.finding`, `.field-error`, `.breakglass-banner`, `.signing-renew-banner`). CSS only.

title: fix(extension): signTrustTask as asDid reaches the VTA without a REST base
body:
## Problem

`doSignTrustTask` only opened a VTA session when the active connection carried a `restBaseUrl`:

```ts
const vta = restBaseUrl ? await getVtaSession(vtaDid, restBaseUrl) : null;
```

A wallet connected to its VTA over TSP or DIDComm only (no REST base on the connection) therefore refused every `asDid` request with:

> cannot sign as did:webvh:…: this wallet has no route to its VTA to sign with that identity

Since #289 this is a hard refusal (before, it quietly fell back to the holder key, which the RP refused anyway). It blocks the VTC console's wallet-authorized signing-key enrolment (`auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2`, verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1903) for operators who signed in via SIOPv2 / proxy-login. Seen on vtc.ic3.dev.

## Fix

`getVtaSession` already picks transports TSP > DIDComm > REST and treats `restBaseUrl` as an optional override. The fix opens the session unconditionally. The `null`-session branches it left unreachable are removed.

## Testing

- `npm test` in `packages/extension`: `tsc -b` + 874 tests, all pass.
- Not yet verified end to end against vtc.ic3.dev.

title: fix: a seated vetter can hand out tickets before its membership credential lands
body:
## Problem

On openvtc main (9e274b1) with one mediator, after a vetter is seated ("You vet for … until …"), pressing `t` still answers "You can hand out tickets once a community you belong to has named you a vetter". The same flow worked with 9b493e2 + vta-sdk 0.61.

## What the code shows

`git diff 9b493e2..9e274b1` doesn't change the check. The ticket form's list is built in `sync()` (`vetting_actions.rs:148`), which keeps a membership only if it is **Active** and has a live vetter grant. The "You vet for" row looks only at the stored grant, and `inbound::vetter_grant` stores a grant for a membership of any status. So both messages appear together exactly when the membership exists, is not Active, and has a live grant: in practice, an approved join whose membership credential hasn't arrived (`approved_awaiting_credential`, added in #406/#411).

## Why draft

- **The cause is inferred, not confirmed.** To check it, look at the vetter's row in the Communities panel. "✓ approved — membership credential not received yet" or Pending would confirm it; Active would rule it out.
- **This may be a symptom of VTI-61 (#415).** If the vetter's membership credential is lost on the way in over TSP (#413 moved member traffic to TSP after a TSP join), the membership stays Pending. #415 would then remove the cause, and this PR becomes a stricter-vs-looser UX choice rather than a bug fix. Worth retesting the `t` flow on #415 first.

## Change

The `sync()` filter becomes `m.status.is_active() || m.approved_awaiting_credential()`. The live-grant requirement stays. The community decides who can vet, and it has already approved and seated this persona.

## Tests

- New test `a_seated_vetter_can_hand_out_tickets` covers four cases: Active with a grant (listed); approved and awaiting the credential, with a grant (listed, and fails before the fix); Pending and never approved, with a grant (not listed); Active with no grant (not listed).
- `cargo test -p openvtc --bin openvtc`: 784 passed. `cargo fmt --check` is clean. The `openvtc-core` and end-to-end tests have not been run.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] R1.2 / R1.3 / R1.4 / R1.5 / R1.6: n/a, local UI gate only
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1): n/a
- [x] Wire types (R3.*): none
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*): still requires a live grant from the community
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*)
- [x] Deviations: none

title: fix: TSP invites and replies share one relationship store (VTI-61)
body:
## Problem (VTI-61)

A terminal-app persona on the shared mediator cannot finish joining a community that runs on its own mediator. The community admits it, but the persona never receives its membership credential, and a vetter grant is discarded the same way. The terminal app logs no relationship control message and then logs `TSP message from <community> discarded: no relationship with <persona>` three times. Older builds and unmodified main (9e274b1) behave the same.

## Root cause

openvtc sends TSP from one ATM and receives replies on another, and the two keep separate relationship stores.

- `TDK::new(.., None)` builds `tdk.atm` with `ATMConfigBuilder::default()`, which gives it a private in-memory `RelationshipStore` (`openvtc/src/main.rs:65`, `state_handler/mod.rs:469`, `:572`).
- Every outbound TSP send (join submit, status poll, members, personhood, vetting) goes through `tsp::send_trust_task` on `tdk.atm`. `form_relationship_routed` records `Pending(persona, community)` in that private store.
- Inbound frames are unsealed by the per-persona listener ATMs (`openvtc-core/src/didcomm.rs:964`), which use the shared `TspStoreHandle` store. That store holds `None` for the community.
- The community's Accept therefore reaches `record_incoming_control` as `ReceiveAccept` from `None`. That is an invalid transition, logged only at debug ("not recorded — a protocol rule refused it"), which is why no control message appears.
- The application frames that follow fail the §7.2.2 check in `unpack_message`, giving "no relationship with <persona>".
- `send_trust_task` sees `Pending` in its own store and never re-invites, so the process can't recover on its own.

The hop sender of the first frame (the community's mediator) is the normal shape for an Accept relayed over a multi-hop route; the mediator reseals at intermediate hops. It is not the cause. The community side is behaving correctly.

On a single mediator without TSP, joins work because the submit goes over DIDComm and the community opens the relationship itself.

## Fix

`TspStoreHandle::adopt_into(tdk)` rebuilds `tdk.atm` on the TDK's shared state with `with_relationship_store(shared)`. `StateHandler` calls it once, after the TDK and config are settled and before the listeners are built. All three TDK construction paths meet at that point. A TDK without an ATM is returned unchanged. If the rebuild fails, it logs `warn!` and keeps the old TDK, which means the old behaviour.

Nothing uses the ATM before the swap. Persona secrets are loaded into the shared state, which the new ATM reuses. The old ATM is dropped without an explicit shutdown; at that point it has no open connections.

A cleaner long-term fix is for the TDK to build its ATM with the store at construction. TDK 0.22 can't take one, so I can raise that against affinidi-tdk-rs separately.

## Tests

- New `tsp_store::tests::adopted_tdk_atm_records_into_the_shared_store`. It records an invite through the TDK's ATM: before `adopt_into` the shared store reads `None`, and after it reads `InviteReceived`.
- `cargo test -p openvtc-core --lib tsp_store`: 4 passed. Clippy on `openvtc` and `openvtc-core` is clean, and `cargo fmt --check` is clean.
- **Not yet verified live.** This needs a run on the Farm: a terminal persona on the shared mediator joining a community on its own mediator.
  - With `RUST_LOG=affinidi_messaging_sdk=debug` you should see `recorded an inbound TSP control message ... state=Bidirectional` for the Accept, where you previously saw "not recorded — a protocol rule refused it".
  - The TSP relationships pane should show the `(persona, community)` row.
  - The shared mediator's log at 2026-10-02 15:08:57.5Z (hop sender keyring-test-mediator, persona pledge-champion) should show the frame stored for the persona with no `delivery.refused`. That would confirm the fault was only on the client.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): n/a
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): relationship state now lands in the durable shared store, which is what makes the flow resumable
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): unchanged
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): unchanged
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*): none
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*): a failure to adopt the store logs at `warn`
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): adopt is in-memory only; a restart re-runs it
- [ ] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none, but see the note on the dropped ATM above

title: fix: TSP invites and replies share one relationship store (VTI-61) (#415)
body:
fix: TSP invites and replies share one relationship store (VTI-61) (#415)

TDK::new builds tdk.atm with the SDK's default in-memory RelationshipStore.
Every outbound TSP send (join submit, status poll, vetting, members) runs on
tdk.atm, so the invite was recorded Pending there, while inbound frames are
unsealed by listener ATMs on the shared TspStoreHandle store, which held None.
The community's Accept was refused (ReceiveAccept from None, logged at debug)
and its replies were discarded as 'no relationship with <persona>', so a
persona on another mediator never received its credential or vetter grant.

TspStoreHandle::adopt_into rebuilds tdk.atm on the shared store before the
listeners start.

title: vti-common-v0.36.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: Join criteria state their own admission (Keyring VTI-13) ([#1907](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1907))

A community's join criteria are its join rules, and the VTC now decides a
  submission by them as vtc/join-requests/submit/0.3 specifies
  (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#710, trust-tasks-rs 0.26.1). Nothing in the service
  assumes a criterion: open admission, review only, invitation only and any
  combination are all criteria an administrator registers.

  - Criteria (vtc/schemas/accepts/{register,list,show}/0.2) carry `admission`
    (automatic | review), an optional DCQL query with `credentialIssuers`
    (community | recognised | any), `invitationRequired` and `vetting`.
    `recognised` without a trust registry is `unsupportedRequirement`.
  - The manifest (vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.3) publishes them in the order
    the community decides by — registration order, kept on replacement.
  - A submission is decided under the criterion it names by digest, else the
    first it meets, else the first published. No criteria → `notAccepting`;
    an unpublished digest → `criterionUnknown`. Superseded versions are kept
    and govern while their `requirementsGrace` lasts.
  - The host verifies the presentation's embedded credentials (proof set,
    validity window, revocation, subject = applicant) and matches the query,
    applying DCQL `type_values`, which the matcher alone ignores.
  - The host holds the policy to the criterion: unmet → never admitted or
    referred (requestMore naming what is missing); met review → refer; met
    automatic → the policy's verdict. Policy may tighten, never loosen.
    The default join.rego follows the criterion.
  - A new community is seeded once with `invited` (automatic) →
    `member-credential` (automatic) → `review`.
  - The criterion and version that governed are recorded beside the request;
    a supplement re-decides under it.

title: ci: script the Release PR bump-size fix the guard asks for
body:
`check-release-bump-sizes.py` fails every Release PR that follows a breaking change to `vti-common` or `vta-sdk` (#1910: 20 crates). release-plz patches the dependents; the fix the guard names cascades through them and is lost when release-plz rewrites the PR.

`scripts/fix-release-bump-sizes.py` applies it: raises each named crate to its next breaking version, moves the workspace requirements and the changelog title, refreshes `Cargo.lock`, and repeats until the guard passes. Used to fix #1910 (guard, `check-workspace-version-reqs`, lockfile self-pin guard and `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked` all pass).

## [0.63.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-sdk-v0.62.1...vta-sdk-v0.63.0) — 2026-10-02 ### Added - **vtc**: Join criteria state their own admission (Keyring VTI-13) ([#1907](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1907)) A community's join criteria are its join rules, and the VTC now decides a submission by them as vtc/join-requests/submit/0.3 specifies (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#710, trust-tasks-rs 0.26.1). Nothing in the service assumes a criterion: open admission, review only, invitation only and any combination are all criteria an administrator registers. - Criteria (vtc/schemas/accepts/{register,list,show}/0.2) carry `admission` (automatic | review), an optional DCQL query with `credentialIssuers` (community | recognised | any), `invitationRequired` and `vetting`. `recognised` without a trust registry is `unsupportedRequirement`. - The manifest (vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.3) publishes them in the order the community decides by — registration order, kept on replacement. - A submission is decided under the criterion it names by digest, else the first it meets, else the first published. No criteria → `notAccepting`; an unpublished digest → `criterionUnknown`. Superseded versions are kept and govern while their `requirementsGrace` lasts. - The host verifies the presentation's embedded credentials (proof set, validity window, revocation, subject = applicant) and matches the query, applying DCQL `type_values`, which the matcher alone ignores. - The host holds the policy to the criterion: unmet → never admitted or referred (requestMore naming what is missing); met review → refer; met automatic → the policy's verdict. Policy may tighten, never loosen. The default join.rego follows the criterion. - A new community is seeded once with `invited` (automatic) → `member-credential` (automatic) → `review`. - The criterion and version that governed are recorded beside the request; a supplement re-decides under it.

title: fix(vtc-service): console key rows stored before expiry existed still read
body:
Follow-up to #1908. A `ConsoleKeyDelegation` written before #1836 has no `expiresAt` (it lasted until revoked), so reading it failed with `missing field expiresAt` and console sign-in still answered 500.

A row with no expiry now reads as expiring `MAX_LIFETIME_DAYS` after creation, the most a fresh enrolment gets: a legacy key never outlives the ceiling, and one older than that is expired and its browser re-enrols. Deserialisation goes through a tolerant `StoredDelegation`; serialisation is unchanged. Adds a regression test with a pre-#1836 row.

title: fix(vtc-service): box the join-decision dispatch arms
body:
The Trust Task dispatcher awaits every handler inline, so its future is the size of its largest arm. #1907 (VTI-13) put the whole criterion decision in the join arms, which overflowed a 2 MiB test thread under `--features vetting-pcs` (`git_ns::tests::an_adoption_never_grants_the_resolver_an_elevated_right`, SIGABRT), turning `Test (VTC)` red on main.

Boxes the three join-decision arms (`handle_submit`, `handle_supplement`, `credential_exchange::handle_present`).

The Trust Task dispatcher awaits every handler inside one match, so its

title: fix: leave over TSP, answered manifest refreshes, and say what a join lacks
body:
Three follow-ups to #412 (join-requests 0.3) and #413 (member verbs over TSP).

## Leave over TSP

#413 moved the acknowledgement, renewal and personhood verbs onto the join's transport but left Leave on DIDComm. A persona that joined over TSP may have no DIDComm route, so its leave never arrived and the community kept a member who had gone.

`join::submit_self_remove` now takes `members::Delivery` and sends through `members::send_document`. The Leave `CommunityJob` sets `over_tsp` from `CommunityRecord::joined_over_tsp`.

## Manifest refreshes are answered

Three paths sent a manifest request without filing a `CommunityQuery`:
- the requirements refresh
- the vetter's session
- the standing refresh

A refusal threaded on an unfiled request matched nothing in `refusal_of` and was dropped. That also meant #412's 0.2 fallback never ran from these paths.

`vetting_actions::sign_and_send` now files a Manifest question for every `Sent::Manifest`, so a future send can't forget to. A manifest answer with no join waiting is ignored, as before. A refusal now reaches the vetting page's status line.

## What a join lacks

A `requestMore` verdict's `needs` (`credentials`, `invitation`, `vetting:*`, `vetting:consistency`, `vetting:independence`) were only traced. Now:
- `messaging::join_verdict_needs` reads them.
- `messaging::describe_join_needs` puts them in the member's words.
- The dispatcher writes "Community (…) has not decided your join yet: it still needs an invitation." to the Community log.

An unknown need is shown as the community sent it, not dropped.

## Testing

- `a_request_more_says_what_the_join_lacks` covers the wording, including an unknown need and the empty case.
- `only_a_request_more_verdict_has_needs`.
- Leave uses the same `members::send_document` path that #413 covers. Filing the query is a single unconditional `ask` per manifest send.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` passes, and so does `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes, with and without default features. `cargo test --workspace` passes, with and without default features (1763 passed each).

title: fix: a membership joined over TSP is spoken to over TSP afterwards
body:
The reciprocal VMC (`members/vmc`), renewal (`R`), and the personhood challenge and assertion all went over DIDComm, whatever transport the join used. A persona that joined over TSP may have no DIDComm route the community can reach.
- Its acknowledgement never arrived, so the community couldn't tell a delivered credential from a lost one: `credentialsDelivered` stayed false (#411).
- The community kept re-sending until both sides' limits ran out (5 on the VTC, 6 per run on the client).

## Change

- `members::Delivery` gains `tsp_mediator_did`. A shared `members::send_document` sends over TSP when it's set (`tsp::send_trust_task`, the same path the join submit and status poll use), and over the DIDComm Trust Task envelope otherwise. `submit_member_vmc` and `request_renewal` both use it.
- `CommunityRecord::joined_over_tsp` reads the join's recorded transport.
  - The join-time acknowledgement (`issue_member_vmc_for`) resolves the community's advertised TSP mediator fresh when it's true, as the join poll does.
  - So does `CommunityJob` (the `m`, `R` and personhood verbs). The personhood route already took a TSP mediator; it was hard-wired to `None`.
- Leaving (`submit_self_remove`) still goes over DIDComm.

No service change is needed: the VTC already dispatches `members/vmc` on its TSP spine and identifies the member by the TSP sender VID.

## Testing

- `a_join_submitted_over_tsp_is_spoken_to_over_tsp`. The send itself is the existing `tsp::send_trust_task`.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass, with and without default features. `cargo test --workspace` passes (1753 passed).

It conflicts with #412 (join-requests 0.3) only on the CHANGELOG; whichever lands second rebases.

`vetting::protocol` carried an outer doc comment on its `pub mod` line in

title: feat: join speaks join-requests 0.3, falling back to 0.2
body:
**Ship before any live VTC is redeployed from VTI main.** OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1907 (Keyring VTI-13, merged) makes a VTC serve only `manifest/0.3` + `submit/0.3`. Released OpenVTC speaks only 0.2, so it cannot join such a VTC, and a community that hasn't moved still speaks only 0.2. This speaks both.

It's built on trust-tasks-rs 0.26.2's generated 0.3 types, so it needs no vta-sdk or VGI release.

## Behaviour

- **Version negotiation.** OpenVTC asks for `manifest/0.3` first. If the community refuses the version, it asks again in 0.2 and submits in whichever version the community answered in.
  - A VTC answers `unsupportedVersion` for a task family it serves at another version, which is what a 0.2 community says to 0.3 (and a VTI-13 one to 0.2, confirmed against #1907). `unsupportedType` also triggers the fallback. Keying on `unsupportedType` alone would never fall back against a live 0.2 VTC.
  - **REST:** `fetch_manifest` keeps the error code (`refusal_detail` now returns it), and a `trust-task-error` that arrives under a 2xx status is still treated as a refusal.
  - **DIDComm:** `refusal_of` re-asks a refused manifest question in 0.2 as a reply, so whoever is waiting keeps waiting instead of seeing a refusal.
  - **Remembered:** `KnownCommunity::protocol` stores the version from the manifest, or `protocol_hints` from the refusal. `VettingBook::protocol_for` reads it, and every manifest send uses it.
- **Manifest.** `vetting::protocol::read_manifest` checks a 0.3 manifest against its own generated type, then carries it into the 0.2 shape the rest of the client reads. Each criterion's `admission` and `invitationRequired` are kept, and `KnownCommunity::routes` now holds every criterion, not only the vetting ones. An admission value it doesn't recognise reads as `review`.
- **Submit.** A 0.3 submit names `criterion`: the vetting application's `requirementsDigest`. Otherwise it omits it, so the community decides under the first criterion met in published order, which with VTI-13's defaults (invited → member-credential → review) is the route the person chose. `extensions.requirementsDigest` is sent only in 0.2; `hiddenVetting` stays in `extensions`, where #1907 still reads it.
- **Replies.** Both submit response types are treated as verdicts. `submit:notAccepting` and `submit:criterionUnknown` are non-retryable and leave no request open, so they end the join with a reason rather than leaving it Pending.
- **Wording.** A `review` criterion is never described as admitting. The invitation row says it goes to administrators, and the vetting row says an administrator decides. The vetting page and the `--invitation` help are neutral. A 0.2 community says nothing about admission, so its wording is unchanged.

## Testing

- **Protocol** (`vetting::protocol`): a 0.3 manifest reads into the 0.2 shape with its admission; a malformed 0.3 manifest is refused; the type URIs and fallback are correct; both refusal codes trigger it.
- **Manifest handling** (`vetting::tests`):
  - `a_v0_3_manifest_is_learned_with_its_version_and_admission`
  - `a_manifest_refused_as_an_unsupported_version_is_asked_again_in_0_2`: a 0.2 refusal after that is reported as a refusal.
- **Submit** (`join::tests::a_v0_3_submit_names_its_criterion`): the 0.3 payload parses as the generated `submit::v0_3::Payload`, and the 0.2 one as `v0_2`, without `criterion`.
- **Refusals** (`messaging::tests::a_v0_3_submit_refusal_ends_the_join_with_a_reason`).
- **Wording** (`join_flow::a_review_criterion_is_never_worded_as_admitting`).
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass, with and without default features. `cargo test --workspace` passes, with and without default features (1760 passed each).

**Not run end to end against a live 0.3 VTC.** A local check is possible: `cargo run -p vtc-service` from #1907 should refer a submit that names nothing, and answer `requestMore` / `invitation` to one that names `invited` without a VIC.

feat: join speaks join-requests 0.3, falling back to 0.2 (#412)

A community on Keyring VTI-13 (VTI #1907) serves only `manifest/0.3` +
`submit/0.3`, and one that has not moved serves only 0.2, so a client
speaking one version cannot join communities on the other. This speaks both,
on trust-tasks-rs 0.26.2's generated 0.3 types, so it does not wait for a
vta-sdk carrying VTI-13.

- `vetting::protocol`: `JoinProtocol { V0_3, V0_2 }` with each version's type
  URIs. `read_manifest` checks a 0.3 manifest against its own generated type,
  then carries it into the 0.2 shape the book, the applicant and the
  attribute questions read. Each criterion's `admission` and
  `invitationRequired` are kept as `CriterionMeta`; an unknown admission reads
  as `review`.
- Fallback: asked in 0.3 first. A refusal coded `unsupportedVersion` (what a
  VTC answers for a task it serves at another version, as a 0.2 community
  does) or `unsupportedType` is asked again in 0.2.
  - REST: `fetch_manifest` keeps the error code (`refusal_detail` returns
    it), and treats a `trust-task-error` arriving under a 2xx as a refusal.
  - DIDComm: `refusal_of` re-asks a refused manifest question in 0.2 as a
    reply, without answering whoever waits.
  - The version is remembered: `KnownCommunity::protocol` from the manifest,
    else `protocol_hints` from the refusal. `VettingBook::protocol_for`
    reads it, and every manifest send uses it.
- Book: `KnownCommunity::routes` keeps every criterion (id, digest,
  admission, invitation, vetting), not only the vetting ones.
- Submit: `JoinPresentation` carries the protocol and `criterion`. 0.3 sends
  the vetting application's `requirementsDigest` as `criterion`, or omits it
  so the community decides under the first criterion met.
  `join_extensions(protocol)` carries the digest only for 0.2.
- Replies: both submit response types are verdicts. `submit:notAccepting` and
  `submit:criterionUnknown` (non-retryable, no request left open) end the
  join with a reason.
- Wording: a `review` criterion is never described as admitting: the
  invitation and vetting rows, the vetting page and the `--invitation` help.

Verified against VTI-13's VTC source (#1907): manifest dispatch,
`unsupportedVersion` for a served family, `hiddenVetting` still read from
`extensions`, and `criterion` as the governing digest. Not run end to end
against a live 0.3 VTC.

title: feat(vtc)!: join criteria state their own admission (Keyring VTI-13) (#1907)
body:
feat(vtc)!: join criteria state their own admission (Keyring VTI-13) (#1907)

A community's join criteria are its join rules, and the VTC now decides a
submission by them as vtc/join-requests/submit/0.3 specifies
(dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#710, trust-tasks-rs 0.26.1). Nothing in the service
assumes a criterion: open admission, review only, invitation only and any
combination are all criteria an administrator registers.

- Criteria (vtc/schemas/accepts/{register,list,show}/0.2) carry `admission`
  (automatic | review), an optional DCQL query with `credentialIssuers`
  (community | recognised | any), `invitationRequired` and `vetting`.
  `recognised` without a trust registry is `unsupportedRequirement`.
- The manifest (vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.3) publishes them in the order
  the community decides by — registration order, kept on replacement.
- A submission is decided under the criterion it names by digest, else the
  first it meets, else the first published. No criteria → `notAccepting`;
  an unpublished digest → `criterionUnknown`. Superseded versions are kept
  and govern while their `requirementsGrace` lasts.
- The host verifies the presentation's embedded credentials (proof set,
  validity window, revocation, subject = applicant) and matches the query,
  applying DCQL `type_values`, which the matcher alone ignores.
- The host holds the policy to the criterion: unmet → never admitted or
  referred (requestMore naming what is missing); met review → refer; met
  automatic → the policy's verdict. Policy may tighten, never loosen.
  The default join.rego follows the criterion.
- A new community is seeded once with `invited` (automatic) →
  `member-credential` (automatic) → `review`.
- The criterion and version that governed are recorded beside the request;
  a supplement re-decides under it.

BREAKING: only accepts register/list/show 0.2, manifest 0.3 and submit 0.3
are served; 0.1/0.2 join versions answer unsupportedVersion. vta-sdk:
JOIN_REQUEST_MANIFEST_0_2_TYPE removed, the manifest/submit constants name
0.3, JoinRequestSubmitBody gains `criterion`. vti-common: SchemaChangeData
gains `admission`.

title: fix(vti-common): retry a rate-limited TSP reply with backoff
body:
## Field report

A VTC setup against a VTA failed with `timed out waiting for the TSP reply`. The VTA log shows the VTA did all the work for `provision/integration/0.3`: it minted and published the DID, exported the keys, handed off the ACL entry and sealed the bundle. Then it logged:

```
failed to send TSP reply … HTTP 429 … mediator-test.ic3.dev/mediator/v1/inbound, body(error code: 1015)
```

That 429 came from Cloudflare in front of the mediator. The VTA logged the failure and dropped the reply. `provision/integration/0.3` is classed `KeyedSecret`, so a retry of the request is answered "already performed" and never with the bundle. The reply was the only copy of the VTC's keys, and the operator was left with a half-provisioned integration.

## Change

- `vti_common::tsp_route::send_reply` (used by both the VTA and the VTC) now re-sends a reply that got a 429:
  - It waits at least `Retry-After`, plus up to 1s of jitter.
  - With no `Retry-After`, it waits a random time within a ceiling that starts at 1s and doubles up to 8s.
  - It keeps trying for at most 20s. If the next wait would end outside that window, it stops and returns the 429.
- Any other failure is returned immediately, as before.
- `vta_sdk::budget::TSP_REPLY_RATE_LIMIT_RETRY_SECS = 20` is the single definition of the window. It is added to `relay_worst_case_secs` because the VTA spends it after the work is done, while the client is waiting. The client floor for relaying tasks rises from 80s to 100s.

## Not in scope

- A limit lasting longer than 20s still loses the reply.
- Making secret-bearing replies recoverable after a lost reply would be a separate change: an outbox entry, or resumable provisioning.

## Tests

Six new unit tests in `tsp_route`:
- a reply that gets a 429 is sent again
- any other failure is returned without a retry
- a limit that never lifts stops inside the window
- a `Retry-After` longer than the window is not attempted
- `Retry-After` is treated as a floor
- the backoff ceiling doubles up to its cap

Run locally:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 5298 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 2514 passed, 0 failed

title: fix(vti-common): retry a rate-limited TSP reply with backoff (#1906)
body:
fix(vti-common): retry a rate-limited TSP reply with backoff (#1906)

A VTA that completed `provision/integration/0.3` lost its reply when the
mediator's edge (Cloudflare 1015) answered the reply post with a 429. The
reply was logged and dropped. Because the task is `KeyedSecret`, a retry of
the request is answered "already performed", never with the sealed bundle,
so the VTC setup timed out with its DID minted and its setup key's ACL entry
already handed off.

`tsp_route::send_reply` (VTA and VTC) now re-sends a rate-limited reply:
`Retry-After` as a floor plus jitter, otherwise full-jitter exponential
backoff (1s up to 8s), within a 20s window. It gives up rather than send
before a `Retry-After` that falls outside the window. Any other failure is
returned at once, as before.

The window is `vta_sdk::budget::TSP_REPLY_RATE_LIMIT_RETRY_SECS` and is added
to `relay_worst_case_secs`, because it is spent after the work on the caller's
clock. The relaying-task client floor rises from 80s to 100s.

title: feat: an approved join asks its community to re-send a credential that never came
body:
This is the client half of credential re-delivery on `join-requests/status/0.1` (spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#709; community side: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1900). A join the community approved but whose membership credential was lost in delivery now asks for it again, without the member doing anything. `R` (#406) stays as the manual rescue.

## Dependencies

| Pin | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| vta-sdk | 0.61 | 0.62 (the status types carry the new members) |
| did-git-sign | 0.10.0 | 0.11.0 (VGI 0.11.0, on vta-sdk ^0.62) |
| vta-service (dev) | 0.50 | 0.51 |

`cargo tree -d` shows one copy of every affinidi / trust-tasks / vta / vti / dtg / did crate.

## Behaviour

- **Recorded:** an approved reply's `credentialsDelivered`, and the community's answer to `resendCredentials` (`queued`, `rateLimited` + `retryAfter`, `notNeeded`), are stored on the membership as `CommunityRecord::credential_delivery`. Serde-defaulted, so existing configs load unchanged.
- **When the poll carries the flag** (`wants_credential_resend`):
  - the join is approved, with no Membership credential yet, 10 min after approval;
  - and **only once the community has itself reported `credentialsDelivered: false`**. A community that predates the member has `additionalProperties: false` on the request schema and would refuse the poll as malformed. That would stop the poll answering at all, so the report is what proves support.
- **Paced by the community:**
  - `retryAfter` is waited out;
  - a `queued` re-send is given 10 min to land;
  - `notNeeded`, or `rateLimited` with no `retryAfter` (limit spent), ends the asking.
- **Bounded (R1.4):** the poll pacer carries the flag at most 6 times per record per process, so a community whose replies never return isn't asked forever. The poll itself is already backed off (1 min doubling to 15 min).
- **Absence isn't read as refusal:** a reply with no `credentialResend` keeps the last answer. The reply handler can't know whether that particular poll carried the flag, because the decision was taken at send time against a clock that has since moved on.
- **UI:** the approved row reads "✓ approved — membership credential not received yet; <what the community said>." and keeps "Press R to have the community re-issue it."

Also fixes a doc comment #406 left on the wrong function (`mark_approved` had taken `pending_unacknowledged`'s).

## Testing

- `credential_resend_is_asked_only_when_the_community_offers_it` covers the full decision matrix, and that the decision reaches `pollable_pending`.
- `status_response_approved_records_credential_delivery` covers the older-community no-op, delivery reporting, `rateLimited` + `retryAfter`, a plain reply keeping the answer, and `queued`.
- `resend_asks_are_capped_per_record` checks the pacer carries the flag exactly 6 times.
- `the_credential_resend_note_says_what_the_community_said` covers the row wording.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass, with and without default features. `cargo test --workspace` passes with and without default features (1752 passed each).

title: fix(vtc-service): an idle console's session ends cleanly
body:
A console left idle past its access token showed **"Sign-out failed: unauthorized: missing or invalid Authorization header (401)"** when the operator clicked Sign out (reported from a 0.11.58 deployment; unchanged on main).

**Cause.** The session cookie's `Max-Age` is the access token's lifetime (300 s at aal2), so the browser had already dropped it. The console's pre-flight renewal was refused for idleness, and `sign_out` required `AuthClaims`, so it answered 401. The result: a failure reported for the outcome the operator wanted, and the HttpOnly refresh cookie left in the jar, because the clearing `Set-Cookie` headers ride only on the 204. Not a security issue: the daemon refuses that refresh token anyway.

**Server** (`routes/auth.rs`)
- `POST /v1/auth/sign-out` answers 204 and clears all three cookies whether or not a live session is presented.
- The session to revoke comes from the access token, or failing that the refresh cookie when it is the token its session currently issues (same currency check as `/auth/refresh`). A superseded token cannot end the session that replaced it.
- A SignedOut audit envelope is written only when a session actually ended.
- The route moves to the unauthenticated, rate-limited chain, since it now answers callers with no session. CSRF still applies.

**Console** (`admin-ui/src/lib/api.ts`)
- `signOut` bypasses `request`: no renewal (it would rotate the refresh token of a session about to end) and no `vtc-session-expired` toast over a requested sign-out.
- A 401 from an older daemon counts as already signed out.

**Idle console shows Login on its own** (`lib/session.ts`, `App.tsx`)
- Why the console went unnoticed: renewal only ran before cookie-carrying requests, and an idle dashboard sends almost none (`/health` needs no sign-in; signed reads authenticate by their proof). The cookie lapsed, and the console kept looking signed in until the next click failed.
- `watchSessionDeadline` wakes ahead of the known expiry and renews, as a request would. A renewal is not activity, so once the daemon's idle timeout passes it refuses. The expiry stays put, and the wake just after it raises `vtc-session-expired`. The existing handler re-probes `whoami` and shows Login with "Your session expired". The daemon still decides when the session ends.
- The watch re-arms on each `whoami` payload, so a session another tab renewed keeps being watched.

**Tests**
- New Rust tests: the session cookie has lapsed and only the refresh cookie remains (204, session revoked, cookies cleared); no credentials; a superseded refresh cookie; CSRF still enforced.
- New vitest: `signOut`, and the deadline watch (renews ahead of the deadline, reports once when renewal is refused, renews at once if started inside the window, nothing after cancel).
- `a_second_sign_out_is_rejected…` becomes `…succeeds_but_is_not_audited_twice`.
- `openapi.json` and `wire.ts` regenerated.
- Local: `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast` (865 + 1619 pass), clippy `-D warnings`, fmt, `npm run lint`, `npm test` (520 pass).

title: docs(vtc): console-signing design note describes what was built
body:
`docs/05-design-notes/vtc-console-signing.md` still said that a browser with no enrolled key, or with no WebCrypto Ed25519, keeps using the bearer routes. Those routes were removed in #1808.

This adds a status line at the top and two **Superseded** callouts in the note's existing style:
- **§6c** describes `enroll/0.2`: the identity's own signature as an alternative to the passkey step-up (VTA wallet sign-in), `replaces` at the cap, and a fresh key minted for every enrolment.
- **§6e** says signing is required and is gated at sign-in (#1899). It also gives the as-built expiry, storage and revocation behaviour, including that a backup restore drops every delegation.

The original design text is kept as the record. Docs only.

title: feat(vtc-service): serve auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2 — wallet-authorized enrolment and key replacement
body:
Follows #1899. Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#712 (`trust-tasks-rs` 0.26.2), served alongside `enroll/0.1`.

## Why
- **VTA-wallet sign-in had no way to enrol a console key.** Enrolment only accepted a passkey step-up, and a wallet-signed-in administrator usually has no passkey at the VTC. Every admin verb is signed, so the console was unusable for the most common sign-in method.
- **The 5-key cap was a dead end.** Lost browsers keep their delegations live until expiry. At the cap, an operator with no working key could neither list nor revoke them, so could not enrol.

## Server (`trust_tasks::signing_key_tasks`)
- **`authorization`** (0.2 item 13): an embedded `auth/signing-key/authorize/0.1` signed by `identityDid` is the authority evidence in place of the step-up. It is verified **as received** (VTI-45):
  - its own proof, made by the identity;
  - `issuer == identityDid`;
  - `recipient` is this VTC;
  - its acceptance window;
  - its payload is RFC 8785-equal to the enrolment's payload minus `authorization`;
  - it is not signed by a delegated key;
  - its `id` is claimed in `accepted_ids` when the delegation is written.

  Any failure is `authorizationInvalid`; there is no fallback to the step-up. Standing is still checked.
- **`replaces`** (item 14): an active delegation of the same identity, revoked in the same critical section as the enrolment and audited as the identity's revocation. Every other case answers `replaceNotFound`, and the check runs only after the evidence is accepted.
- **Cap** (item 8): decided after evidence and standing, counting a replaced key as gone. 0.2 lists `details.activeKeys` (least recently used first, at most 16), never before the evidence is accepted. 0.1's details are unchanged.

## Console
- A wallet sign-in (session `amr` has no `passkey`) defaults to **"Set up signing with your wallet"**: one approval. The VTA signs the terms as the persona via `signTrustTask({ asDid })`, and the console checks the proof names that persona. The operator can switch to a passkey.
- At the cap, setup lists the active keys with the least recently used preselected; **Replace it and set up signing** takes one more approval.
- Renewal follows the sign-in method.
- Wallet side: the silent holder-key fallback for an unknown `asDid` is fixed in OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#289 (merged).

## Tests
- `tests/it/signed_step_up.rs` adds 5 end-to-end cases: wallet-authorized enrol with no gesture; mismatched terms, wrong signer and bad proof all refused; at the cap, the key list followed by a replace; no list before the evidence; `replaceNotFound` for another identity's key and for an unknown key. 30/30 pass.
- `trust_task_manifest`: the console now sends `enroll/0.2`; `authorize/0.1` gets a new embedded-only category, asserted as served by nothing.
- Also passing: trust-task lib tests (234 incl. censuses), admin-ui vitest 517, `tsc`, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt.
- The full `vtc-service` integration run was not completed locally (90-minute limit); CI covers it.
- `Cargo.lock` is cargo's own output for the `trust-tasks-rs` floor bump. It also normalises three unrelated edges (syn/base64), and `--locked` passes.

title: Rotation under the identifier commitment profile: record 025, WG-17
body:
Following the chair's question on the admission proof and DIDs (task-force discussion, 2 October): how proofs rooted in a holder secret meet DIDs, which carry several identifiers and key rotation over time.

**Integration — Rotation under the identifier commitment profile.** The identifier's signing keys, the commitment to the holder secret (the verification method of WG-14) and the secret itself are kept apart:

- signing-key rotation: the commitment carries forward; nothing is re-proven
- commitment refresh: shown continuous by record 007's relation across the two DID document versions
- secret rotation: pre-rotation — the DID method's for a public identifier (`did:webvh` `nextKeyHashes`, KERI), the enrolment leaf's for a hidden enrolment (record 025)

An enrolment is bound to a DID once, at enrolment; no DID is resolved inside a circuit or at presentation. The privacy of the arrangement is read across the DID log, the enrolment root and the presentations together: resolution at enrolment only, one binding per community, a DID-bound rotation is visible, rotations batched.

**Records.** New composed record **025** — secret rotation with enrolment continuity (components 001, 002, 003, 006), `specified`, unmeasured. Record 007's horizon split by key profile. Record 024 gains an issuance line for DID-rooted enrolment.

**WG-17** (proposed for discussion): which identifier an enrolment binds to (`did:peer` does not rotate; `did:webvh` rotates through a public log), pre-rotation digests in enrolment leaves, the rotation batch size, and per-context nullifiers across a secret rotation.

Appendix D and E updated; Appendix B pins evidence commit `f540790`. `validate` 24/24, conformance tests pass, render clean. No state promoted; nothing adopted.

title: fix(deps): take affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.32.1 — inbound messages are no longer dropped
body:
Requested by the affinidi-tdk-rs session (affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#921).

**The bug:** `live_stream_next` waited up to `wait`, then dropped its receiver and sent `CancelNext`. A DIDComm message arriving in that gap went to the dead waiter (`let _ = sender.send(..)`) and was discarded. The mediator had already delivered it, and it was never cached. A `live_stream_get` that gave up early lost its reply the same way. Measured loss was 3–5% of single messages under a 500 ms poll loop (6/200 before the fix, 0/200 after).

**Change:** `Cargo.lock` moves 0.32.0 → 0.32.1, and the workspace floor is raised to `0.32.1` so a published consumer cannot resolve the lossy release. There is no API change.

**Behaviour:** messages that used to vanish now arrive. A caller that compensated with blind resends may also see the original; de-dup by message id covers that.

**Local checks:** `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast` passed 5292, failed 0. The VTC/vtc-client run did not finish locally: it hit the 90-minute background limit while sharing the machine with another VTC run. CI's `Test (VTC)` job covers it. `cargo metadata --locked` passes.

title: fix(extension): signTrustTask as asDid refuses instead of signing with the holder key
body:
`window.vtaWallet.signTrustTask({ envelope, asDid })` asks for a document signed **as** a persona, whose key the VTA holds. In two cases `doSignTrustTask` signed with the **holder key** instead, logging only a `console.warn` in the offscreen document:

1. `asDid` matched no `didSelfIssued` / `didcommPeer` vault entry;
2. no REST base was known for the VTA. This one was silent: the `asDid` branch was skipped entirely.

The page received a document whose `issuer` names one identity and whose proof is by another. The relying party then refuses it with an issuer/signer mismatch that tells the user nothing.

## Change
- Both cases now **refuse before signing**, with the stable code `sign-trust-task/as-did-unavailable` (R3.7) and a message naming the DID.
- `asDid` equal to the holder's own DID still signs with the holder key.
- The decision moved into `src/sign-identity.ts` (no `chrome.*`), so it is unit-tested; `offscreen.ts` calls it, and its `asDid` branch can now only end in a VTA signature or a refusal.

## Why now
The VTC admin console now enrols its browser signing key with the identity's own signature through this method (`auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2` + `authorize/0.1`, trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#712). The console already checks the returned proof's verification method against `asDid`, but the wallet should not produce the mismatched document in the first place.

## Tests
`npm run lint` clean; extension `npm test`: 874 passed (4 new in `tests/sign-identity.test.mts`).

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.26.2
body:
### Added

- **auth/signing-key**: Enroll 0.2 — the identity's own authorization, and key replacement ([#712](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/712))

auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2 adds two optional members to 0.1:

  - authorization: a complete auth/signing-key/authorize/0.1 document (new),
    issued and signed by identityDid, addressed to the consumer, whose payload
    is the enrolment's payload with authorization removed. A valid one is the
    authority evidence of control over identityDid in place of an
    operation-bound step-up. For a holder who signs in with a key its agent
    holds (a VTA wallet persona) and has no passkey at the consumer, it is the
    only evidence available, and it is the stronger of the two.
  - replaces: an active delegation of the same identity revoked in the same
    critical section as the enrolment. At the consumer's cap a holder whose
    other keys live on browsers it no longer has could neither list nor revoke
    them — both need a working key — and so could not enrol at all.

  tooManyKeys gains details.activeKeys, listed only once the enrolment's
  authority evidence has been accepted. New codes: authorizationInvalid,
  replaceNotFound (one answer for every reason). The cap is decided after the
  evidence and standing, counting a replaced key as gone. Producers SHOULD mint
  a new key per enrolment: an expired delegation still answers
  alreadyEnrolled.

  authorization is an open object in the enroll schema on purpose: its proof
  covers every member, so a binding must not narrow it to a typed struct that
  drops one before verification.

title: feat(auth/signing-key): enroll 0.2 — the identity's own authorization, and key replacement
body:
Two gaps in `auth/signing-key/enroll/0.1`, both found running the VTC admin console against real operators.

## 1. Holders who sign in with their identity's key cannot enrol

0.1's reference evidence is an operation-bound passkey step-up. An administrator who signs in through a VTA wallet (the key is held by their agent and signs a per-site persona DID) usually has **no passkey at the consumer**, so cannot enrol a console key at all, and the console signs every administrator verb. 0.1 already says a consumer *MAY* accept "a proof by `identityDid`'s own key over the same payload, delivered in `ext`". This PR makes that a first-class, interoperable shape:

- **New `auth/signing-key/authorize/0.1`**: a document issued and signed by `identityDid`, addressed to the consumer, whose payload is the enrolment's terms. It is never sent alone. Consumer rules: verify it as a document in its own right (proof, issuer binding, recipient, acceptance window, `id` replay), require `issuer == identityDid`, and require its payload to be **RFC 8785-equal** to the enrolment's payload with `authorization` removed.
- **`enroll/0.2` `authorization`** carries that document. A valid one *replaces* the step-up (Conformance item 13), and standing is still checked before writing. It is the stronger evidence: a signature by a key the identity's own DID document lists, verifiable by anyone, versus possession of an authenticator registered at this consumer.
- The wallet already exposes "sign this Trust Task as persona X for the RP this origin signed in to" (`window.vtaWallet.signTrustTask({ asDid })`, signed by the VTA), so this needs no new wallet primitive.

## 2. The active-key cap is a dead end

A delegation outlives the browser that holds it (cleared site data, Safari's 7-day storage cap, a new machine). Every lost browser leaves its delegation live until expiry. At the cap, a holder with no working key cannot list or revoke the others (both need a working key), so cannot enrol either.

- **`replaces`**: an active key of the same identity, revoked in the same critical section as the enrolment, under the same authority evidence. Item 14 covers this, with one `replaceNotFound` answer for every reason.
- **`tooManyKeys` `details.activeKeys`** (bounded at 16 items) lets the holder choose which key to replace. It is listed **only after** the authority evidence has been accepted (item 8); before that, the requester has shown only that it can mint a key and type a DID.
- Item 15: re-sending with `replaces` is a new payload, so it needs fresh evidence.

## Other
- Producer item 5: mint a new key per enrolment, because an *expired* delegation still answers `alreadyEnrolled` (this bit the reference console at day 30).
- `authorization` is an **open object** in the enroll schema on purpose. Its proof covers every member, and a typed struct would drop unknown members (`expiresAt`, `threadId`, `ext`) before verification. The generated Rust type is `serde_json::Map`.
- 0.1 is untouched; 0.2 is a new folder so consumers can serve both.

## Checks
`npm run build` clean (no new warnings). All four bindings regenerated; `npm run check-bindings` reports all agree. Local `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs` is still running; CI covers it.

Consumer implementation (VTC) and console/wallet wiring follow in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure once this lands and `trust-tasks-rs` publishes.

feat(auth/signing-key): enroll 0.2 — the identity's own authorization, and key replacement (#712)

auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2 adds two optional members to 0.1:

- authorization: a complete auth/signing-key/authorize/0.1 document (new),
  issued and signed by identityDid, addressed to the consumer, whose payload
  is the enrolment's payload with authorization removed. A valid one is the
  authority evidence of control over identityDid in place of an
  operation-bound step-up. For a holder who signs in with a key its agent
  holds (a VTA wallet persona) and has no passkey at the consumer, it is the
  only evidence available, and it is the stronger of the two.
- replaces: an active delegation of the same identity revoked in the same
  critical section as the enrolment. At the consumer's cap a holder whose
  other keys live on browsers it no longer has could neither list nor revoke
  them — both need a working key — and so could not enrol at all.

tooManyKeys gains details.activeKeys, listed only once the enrolment's
authority evidence has been accepted. New codes: authorizationInvalid,
replaceNotFound (one answer for every reason). The cap is decided after the
evidence and standing, counting a replaced key as gone. Producers SHOULD mint
a new key per enrolment: an expired delegation still answers
alreadyEnrolled.

authorization is an open object in the enroll schema on purpose: its proof
covers every member, so a binding must not narrow it to a typed struct that
drops one before verification.

title: feat(vtc): an approved applicant can ask for its credentials again (tf#709)
body:
A join can be approved while its credentials are lost in delivery. The persona is on the member list, but its client stays Pending, and nothing re-sends a push that failed. [trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#709](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/709), released in trust-tasks-rs 0.26.1, lets the applicant ask for the credentials again on `join-requests/status/0.1`. This PR is the community's answer.

Field case: an OpenVTC persona was approved by the cpunks VTC but never received its membership credential. #1894 fixed the reply routing that hid the approval. This closes the delivery gap that would have kept it Pending anyway.

## vta-sdk

- `JoinRequestStatusBody.resend_credentials` (omitted when false).
- `JoinRequestStatusResponseBody.{credentials_delivered, credential_resend, retry_after}`.
- `CredentialResend { Queued, NotNeeded, RateLimited }`.

**Semver:** these pub structs gain fields, so expect a minor bump.

## vtc-service (`routes/join_requests/status.rs`)

- **`credentialsDelivered`** on an approved request means the member's `members/vmc` acknowledgement is held. A push outcome of "collected" only proves the mediator handed it over, not that the wallet accepted it.
- **Re-send, never re-issue.** `resendCredentials` re-pushes the bodies stored on the member (`current_vmc`, `current_role_vac`) through `deliver_credentials`, the same durable push admission used. Re-issuing, which is what `renew` does, would mint a second VMC, clear the acknowledgement and leave two unrevoked credentials on one status slot.
- Only the request's applicant is sent anything.
- The push runs detached with a 30s enqueue timeout, so the poll reply doesn't wait on it.
- **Rate limit (R1.4):** per request, 10 min doubling to 6 h, at most 5. Past the cap the answer is `rateLimited` with no `retryAfter`, plus an operator `warn!`. This matters because a TSP-joined persona's acknowledgement goes back over DIDComm only, so it can look undelivered forever.
- Each honoured ask is recorded before the push, so a burst of polls can't queue several pushes.
- **Bookkeeping:** the count lives in a `join_resend:<id>` row beside the request, deleted with it by `delete_join_request`. The canonical `JoinRequest` component is unchanged.
- **The id-less poll** now falls back to the applicant's latest approved request. Previously it only found Pending or Deferred ones, so an applicant whose every reply was lost got `notFound` after approval.
- A member without stored bodies gets no `credentialResend`, which the spec reads as "not supported", and a `warn!` is logged.

trust-tasks-rs's floor moves to 0.26.1, because 0.26.0's generated schema refuses `resendCredentials`.

## Testing

- `the_rate_limit_backs_off_and_stops` covers the backoff arithmetic and the cap.
- `an_approved_applicant_can_ask_for_its_credentials_again`: reports delivery, queues, rate-limits the next ask, and the id-less poll finds the approved request.
- `an_acknowledged_delivery_needs_no_resend` and `a_pending_request_carries_no_delivery_members`.
- Conformance: the status/0.1 witness sends `resendCredentials: true`, and `status_credential_delivery_speaks_its_published_schema` validates all three `credentialResend` values against the generated `Response`.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy -p vta-sdk -p vtc-service --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` pass. `cargo test -p vta-sdk --all-features` passes (1250) and `cargo test -p vtc-service --all-features` passes (2506). Full workspace suite left to CI.

## Follow-ups

- **OpenVTC client:** send the flag after a grace period, and show the answer on the approved row. This follows the vta-sdk release.
- Separately, OpenVTC's `members/vmc` acknowledgement is DIDComm-only, a gap for TSP-joined personas.

title: fix(vtc-service): the console sets up signing before it shows the dashboard
body:
An administrator whose browser held no key the VTC accepted (new browser, expired or revoked delegation, cleared site data, or a restore — `console_keys` is excluded from backup by design) was shown the whole console. Every screen then sent documents signed by that unknown key; `routing::trust_task_admission` charges those to the per-address anonymous budget (burst 10, then one per 5 s), so a few clicks exhausted it and the enrolment that would have fixed things answered **429**. Reported as "lost my signing keys and can't create new ones".

## Changes (admin-ui + operator docs only; no server change)

- **Setup gate.** After sign-in, an administrator's browser is checked once with `auth/signing-key/list/0.1`. Without an accepted key the operator gets **Set up signing** (name the browser, one passkey confirmation) instead of the console, so nothing signs with an unknown key. States: no key / no longer accepted / belongs to another admin / browser can't sign. A failed *check* (network, 5xx, rate limit, storage) offers retry, never re-enrolment. A signed document refused with `permissionDenied` triggers a re-check, so a key revoked elsewhere lands back on the gate instead of failing screen by screen. `/step-up` stays reachable.
- **Always a fresh key.** `key_refusal` answers `alreadyEnrolled` for an *expired* delegation, and the console reused the held key — so every browser became unrecoverable 30 days after enrolment. Enrolment now mints a key, stores it only after the VTC accepts it (a cancelled ceremony leaves the old key in place), then revokes the key it replaced. Renewal banner 5 days before expiry; "Renew this browser's key" on Signing keys.
- **Durable storage, no silent fallback.** A refused IndexedDB write used to fall back to memory (key gone on reload, delegation left live); a read failure was treated as "no key" and the next enrolment overwrote it. Now: write errors throw, the write is read back, `navigator.storage.persist()` is requested, read errors are distinguished from absence.
- **429 handling** on `/v1/trust-tasks`: waits out `retryAfterSecs` ≤ 10 s once with the identical document (admission refuses before the spine records the `id`), otherwise says how long to wait.
- Copy claiming signing is optional / "older route" removed. `docs/03-vtc/website-and-admin.md` and `getting-started.md` describe the gate, per-origin keys, lifetime and durability.

## Known follow-ups (not here)
- At the 5-active-key cap (`tooManyKeys`) a browser with no working key cannot list or revoke the others; planned: `auth/signing-key/enroll/0.2` with `replaces`.
- VTA-wallet (persona) sign-in has no passkey to answer the enrolment step-up; planned: identity-signed enrolment authority in the same 0.2.

## Tests
admin-ui `vitest` 512 passed (new: signing-status states, fresh-key enrolment and failure rollback, 429 retry/give-up, refusal event, setup page), `tsc -b`, `wire:check`, `vite build`. Not exercised against a live VTC in a real browser.

title: chore(deps): affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.32.1, which stops losing late DIDComm replies
body:
affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.32.1 (affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#921) fixes a silent inbound-message loss.

**The bug.** `live_stream_next` waits up to `wait`, then drops its receiver and sends `CancelNext`. A DIDComm message arriving in that gap went to the dead waiter and was discarded: it was never cached, and the mediator had already delivered it. A `live_stream_get` that gave up a moment early lost its reply the same way. Upstream measured 3–5% of single messages lost under a 500 ms poll (6/200 before, 0/200 after).

**Why OpenVTC is exposed.** Every call a DIDComm-backed `VtaClient` makes goes through vta-sdk's `send_and_wait`, which polls `live_stream_next`. So a VTA reply could vanish and the call time out. The same path serves the startup key fetches in `openvtc-core/src/config/keys.rs`.

**Change.** The floor moves from 0.32.0 to 0.32.1, with a note on why. There is no API change. Messages that used to vanish now arrive.

## Testing

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass (1748 passed).

title: feat: keep the community's own vetted/1 and offer it as personhood evidence
body:
OpenVTC dropped the community's own `vetted/1` identity check: it was logged as "of no known kind", as the `IdentityVerificationCredential` it replaced had been. So it could never be offered as personhood evidence. VTI #1898 (merged) now delivers that statement to the member, and this PR keeps it.

**What changes**
- **New kind:** `CredentialKind::CommunityVetting` (config key `CommunityVetting`). It's a `StatementCredential` that `dtg::is_community_vetting` accepts: the predicate is `vetted/1`, it has none of the vetter-only members, and its `community` is the issuer. `credential_issue_admissible` already requires the issuer to be the community that sent it, so only the community's own check about our persona is stored.
- **Offered as evidence with no other change:** `AssertPersonhood` already sends every credential stored on the membership, `presentation::held_credentials` lists it, and the credential list shows it as "Statement: vetted (verified by the community)" through the existing `dtg::describe`.
- **Doesn't activate a membership.** A vetter's `vetted/1` still goes to the vetting handler, which already skips community-issued statements, and is never stored as this kind. A statement about another community is still of no known kind.
- **Fixtures:** `dtg::fixtures` gains `vetted_statement` and `community_vetting`. The per-kind registry tests (`credential_kind_registry_is_self_consistent` and `credential_issue_handles_every_registered_kind`) cover the new kind.

**New test:** `the_communitys_own_vetting_statement_is_stored_and_does_not_activate`. It checks the statement is stored and doesn't activate the membership, and that a vetter's value and another community's check are both refused.

**Compatibility:** an older build reading a config written by this one drops the `CommunityVetting` entry with a warning. That's the existing rule for unknown kinds, and the VTC can re-deliver it.

**Overlap check:** openvtc-43 confirmed this is clear of its in-flight work (the join-status poll, resend tracking and the vta-service 0.50 dev-dependency).

**Checked locally**
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 1748 passed, 0 failed.
- fmt is clean.

body:
Under `vetted/1`, `vtc/endorsements/issue` records **the community's own identity check** of a member. That statement replaced the community-issued `IdentityVerificationCredential`, and the member is the one who presents it as personhood evidence. But it was only returned to the administrator who issued it, so it never reached the member's wallet. The VTC's push to a member's wallet sends only the membership, role and invitation credentials.

**What changes**
- **Delivery:** after issuing and recording it, the community's own `vetted/1` is pushed to its subject as one `credential-exchange/issue`, the same way the role VAC is sent (`delivery::deliver_credentials`).
- **Best effort:** the statement is already issued and recorded, so a delivery failure is logged with `warn!` and the issue still succeeds. This matches the admission path.
- **Kept for re-delivery:** the signed statement is now stored on the endorsement row (`Endorsement.credential`, which until now held only vetter grants), so it can be delivered again later.
- **Unchanged:** other predicates' statements are untouched. They're still returned only to the administrator who issued them.

**Test:** `the_community_records_its_own_identity_check_as_a_vetted_statement` now also asserts that the row keeps the signed statement, and that the issue succeeds even though delivery fails (the test subject's DID doesn't resolve).

**Client side:** the matching OpenVTC PR stores the statement as a new credential kind. Personhood assertions already send every stored membership credential, so storing it is enough to offer it as evidence.

**Checked locally:** `cargo test -p vtc-service --test it endorsements::` passes (34 tests), `cargo check -p vtc-service --all-targets` is clean, and fmt is clean.

  was a DCQL query (presentation-definition) with optional vetting, so it could
  not say:
  - that nothing is required: DCQL asks for at least one credential, so an
    open community had to delete every criterion;
  - that a submission meeting it is reviewed rather than admitted;
  - that an invitation is required, outside `vetting`;
  - whose credentials count.

  could not tell an automatic path from a queue.

body:
A community's join criteria could not express its join policy. A criterion
was a DCQL query (presentation-definition) with optional vetting, so it could
not say:
- that nothing is required: DCQL asks for at least one credential, so an
  open community had to delete every criterion;
- that a submission meeting it is reviewed rather than admitted;
- that an invitation is required, outside `vetting`;
- whose credentials count.
And submit decided against an unseen "active join policy", so an applicant
could not tell an automatic path from a queue.

A criterion is now one way into the community: what it requires and how a
submission meeting it is decided.
- vtc/_shared/0.2 schema-registry: AcceptsCriterion gains `admission`
  (REQUIRED: automatic | review), `credentialIssuers` (community | recognised
  | any, with `query`) and `invitationRequired`. `query` becomes OPTIONAL.
- vtc/schemas/accepts/register, show, list 0.2: adopt it.
  register/0.2 adds `unsupportedRequirement`.
- vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.3: `admission`, `credentialIssuers` and
  `invitationRequired` on Criterion; `presentationDefinition` OPTIONAL;
  `requirementsDigest` REQUIRED on every criterion. Criteria are listed in the
  order the community decides by. An empty list means no applications are
  accepted.
- vtc/join-requests/submit/0.3: `criterion` names the criterion by digest. A
  submission naming none is decided under the first criterion it meets.
  Deciding is stated normatively. Not meeting a criterion never admits;
  `review` refers and never admits by itself; `automatic` admits unless the
  community refuses or refers on recorded grounds outside its criteria.
  Nothing outside a criterion admits anyone. New codes `criterionUnknown` and
  `notAccepting`.

The specifications state no default criterion and prefer none. Open
admission, review only (where invitations and trusted credentials admit no
one), invitation only, credential-gated, vetted, and any combination or set
of alternatives are expressed the same way, and each community's
administrators choose. Earlier versions are unchanged.

Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>


## Policies this expresses (examples in accepts/register/0.2 and manifest/0.3)

| Policy | Criteria |
|---|---|
| Open, straight through | `{admission: automatic}` |
| Open by review | `{admission: review}` |
| Review only: invitations and trusted credentials admit no one | only `{admission: review}` |
| Invitation only | `{admission: automatic, invitationRequired: true}` |
| A partner community's members | `{admission: automatic, query, credentialIssuers: recognised}` |
| Credential + vetting, then reviewed | `{admission: review, query, credentialIssuers, vetting}` |
| Invited or vetted, otherwise reviewed | three criteria, the review one last |

## Checks run locally

- `npm run validate`: 647 specs.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all four languages agree.
- `TT_STRICT_SECURITY_PRIVACY=1 npm run build`: passes.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` on rustc 1.99: pass.
- Every `requirementsDigest` in the manifest/0.3 examples was recomputed. The same JCS/SHA-256/base58btc code reproduces the two published 0.2 values.

## Follow-up

VTI implements this once a trust-tasks-rs release carries it. The VTC will serve the new versions, ship today's default as three ordinary criteria (invitation → automatic, a recognised issuer's credential → automatic, otherwise → review), and enforce "never admit outside a criterion; review never admits" as a host invariant.
