title: spec(vtc/join-requests/status): an approved applicant can ask for its credentials again
body:
An approved join isn't finished until the membership credential reaches the applicant. Until now nothing in the family could report that it hadn't arrived, or ask for it again.

**Field case.** A persona was approved and listed as a member, but stayed Pending in OpenVTC. The credential push was lost, and a `status` poll answering `approved` sent nothing. A related routing defect, the TSP replies themselves going astray across mediators, was fixed in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1894.

## Change (status/0.1, draft, edited in place)

| Member | Where | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `resendCredentials` | request | Ask for the already-issued credentials again |
| `credentialsDelivered` | response, on `approved` | Whether the community holds the applicant's acknowledgement that the credential arrived |
| `credentialResend` | response | `queued`, `notNeeded` or `rateLimited`. Absent after the flag means the community doesn't support re-delivery |
| `retryAfter` | response | With `rateLimited`: the earliest time another re-delivery will be honoured |

Normative rules:
- A re-delivery **MUST** send what was issued and **MUST NOT** issue anew. Re-issuing would mint a second credential for one membership; that's what `members/renew` does, and why renew isn't the right tool here.
- It goes only to the request's applicant, never to a party named in the payload.
- The consumer rate-limits it and should back off. A producer must not set the flag on every poll.

The task's classification changes too:
- `sideEffects` moves from `none` to `mutating`, which makes the task consequential.
- It therefore declares `issuedAtRequirement: REQUIRED`, so a captured poll can't be replayed to trigger a delivery.
- It gains an `## Authorization` section, which names ownership of the request as the authority.

The new members are additive on the wire. The generated Rust types are `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the new fields don't break source either.

## Checks

- `npm run validate` passes, including the freshness floor (363/363). `npm run check-bindings` passes (Rust, TS, Go and Dart all agree).
- Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings are regenerated, and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features` passes (1539 passed).
- A new invalid example rejects `resendCredentials: "true"`.

## Follow-ups

The VTC implementation (vtc-service status handler, plus vta-sdk carrying the fields) and the OpenVTC client both follow a trust-tasks-rs release. OpenVTC ships a manual rescue meanwhile: `R` / `members/renew` for an approved join whose credential never arrived.

title: feat: an approved join whose credential never arrived can be rescued with R
body:
A community can approve a join while the membership credential is lost in delivery. The persona is on its member list, but OpenVTC stays Pending and says the request "may not have been received", which is wrong. A status poll answering `approved` only stamped `receipt_at`, so nothing could tell the two cases apart, and `R` (`vtc/members/renew/0.1`) was Active-only.

## Change

- **`CommunityRecord::approved_at`** is set by the `approved` status arm (`mark_approved`). `approved_awaiting_credential()` and `can_renew()` read it. It's serde-defaulted, so existing configs load unchanged.
- **The row** reads "✓ approved — membership credential not received yet. Press R to ask the community to re-issue it." and offers `R`. The "may not have been received" warning no longer appears for it, because an approval stamps `receipt_at`.
- **`apply_renewal`** accepts that membership and activates it, as a delivered credential would. It returns the request it closed (`RenewalSummary::closed_join`), so the reciprocal VMC goes out with `closes_request` exactly as on delivery.
- The **key handler, hint row and runtime guard** all use the same `can_renew` gate.

It's manual only, because renewal re-issues. The automatic path re-sends the credentials already issued, and is OpenVTC/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf `resendCredentials` on `join-requests/status/0.1`, which needs a VTI release.

The persona this was found on became reachable once OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1894 (TSP replies to a sender on another mediator) is deployed. Its next status poll gets `approved`, and `R` then rescues it.

## Testing

- **Renewal:** `a_renewal_rescues_an_approved_join_whose_credential_never_arrived` checks that it activates, closes the right request, and that an Active renewal closes nothing. The existing `a_renewal_needs_an_active_membership` still refuses a Pending join nobody approved.
- **Status:** `status_response_approved_awaits_the_credential` now asserts `approved_at`, `can_renew`, that the join no longer reads as unacknowledged, and that a repeat poll changes nothing.
- **Panel:** `renew_is_offered_on_an_approved_join_awaiting_its_credential` checks the hint row and the panel text.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass, with and without default features. `cargo test --workspace` passes (1747 passed).

title: feat: an approved join whose credential never arrived can be rescued with R (#406)
body:
feat: an approved join whose credential never arrived can be rescued with R (#406)

A community can approve a join while the membership credential is lost in
delivery: the persona is on its member list, and OpenVTC stays Pending,
saying the request "may not have been received". A status poll answering
`approved` only stamped `receipt_at`, so nothing could tell the two apart,
and `R` (vtc/members/renew/0.1) was Active-only.

- `CommunityRecord::approved_at`, set by the `approved` status arm
  (`mark_approved`); `approved_awaiting_credential` and `can_renew` read it.
- The row says "✓ approved — membership credential not received yet" and
  offers `R`.
- `apply_renewal` accepts that membership, activates it as a delivered
  credential would, and returns the request it closed, so the reciprocal VMC
  goes out with it.

Manual only, because renewal re-issues. The automatic path, a re-send of the
credentials already issued, is the `resendCredentials` flag on
`join-requests/status/0.1` (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf), which needs a VTI release.

title: fix: a TSP reply reaches a sender on another mediator
body:
Both the VTC (`vtc-service/src/messaging.rs::handle_tsp`) and the VTA (`vta-service/src/messaging/service.rs` → `TspTransport::send_to`) answered an inbound TSP Trust Task by routing `[own_mediator, sender]`. That ends at a mediator that does not host a sender on another one, which refuses it. The request arrives and the answer never does.

**Field report.** An OpenVTC persona on `ic3-mediator` joined a VTC on `cpunks-mediator`. The admin approved the join and the persona is listed as a member, but it stayed Pending in OpenVTC: "no response from the community yet (sent over TSP)". Its submit receipt and every `join-requests/status` poll reply (OpenVTC polls Pending joins with backoff) were refused at the VTC's mediator. OpenVTC #405 fixed the same failure in the other direction. The admin sees at most a `warn!` "failed to send TSP reply", and only when the refusal comes back on the send call.

## Change

- **`vti_common::tsp_route::send_reply`** looks the sender's mediator up through the SDK's `peer_mediator`, which takes a mediator learned from the sender's routed invite first, else its DID document's `#tsp` service. When that is another mediator, it nests the reply `[own, peer_mediator]`, the same route VTI-56 gave sends a node starts. Otherwise it keeps the routed `[own, peer]` send.
  - The lookup is bounded by `PEER_MEDIATOR_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT` (10s, R1.2). A failed or timed-out lookup falls back to the old route with a warning.
  - `send_routed_to` is the route choice on its own, for a caller that already knows the peer's mediator.
- **VTC** `handle_tsp` replies through `send_reply`.
- **VTA** gains `TspTransport::send_reply`, and `handle_tsp` uses it.
- The relationship accept is unchanged: the SDK already routes it via the Reply_Path or the learned mediator.

Not yet catalogued in `design-docs/vti-networking-remediation-plan.md`.

**Known follow-up (not in this PR).** On approval the credentials go out through `trust_task_push`, which does route via the persona's `#tsp` mediator. In the field report they still did not arrive, and a `status` reply of `approved` does not re-send them. So a persona whose credential push was lost stays Pending even with this fix. That needs either a re-send path on the VTC or a re-request from OpenVTC, to be decided separately.

## Testing

- New `a_reply_reaches_a_sender_on_another_mediator` (two in-process mediators, no mediator handed in): fails on the old `send_to` route (bob's inbox stays empty for 15s) and passes on `send_reply`.
- `send_metadata_private_reaches_a_cross_mediator_peer` and `vti_56_a_cold_relationship_with_a_cross_mediator_peer_forms` still pass.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --all-features --lib -- messaging` (37 passed) and `cargo test -p vti-common --all-features --lib -- tsp_route` pass.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy -p vti-common -p vtc-service -p vta-service --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` pass on the rebased branch. Full workspace suite left to CI.

title: fix(ci): release guard catches a moved dependency on an unbumped crate
body:
This is the guard fix promised in #1890. It closes the gap that let #1888 stop part-way through publishing.

**The gap.** `check-release-bump-sizes.py` skipped any crate whose current version was already on crates.io, on the grounds that nothing of it was about to ship. In #1888, release-plz moved `vti-rooms` to `vti-common ^0.33` but left it at 0.4.0, which was already published on ^0.32. `vti-rooms-dtg` was released in the same run and packaged against the published 0.4.0, so it found two `vti_common::AppError` types and the release stopped (run 36917925028).

**Rule 3.** On a release, a crate whose version is already published must keep its internal requirements in the same compatibility ranges as that published release. If one has moved, the crate needs a new breaking version. Like rule 2, it only reports when some member is about to publish, so a feature PR that moves a dependency floor isn't held to a version the Release PR will set. The shared requirement comparison is factored out into `moved_reqs`.

**Verified locally:**
- **`1a5d7f65` (#1888):** fails. It names `vti-rooms`, plus `vta-keyspaces`, `vta-persona`, `vta-sweepers` and `vta-tee`, which had the same latent problem.
- **`5427f96f` (#1890 head):** passes, 23 published members checked.

> [!NOTE]
> **Merge after #1890 publishes.** Main is currently mid-release: crates #1888 never published are still at unpublished versions. Rule 3 correctly fails on that state, so this PR's `lockfile self-pins` job stays red until #1890 has published.

title: vta-cli-common-v0.31.0
body:
### Added

- Serve vta/webvh/dids/create/1.1, whose response states `serverless` (VTI-20) ([#1886](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1886))

A serverless did:webvh exists only in the VTA until the caller serves its
  first log entry. create/1.0 said so only by leaving out `serverId`, so a
  client could infer it but not be told. The Keyring report met a persona
  minted on a VTA with no hosting server get through whoami, contexts, mint
  and key borrow, then fail resolving a document nobody published, with an
  error naming the persona rather than the cause.

  create/1.1 (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#702, trust-tasks-rs 0.25.4) REQUIRES
  `serverless` in its response. The VTA serves both. 1.1 states it. 1.0 is
  answered in 1.0's shape, whose response refuses unknown members.
  VtaClient::create_did_webvh sends 1.1. CreateDidWebvhResultBody gains
  `serverless: Option<bool>` (None from a 1.0 answer or a bundle written
  before 1.1) and `is_serverless()`, which falls back to an absent
  `server_id`. `pnm did-mgmt dids create` reads it: the summary says
  "Hosting: serverless" and the hosting guidance keys off it.

  The VTA already refuses a create that names neither `serverId` nor `url`,
  so a serverless mint is always one the caller asked for. Choosing it when no
  hosting server is registered is a client decision.

  trust-tasks-rs floor 0.25.4.

body:
This moves VTI onto the **affinidi-data-integrity 0.8** stack in one step and **drops the `=0.7.13` pin** from #1882.

| Dependency | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| affinidi-data-integrity | =0.7.13 | 0.8 |
| affinidi-bbs | 0.3 | 0.4 |
| affinidi-tdk | 0.21 | 0.22 |
| affinidi-messaging-sdk | 0.31.1 | 0.32 |
| affinidi-tdk-common | 0.6.11 | 0.7 |
| affinidi-messaging-test-mediator | 0.15 | 0.16 |
| affinidi-messaging-mediator-admin / -tui | 0.6 | 0.7 |
| didwebvh-rs | 0.7 | 0.8 |
| affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk | 0.8.39 | 0.8.41 |
| trust-tasks-* | 0.25 (rs 0.25.4) | 0.26 (carries #702, so the 0.25.4 floor holds) |
| dtg-credentials | 0.12 | 0.13 |

Where these come from:
- The affinidi crates are from affinidi-tdk-rs #918 and the earlier steps of the same update.
- The trust-tasks crates are from trust-tasks-tf #705 and #707.
- `dtg-credentials` 0.13 is from OpenVTC/dtg-credentials#35. It is the same crate on data-integrity 0.8, with no wire change.

**Why it moves in one step.** Data-integrity 0.8 uses `affinidi-bbs` 0.4 in its public API. Holding back any crate in this list would put two `affinidi_bbs` or two `DataIntegrityProof` types into the build. That is exactly what the `=0.7.13` pin was preventing.

**Source changes:** none.

**Breaking:** `vta-sdk` and the other crates expose types from trust-tasks and the tdk, so their next releases are breaking minors.

**Checks run locally**
- `cargo tree -d` shows no duplicate affinidi, trust-tasks, didwebvh, vta, vti or dtg crate.
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features` is clean.
- `check-workspace-version-reqs`, `check-nitro-copies-every-member` and `check-lockfile-self-pins` pass, and fmt is clean.

**After this:** release VTI. Then tell the VGI and affinidi-tdk-rs sessions the new `vta-sdk` version. The affinidi-tdk-rs session will then tighten the mediator's `vta-sdk` requirement.

title: feat!: serve vta/webvh/dids/create/1.1, whose response states `serverless` (VTI-20)
body:
A serverless did:webvh exists only in the VTA until the caller serves its
first log entry. create/1.0 said so only by leaving out `serverId`, so a
client could infer it but not be told. The Keyring report met a persona
minted on a VTA with no hosting server get through whoami, contexts, mint
and key borrow, then fail resolving a document nobody published, with an
error naming the persona rather than the cause.

create/1.1 (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#702, trust-tasks-rs 0.25.4) REQUIRES
`serverless` in its response. The VTA serves both. 1.1 states it. 1.0 is
answered in 1.0's shape, whose response refuses unknown members.
VtaClient::create_did_webvh sends 1.1. CreateDidWebvhResultBody gains
`serverless: Option<bool>` (None from a 1.0 answer or a bundle written
before 1.1) and `is_serverless()`, which falls back to an absent
`server_id`. `pnm did-mgmt dids create` reads it: the summary says
"Hosting: serverless" and the hosting guidance keys off it.

The VTA already refuses a create that names neither `serverId` nor `url`,
so a serverless mint is always one the caller asked for. Choosing it when no
hosting server is registered is a client decision.

trust-tasks-rs floor 0.25.4.

Breaking: CreateDidWebvhResultBody has a new public field. An older VTA
answers create/1.1 with unsupportedType.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>


## Testing

- New `vti_20_create_1_1_states_serverless_and_1_0_keeps_its_shape` drives both versions through dispatch. A serverless mint over 1.1 answers `serverless: true`, a `logEntry` and no `serverId`, and parses as the generated `create::v1_1::Response`. The same mint over 1.0 has no `serverless` and parses as `v1_0::Response`. The SDK reads both, and `is_serverless()` is true for each.
- New SDK unit tests for `is_serverless`. The CLI hosting-guidance tests are updated.
- The `conformance` census has a 1.1 entry.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast` and `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 7794 passed, 0 failed. fmt is clean, and clippy is clean workspace-wide and with `--features rest`.

Not covered: a server-managed mint over 1.1 (`serverless: false`). It needs a mock hosting server; the code path sets `Some(false)` beside `serverId`.

title: fix: record the peer's mediator before the Rev 3 invite so it is routed
body:
## Problem
Joining a community whose VTC is on a different mediator than the persona fails:

```
Failed to submit join request: ... could not form the Rev 3 relationship its mediator did:webvh:...:cpunks-mediator requires ... (posted through our own mediator did:webvh:...:ic3-mediator): ... status(403) ... e.p.delivery.refused "Message not accepted for delivery"
```

The sender's mediator log shows `delivery refused ... reason=recipient is not local to this mediator`: the invite was posted Direct to the VTC's DID rather than routed.

## Cause
`send_trust_task` knows the VTC's mediator but only used it for the later `send_routed`. The invite is sent by the SDK's `send_control`, which routes `[our_mediator, peer_mediator, peer]` only when it knows a peer mediator (learned earlier, or a `TSPTransport` service in the peer's DID document). The VTC's DID document did not supply it, so the invite went out Direct and was refused.

## Fix
Call `set_peer_mediator` with the known mediator before `form_relationship_routed`.

## Testing
`cargo check -p openvtc-core` passes. Not yet verified end to end against the reporting user's setup, and no regression test added.

## Note
The peer's mediator must also allow inter-mediator relay (`enable_inter_mediator_relay`), or the relayed hop will be refused there.

significance_reasons: Normative requirement language changed

title: fix: record the peer's mediator before the Rev 3 invite so it is routed, not sent direct (#405)
body:
fix: record the peer's mediator before the Rev 3 invite so it is routed, not sent direct (#405)

send_trust_task knew the VTC's mediator but only used it for the later
send_routed. The invite goes through the SDK's send_control, which routes
via the peer's mediator only if it learned one (set_peer_mediator, or a
TSPTransport service in the peer's DID document). Otherwise it sent the
invite Direct and the sender's own mediator refused it:
403 e.p.delivery.refused (recipient is not local to this mediator).

Call set_peer_mediator before form_relationship_routed.

title: chore(release)!: 0.13.0 — affinidi-data-integrity 0.8
body:
This moves **`affinidi-data-integrity` from 0.7 to 0.8**, which uses `affinidi-bbs` 0.4, and releases the crate as **0.13.0**.

**Why a breaking release:** `DataIntegrityProof`, `SignOptions`, `VerifyOptions` and `DataIntegrityError` are part of this crate's API. So 0.12 and a caller on data-integrity 0.8 end up with two separate proof types. VTI is currently in exactly that position: everything else in VTI is on 0.8 (affinidi-tdk-rs #918), and `dtg-credentials` 0.12 is the only thing still pulling in 0.7.13.

**What doesn't change:** nothing on the wire. Credentials and proofs are byte-identical to 0.12, and there is no source change.

**Also:** the `affinidi-tdk` dev-dependency moves from 0.16 to 0.22.

The version number and CHANGELOG entry are in this PR. Once it's merged, pushing tag `v0.13.0` publishes the crate.

**Checks run locally:** fmt, `clippy --all-features -D warnings`, and `cargo test --all-features` (213 passed).

title: vta-sdk-v0.60.0
body:
### Added

- **vta-sdk**: A holder client's grant hint names persona-holder ([#1885](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1885))

When the setup DID is not authorized, verify_authorization prints the
  `pnm acl create` the operator should run. For a holder client — OpenVTC, a
  personal agent — that grant also needs `--capabilities persona-holder`,
  which no role carries: the hint without it gets the client through
  provisioning and then refused the holder's attribute pool.

  `ProvisionAsk` gains `holder` (set via `as_holder()`). It changes nothing on
  the wire and is read only to word the hint, so an integration is never told
  to take holder authority. verify_authorization now takes the ask rather than
  its context.

title: fix(vta-sdk): read a DTG credential's shape without its proof, so a proof set parses (VTI-57)
body:
dtg-credentials 0.12 models `proof` as one DataIntegrityProof. A community
holding two signing keys signs each credential once per key and writes a
proof set, so every DTGCredential parse of such a credential failed. #1868
taught the proof *verifiers* to read a set (VTI-44), but these shape parses
were left:

- vetting::eligibility::community_roles returned None in silence, so
  openvtc filed a two-key community's vetter grant as a plain role and never
  seated the vetter (the Keyring report's VTI-57, blocking TUI-as-vetter).
- verify_eligibility_vp refused the same grant as malformed when a vetter
  presented it.
- vetting::statement::verify_statement refused the community's own
  vetted/1 statements.
- vtc-service's statement intake (credentials/ingress.rs) and its predicate
  check (vetting/mod.rs).

vta_sdk::vetting::dtg_shape parses the credential with its proof set aside,
and every site above uses it. It is a shape check (classification, subtype
members, predicate profile) and reads nothing from the proof. Each proof is
still verified over the credential as received, by verify_attached_proof,
which reads a set. A tampered proof in a set is still refused (pinned).
dtg_shape becomes a plain parse once dtg-credentials models `proof` as
one-or-many.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>


## Testing

- New tests: `vti_57_a_grant_carrying_a_proof_set_names_its_roles`, `vti_57_an_eligibility_vp_over_a_proof_set_grant_verifies` and `vti_57_a_statement_carrying_a_proof_set_verifies`. Each fails with the proof kept in the parse and passes with it set aside. `vti_57_a_tampered_proof_in_the_set_is_still_refused` passes either way, as it should.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast` and `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 7796 passed, 0 failed.
- fmt is clean, and clippy is clean workspace-wide and for `vtc-service --features vetting-pcs`.

Not covered: no new VTC-side test drives a proof-set statement through intake. The two VTC sites use the same helper the SDK tests pin.

title: fix(vtc): emit the declared codes for invitation issue/revoke and hidden-vetting publish (#1600)
body:
`vtc/invitations/issue`, `vtc/invitations/revoke` and `vtc/vetting/hidden/publish` answered every refusal through the generic `app_error_to_reject`, so the codes their specifications declare reached callers as a bare `taskFailed`.

- `invitations/issue:unknownRole` for a role that does not parse. `admin` parses and stays the framework's refusal (the privilege ceiling); a test pins that it is not reported as `unknownRole`. A community keeps no register of its `custom:<name>` roles, so any well-formed custom name is one it can seat.
- `invitations/revoke:notFound` for an absent invitation, including one outside the caller's inviter scope.
- `vetting/hidden/publish:noSuchCriterion` and `:noVetting`, now driven by a signed-document test.

Each gains a census witness. The unwitnessed baseline falls from 10 to 8 (12 to 8 with `vetting-pcs`), and the ceiling ratchets down to match.

Raised from the RAHP assurance review: sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit#691 and #849.

title: chore(deps)!: vta-sdk 0.59 / vta-service 0.48 — community-issued vetted/1
body:
This moves OpenVTC to **`vta-sdk` 0.59.0** and **`vta-service` 0.48.0** (VTI #1874, #1876 and #1867).

## What changed upstream
- **Optional vetter fields.** `VettedObjectValue`'s three vetter-only fields (`identity_commitment`, `card_digest_multibase`, `declared_relationship`) are now `Option`, and all-or-nothing.
- **Community-issued statements.** A community can now issue `vetted/1` itself to record its own identity check. Such a statement carries none of the three fields. It replaces the plain `IdentityVerificationCredential`.

## Changes here
- **Vetter flow:** wraps all three fields in `Some(..)` when building a statement.
- **Applicant `on_statement`:** reads them through `vetter_members()` and refuses a statement without them, so vetter paths stay strict.
- **Hidden vetting:** `vetting::hidden::statement_meta` now returns `Option<StatementMeta>`, and `book.rs` turns `None` into an error on this path. This is a public API change.
- **Community-issued `vetted/1`**, meaning one whose issuer is the community named in the value and that has no vetter fields:
  - It is labelled "Statement: vetted (verified by the community)" (`dtg::is_community_vetting`).
  - It is no longer routed to the vetting handler (`vetting::wire::is_community_issued`), so it never answers a vetting request or counts toward a vetter threshold.
- **Tests:** two new tests cover a community statement, a vetter statement, and both mixed cases.
- **CHANGELOG** entry.

## Known duplicate
`did-git-sign` 0.6.0 still requires `vta-sdk` ^0.58, so 0.58.1 stays in the graph through that edge alone. It goes when VGI releases `did-git-sign` on 0.59 (VGI #121 and #122, in progress). Check with `cargo tree -i vta-sdk@0.58.1`.

## Not in this PR
The client still doesn't **store** a community-issued `vetted/1`. A membership only keeps Membership and Role credentials, so one is logged as "of no known kind" and dropped, and it's never offered as personhood evidence. This was already true of the old `IdentityVerificationCredential`, so it isn't a regression. Fixing it needs a new stored-credential kind, which affects saved config and the UI, so it's a separate follow-up.

## Checks
- fmt, `clippy -D warnings` and `doc -D warnings` are clean.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 1745 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo deny check bans` is ok.

The three vetter-only members of a vetted/1 value are now optional and
all-or-nothing (VTI #1874, #1876). The vetter desk wraps them in Some; the
applicant, hidden-vetting attestation and reference example read them via
VettedObjectValue::vetter_members and refuse a statement without them.

A vetted/1 the community issues for itself (its own identity check, which
replaced the community-issued IdentityVerificationCredential) is labelled
'vetted (verified by the community)' in the credential views and is no
longer claimed by the vetting handler as a vetter's statement, so it
answers no request and counts toward no vetter threshold.

### Chore

- **proof**: Affinidi-data-integrity 0.8 in trust-tasks-proof ([#705](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/705))

* chore(proof)!: affinidi-data-integrity 0.8 in trust-tasks-proof

  affinidi-data-integrity 0.7.14 moved its public affinidi-bbs dependency
  from 0.3 to 0.4 as a patch release; 0.8.0 re-releases the same code under
  the version that change needed. trust-tasks-proof now depends on
  affinidi-data-integrity 0.8 (the `affinidi` feature, on by default).

  This is breaking for trust-tasks-proof's dependents: the crate re-exports
  data-integrity types in its public API (`AffinidiSigner` is
  `affinidi_data_integrity::signer::Signer`, `AffinidiDidKeyResolver` is
  `affinidi_data_integrity::DidKeyResolver`, plus `SignOptions` and
  `CryptoSuite`, and `Verifier::with_options` takes data-integrity's
  `VerifyOptions`). Code that implements or passes those types must be
  built against affinidi-data-integrity 0.8 as well. No source change was
  needed here; the 0.8 API is identical to 0.7.14.

  Part of the cascade onto affinidi-data-integrity 0.8: the
  affinidi-tdk-rs crates (messaging-sdk, mediator) move onto this release
  next. Until affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk 0.8.41 (didwebvh-rs 0.8)
  publishes, the lockfile still carries affinidi-data-integrity 0.7.14
  through didwebvh-rs 0.7 and the affinidi-tdk 0.17 dev graph of
  trust-tasks-didcomm.

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.25.4` → `0.26.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.25.4` → `0.26.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.25.4` → `0.26.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.25.4` → `0.26.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.25.4` → `0.26.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.25.4` → `0.26.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.25.4` → `0.26.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.25.4` → `0.26.0` | breaking |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: chore: release 0.8.0
body:
Bumps the workspace from 0.7.1 to **0.8.0**:
- the workspace version
- the five internal `vgi-*` and `verify-trust` pins
- the lockfile entries for the eight workspace crates, with no external dependency moving
- `bridge.example.toml`'s `[verify_trust] version`, now `v0.8.0`

This is a **minor** release because it carries a breaking change.

## What's in it, since v0.7.1

- **verify-trust (BREAKING):** the **legacy resource format is removed** (#119, closes #109). Resources are forge-qualified only: `<forge-host>/<owner>[/<repo>]`.
  - `--resource-format legacy`, or `resource-format: legacy` on the action, is refused with how to move over: reissue the grants as `<forge-host>/<owner>[/<repo>]`, or pin **v0.7.x** meanwhile.
  - The flag and `ResourceFormat` remain. `ResourceFormat` is now just `Qualified` and `#[non_exhaustive]`. Workflows passing `resource-format: qualified` are unaffected, which includes every one a bridge bootstraps.
  - The VTC never wrote `owner/repo` grants, and a leftover one authorizes nothing.
- **vgi-bridge:** the example config pins verify-trust `v0.8.0`.

## Before tagging `v0.8.0`

The tag push publishes to crates.io and cuts the GitHub Release. Neither can be undone.

- [ ] Tell anyone still on hand-issued `owner/repo` grants to reissue them qualified, or to pin the action and `version` to v0.7.x.

## Verification

On Rust 1.99, all pass:
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace`

`verify-trust --version` reports `0.8.0`.

title: vta-service-v0.48.0
body:
### Fixed

- Take affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.31.1; the SDK routes a cross-mediator invite itself ([#1880](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1880))

affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.31.1 (affinidi-tdk-rs #913) routes a TSP
  relationship invite to a peer on another mediator through the mediator the
  peer's DID document names, and keeps a Delivery-Request-collected message's
  own id so a reply threads to it (VTI-49). The workspace floor moves to
  0.31.1, because ^0.31 resolving 0.31.0 would bring the cross-mediator
  refusal back.

  So the set_peer_mediator half of vti_common::tsp_route ([#1873](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1873)) is gone. It
  recorded the same DID-document mediator the SDK now reads.
  tsp_route::send_reestablishing stays: the SDK's own sends the payload along
  the route it is given, and [our_mediator, peer] cannot reach a peer on
  another mediator. vti_56_a_cold_relationship_with_a_cross_mediator_peer_forms
  now uses peers that name their mediator by DID, as a VTI-provisioned DID
  does, and holds both halves.

- **vta**: Mnemonic export on a DID-less VTA, and a CLI to open the bundle ([#1878](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1878))

* fix(vta-service,pnm-cli): mnemonic export on a DID-less VTA, and a CLI to open the bundle

  A TEE VTA can hold first-boot entropy (the export window active) before it
  has a DID: tee.kms.vta_did_template unset, or auto-generation still
  pending/failed-non-fatally. signed_by_the_caller already refuses the
  export then (no DID to bind the request's `recipient` to, and the spec
  requires `recipient` present and naming the recipient's own DID on both
  channel paths) — but the refusal pointed operators at `vta setup`, which
  doesn't apply to vta-enclave (built without the `setup` feature, the only
  binary with a mnemonic guard). Point at the real remedy instead, and add
  tests proving the refusal on either path leaves the window unspent.

  Add `pnm vta mnemonic open <bundle>` to decrypt a sealed
  mnemonic-export bundle locally: refuses any non-SeedMnemonic payload,
  prints the words to the terminal only, consumes the local request
  secret on success, and writes to a file only when `--out` is passed
  explicitly (0600, via the existing write_secret_export helper).

- Build clean on rustc 1.99 (CI) without raising the 1.95 MSRV ([#1877](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1877))

CI picked up rustc 1.99.0 (2026-09-28) and builds with -D warnings, so two
  new lints failed Clippy and Test (VTC) on every PR:

  - Atomic*::fetch_update is deprecated in favour of try_update, which is
    newer than the workspace rust-version (1.95.0). The two call sites
    (vta-service test_support, vtc-service member_count_dec) keep
    fetch_update under a statement-level #[allow(deprecated)].
  - clippy needless_borrows_for_generic_args in vtc-service messaging:
    .map(&absolutize) -> .map(absolutize).

  cargo +1.99.0 clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings is clean.

- A TSP relationship can be started with a peer on another mediator (VTI-56) ([#1873](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1873))

A node that starts a TSP relationship with a peer on another mediator had
  its invite refused by its own mediator (403 e.p.direct_delivery.denied,
  "must be relayed through a routing envelope"), every attempt. The SDK
  routes a control message across mediators only when it already knows the
  peer's mediator, learned from a routed invite from the peer or set with
  set_peer_mediator. An initiator has neither, and nothing here set it. That
  is why the Farm VTC's TSP push to a member on the other mediator never left
  its own mediator and fell back to DIDComm an hour later. The existing
  cross-mediator tests pre-form the relationship (relate_directly), so they
  never sent an invite.

- Keyring findings round — proof sets, verify-as-received, VTC delivery (VTI-44, VTI-45, VTI-50, VTI-56) ([#1868](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1868))

* fix(vta-cli-common): opening a bundle to inspect it keeps the request seed

  pnm, cnm and vta `bootstrap open` consumed the single-use request seed
  right after decrypting, even when they wrote nothing. The seed is the only
  key that opens the bundle, so inspecting a template bundle destroyed the
  integration's keys, and cnm's own follow-up hint (`cnm auth login
  --credential-bundle`) could never succeed (VTI-53).

  Inspection now opens with the seed kept and says where it is. pnm consumes
  it only after a successful --out write, so a refused bundle no longer costs
  a fresh request cycle either. open_armored_bundle_keeping_secret and
  consume_request_secret are now public.

title: pnm-cli-v0.28.0
body:
### Fixed

- **vta**: Mnemonic export on a DID-less VTA, and a CLI to open the bundle ([#1878](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1878))

* fix(vta-service,pnm-cli): mnemonic export on a DID-less VTA, and a CLI to open the bundle

  A TEE VTA can hold first-boot entropy (the export window active) before it
  has a DID: tee.kms.vta_did_template unset, or auto-generation still
  pending/failed-non-fatally. signed_by_the_caller already refuses the
  export then (no DID to bind the request's `recipient` to, and the spec
  requires `recipient` present and naming the recipient's own DID on both
  channel paths) — but the refusal pointed operators at `vta setup`, which
  doesn't apply to vta-enclave (built without the `setup` feature, the only
  binary with a mnemonic guard). Point at the real remedy instead, and add
  tests proving the refusal on either path leaves the window unspent.

  Add `pnm vta mnemonic open <bundle>` to decrypt a sealed
  mnemonic-export bundle locally: refuses any non-SeedMnemonic payload,
  prints the words to the terminal only, consumes the local request
  secret on success, and writes to a file only when `--out` is passed
  explicitly (0600, via the existing write_secret_export helper).

body:
Moves `trust-tasks-proof` to **`affinidi-data-integrity` 0.8**. This is step 4 of the data-integrity 0.8 cascade.

**Why.** `affinidi-data-integrity` 0.7.14 shipped a breaking public-dependency change (`affinidi-bbs` 0.3 → 0.4) as a patch release. The user chose a full cascade to 0.8.0 over yanking it. `trust-tasks-proof` re-exports data-integrity types (`AffinidiSigner`, `AffinidiDidKeyResolver`, `SignOptions`, `CryptoSuite`, and `VerifyOptions` via `Verifier::with_options`), so this is a **breaking** release for its dependents. The affinidi-tdk-rs 3b crates (messaging-sdk 0.32, mediator 0.35 and the rest) build on it.

**Change.** `affinidi-data-integrity = { version = "0.8", optional = true }`, plus `Cargo.lock`. No source change: 0.8.0 is the same code as 0.7.14, and only the BBS functions changed type, which this crate doesn't use.

**Draft until affinidi-tdk-rs 3a is on crates.io** (`did-scid` 0.3.0, `affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk` 0.8.41). Until then, a 0.7 copy of data-integrity remains through the resolver cache's `didwebvh-rs` 0.7.

**Out of scope:** `trust-tasks-didcomm` stays on `affinidi-tdk` 0.17; it moves to tdk 0.22 in a follow-up after 3b.

**Checks:**
- `cargo fmt --check` is clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`: 1332 passed.
- `trust-tasks-rs --features validate`: 1628 passed.
- `trust-tasks-proof --all-features` passes.

title: feat(verify-trust)!: remove the legacy resource format
body:
Step 3, the last, of #109. **This is a breaking change, so release it as 0.8.0.** It closes #109.

## Why

SEC-4045 / VGI-03. The bare `owner/repo` resource names no forge, so `github.com/acme` and `codeberg.org/acme` can't be told apart. v0.7.0 (#114) made `qualified` the default. This PR removes `legacy` as planned.

## What

- **`ResourceFormat`:** only `Qualified` is left, and the type is now `#[non_exhaustive]`. I kept the type, `select_resources(format, …)` and the `--resource-format` flag on purpose:
  - every bridge-bootstrapped workflow passes `resource-format: qualified`
  - the action passes the flag on every run
  - library callers such as `vgi-bridge`'s tests pass `ResourceFormat::Qualified`

  All of those keep working with no change.
- **Removed:** `check_legacy` and the legacy branch of `select_resources`.
- **`legacy` is refused, with how to move over:** reissue the grants as `<forge-host>/<owner>[/<repo>]`, or pin v0.7.x meanwhile. This replaces clap's bare "invalid value" message, via `FromStr` and the exported `LEGACY_REMOVED`. For example:
  ```
  error: invalid value 'legacy' for '--resource-format <RESOURCE_FORMAT>': `legacy` (bare `owner/repo` resources) was removed in verify-trust 0.8.0: write the registry grants as `<forge-host>/<owner>[/<repo>]` (e.g. `github.com/acme/widgets`, org grant `github.com/acme`) — the form the VTC writes — and drop `resource-format: legacy` (or --resource-format legacy). Until the grants are reissued, pin verify-trust v0.7.x.
  ```
- **Action:** `resource-format: legacy` fails with the same guidance, and the input descriptions no longer offer it.
- **Docs:** README, `crates/verify-trust/README.md`, RUNBOOK and BRIDGE now describe qualified as the only form. RUNBOOK covers moving off `owner/repo` grants: reissue them, drop the input, then revoke the old ones.

## Who this affects

The VTC never wrote `owner/repo` grants, since its projection is qualified-only and doesn't dual-write. Bridge-bootstrapped workflows set `qualified`. So only runs that **explicitly pass `legacy`** are affected, and they fail loudly with the steps above. A leftover `owner/repo` grant in the registry authorizes nothing: a run never falls back to the slug.

## Tests

- New `legacy_is_refused_with_how_to_move_over`: `qualified` parses, `legacy` gets the migration message, and an unknown value is refused.
- The CLI test now checks that `--resource-format legacy` fails with that message.
- The e2e test is now `a_leftover_legacy_grant_never_authorizes`: a registry holding only `Example/Repo` gives `unauthorized`, and the run queried `github.com/example/repo`.
- I removed the tests that only exercised legacy mode, including the four SEC-4045 legacy-validation tests added in #103. They tested the code this PR deletes.
- All pass on Rust 1.99: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo test -p did-git-sign --features insecure-policy-bypass`. `ci_workflow_hardening` covers the action.

## Release

Ship this as 0.8.0, with release notes that call out the breaking change and the v0.7.x opt-out for anyone still on `owner/repo` grants.

title: Switch --resource-format default to qualified, then remove legacy
body:
Reminder, from the SEC-4045 / VLM-4232 round 3 remediation (VGI-03).

## Background

VGI-03 (Medium): under `--resource-format legacy`, the TRQP resource that alone scopes a signer to a repository took any string.

- #103 fixed the non-breaking part. Legacy values must now be `owner` or `owner/repo`, with no whitespace, control characters or empty segments, and a legacy fallback must be the repository's own owner.
- **Legacy is still the default.** The qualified grammar (`<forge-host>/owner[/repo]`, validated and lowercased, with a fallback that must *contain* the resource) is the real fix.
- The bridge-posted check already uses the qualified form.

The migration plan is already documented in `crates/verify-trust/README.md` (§ Migration) and in `action.yml`:

1. **Now:** `legacy` is the default; qualified is opt-in.
2. **Next minor release:** flip the default to `qualified`. Pinning `resource-format: legacy` keeps the old behaviour for one more release.
3. **The release after that:** remove `legacy`.

This issue tracks steps 2 and 3.

## Before step 2

- [ ] Confirm registry grants exist in qualified form for every namespace, whether VTC-written or hand-issued, so that no deployed check starts failing as `unauthorized`.
- [ ] Announce the flip to operators, with the one-line opt-out (`resource-format: legacy`).

## Step 2: flip the default

- [ ] `crates/verify-trust/src/resource.rs`: move `#[default]` from `ResourceFormat::Legacy` to `Qualified`.
- [ ] `crates/verify-trust/src/main.rs`: change `default_value_t = ResourceFormat::Legacy` to `Qualified`.
- [ ] `.github/actions/verify-trust/action.yml`: change the `resource-format` default to `"qualified"` and update the input descriptions.
- [ ] Update the tests that pin the legacy default (e.g. `legacy_is_the_default_and_passes_values_through_untouched`).
- [ ] Update the docs that say "legacy (default)":
  - [ ] `README.md`
  - [ ] `crates/verify-trust/README.md`
  - [ ] `docs/RUNBOOK.md`
  - [ ] `docs/BRIDGE.md`
- [ ] Release notes: call the change **breaking** and give the opt-out.

## Step 3: remove legacy (one release later)

- [ ] Remove `ResourceFormat::Legacy`, the `check_legacy` validation and the legacy arm of `select_resources`.
- [ ] Remove `legacy` from the action input.
- [ ] Remove the legacy rows from the docs.
- [ ] Release notes.

title: cnm-cli-v0.22.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: Bind the community's own check to a uniqueness pseudonym server-side ([#1876](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1876))

A community enforcing `personhood.singleMembership` could not satisfy it with
  its own `vetted/1` identity check, because the statement has no member for a
  pseudonym. The binding now happens server-side, at issue.

  - `vtc/endorsements/issue/0.1` under `vetted/1` reads the payload extension
    `ext["org.openvtc.uniqueness"] = { "pseudonym": "<value>" }`. It is never
    written into the credential. The pseudonym is bound to the subject in the
    existing pseudonym store (`members::pseudonym::claim_for_statement`), which
    stores only the community-scoped salted digest. The claim row is tagged
    with the statement's endorsement id. The binding is made before anything is
    minted, and released again if minting fails.
  - A pseudonym already bound to another member refuses the issue with
    `AppError::Conflict`: `taskFailed` with `details.reason` `conflict`, the
    same collision semantics personhood assert already has. Nothing is minted.
    No declared `endorsements/issue` code fits a duplicate person, and
    `claimSchemaViolation` would tell the caller to fix a claim that is valid.
  - The extension is read only under `vetted/1`, and only as
    `{ "pseudonym": "<non-empty string>" }`. Anything else is
    `malformedRequest`.
  - At personhood assert under `singleMembership`, the community's own
    `vetted/1` statement about the member satisfies uniqueness only when the
    community holds a binding for that member DID (`pseudonym::is_bound`).
    Credentials from an accepted IDVP still use `credentialSubject.pseudonym`.
  - `vtc/endorsements/revoke/0.1` on a `vetted/1` row releases the binding it
    made (`pseudonym::release_for_statement`). A binding an outside provider's
    credential made is untagged and is kept. Purge still releases every binding
    of the member.
  - vtc-client gains `issue_endorsement_with_ext` (additive).
    `cnm member endorse` gains `--uniqueness-pseudonym`.

- Record the community's own identity check as a vetted/1 statement ([#1874](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1874))

* feat(vta-sdk)!: vetted/1 vetter-only members are optional and all-or-nothing

  Registry `vetted/1` (trustoverip/dtgwg-vsc-registry#24) admits the community
  itself as issuer of a statement recording its own identity check. Such a
  statement carries none of the three vetter-only members; a vetter's statement
  carries all three. The schema makes them all-or-nothing (`dependentRequired`).



### Fixed

- Keyring findings round — proof sets, verify-as-received, VTC delivery (VTI-44, VTI-45, VTI-50, VTI-56) ([#1868](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1868))

* fix(vta-cli-common): opening a bundle to inspect it keeps the request seed

  pnm, cnm and vta `bootstrap open` consumed the single-use request seed
  right after decrypting, even when they wrote nothing. The seed is the only
  key that opens the bundle, so inspecting a template bundle destroyed the
  integration's keys, and cnm's own follow-up hint (`cnm auth login
  --credential-bundle`) could never succeed (VTI-53).

  Inspection now opens with the seed kept and says where it is. pnm consumes
  it only after a successful --out write, so a refused bundle no longer costs
  a fresh request cycle either. open_armored_bundle_keeping_secret and
  consume_request_secret are now public.

  peer's DID document names, and keeps a Delivery-Request-collected message's
  own id so a reply threads to it (VTI-49). The workspace floor moves to
  0.31.1, because ^0.31 resolving 0.31.0 would bring the cross-mediator
  refusal back.

  So the set_peer_mediator half of vti_common::tsp_route ([#1873](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1873)) is gone. It
  recorded the same DID-document mediator the SDK now reads.
  tsp_route::send_reestablishing stays: the SDK's own sends the payload along
  the route it is given, and [our_mediator, peer] cannot reach a peer on
  another mediator. vti_56_a_cold_relationship_with_a_cross_mediator_peer_forms
  now uses peers that name their mediator by DID, as a VTI-provisioned DID
  does, and holds both halves.

- A TSP relationship can be started with a peer on another mediator (VTI-56) ([#1873](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1873))

A node that starts a TSP relationship with a peer on another mediator had
  its invite refused by its own mediator (403 e.p.direct_delivery.denied,
  "must be relayed through a routing envelope"), every attempt. The SDK
  routes a control message across mediators only when it already knows the
  peer's mediator, learned from a routed invite from the peer or set with
  set_peer_mediator. An initiator has neither, and nothing here set it. That
  is why the Farm VTC's TSP push to a member on the other mediator never left
  its own mediator and fell back to DIDComm an hour later. The existing
  cross-mediator tests pre-form the relationship (relate_directly), so they
  never sent an invite.

- Keyring findings round — proof sets, verify-as-received, VTC delivery (VTI-44, VTI-45, VTI-50, VTI-56) ([#1868](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1868))

* fix(vta-cli-common): opening a bundle to inspect it keeps the request seed

  pnm, cnm and vta `bootstrap open` consumed the single-use request seed
  right after decrypting, even when they wrote nothing. The seed is the only
  key that opens the bundle, so inspecting a template bundle destroyed the
  integration's keys, and cnm's own follow-up hint (`cnm auth login
  --credential-bundle`) could never succeed (VTI-53).

  Inspection now opens with the seed kept and says where it is. pnm consumes
  it only after a successful --out write, so a refused bundle no longer costs
  a fresh request cycle either. open_armored_bundle_keeping_secret and
  consume_request_secret are now public.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.25.4
body:
### Added

- **vta/webvh/dids/create**: 1.1 states `serverless` in the response ([#702](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/702))

* feat(vta/webvh/dids/create): 1.1 states `serverless` in the response

  A serverless DID exists only in the VTA until the caller serves its first log
  entry. In 1.0 the response says so only by leaving out `serverId`. A client
  that missed the absence went on to resolve a DID nobody serves, and failed later
  with an error naming the DID rather than the cause (Keyring VTI-20: a persona
  minted on a VTA with no hosting server registered got through whoami, contexts,
  mint and key borrow before failing).

  1.1's response REQUIRES `serverless`. It is true exactly when the request named
  no `serverId`, and then the response carries `logEntry` and no `serverId`. A
  producer reads it rather than inferring it. 1.1 is a new version rather than an
  edit to 1.0 because 1.0's response refuses unknown members; both stay draft
  (SPEC §5.2 permits the required member as a MINOR at draft). The request schema
  is unchanged.

  Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

title: fix: setup's start page lists the steps setup runs; the setup DID is new each run
body:
Two setup UX fixes.

**Start page.** "New profile setup" promised choosing a mediator and creating your DID. Both moved to joining a community (R-A-5): the VTA's DID document names its own mediator, and the persona is minted per join. The page now lists what setup does:

- Connect to your Verifiable Trust Agent (VTA)
- Authorise OpenVTC from your Personal Network Manager (PNM)
- Optionally set up a hardware token (`openpgp-card` builds only)
- Set an unlock code to protect this profile

It also says the DID is created when you join your first community.

**ACL instructions.** The setup did:key is minted per run and held only in memory, so a grant made for an earlier run's DID is for a key that no longer exists, and the VTA reports `DID not in ACL`. The page now says so under the setup DID.

## Testing

- New `the_new_profile_steps_name_only_what_setup_does` stops the mediator and DID steps from coming back.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets -- -D warnings` (with and without default features) pass, and `cargo test -p openvtc --bin openvtc setup_flow` passes (35 passed).

Follow-up once OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure's `ProvisionAsk::as_holder` is released: call it in `setup_vta_actions.rs`, so the SDK's "not authorized" hint names `persona-holder` too.

title: feat(vta-sdk): a holder client's grant hint names persona-holder
body:
When the setup DID is not authorized, `verify_authorization` prints the `pnm acl create` the operator should run. For a holder client (OpenVTC, a personal agent) that grant also needs `--capabilities persona-holder`, which no role carries. A hint without it gets the client through provisioning, and the client is then refused the holder's attribute pool.

- `ProvisionAsk` gains `holder: bool`, set via `as_holder()`. It changes nothing on the wire and is read only to word the hint, so an integration is never told to take holder authority.
- `verify_authorization` takes the `&ProvisionAsk` rather than its context (internal, `pub(super)`).

**Semver:** `ProvisionAsk` has all-public fields, so adding one breaks struct-literal construction. Nothing in this repo builds it that way (every caller uses the builders), but expect a minor bump.

Follows #1884, which fixed the same omission in the VTA's hand-off re-grant hint. OpenVTC will call `.as_holder()` once this is released.

## Testing

- New `a_holder_ask_is_told_the_holder_capability` covers both the hand-off and permanent forms. The existing hint test is unchanged in its expectations, so non-holder asks see no difference.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p vta-sdk --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test -p vta-sdk --all-features --lib -- provision_client` (84 passed) pass. Full workspace suite left to CI.

It recorded the same DID-document mediator the SDK now reads. tsp_route::send_reestablishing stays: the SDK's own sends the payload along the route it is given, and [our_mediator, peer] cannot reach a peer on another mediator. vti_56_a_cold_relationship_with_a_cross_mediator_peer_forms now uses peers that name their mediator by DID, as a VTI-provisioned DID does, and holds both halves. - **vta**: Mnemonic export on a DID-less VTA, and a CLI to open the bundle ([#1878](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1878)) * fix(vta-service,pnm-cli): mnemonic export on a DID-less VTA, and a CLI to open the bundle A TEE VTA can hold first-boot entropy (the export window active) before it has a DID: tee.kms.vta_did_template unset, or auto-generation still pending/failed-non-fatally. signed_by_the_caller already refuses the export then (no DID to bind the request's `recipient` to, and the spec requires `recipient` present and naming the recipient's own DID on both channel paths) — but the refusal pointed operators at `vta setup`, which doesn't apply to vta-enclave (built without the `setup` feature, the only binary with a mnemonic guard). Point at the real remedy instead, and add tests proving the refusal on either path leaves the window unspent. Add `pnm vta mnemonic open ` to decrypt a sealed mnemonic-export bundle locally: refuses any non-SeedMnemonic payload, prints the words to the terminal only, consumes the local request secret on success, and writes to a file only when `--out` is passed explicitly (0600, via the existing write_secret_export helper). - Build clean on rustc 1.99 (CI) without raising the 1.95 MSRV ([#1877](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1877)) CI picked up rustc 1.99.0 (2026-09-28) and builds with -D warnings, so two new lints failed Clippy and Test (VTC) on every PR: - Atomic*::fetch_update is deprecated in favour of try_update, which is newer than the workspace rust-version (1.95.0). The two call sites (vta-service test_support, vtc-service member_count_dec) keep fetch_update under a statement-level #[allow(deprecated)]. - clippy needless_borrows_for_generic_args in vtc-service messaging: .map(&absolutize) -> .map(absolutize). cargo +1.99.0 clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings is clean. - A TSP relationship can be started with a peer on another mediator (VTI-56) ([#1873](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1873)) A node that starts a TSP relationship with a peer on another mediator had its invite refused by its own mediator (403 e.p.direct_delivery.denied, "must be relayed through a routing envelope"), every attempt. The SDK routes a control message across mediators only when it already knows the peer's mediator, learned from a routed invite from the peer or set with set_peer_mediator. An initiator has neither, and nothing here set it. That is why the Farm VTC's TSP push to a member on the other mediator never left its own mediator and fell back to DIDComm an hour later. The existing cross-mediator tests pre-form the relationship (relate_directly), so they never sent an invite. - Keyring findings round — proof sets, verify-as-received, VTC delivery (VTI-44, VTI-45, VTI-50, VTI-56) ([#1868](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1868)) * fix(vta-cli-common): opening a bundle to inspect it keeps the request seed pnm, cnm and vta `bootstrap open` consumed the single-use request seed right after decrypting, even when they wrote nothing. The seed is the only key that opens the bundle, so inspecting a template bundle destroyed the integration's keys, and cnm's own follow-up hint (`cnm auth login --credential-bundle`) could never succeed (VTI-53). Inspection now opens with the seed kept and says where it is. pnm consumes it only after a successful --out write, so a refused bundle no longer costs a fresh request cycle either. open_armored_bundle_keeping_secret and consume_request_secret are now public.

- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vta/webvh/dids/create): 1.1 states `serverless` in the response
body:
A serverless DID exists only in the VTA until the caller serves its first log
entry. In 1.0 the response says so only by leaving out `serverId`. A client
that missed the absence went on to resolve a DID nobody serves, and failed later
with an error naming the DID rather than the cause (Keyring VTI-20: a persona
minted on a VTA with no hosting server registered got through whoami, contexts,
mint and key borrow before failing).

1.1's response REQUIRES `serverless`. It is true exactly when the request named
no `serverId`, and then the response carries `logEntry` and no `serverId`. A
producer reads it rather than inferring it. 1.1 is a new version rather than an
edit to 1.0 because 1.0's response refuses unknown members; both stay draft
(SPEC §5.2 permits the required member as a MINOR at draft). The request schema
is unchanged.

Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>


## Checks run locally

- `npm run validate`: 642 specs validated.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all four languages agree.
- `npm run build` and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features` pass.

## Follow-up

VTI serves 1.1 and emits `serverless` once a trust-tasks-rs release carries this.

title: feat(vgi-bridge): reach the VTC, VTA and registry over TSP
body:
The bridge was DIDComm-only on every link, and its docs said so with reasoning that no longer holds: the VTC now resolves the bridge's DID, intersects transports and sends jobs over TSP when the bridge advertises it (`vtc-service` `git_ns::bridge`). This makes the bridge speak TSP, then DIDComm, on all three links, and fixes the wording.

## Per link

**Bridge and VTC** (`transport.rs`, `lib.rs`)
- `DidcommLink` becomes `MediatorLink`: one mediator websocket carrying TSP and DIDComm. The messaging SDK's delivery transport already surfaces both protocols off that socket, tagged, the same way the VTC does. There is no second session.
- Inbound TSP: a Trust Task document inside the published `trust-tasks-tsp` envelope (`vta_sdk::tsp_binding`), with the TSP-verified sender VID passed as `authenticated_sender`. `InboundDoc` gains `via`.
- Replies (job answers, discovery answers, errors) go back over the transport the request came in on. The link remembers the last 1024 inbound document ids and their transport.
- Results, events and outbox resends go over the first of TSP and DIDComm that the VTC's DID document advertises (`preferred_via`). They use the recovery-aware TSP send: invite first when there is no relationship, and routing through the peer's own mediator when it is a different one (mirrors `vti_common::tsp_route`).
- Relationship invites are accepted from the VTC and the registry only. On every connect the bridge offers the VTC a relationship (`MediatorLink::relate`). This side's relationship store is in memory, and without the offer a VTC that kept its half would have its next job silently dropped after a bridge restart.
- `VtcLink` gains `send_via` to pin a transport.

**Registry check** (`registry_channel.rs`, `checks.rs`, `config.rs`)
- `BridgeRegistryChannel` takes a `Via`. The bridge registers a TSP channel and then a DIDComm channel, so `auto` resolves to TSP, then DIDComm, then HTTPS, through verify-trust's `choose_route`, with no fallback once chosen. This is the same semantics as verify-trust.
- Removed the refusal of `verify_trust.transport = "tsp"` while `bridge_checks` is on, and its test. Replaced with `tsp_is_taken_while_the_bridge_posts_checks` and `the_registry_is_queried_over_tsp_then_didcomm_then_https`.

**VTA** (`vta.rs`)
- vta-sdk 0.58 does offer this: `VtaClient::connect_didcomm_with_tsp` (feature `tsp`). When the VTA's DID document advertises `#tsp`, the bridge connects with a TSP leg: Trust Tasks go over TSP, and the DIDComm session holds the mediator socket. Otherwise it connects over DIDComm as before. If the TSP leg cannot be established, the bridge falls back to DIDComm with a warning, which is vta-sdk's own `Auto` policy. REST is still never used.

**Identity** (`identity.rs`)
- The minted `did:peer:2` advertises a `#tsp` `TSPTransport` service (bare mediator DID, the shape the TSP stack reads) next to `DIDCommMessaging`, so the VTC selects TSP. `check_reachable` also checks the TSP mediator, and accepts a TSP-only DID.
- A `did:peer` minted by an earlier release still works over DIDComm. Re-mint it to be reached over TSP.

**Wording**
- Crate docs, the Cargo description and keywords, `bridge.example.toml`, `README.md`, `crates/vgi-bridge/README.md`, `docs/BRIDGE.md`, `docs/RUNBOOK.md` and `docs/SETUP-GITHUB-VTC.md` now describe TSP, then DIDComm, where that is true. The did:webvh templates are told to carry a `TSPTransport` service. verify-trust's own three-binding text is untouched.

`Cargo.lock`: affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.31.0 to 0.31.1, the release that routes a relationship invite through a cross-mediator peer's `TSPTransport` mediator (VTI-56). No version bump: no release guard requires one, and the crate has no CHANGELOG.

## Security

- **TSP sender authentication is as strict as DIDComm's, or stricter.** A TSP frame becomes a document only with a sender VID that the TSP unpack verified (`sender` and `verified` must both be set; `tsp_sender`). There is no plaintext-sender fallback. A TSP frame without a proven sender is dropped, where DIDComm would pass it on with no sender. The proven VID goes to `DocChecker::check`, so the `identityMismatch` refusal applies unchanged: a job is believed only when the TSP-authenticated sender is the VTC's DID and the issuer and proof check out.
- **Registry replies:** `RegistryReplies::route` takes a reply only when the authenticated sender is the registry DID, the thread is a query in flight, and the reply came over the transport the query went out on. A correlated reply over the other transport is not an answer. New end-to-end regression test, `tests/registry_tsp.rs::a_correlated_tsp_reply_from_another_vid_is_not_believed`: on the in-process mediator, Mallory sends a valid TSP reply on the query's thread naming the registry as issuer. The query times out, and a canary sent afterwards proves the link stayed live and that Mallory's message surfaced with Mallory as the proven sender. A forged TSP signature, as opposed to an impostor, is refused by the SDK's unpack before it reaches the bridge.
- **Envelope strictness:** inbound TSP payloads must be the published binding envelope; bare documents are dropped.
- **Relationships:** invites are accepted only from the VTC and the registry. The SDK records an invite before the bridge sees it, so a stranger's invite is reset (`reset_relationship`), not just left unanswered, and TSP application messages from DIDs the link does not serve are dropped before they reach the job path (covered by `tests/registry_tsp.rs`: the stranger's invite and payload never surface and leave no relationship). Only the VTC's request ids (at most 256 bytes) are remembered for picking the reply transport.
- **VTA fallback:** TSP to DIDComm, only when the TSP leg itself failed (`VtaError::TspTransport`). Both are end-to-end confidential and authenticated, so this is not a downgrade. REST is still never used for key release.

## Notes

- A minted `did:peer` carries the mediator DID once per service. When the mediator's own DID is too long for both services, `init` mints a DIDComm-only `did:peer` with a warning, and the VTC reaches it over DIDComm.
- Not covered end to end here: a VTC-to-bridge job over TSP against a real `vtc-service`. That path is covered by the link's unit tests and the TSP registry test on the same link, and needs a deployment check.

## Checks (targeted)

- `cargo test -p vgi-bridge`: all pass, including the new `tests/registry_tsp.rs` (2) and the unit tests in `transport`, `registry_channel`, `checks`, `config` and `identity`.
- `cargo clippy -p vgi-bridge --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.

title: chore: release 0.7.0
body:
Bumps the workspace to **0.7.0**. That covers the workspace version, the five internal `vgi-*` and `verify-trust` dependency pins, and the lockfile entries for the eight workspace crates; no external dependency moves. It also points `bridge.example.toml`'s `[verify_trust] version` at `v0.7.0`.

This is a **minor** release because it carries a breaking default change.

## What's in it, since v0.6.0

- **verify-trust (BREAKING):** `--resource-format` defaults to **`qualified`** (`<forge-host>/owner[/repo]`), in the CLI, `ResourceFormat` and the action (#114, step 2 of #109).
  - VTC-written grants are already qualified, since the VTC never writes `owner/repo`.
  - Bridge-bootstrapped workflows already set `resource-format: qualified`.

title: feat(verify-trust)!: default --resource-format to qualified
body:
Step 2 of #109. **This is a breaking change, so release it as 0.7.0.** Step 3, removing `legacy`, is for the release after, so this PR refers to #109 rather than closing it.

## Why

SEC-4045 / VGI-03: under `legacy`, the resource that alone scopes a signer to a repository is a bare `owner/repo` slug.
- The slug names no forge, so `github.com/acme` and `codeberg.org/acme` can't be told apart.
- #103 bounded the legacy form, but the real fix is the qualified grammar. That grammar is `<forge-host>/owner[/repo]`, validated and lowercased, with a fallback that must *contain* the resource.

## Who this affects

I checked the prerequisite from #109 against the code:
- **VTC-written grants are already qualified.** `vtc-service`'s `git_ns::model::Resource` refuses an unqualified `owner/repo`, and `docs/03-vtc/git-namespaces.md` (§ Limits) says legacy tuples are **not dual-written**.
- **Bridge-bootstrapped workflows already pin it.** Both the GitHub and Forgejo plans write `resource-format: qualified` explicitly.

So the only runs affected are hand-written workflows or CLI invocations that **rely on the default _and_ use hand-issued `owner/repo` grants**. They now query the qualified form. To keep the old behaviour for one more release they pin `resource-format: legacy`; the better fix is to reissue the grants in qualified form.

**Before release:**
- [ ] Announce the change to operators, with that one-line opt-out (#109).
- [ ] Confirm with the VTC or registry operators that no namespace depends on hand-issued legacy grants. The code shows the VTC never writes them, but it can't show what was issued by hand.

## What

- **`ResourceFormat`:** `#[default]` moves from `Legacy` to `Qualified`.
- **CLI:** `--resource-format` now defaults to `qualified`, with updated help text.
- **Action** (`.github/actions/verify-trust/action.yml`):
  - The `resource-format` default is now `"qualified"`, and the `resource` and `fallback-resource` descriptions put qualified first.
  - **The flag is now always passed**, where before it was left out for `legacy`. A `version:` pinned to a release before this one defaults to legacy, so leaving the flag out would silently run that release in the other form.
  - Only `qualified` or `legacy` are accepted; anything else fails before the binary runs.
  - It needs `version` ≥ **v0.4.13**, the release that added the flag. Older releases also lack every SEC-4045 fix.
- **Docs** (README, `crates/verify-trust/README.md`, `docs/RUNBOOK.md`):
  - The default and the migration steps are updated.
  - Corrected the claim that "the VTC can write both forms": it doesn't.

## Tests

- **`resource.rs`:** a new `qualified_is_the_default` test checks the default derives `github.com/acme/widgets` from the GitHub CI environment. The legacy passthrough test is kept, renamed `legacy_still_passes_values_through_untouched`.
- **`main.rs`:** a new `the_cli_defaults_to_the_qualified_form` test checks that clap's default matches `ResourceFormat::default()`, and that `--resource-format legacy` is still accepted.
- **Action:** `ci_workflow_hardening` still passes. `action-selftest` feeds `resource-format` shell syntax, which the new `case` now refuses before the binary runs, so the run still fails without executing anything.
- All of these pass on Rust 1.99:
  - `cargo fmt --all --check`
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`
  - `cargo test --workspace`
  - `cargo test -p did-git-sign --features insecure-policy-bypass`

title: fix(vta-service): the hand-off re-grant hint runs as printed
body:
When an expiring ephemeral without a one-time hand-off tries to roll over (VTI-ACL-053/054), the refusal prints a re-grant. Two things in it were wrong:

- **`pnm acl delete --did <did>`**: `acl delete` takes the DID positionally (`AclCommands::Delete { did }`), so clap rejected the command before it reached the VTA. Now `pnm acl delete <did>`.
- **The `pnm acl create` dropped the entry's capabilities.** Deleting the row drops them, so a holder client provisioned with `pnm contexts create --admin-holder` (OpenVTC setup) came back without `persona-holder` and was then refused the holder's attribute pool. The hint now echoes the row's own capabilities (`--capabilities persona-holder` for that case). It never adds any, so an integration is not told to take holder authority it was not given.

Also corrects the same `acl delete` spelling in `docs/03-vtc/non-interactive-setup.md`. `vta-service/CHANGELOG.md` is git-cliff generated and left alone.

Found from OpenVTC setup, where the printed re-grant failed as written (OpenVTC/openvtc#401 now prints the correct commands on its own instructions page).

## Testing

- `an_expiring_ephemeral_cannot_roll_over_to_a_permanent_successor` now asserts the positional delete, and that an entry with no capabilities is not told to take any.
- New `the_regrant_hint_carries_the_entrys_capabilities`: a `persona-holder` entry's hint carries `--capabilities persona-holder`.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p vta-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test -p vta-service --lib -- provision_integration` (68 passed) pass. Full workspace suite left to CI.

title: test(vta-service): judge the live-prover test after the proof, not by sampling during it
body:
live_prover_provisions_acl_and_completes_cross_mediator_trust_ping sampled
the candidate transport's state every 20 ms while the proof ran and
panicked if the proof finished first. A proof that connected and completed
inside one interval failed with "proof finished before candidate

once in a parallel harness run.

(live_prover.rs) and has just trust-pinged through it, so the test now
awaits the proof (bounded at 10 s) and asserts once that the transport is
installed and connected.

title: fix: setup's ACL instructions cover an existing context and a retry
body:
The ACL instructions page printed only `pnm contexts create`, which refuses a context that already exists. A retry after the VTA refuses the rollover to the long-term admin (VTI-ACL-054) also needs the setup DID's entry re-created, because the hand-off is fixed when an entry is created.

The page now shows both paths, carrying the same grant:

| Situation | Command |
|---|---|
| New context (`F2` copies) | `pnm contexts create --id <ctx> --name "OpenVTC" --admin-did <did> --admin-expires 1h --admin-holder --admin-handoff` |
| Existing context / retry | `pnm acl delete <did>` (only if the DID already has an entry), then |
| (`F3` copies the create) | `pnm acl create --did <did> --role admin --contexts <ctx> --expires 1h --handoff --capabilities persona-holder` |

Flags verified against `pnm-cli`'s `ContextsCommands::Create` and `AclCommands::{Create, Delete}` (R3.6).

The VTA's own re-grant suggestion for this refusal (`vta-service/src/operations/provision_integration/mod.rs`) passes `--did` to `acl delete`, which takes the DID positionally, and leaves out `persona-holder`. The failure screen now recognises that refusal and points at the instructions page instead. The VTA's text needs fixing upstream in verifiable-trust-infrastructure.

## Testing

- Tests pin every flag on both grant commands, the positional DID on `acl delete`, the setup DID and typed context id reaching all three commands, and clean line continuations.
- Tests for recognising the missing-hand-off refusal and not mistaking other failures for it.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p openvtc --bin openvtc vta_` pass.

title: chore(deps): take affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk 0.8.39 — a deactivated did:webvh no longer resolves
body:
## Why

SEC-4045 / VGI-04. Before `affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk` 0.8.39 (affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#907), resolving a `did:webvh` whose log ends in a deactivation succeeded and returned the last DID document, keys included. The deactivation showed up only in metadata, and the client threw that metadata away. So anything verifying signatures through the cache SDK kept accepting a deactivated `did:webvh` signer with no end date.

0.8.39 makes that resolution fail: `DIDWebVHError::DeactivatedError`, surfaced as a `DIDCacheError::DIDError` whose message names the DID as deactivated. `did:web` already behaved this way, because a deactivated `did:web` returns a 404. `did-scid` 0.2.8 brings the same fix to `did:scid:vh`.

## What

- `Cargo.toml`: the workspace floor for `affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk` goes from `0.8.37` to `0.8.39`, with a one-line comment saying why 0.8.39 is the minimum.
- `deploy/nitro/enclave-proxy/Cargo.toml`: `0.8.37` to `0.8.39`.
- `Cargo.lock`, `deploy/nitro/enclave-proxy/Cargo.lock`: `cargo update -p affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk -p did-scid` in each. No bare `cargo update` was run.

### Lockfile package changes (identical in both lockfiles)

| package | from | to |
|---|---|---|
| affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk | 0.8.38 | 0.8.40 |
| did-scid | 0.2.7 | 0.2.8 |

No other package changes version. In the root lockfile, the dependency lists of those two crates now point at the `base64 0.22.1` that is already in the graph, where they used to point at `base64 0.21.7`. No package was added or removed. Cargo picked 0.8.40, the newest release that satisfies `>= 0.8.39`. Its changelog says it is clippy-only (`collapsible_if`) with no behaviour change on top of 0.8.39.

## Verification (local, rustc 1.99.0 `stable` as in CI, macOS arm64)

Root workspace:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: ok
- `cargo metadata --locked`: ok, so the lockfile satisfies the manifests
- `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: ok
- `cargo +stable test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: ok, 5276 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo +stable test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: ok, 2504 passed, 0 failed

`deploy/nitro/enclave-proxy`:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: ok
- `cargo +stable clippy --release --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: ok
- `cargo +stable build --release --locked`: ok
- `cargo +stable test --release --locked --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=1`: ok, 39 passed

## Compatibility

**Behaviour change for every consumer:** a deactivated `did:webvh` or `did:scid:vh` no longer resolves. Code that relied on getting the last document back now gets an error.

I checked this repo for anything that depends on resolving a deactivated DID and found nothing:
- there is no DID deactivation flow
- in VTC member rotation, the old DID is a `did:key`
- audit checkpoint verification resolves the community's current DID
- `vta-sdk/src/didcomm_light.rs` now errors when it resolves a deactivated VTA DID, which is the intended effect

No API changes and no code changes were needed.

body:
affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.31.1 (affinidi-tdk-rs #913) routes a TSP
relationship invite to a peer on another mediator through the mediator the

another mediator. vti_56_a_cold_relationship_with_a_cross_mediator_peer_forms
now uses peers that name their mediator by DID, as a VTI-provisioned DID
does, and holds both halves.

## Why

SEC-4045 / VGI-04. Before `affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk` 0.8.39 (affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#907), resolving a `did:webvh` whose log ends in a deactivation returned the **last DID document, keys included**. `didwebvh-rs` flags deactivation only in metadata, and the resolver dropped it. As a result, a retired DID kept being trusted indefinitely, as a peer, a signer or a join target, by anything in openvtc that resolves through the cache SDK.

0.8.39 makes that resolution fail, as a deactivated `did:web` (a 404) already did. `did-scid` 0.2.8 does the same for `did:scid:vh`.
