  - `did-scid` 0.2.7 → 0.2.8

No source changes.

## Compatibility

A deactivated did:webvh no longer resolves. I surveyed the repo for code relying on the old behaviour and found none: openvtc has no DID-deactivation flow. The visible effect is wording. title: chore(deps): take affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk 0.8.39 — a deactivated did:webvh issuer is refused
body:
## Why

SEC-4045 / VGI-04. Before `affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk` 0.8.39 (affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#907), resolving a `did:webvh` whose log ends in a deactivation entry returned the last DID document as `Ok`, with its keys still in it.

The gateway's proof verifier (`src/proof.rs`, `IssuerKeys::resolve_vm_for_purpose`) resolves the issuer through the cache SDK and takes the signing key from the document it gets back. So on 0.8.38 the gateway **accepts a `push/provision` / `push/wake` proof signed by a deactivated did:webvh issuer**.

With 0.8.39, resolving a deactivated did:webvh fails. The verifier already treats any resolution failure as a final refusal ("could not resolve the proof issuer's DID document"), so no code change is needed. `did-scid` 0.2.8 does the same for `did:scid:vh`.

`src/tsp.rs` `check_advertised` only logs a warning when resolution fails, so this change doesn't affect what it does.

## What

- `Cargo.toml`: `affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk` floor goes from `0.8.38` to `0.8.39`. A comment next to the existing 0.8.37 SSRF note explains why this is a floor.
- `Cargo.lock`: only the two targeted packages were updated (`cargo update -p affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk -p did-scid`).

## Lockfile changes

| package | from | to |
|---|---|---|
| affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk | 0.8.38 | 0.8.40 (highest compatible on crates.io) |
| did-scid | 0.2.7 | 0.2.8 |

No other package moved. The graph has one copy of each.

## Verification

All run locally on Rust 1.99.0 (`+stable`, which matches CI's `stable`), with `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings"` as CI sets it:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: ok
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: ok
- `cargo test --all-targets`: ok, 141 passed (84 lib, 25 + 32 integration), 0 failed
- `cargo deny check`: advisories, bans, licenses and sources all ok

No regression test is added. The existing `IssuerKeys` / document-auth tests use `did:key` issuers with a default resolver. A loopback deactivated-did:webvh test would need new infrastructure: a dev-dependency to build and sign a webvh log with a deactivation entry, a local HTTP server, and a `HostPolicy` opt-out. No API or source changes. The only change in behaviour is the intended one: a deactivated `did:webvh` / `did:scid:vh` issuer can no longer authorise provision or wake.

title: feat(vtc): bind the community's own check to a uniqueness pseudonym server-side
body:
Follow-up to #1874. It restores `singleMembership` (one person, one membership) for a community that checks identities itself.

**Why.** Before #1874, the community's own identity check produced an `IdentityVerificationCredential`. Its `credentialSubject.pseudonym` fed the uniqueness check. Since #1874 that check is a `vetted/1` statement, whose registry schema can't carry a pseudonym. So a community desk check proved identity but could never satisfy `singleMembership`.

**Design.** Uniqueness is the community's internal bookkeeping, so it never goes in a credential. The community binds the pseudonym in its own store when it records the check.

## Changes
- **Issue:** `vtc/endorsements/issue` for `vetted/1` accepts a namespaced payload extension, `ext["org.openvtc.uniqueness"] = { "pseudonym": "<value>" }` (exported as `routes::endorsements::UNIQUENESS_EXT`).
  - The VTC claims the pseudonym in the existing pseudonym store against the member's DID, before minting. It stores only the digest key, as today.
  - The pseudonym is **never written into the credential**, and a test checks that.
  - A pseudonym already held by another member is refused with `taskFailed` / `details.reason: "conflict"`, the same collision behaviour personhood assert has. Nothing is minted. If minting fails after binding, the binding is released.
  - A misplaced or malformed extension is `malformedRequest`.
- **Personhood assert under `singleMembership`:**
  - External identity credentials still use `credentialSubject.pseudonym` as before.
  - Otherwise, the community's own `vetted/1` satisfies uniqueness only if the community holds a binding for that member DID.
- **Release:**
  - Revoking the `vetted/1` row releases the binding it made. A binding from an outside provider survives that revoke.
  - Member purge releases all of the member's bindings, as before.
- **Store:** a claim row gains an optional `endorsementId`. It is serde-defaulted, so existing rows still read. New helpers: `claim_for_statement`, `is_bound` and `release_for_statement`.
- **CLI and client:** `cnm member endorse … --uniqueness-pseudonym <value>`. vtc-client gets an additive `issue_endorsement_with_ext`.
- **Docs:** `personhood-and-graph.md` has a new "binding at issue" subsection, and the `acceptedIdvps` text is updated. The OpenAPI snapshot and `wire.ts` are regenerated for the field-doc change.

## Not in this PR
- **Admin console:** it has no issue path for this check yet, and the docs say so.
- **Spec text:** the `org.openvtc.uniqueness` extension isn't described in the Trust Tasks spec text. The generated schema already accepts any namespaced `ext`.

## Checks
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` are clean.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vta-sdk --no-fail-fast` passes, including 34 endorsements integration tests on this branch.

title: feat(vtc): bind the community's own check to a uniqueness pseudonym server-side (#1876)
body:
feat(vtc): bind the community's own check to a uniqueness pseudonym server-side (#1876)

A community enforcing `personhood.singleMembership` could not satisfy it with
its own `vetted/1` identity check, because the statement has no member for a
pseudonym. The binding now happens server-side, at issue.

- `vtc/endorsements/issue/0.1` under `vetted/1` reads the payload extension
  `ext["org.openvtc.uniqueness"] = { "pseudonym": "<value>" }`. It is never
  written into the credential. The pseudonym is bound to the subject in the
  existing pseudonym store (`members::pseudonym::claim_for_statement`), which
  stores only the community-scoped salted digest. The claim row is tagged
  with the statement's endorsement id. The binding is made before anything is
  minted, and released again if minting fails.
- A pseudonym already bound to another member refuses the issue with
  `AppError::Conflict`: `taskFailed` with `details.reason` `conflict`, the
  same collision semantics personhood assert already has. Nothing is minted.
  No declared `endorsements/issue` code fits a duplicate person, and
  `claimSchemaViolation` would tell the caller to fix a claim that is valid.
- The extension is read only under `vetted/1`, and only as
  `{ "pseudonym": "<non-empty string>" }`. Anything else is
  `malformedRequest`.
- At personhood assert under `singleMembership`, the community's own
  `vetted/1` statement about the member satisfies uniqueness only when the
  community holds a binding for that member DID (`pseudonym::is_bound`).
  Credentials from an accepted IDVP still use `credentialSubject.pseudonym`.
- `vtc/endorsements/revoke/0.1` on a `vetted/1` row releases the binding it
  made (`pseudonym::release_for_statement`). A binding an outside provider's
  credential made is untagged and is kept. Purge still releases every binding
  of the member.
- vtc-client gains `issue_endorsement_with_ext` (additive).
  `cnm member endorse` gains `--uniqueness-pseudonym`.

Docs: personhood-and-graph (binding at issue, acceptedIdvps, the weak
case), the `acceptedIdvps` field description (OpenAPI snapshot and wire.ts
regenerated).

body:
## Summary
- Implements the `// TODO(notify)` left in `vtc-service/src/step_up_passkey.rs` (#1872): a signed `vtc/members/step-up-passkey-notice/0.1` notice to the member whenever a step-up passkey is enrolled for them or revoked from them.

title: feat!: record the community's own identity check as a vetted/1 statement
body:
The community now records its own identity check as a **`vetted/1` statement** it issues for itself. This replaces the plain `IdentityVerificationCredential`. The default personhood policy reads that statement.

Companions:
- trustoverip/dtgwg-vsc-registry#24 (merged): `vetted/1` issuer widened, vetter-only members all-or-nothing.
- trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#697 (merged, released): the `endorsements/issue` spec.

**Why.** That credential was evidence: the same act a vetter records, made by the community. It belongs under the registry predicate, where it has a definition and a place in the fail-closed accept list. It doesn't belong in an ad-hoc type. Personhood itself stays the community's decision on the VMC.

## Changes
- **`vta-sdk` (breaking → 0.59)**
  - `VettedObjectValue.identity_commitment`, `card_digest_multibase` and `declared_relationship` are now `Option`, and all-or-nothing in `check_shape`.
  - New: `vetter_members() -> Option<VetterMembers>` and `has_no_vetter_members()`.
  - Vetter paths stay strict: `sign_statement`, `check_against_card` and `check_against_session` require all three.
- **`vtc/endorsements/issue`, when `typeUri` is `vetted/1`:**
  - The community mints the statement: issuer is the community, `issuerScope: public`, with a revocation slot.
  - It cites this request: `taskContext` is the request `id`, and `taskDigestMultibase` is its task digest.
  - The claim must name this community and carry none of the vetter-only members. Otherwise it's refused with `claimSchemaViolation`.
  - `witnessed/1` and `presented/1` are still `predicateNotIssuable`.
  - `credentials/idvc.rs` and the `IdentityVerificationCredential` reservation are removed. A seeded row is withdrawn at boot; an operator's row is kept.
- **Personhood:** the default `personhood.rego` accepts the community's own `vetted/1` (issuer and `object.value.community` are the community, the subject is the applicant). A workspace-authored #1859 default is auto-replaced at boot; an operator-authored one is kept.
- **Admission counting** never counts a statement without the vetter-only members. It records the new failure code `not-a-vetter-statement`.
- **Docs, OpenAPI snapshot and `wire.ts`** are updated, including the operator note in `policy-upgrade-dtg-v1.md`.

## ⚠ Open question before merge: `singleMembership`
The old credential carried `credentialSubject.pseudonym`. `members/pseudonym.rs` reads that for the `singleMembership` uniqueness check, which stops one person from holding two memberships. A `vetted/1` value can't carry a pseudonym, because the registry schema has `additionalProperties: false`.

So after this PR, a community **can no longer be its own identity-verification provider for `singleMembership`**. It would need an accepted outside provider. The docs and the `acceptedIdvps` description say so. This needs a decision; see the PR comments.

## Checks (local)
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` are clean.
- `cargo test -p vta-sdk -p vtc-service`: all pass except 6 admin-ui tests that need the built `admin-ui/dist`, which isn't present in that worktree.
- Rest of the workspace: 5256 passed, 0 failed.

title: feat!: record the community's own identity check as a vetted/1 statement (#1874)
body:
feat!: record the community's own identity check as a vetted/1 statement (#1874)

* feat(vta-sdk)!: vetted/1 vetter-only members are optional and all-or-nothing

Registry `vetted/1` (trustoverip/dtgwg-vsc-registry#24) admits the community
itself as issuer of a statement recording its own identity check. Such a
statement carries none of the three vetter-only members; a vetter's statement
carries all three. The schema makes them all-or-nothing (`dependentRequired`).

BREAKING CHANGE: in `vta_sdk::protocols::vetting::VettedObjectValue`,
`identity_commitment`, `card_digest_multibase` and `declared_relationship`
change from `String` / `String` / `VettingRelationship` to
`Option<String>` / `Option<String>` / `Option<VettingRelationship>`
(serde: skipped when `None`, defaulted when absent). Code building a
vetter's value wraps each in `Some(..)`; code reading one goes through the new
`VettedObjectValue::vetter_members() -> Option<VetterMembers<'_>>`
(`identity_commitment: &str`, `card_digest_multibase: &str`,
`declared_relationship: VettingRelationship`). Also new:
`VettedObjectValue::has_no_vetter_members()` and the `VetterMembers` struct.

- `CheckShape for VettedObjectValue` keeps the base58btc checks when the
  members are present, and refuses a value carrying only some of the three.
- Vetter paths stay strict: `vetting::statement::sign_statement` refuses a
  draft without all three; `VerifiedVettingStatement::check_against_card`
  and `check_against_session` answer `Binding("identityCommitment")` for a
  statement without them. `verify_statement` reads either kind.
- vtc-service admission counting never counts a statement without the
  vetter-only members (failure code `not-a-vetter-statement`): the
  community's own statement is personhood evidence, not admission evidence.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc)!: record the community's own identity check as a vetted/1 statement

The community no longer mints a plain `IdentityVerificationCredential` for its
own identity checks. It records them as a statement under registry `vetted/1`
(trustoverip/dtgwg-vsc-registry#24), issued under its own DID, so every
identity check in the graph has one shape whoever made it.

`vtc/endorsements/issue/0.1` with `typeUri`
`https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/vetted/1` now mints that statement
(`credentials::dtg::issue_vetted_statement`, via
`DTGCredential::new_vetted_vsc`): issuer the community, `issuerScope`
`public`, subject `subjectDid`, `object.value` the claim, revocation slot and
endorsement row like any other statement. The profile's required citation
names the issue request document itself: `taskContext` is its `id` and
`taskDigestMultibase` its task digest. The claim must be a `VettedObjectValue`
naming this community and carrying none of the vetter-only members
(`identityCommitment`, `cardDigestMultibase`, `declaredRelationship`);
anything else is `claimSchemaViolation`. `witnessed/1` and `presented/1` stay
`predicateNotIssuable`; `role:vetter` stays reserved.

Removed: `credentials::idvc`, the reserved `IdentityVerificationCredential`
type URI and its claim check, and its seeded Issues registration (a row the
seed wrote is withdrawn at boot; an operator's is kept).

The default `personhood.rego` replaces the IdentityVerificationCredential rule
with one accepting a `StatementCredential` under `vetted/1` whose issuer is
`input.community_did`, whose subject is the applicant, and whose
`object.value.community` is this community. The witnessed/1 rule is
unchanged. The statement is evidence; personhood stays the community's
decision on the VMC. A workspace-authored default from #1859 refuses that
statement, so `is_stale_personhood_default` gains a probe for it and the boot
upgrade replaces it (operator-authored policies are never touched).

The community's own statement carries no pseudonym, so it does not satisfy
`personhood.singleMembership`; that still needs an accepted outside IDVP.

Docs: personhood-and-graph, credentials, policy-upgrade-dtg-v1 §2,
community-lifecycle, vtc-mvp, the retired endorsement-types/register spec.
OpenAPI snapshot and admin-ui wire.ts regenerated (doc text only).

title: fix(verify-trust): the git path refuses an empty repository or range
body:
## Why

This is a follow-up from the security team's verification of the SEC-4045 remediation. All 8 findings are confirmed closed on `b83f178`.

> the bridge still builds VerifyTrustArgs with an empty repo_dir and range (checks.rs:392). It is unused right now under verify_prepared_with_facts, but a future switch back to verify_prepared would silently reopen VGI-01.

That's right. git reads `-C ""` as the current directory, so the empty fields only stay harmless while nothing passes them to the git path.

## What

- **`verify_prepared_with`**, and so `verify_prepared`, now **refuses an empty `repo_dir` or `range`** before verifying anything. The error names `verify_prepared_with_facts` as the path for callers that have no checkout.
  - The check runs up front, not only when a platform merge reaches git. A caller that drifts back onto the git path fails on its first check of *any* commit, so the regression can't sit unnoticed until someone opens an "Update branch" PR.
- The `VerifyTrustArgs` docs now say which entry points read `repo_dir` and `range`.
- The bridge comment at `checks.rs:392` explains why the fields stay empty: the git path refuses them.
- The verify-trust unit tests' `args_for_registry` now uses a placeholder checkout (`.` and `HEAD`). Those tests never reach git.

## Tests

- New `the_git_path_refuses_an_empty_repository_or_range`: the four empty combinations (repo, range, whitespace range, both) are each refused **before the registry is queried**. The facts path still accepts the same empty fields.
- **Regression check:** I temporarily switched the bridge back to `verify_prepared_with`. **3 bridge tests fail**, all with the new error, and **two of them have no platform merge at all**: `the_real_verifier_trusts_a_namespace_grant_and_refuses_the_rest` and `the_bridge_queries_the_registry_as_its_own_did_over_its_link`. The third is `an_update_branch_merge_is_recomputed_from_the_fetch`.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` all pass, on `44cf197`.

## Compatibility

A library caller passing an empty `repo_dir` or `range` to `verify_prepared` / `verify_prepared_with` now gets an error. The CLI always passes both, and the bridge uses `verify_prepared_with_facts`.

title: feat(vtc-service): step-up passkey self-revoke, change notices, approve-response 0.5
body:
## Summary
- A member can revoke their own step-up passkey (`auth/passkey/revoke/{start,finish}/0.2`), per the spec's Authorization section — `payload.subject` absent targets the producer, verified with their own remaining step-up passkeys. An administrator revoking for someone else is unchanged in effect, but is now gated inside `step_up_passkey::revoke_start`/`revoke_finish` rather than by `admin_signer`, which refused any non-admin signer before the handler ever ran.
- `auth/step-up/approve-response/0.5` is served alongside 0.4: 0.5 requires the approver's `assertionMethod` proof on every response (0.4 still admits an unsigned console-passkey answer); enforced by the spine's own proof policy (`IS_PROOF_REQUIRED`) before the handler runs. The 0.5 payload converts to 0.4's generated type to reach the one verifier rather than forking the logic — backed by a wire-identity test.
- The member-notification item (telling the member when a step-up passkey is enrolled or revoked for them by someone else) was pulled from this PR: it had no published Trust Task spec behind it, and `trust_task_manifest::every_bound_canonical_task_exists_in_the_registry` correctly rejects a sent type URI with nothing in the registry. It follows in a later PR once a `vtc/members/*` notice spec exists (alongside `removal-notice`/`break-glass-notice`); a `// TODO(notify)` marks the spot in `step_up_passkey.rs`.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib -- step_up_passkey_tasks:: step_up_passkey:: spine_proof_tests:: bound_step_up::` — 54 passed

The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.25.2` → `0.25.3` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.25.2` → `0.25.3` | patch |

| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.25.2` → `0.25.3` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.25.2` → `0.25.3` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.25.2` → `0.25.3` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.25.2` → `0.25.3` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.22.2` → `0.22.3` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.4.3`) | `0.4.2` → `0.4.3` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.4.2` → `0.4.3` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: fix!: a TSP relationship can be started with a peer on another mediator (VTI-56)
body:
A node that starts a TSP relationship with a peer on another mediator had
its invite refused by its own mediator (403 e.p.direct_delivery.denied,
"must be relayed through a routing envelope"), every attempt. The SDK
routes a control message across mediators only when it already knows the
peer's mediator, learned from a routed invite from the peer or set with
set_peer_mediator. An initiator has neither, and nothing here set it. That
is why the Farm VTC's TSP push to a member on the other mediator never left
its own mediator and fell back to DIDComm an hour later. The existing
cross-mediator tests pre-form the relationship (relate_directly), so they
never sent an invite.

vti_common::tsp_route records the peer's mediator (its DID document's #tsp
endpoint, which every caller already read to choose TSP) before any invite,
and its send_reestablishing sends the payload nested via that mediator
rather than [our_mediator, peer]. Used by:

- the push engine (trust_task_push), which already nested its payload;
- the VTA's outbound TSP (TspTransport): the D6 and idle re-establishing
  resends now nest instead of going direct, and a first contact with no
  relationship invites alongside the first send instead of waiting out the
  30 s reply timeout before D6 re-invites (OBS-09's ~31 s first mint);
- the VTC registry client and git-ns bridge client, whose TSP route
  [our_mediator, peer] could not reach a peer on another mediator at all.

The proper fix is in the SDK (fall back to the peer's DID document when no
mediator was learned). vti_56_a_cold_relationship_with_a_cross_mediator_peer_forms
pins the SDK's current refusal, so it will say when this can go.

Breaking: TspTransport::send_reestablishing and relate take the peer's
mediator.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>


## Testing

On the branch before rebasing onto main at d5642c09: `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast` and `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast` passed (7762 passed, 0 failed). The `transport-harness` TSP tests also passed, and clippy passed workspace-wide and under the `rest` and `tsp` reduced feature sets. After the rebase I re-ran clippy, fmt and `vti_56_a_cold_relationship_with_a_cross_mediator_peer_forms`.

Not covered: a live run on the Farm.

title: spec(vtc/endorsements): a community records its own identity checks as vetted/1
body:
When a community's own operators check a member's identity, they now record it as a `vetted/1` statement the community issues for itself. This replaces the reserved plain `IdentityVerificationCredential` that #695 added. It companions trustoverip/dtgwg-vsc-registry#24 (merged), which lets the community issue `vetted/1` and makes the three vetter-only members all-or-nothing.

**Why.** That credential was evidence: the same act a vetter records, made by the community. Personhood is governed status and stays the community's decision on its VMC. Recording the check as `vetted/1` gives it a registry definition and a place in a verifier's fail-closed accept list. It also gives every identity check in the graph one shape. External identity credentials from accepted providers are unchanged.

## Changes
- **`vtc/endorsements/issue/0.1`**
  - `typeUri` `…/dtg/vsc/vetted/1` mints the community's `vetted/1` statement: issuer is the community, `issuerScope: public`, and the `claim` goes in `object.value`.
  - The `claim` MUST validate against the registry's `vetting.schema.json`, and `claim.community` MUST be this community.
  - The `claim` MUST NOT carry `identityCommitment`, `cardDigestMultibase` or `declaredRelationship`. The salt behind the commitment must never reach the community, and the community links to its vetters' statements by subject.
  - `taskContext` and `taskDigestMultibase` cite this request (SPEC §4.9.3 task digest). `outcomeEvidence` and `retention: durable` are added, as SPEC §7.3 item 20 requires for a cited request.
  - A worked desk-check example is added; its digest is computed from the printed request.
  - `predicateNotIssuable` no longer covers `vetted/1`, and still covers `witnessed/1` and `presented/1`.
- **`vtc/endorsement-types/*`, `vtc/endorsements/{list,show,revoke}` and the shared schemas**: only `role:vetter` is reserved. A row's `typeUri` is a registered predicate IRI or `role:vetter`.
- **`vtc/members/personhood/assert/0.1` and `acceptedIdvps`**: the evidence is an accepted provider's W3C VC or the community's own `vetted/1`. Personhood itself is the community's decision on the VMC.

**Bindings:** there are no type, field or error-code changes in any language, only doc comments and embedded schema text.

**Checks:** all green.
- `validate`, ceremonies and `check-bindings`
- Rust workspace and `--features validate`
- TS 79/79, Go, Dart 74/74

**Note:** `vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.2` still counts statements only from issuers holding the vetter role. So a community-issued `vetted/1` is personhood evidence and doesn't count toward the admission threshold. That's intended.

title: test(proof): the verifier clock in the Go and TS tests never runs behind real time
body:
Since 2026-10-01 00:00 UTC, the Go and TS `proof` test suites fail on **every** PR and on main. This includes #697: `go test trust-tasks-go/proof` (stable and 1.22) and `trust-tasks-ts-proof`.

**Cause.** A date time bomb in the tests:
- The verifier clock is pinned at `2026-10-01T00:00:00Z` (Go `laterClock()`, TS `now`), so the September Rust interop fixture isn't "in the future".
- The sign-then-verify tests stamp `proof.created` with the *real* current time.
- Once real time passed the pinned instant, every fresh proof was hours ahead of the verifier. The verifier refuses those as `malformedProof` (`proof.created is more than 1m0s in the future`), so tests expecting `signatureInvalid` or `issuerMismatch` saw `malformedProof` instead.

**Fix.** Each pinned clock is now *the later of the pinned instant and the real time*. The interop fixture still verifies, and new signatures are never in the future. This is tests only, with no library change.

Locally: `go test ./...` in `trust-tasks-go/proof` is ok, and `npm test` in `trust-tasks-ts-proof` passes 16/16.

title: fix!: Keyring findings round — proof sets, verify-as-received, VTC delivery (VTI-44, VTI-45, VTI-50, VTI-56)
body:
Fixes the findings in Keyring's VTI upstream findings round (v1.78, 2026-09-30) that are defects in this repository. Each one is a separate commit; this PR's body is the changelog entry, so the detail is in each commit message.

## Breaking
- **VTI-44 — proof sets.** A VTC with several signing keys issues each credential with a proof set (`[eddsa-jcs-2022, mldsa44-jcs-2024]`). The VTA credential vault (`vault/credentials/receive`), status-list verification and vta-sdk vetting read `proof` as a single object and refused every such card (80 of 80 in the field). There is now one proof-set implementation in `vta_sdk::trust_task_proof::proof_set`, moved from vtc-service, which now re-exports it: every proof this build can check must verify, at least one is required, and all must name one signer. The vault verifies ML-DSA proofs through `TrustTaskVmResolver` and keeps the issuer binding. Public API: `vta_vault::receive` takes `IssuerKey`; `receive_di_vc` takes a `PurposeVmResolver`; `resolve_di_issuer_key` is replaced by `verify_di_issuer_proofs`. The vault now also refuses (as vtc-service already did, VTI-KEY-022) a credential proof not made for `assertionMethod`, and a `did:key` method other than `did:key:<id>#<id>`.
- **VTI-45 — verify the JSON as received.** Trust Task proofs were verified over a re-serialised `TrustTask`, so a correctly signed `.000Z` timestamp (JavaScript `toISOString()` on a whole second), a `+00:00` offset or a `null` optional member failed as a bad signature. New `verify_trust_task_proof_value` / `verify_approval_proof_value`. Every network ingress uses them: the VTA and VTC spines, auth, step-up, task consent, attestation, reply waiters, the SDK client, room-host and mobile-core. VTA handlers reach the received JSON through a task-local (`trust_tasks/received.rs`), used only when it matches the handler's document. `PendingReplies` now carries the received `Value`. affinidi-data-integrity rebuilds the proof config from its typed struct and drops `challenge`, `domain`, `expires`, `id` and `previousProof`. A proof carrying one of those is now refused up front with a cause naming it.

## Fixes
- **VTI-50:** the VTC collected live pushes only. A push lost mid-session waited for the next reconnect and could expire first. An inbox catch-up loop (status-request every 30 s on the same socket; re-enables live delivery when messages wait) recovers them through the normal ack path. The VTA has the same gap, not changed here.
- **VTI-56:**
  - A push whose hand-off keeps failing (5 failed sends while queued) moves to the next advertised transport instead of retrying for the whole 1 h window (`vti_common::trust_task_push`). The last advertised transport still retries to its deadline.
  - Invitation and vetter-grant pushes now log "queued", not "delivered", when only queued (R1.1).
- **VTI-51:** the VTC retried its first mediator connect only once. It now retries with capped, jittered backoff, and every error path after `profile_add` calls `graceful_shutdown`.
- **VTI-53:** `pnm` / `cnm` / `vta bootstrap open` consumed the single-use request seed even when they wrote nothing. That destroyed a template bundle's keys, and broke `cnm`'s own follow-up hint. Inspection keeps the seed; only a successful `pnm --out` consumes it.
- **VTI-47:** the git-ns projector scanned every member every 5 s even with no namespace bound (~7% idle CPU). It now checks the snapshot first.
- **VTI-11:** both setup summaries print the offline `vtc acl add` command for seeding the first admin before the install is claimed.
- **OBS-02:** admin-remove of an already-departed member re-ran the removal and sent a second notice. It is now `notFound`.
- **OBS-04:** invitation list rows mixed `+00:00`-with-microseconds and `Z`. They now use one form.
- fmt of the test files #1862 moved to `vtc-service/tests/it/`.

## Not addressed here
VTI-01 and VTI-13 are by design. VTI-20 needs a spec change first. VTI-48 is a public URL. VTI-49 and VTI-51 (mid-session reconnect) are in the messaging SDK / did-hosting. VTI-55 and VTI-Q38 are openvtc. OBS-05 is the mediator. For VTI-56, the root cause of the TSP attempts failing is still open. Cross-mediator nesting exists (#1559), and the community's own mediator saw no TSP line at all, so the failure may be on the VTC side. One suspect is relationship (re)formation via the non-nested `form_relationship_routed`. The Farm mediators' relay settings are a second suspect.

## Known caveat
For VTI-56, the escalation's abandon is a non-atomic read-modify-write of the outbox entry. A TSP send that succeeds just as the push switches transport can deliver twice.

## Testing
Locally, before the last merge of main:
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: green.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 1 failure, the census path #1862 broke, since fixed on main by #1864.
- fmt and clippy (workspace, `vta-service --features rest`, `vtc-service --features vetting-pcs`): clean.

After merging main (#1864/#1865): clippy, fmt and the vta-service and vtc-service census/conformance tests are green.

Not run separately: plain `cargo test -p vta-sdk`, whose `typed_proof_verify` needs a feature only workspace unification turns on (reportedly already the case on main).

The seed is the only key that opens the bundle, so inspecting a template bundle destroyed the integration's keys, and cnm's own follow-up hint (`cnm auth login --credential-bundle`) could never succeed (VTI-53). Inspection now opens with the seed kept and says where it is. pnm consumes it only after a successful --out write, so a refused bundle no longer costs a fresh request cycle either. open_armored_bundle_keeping_secret and consume_request_secret are now public. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * perf(vtc-service): skip the git-ns member scan when no namespace projects roles The projector ticks every 5 s and project_roles listed and decoded every member before looking for a bound bridge namespace, so a community using no git namespaces paid ~7% idle CPU for nothing (VTI-47). It now checks the snapshot first and returns before the scan. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * fix(vtc-service): removing an already-departed member is notFound A tombstoned or historical member row with no ACL entry counted as removable, so a second admin-remove re-ran the ceremony, audited a second removal and pushed a second removal notice (OBS-02). Such a subject is now admin-remove:notFound (self-remove:notMember). A live member row without an ACL entry (#1194) stays removable. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * fix(vtc-service): setup summary names the offline admin grant The ACL is empty until the install URL is claimed, so the setup's admin DID cannot authenticate before then, and neither summary said how to seed it without a browser (VTI-11). Both now print the runbook's Path B command (`vtc --config acl add --did --role admin`); `setup --from` as offline_admin_grant=. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * fix(vtc-service): one timestamp form per invitation list row issuedAt and revokedAt used chrono's default (+00:00, microseconds) beside a validUntil echoed from the signed credential (Z, whole seconds), so one row mixed two formats (OBS-04). The record's instants are now written as whole-second Z. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * fix(vtc-service): collect missed live pushes and retry a failed mediator connect VTI-50: the VTC receives only by live delivery. The mediator redelivers the stored inbox when a socket enables live delivery (every connect), but nothing redelivers it in between, so a live push that did not arrive waited for the next token-refresh reconnect and messages with a shorter expiry were swept uncollected. Every 30 s the VTC now sends a Message Pickup 3.0 status-request on its one socket and, when a message has waited over 30 s, re-sends live-delivery-change(true), which makes the mediator redeliver the inbox down the live stream — the same path as a connect, so redelivered messages go through the delivery layer and are acked as usual. No second socket. VTI-51: a failed first connect left messaging off until restart. The connect is now retried with capped exponential backoff and full jitter until it succeeds or the VTC shuts down, and build_messaging tears the ATM down (graceful_shutdown) on every error path after profile_add, so a retry never leaks a socket that duels for the mediator's one-per-DID slot. An established session's reconnect remains the SDK websocket's, which retries indefinitely. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * fix(vti-common): escalate a push whose hand-off keeps failing; log queued, not delivered VTI-56: a push attempt whose send kept failing (a TSP relay to a peer on another mediator) was retried for its whole hour-long ATTEMPT_WINDOW before moving to the next transport. The window is for silence — an accepted message not yet collected. A refused hand-off is a definitive answer, so after FAILED_SENDS_BEFORE_ESCALATION (5) failed sends inside the window the push now moves to the next transport the recipient still advertises (VTI-TRN-042), settling the abandoned outbox entry so the delivery layer stops retrying it. Queue-full back-pressure does not count, a Sent attempt is still judged by the window, and the last advertised transport keeps retrying to the deadline — never a downgrade past what the peer advertises. Shared by the VTA and the VTC. R1.1: "delivered an invitation" and "vetter grant credential delivered again" were logged when the document was only queued. They now say queued (or returned, for the out-of-band offer channel); the push engine's "trust-task push delivered" remains the log line backed by evidence. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * fix(vta-vault)!: accept Data-Integrity proof sets on receive, status lists and vetting (VTI-44) A VTC holding several signing keys signs each credential once per key, so its `proof` is an array (`[eddsa-jcs-2022 by #key-0, mldsa44-jcs-2024 by #key-2]`). Every verifier outside vtc-service read `proof` as one object and refused every such credential: `vault/credentials/receive/0.1` failed with "Data-Integrity proof has no `verificationMethod`" (80/80 membership cards refused in the field), the vault's status-list check and the vetting client's proof check failed the same way, and the vault resolved Ed25519 keys only. The proof-set reader vtc-service already had moves to `vta_sdk::trust_task_proof::proof_set`, so there is one implementation: `proof_set` (object or array; skip a suite this build does not implement; refuse a malformed proof), `verify_one` (purpose-bound, VTI-KEY-022), `accept_all` (RequireAll over the checkable proofs, at least one, one signer), `require_suites`, and a new high-level `verify_proof_set`, which verifies each proof over the received JSON with `proof` removed and returns a `VerifiedProofSet` naming the one signer. vtc-service's module is reduced to re-exports plus the tests that pin its own `DidVmResolver`. - vta-vault: `di_verify::verify_di_issuer_proofs` replaces `resolve_di_issuer_key`. Every proof's `verificationMethod` must be under the credential `issuer`, checked before anything is parsed or resolved (issuer-spoofing guard); every checkable proof, ML-DSA-44 included, must verify for `assertionMethod`; a `bbs-2023` proof is refused on this path. `receive_di_vc` takes a `&dyn PurposeVmResolver` instead of one Ed25519 key, `receive` takes a new `IssuerKey` (None / Resolver / PublicKey) instead of `Option<&[u8]>`, and the status-list signature check uses the same rule. Callers pass `TrustTaskVmResolver::from_optional(did_cache)`. - vta-sdk vetting: `verify_attached_proof` accepts a proof set through the shared helper and returns the single signer DID. - vta-service: `vault/credentials/receive` and the credential-exchange issue path build the resolver from the DID cache. Behaviour that tightens: a credential proof must now declare `assertionMethod` and its key must be listed under that relationship in the issuer's DID document (VTI-KEY-022), and a `did:key` issuer's method must be `did:key:#` — the old vault path accepted any listed key and any `did:key` fragment. BREAKING CHANGE: `vta_vault::receive_di_vc` takes a resolver in place of the issuer public key; `vta_vault::receive` takes `IssuerKey` in place of `Option<&[u8]>`; `vta_vault::di_verify::resolve_di_issuer_key` is removed in favour of `verify_di_issuer_proofs`. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * fix(vta-sdk)!: verify Trust Task proofs over the JSON as received (VTI-45) Every ingress verified an eddsa-jcs-2022 proof over a re-serialisation of the parsed TrustTask

. trust-tasks-rs parses issuedAt/expiresAt and the proof's created as DateTime and writes them back in its own spelling, drops null optional members, and drops proof members its Proof type does not model. A correctly signed document from a JavaScript producer (toISOString() writes `.000Z` on every whole second), or one using +00:00, a one-digit fraction, a lowercase z, or `"threadId": null`, was refused as "proof verification failed". vta-sdk gains verify_trust_task_proof_value / verify_approval_proof_value, which verify over the received serde_json::Value with only the top-level `proof` removed, and read the proof from that JSON. The typed and value forms share one core, so purpose binding (VTI-KEY-022), the cached-DID refresh-and-retry (VTI-KEY-134), classify() and the wire text are unchanged. The typed forms remain, and are now documented as being for documents this process built. affinidi-data-integrity hashes a proof configuration it rebuilds from its typed DataIntegrityProof. That rebuild drops challenge, domain, expires, id and previousProof, and drops a null on any optional member. Such a proof is now refused up front as VerifyFailed, and its cause names the members. This is the documented limitation, not a workaround. Lifting it belongs upstream. Moved onto the received form: - vta-service: bind_document_to_sender, deliver_reply/verified_issuer, the spine's SPEC §7.2 item 7 check, pre-session auth/authenticate 0.2/0.3, and outbound reply verification. TSP replies now reach their waiter as received JSON rather than a re-serialised TrustTask. - vta-service handlers that check a proof themselves (the step-up gate, the task-consent decision, the attestation mnemonic export) go through trust_tasks::received. That is a task-local the spine sets to the received JSON, used only when it parses equal to the handler's document. - vtc-service: the spine's proof check (general and approval), resolve_holder (now reads the spine's verified signer), reply waiters over TSP and DIDComm, and the REST authenticate route. - vta-sdk client reply verification, AgentSession, ConsentRequest::verify, room-host's presenter (task-local, same rule), and vta-mobile-core's verify_signature. BREAKING (vta-service): PendingReplies::register now returns oneshot::Receiver, and PendingReplies::complete takes the received &Value instead of &TrustTask. New pub API (vta-sdk, re-exported by vti-common): verify_trust_task_proof_value, verify_approval_proof_value. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * test(vtc-service): census reads witnesses from tests/it; fmt the moved tests #1862 moved every vtc-service integration test under tests/it/ but the error-code census still read its witnesses from tests/, so every_declared_error_code_is_witnessed_or_baselined panicked on a missing file, and the moved files were never formatted (cargo fmt --check failed on 44 of them). Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore * fix(vta-service): keep contexts/create inside the VTI-08 stack budget VTI-45's received::scope was an async fn around tokio's task-local scope. On first poll a debug build moves the wrapped future, the whole validated dispatch, through a temporary in that wrapper's poll frame, which stays live under every handler. That was ~64 KiB: contexts/create needed ~468 KiB on macOS where main needs ~404, and on Linux CI it passed the 512 KiB budget (vti_08_context_create_fits_half_a_default_worker_stack). scope now returns tokio's TaskLocalFuture directly, and the spine builds it through boxed_task as it does handler futures. Measured back at main's 404 KiB. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore --------- Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore

title: feat(tsp): persist TSP relationship state across restarts
body:
## Summary

The gateway's TSP relationship state (invite/accept/Bidirectional, thread
digests, reply path, learned peer capability including the peer's mediator
DID) was held in the SDK's in-memory `InMemoryRelationshipStore`. A gateway
restart wiped it, and the SDK's §7.2.2 gate then silently dropped every
peer's application traffic until it re-invited.

- `src/relationships.rs`: `RelationshipFileKv`, a `RelationshipKv` over the
  same JSON-snapshot mechanism `Store` (`src/store.rs`) already uses for the
  push registry — in-memory map, debounced background flush, owner-only
  atomic writes (`secretfile::write_owner_only_atomic`, extracted from
  `store.rs` so both snapshots share it). Wrapped in the SDK's
  `PersistentRelationshipStore`, which gets every facet the trait keeps
  (state, digests, reply path, capability) for free from the same
  `get`/`put` calls — nothing extra was needed to also persist the learned
  peer-mediator mapping.
- Wired into the mediator listener via `ListenerConfig::relationship_store`
  (`src/didcomm.rs`), built from `GATEWAY_RELATIONSHIPS_FILE` (falls back to
  in-memory with a warning, matching the push registry's own
  `GATEWAY_STORE_FILE` pattern).
- Growth bound: a periodic idle-eviction sweep (`EvictionPolicy`, 7-day
  default) mirrors `verifiable-trust-infrastructure`'s
  `vti_common::relationship_store` (same design note,
  `tsp-relationship-recovery.md` D5/D6) — the SDK's own answer to a store
  that could otherwise be grown by anyone who can send the gateway an
  unauthenticated invite. `src/tsp.rs` stamps activity (`touch`) on every
  admitted inbound TSP frame and accepted invite, so only abandoned
  relationships age out.
- Security: the snapshot is written owner-only (0600, atomic rename, same
  path as the push-token snapshot) — nothing but the gateway's own TSP
  handling can read or write it.

Cross-mediator note (per the coordinating session's keyring/VTI-56 finding):
the gateway never calls `ATM::send_to` or forms an outbound relationship
itself — it only accepts inbound invites and replies within the same socket
session (`TspIntake`) — so it never needs the learned peer-mediator routing
that finding is about. The mapping is still persisted regardless, since it
rides the same generic `PersistentRelationshipStore` facets as everything
else.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test --lib relationships` — new unit tests, incl.
      `relationship_survives_a_restart_and_admits_a_payload` (sets
      `Bidirectional`, drops the store, builds a fresh instance over the same
      file, asserts state + `admits_application_message()`)
- [x] `cargo test --lib` (84 passed) and `cargo test --test api --test
      document_auth` (57 passed) — no regressions from the `store.rs`
      refactor or the new `AppState` field
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean

title: vetted/1: the community may issue it for its own identity checks
body:
## Why

When a community's own operators check a member's identity in person, VTI records it as a separate, plain W3C credential, `IdentityVerificationCredential`. The member later presents that credential, and the community's personhood policy reads it before granting personhood.

That credential is **evidence**. It is the same act a vetter records under this predicate, "the issuer checked the subject's claimed identity by this method", only made by the community instead of a member. As an ad-hoc type it has:
- no registry definition of what it establishes or doesn't
- no `issuerScope`
- no defined context term
- no place in a verifier's fail-closed accept list

Recording it under `vetted/1` gives every identity check in the graph one shape, whoever made it.

The **decision** stays where the specification puts it. Personhood is governed status, so it must not be a predicate (GOVERNANCE §5, criterion 2). It remains the community's decision, recorded on its membership credential. This entry now says explicitly that a `vetted/1` statement does not establish personhood.

External identity credentials, such as a government eID or an identity-verification provider's credential, are unaffected. They stay any W3C credential meeting the community's identity-proofing rules, as the specification's IDVC section says.

## Changes

- **`issuer`:** an eligible member vetter, **or the community named in `object.value.community` itself**, under its own DID. A community-issued statement needs no eligibility check.
- **`vetting.schema.json`:** `identityCommitment` and `cardDigestMultibase` become optional. A vetter's statement always carries them; a community desk check without a card may omit them. `declaredRelationship` stays required, and the community declares `none`.
- **`establishes` / `doesNotEstablish`:** cover either issuer, and add "that the subject has personhood or any other status the community confers".
- **`profile.md`:** explains the community path, that `taskContext` names the request in which the community recorded its check, and that the statement is evidence rather than status.
- **New example:** `examples/community-desk-check.json`.

`vetted/1` is still `draft`, so the change is made in place (§4.2). Two editor approvals apply (§6). `npm run check` passes with both examples validated.

## Companion changes

- Trust Tasks: `vtc/endorsements/issue` mints `vetted/1` from the community instead of the reserved `IdentityVerificationCredential`.
- VTI: the issue path and the default personhood policy.
- OpenVTC: follows the `vta-sdk` release.

title: fix(vtc-service): an abandoned backup import releases boot after its TTL
body:
## Summary
- The `backup:import_in_progress` sentinel (`vtc-service/src/backup.rs`) is stamped into the `config` keyspace before `import_backup`'s destructive clear-and-replay, and removed only on success. A crash, client disconnect, or a `finalize-import` that never landed leaves it behind, and `server::run` refuses to boot while it's present — permanently, since the only thing that could let an operator retry the import (the daemon itself) is what the sentinel refuses to start.
- **The fix is explicit operator recovery, not a TTL.** The sentinel still blocks boot regardless of its age: the backed-up keyspaces are half cleared and half replayed while it's set, and that doesn't become safer to serve just because time passed. (An earlier push on this PR tried a 10-minute auto-expiry; that's reverted — see the PR comment below.)
- Recovery is now a deliberate operator decision:
  - **If the original backup bundle is still at hand**: re-run `cnm backup import` with it — that finishes the restore.
  - **Otherwise**: `vtc admin discard-interrupted-import` (offline, confirmable, loud) wipes every backed-up keyspace back to empty and clears the sentinel. It does not restore anything — no password, no bundle available to it.
- The boot-refusal message names both options and the RFC 3339 timestamp the interrupted import started at (the sentinel's value, kept only for that — never for an age check).
- `backup::discard_interrupted_import` is store-level so it runs identically offline (same as the other `vtc admin` / `vtc acl` recovery commands); `TestVtc` now exposes its underlying `Store` so tests exercise the same path the CLI does.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --test it -- backup::` — 11/11 pass:
  - `a_set_sentinel_blocks_boot_regardless_of_age` — no sentinel boots clean; a fresh sentinel blocks; a week-old sentinel blocks exactly the same way.
  - `discard_interrupted_import_resets_and_clears_the_sentinel_so_a_new_import_succeeds` — no-op when nothing to discard; wipes a half-written row and clears the sentinel; a brand-new import then succeeds immediately.
- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --features test-support --all-targets` — clean.
- [x] `cargo fmt -p vtc-service -- --check` — clean.
author: stormer78

title: fix(vtc-service): an abandoned backup import releases boot after its TTL (#1870)
body:
fix(vtc-service): an abandoned backup import releases boot after its TTL (#1870)

* fix(vtc-service): an abandoned backup import releases boot after its TTL

The import-in-progress sentinel was a bare marker with no expiry: stamped
before the destructive clear-and-replay, cleared only on success. A crash,
disconnect, or failed finalize between those two points left it behind, and
boot refuses to start while it's present — permanently, since the daemon
that would let an operator retry the import is the same daemon the sentinel
refuses to boot.

Stamp the sentinel with a timestamp instead of a bare "1", and treat it as
stale past a 10-minute TTL (generous headroom over the in-process replay's
real runtime). A stale marker self-heals at the next boot attempt instead of
needing manual sentinel surgery, while a fresh marker still blocks boot as
before.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc-service): explicit operator recovery for an interrupted backup import

The previous commit on this branch gave the import-in-progress sentinel a
10-minute TTL so it would self-clear. That's unsafe: the sentinel means the
backed-up keyspaces are half cleared and half replayed, and a partial ACL or
member set does not become safe to serve just because nobody looked at it in
time. Revert to no expiry — a set sentinel refuses boot regardless of age.

Recovery is now an explicit operator decision instead of a clock:

- `vtc admin discard-interrupted-import` (offline, confirmable) wipes every
  backed-up keyspace back to empty and clears the sentinel. It does not
  restore anything — no password, no bundle — so the boot-refusal message
  also points at re-running `cnm backup import` with the original bundle
  when the operator still has it, which actually finishes the restore.
- `backup::discard_interrupted_import` is the core (store-level, so it runs
  identically offline); `TestVtc` now exposes the underlying `Store` so
  tests can exercise it the same way the CLI does.
- The boot-refusal message names both recovery options and the timestamp
  the interrupted import started at.

title: fix(vgi-bridge): require authentication proof purpose, not assertionMethod
body:
## Summary
- SPEC.md ("Which purpose a producer signs with") has a producer sign a Trust Task document under `authentication`; `assertionMethod` is reserved for a task whose own spec defines the proof as an attestation. Neither `git-ns/bridge/job/0.4` nor `git-ns/bridge/result/0.1` does.
- `wire::DocChecker::check` required `assertionMethod` and refused everything else, including a spec-conforming VTC signing with `authentication`.
- Checked verifiable-trust-infrastructure (`vtc-service/src/credentials/signer.rs`, `LocalSigner::sign_operational_doc`): the VTC already signs bridge jobs with `authentication` — no VTC-side change needed.
- `DocChecker::check` now requires `authentication` and refuses `assertionMethod`, `keyAgreement`, and anything else.
- `BridgeIdentity::sign` (used for every `git-ns/bridge/result` and `event` the bridge sends back) now signs with `authentication` too, matching `sign_trust_task`'s own default.
- Verified both locally-resolvable identities (`did:key`, `did:peer` via `PeerPurpose::Verification`) list their signing key under both `authentication` and `assertionMethod`, so no identity shape silently loses the ability to produce an accepted proof.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p vgi-bridge` — full suite green, including new/updated cases in `wire.rs`:
  - an `authentication`-purpose VTC job is accepted
  - `assertionMethod` and (forged) `keyAgreement` purposes are refused
  - an `authentication` proof is refused when the resolver lists the key only under `assertionMethod` (exercises `verify_raw`'s purpose-bound key resolution, not just the `proofPurpose` string)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p vgi-bridge --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all`

Test deployments only — no grace period; this lands as a hard requirement change.

title: witnessed/1: state the one-statement-per-direction SHOULD normatively
body:
## Why

Before trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#71, the specification's VWC section said:

> A witnessed exchange of a complete DTG edge is bidirectional … For such exchanges the witness **SHOULD** issue one VWC per direction.

#71 replaced that section with a reference to this entry, and #22 made `witnessed/1` the profile's normative definition. The other two obligations from the old section survived:

- The subject–object **MUST** is in `subjectObjectRelationship`.
- The **SHOULD** about making the referenced credential available stayed in the spec's VWC paragraph.

One-per-direction landed only in `profile.md`, as lowercase "should". GOVERNANCE treats `profile.md` as prose rather than a normative member:

- §4.2 lets it change at any status.
- §6 lets one editor change it.

So since #71 the requirement has had no normative home. This was raised in review of #71 and #22; both merged without it.

## What changes

- **`predicate.jsonld`, `subjectObjectRelationship`:** the SHOULD is added next to the direction-binding rule it supports: "Where one witnessing event forms both edge credentials of a complete DTG edge (two VRCs, or the grant and acknowledgement VMCs of a membership edge), the witness SHOULD issue one statement per direction."
- **`profile.md`:** the sentence uses the capitalised keyword, and says the obligation is stated normatively in the entry's subject–object relationship.

## Is this a meaning change?

title: feat: renew a membership from the Communities view (vtc/members/renew/0.1)
body:
Adds **renew membership** to the client using `vtc/members/renew/0.1`. After the DTG Credentials v1 migration (#397), OpenVTC sets aside stored pre-v1 credentials and tells the member to have the community re-issue them, but the member had no way to ask from the TUI. This adds that.

## UX
- **Trigger:** in the Communities view, press **`R`** on an Active membership. The `R: renew` hint shows only on Active rows.
- **Progress:** the status line reads "Asking the community to renew your membership…", then "Renewal requested — waiting for the community to re-issue your credentials."
- **Outcome**, on the status line and in the activity and Community logs:
  - **Renewed:** says which role was re-issued, whether personhood changed, and whether the acknowledgement was sent. If sending the acknowledgement failed, it says to press `m`.
  - **Not a member:** "Renewal refused: the community says you are not a member. If you were removed, join again."
  - **Other refusals:** the community's code and message.
- **Retired notices:** the "set aside" notice now says "press R to renew your membership". It clears once the replacement credentials are stored.

## How it works
- **Send:** `openvtc_core::renewal::request_renewal` (new `openvtc-core/src/renewal.rs`) is fire-and-forget over DIDComm, like the other member verbs. It uses the same delivery and signing path as `members::submit_member_vmc`. The request is recorded in memory so only a reply threaded on it is taken.
- **Verify** (`verify_renewal_response`, run off the loop as `VerifyJob::Renewal`):
  - The payload must parse, and `did` must be the recipient.
  - Both credentials must pass `dtg::parse_conformant`.
  - The VMC must be a Membership credential with `issuerScope: public`, issued by the community, with our member DID as subject.
  - The VAC must pass `dtg::community_roles`: scope is the community, public, no parent, subject is our member DID.
  - The community's signed document is verified, and each credential goes through `verify_issued_credential` (proof, validity window, revocation status, failing closed).
- **Store** (`apply_renewal`): on an Active membership only, it replaces the Membership and Role credentials and clears their retired notices. Personhood follows from the new VMC.
- **Acknowledgement:** a reciprocal member VMC is always issued and sent with `issue_member_vmc_for`, as join does. The new grant's digest changes, so the old acknowledgement no longer binds.
- **Refusals:** a `trust-task-error` threaded on a pending renewal is verified as the community's signed reply. `vtc/members/renew:notMember` is recognised.

## Tests
- **Core (10):**
  - success, with both credentials stored and notices cleared
  - another member's renewal
  - non-conformant VMC, and non-conformant VAC
  - a credential the community didn't sign
  - no Active membership
  - `notMember`
  - request shape and request correlation
  - status wording
- **Dispatcher (3):**
  - success end to end through `process_inbound_message`
  - an unsolicited reply ignored
  - `notMember` reported with no state change
- **UI:** `R` gating, the hint, and the status line. The inbound gate census includes the renew response type.

All pass locally:
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`
- `cargo test --workspace`

## Known limits
- **Restart while pending:** if the client restarts while a renewal is outstanding, the reply isn't taken. Pressing `R` again is harmless, because the VTC re-mints into the same status-list slot.
- **A reply that fails verification** is reported but doesn't cancel the pending request, so a forged reply can't pre-empt the real one.

feat: renew a membership from the Communities view (vtc/members/renew/0.1) (#398)

After the DTG Credentials v1 migration a member's pre-v1 VMC and role
credential are set aside on load, and the notice told them to ask the
community to re-issue them. There was no way to do that from the TUI.

openvtc-core: new `renewal` module.
- request_renewal sends vtc/members/renew/0.1 (no parameters, signed by
  the persona's authentication key) in the DIDComm binding envelope, the
  same delivery path as members/vmc, and records the request so only a
  reply threading on it is taken.
- verify_renewal_response holds the reply to the community's signed
  operational document (authentication key, addressed to the persona,
  fresh) and checks both credentials: conformant v1 (parse_conformant),
  issued by the community to that persona, the VMC a MembershipCredential
  with issuerScope public, the VAC a community role credential in the
  community's own scope (community_roles); then verifies each as an
  issued credential (assertionMethod proof, validity, revocation status).
  Local checks run before anything is resolved.
- apply_renewal stores both on the Active membership, replacing the old
  ones and clearing their retired notices; store_acknowledgement records
  the fresh member VMC. RenewalRefusal recognises
  vtc/members/renew:notMember; RenewalOutcome::describe is the member's
  status line.

openvtc:
- `R` on an Active community (Action::RenewMembership -> community job
  Verb::Renew). Status: "Asking..." -> "Renewal requested - waiting..."
  -> the outcome when the reply lands.
- The reply is verified off the loop (VerifyJob::Renewal), stored, and
  answered with a fresh members/vmc acknowledgement, as the join flow
  does on admission (the new grant has a new digest). A trust-task-error
  threading on a renewal is reported as a renewal refusal rather than
  falling into the join-error handler.
- The pre-v1 notice now says to press R.

Tests: core verification/storage over a did:key community (success with
retired notices cleared, wrong member, non-conformant credentials, a
credential the community did not sign, no Active membership), notMember;
dispatcher end-to-end for success, an unsolicited reply, and notMember;

title: test: derive trust-task census checks from the dispatch table
body:
Adding or moving a Trust Task meant hand-editing several census places; every one broke CI at least once this week. This converts each hand-maintained count/list into a property derived from the dispatch table and spec registry, keeping each check's protective intent.

## Census 1 — `vtc-service` `the_dispatched_set_declares_the_proofs_the_design_note_records`

- **Before:** `assert_eq!(required.len(), 100 + hidden_vetting, "<huge prose paragraph>")`.
- **After:** every dispatched URI either has its spec's `is_proof_required` enforced by the spine's universal `policy.enforce` gate, or is named in `DISPATCHED_WITHOUT_PROOF` with the reason an unsigned caller is still refused (ACL row, WebAuthn assertion, bearer token, first-admin bootstrap token, ...). A stale or unreasoned entry fails naming the exact URI.

## Census 2 — `vtc-service` `dispatcher_routes_every_dispatched_uri`

- **Before:** `DISPATCHED_URIS` checked against `declared`, a ~90-entry hand-retyped copy of the same list.
- **After:** every URI in `DISPATCHED_URIS` has a published spec policy (`trust_tasks_rs::schema_index::spec_policy_for(uri).is_some()`) — the property that actually matters, since an unrouted URI already fails in `dispatch_typed` and a routed-but-unpublished one would skip every SPEC §7.2 check.

## Census 3 — `vtc-service` `routes::openapi_tests` + `vta-service` `routes::cors_tests` REST route census

- **Before:** a representative-path list plus a `paths.len() >= N` floor, and (vtc-service only) a ~100-entry "must not exist" list grown on every verb that migrated off REST.
- **After:** every REST route the OpenAPI spec documents is either a deliberate, reasoned exception (`REST_EXCEPTIONS`) or self-evidently fine (`is_public_health_or_webauthn`). Shrinking the REST surface needs no edit here any more; growing it, or a route regressing back from Trust-Task-only, fails naming the exact route. Caught a real gap while landing it: the `tee` feature's `/attestation/did-log` route wasn't accounted for.

## Census 4 — `vtc-service` error-code `UNWITNESSED` baseline

- **Before:** `UNWITNESSED: usize` exact-equality assertion, hand-decremented on every witness landing even though nothing was wrong.
- **After:** renamed to `UNWITNESSED_CEILING` and compared with `<=` — a true ratchet. A witness landing needs no edit here (the census reports how far below the ceiling the baseline now sits); only growing the baseline past the ceiling demands a reasoned bump. Also fixed `tests_dir` to look under `tests/it/`, where #1862 moved every witness file — a path assumption the census's own witness-reading loop had gone stale on.

## Census 5 — vta-sdk `retry_safety::tests::every_uri_is_classified`, vta-mcp `guard::tests::every_dispatchable_uri_has_a_known_verb`

These already force a correct per-URI decision; kept as-is. Improved the failure message to print the exact line (`("uri", RetrySafety::Keyed),` / `"verb", // uri`) ready to paste into the right table.

## Census 6 — conformance witnesses (`every_published_dispatched_uri_has_a_witness` in vta-service, `every_bound_published_uri_has_a_witness` in vtc-service)

Kept as-is — they need real per-task fixtures no derivation can supply. Improved the failure message to print a ready-to-fill `checked!(...)` template for each missing URI.

Checks run: `cargo clippy -p vtc-service -p vta-service -p vta-sdk -p vta-mcp --all-targets -- -D warnings` (default features, plus `--features tee` for vta-service), `cargo fmt --all`, and the lib tests for each changed census — vtc-service also with `--features vetting-pcs`, vta-service also with `--features tee`.

title: feat!: DTG Credentials v1 — role VACs, vetted/1 and witnessed/1 statements, issuerScope
body:
This moves every DTG credential OpenVTC issues, receives, verifies, stores, displays or documents onto the DTG Credentials Core Specification (WD 0.6.0) and the DTG VSC predicate registry. The DTGWG reviewed and agreed the migration plan.

**This is a draft because it builds against unreleased crates.** The last commit, `chore: DO NOT MERGE — patch …`, points `dtg-credentials`, `vta-sdk` and `trust-tasks-*` at local worktrees, so CI cannot build it yet. Once these release, the commit is replaced with version bumps:
- OpenVTC/dtg-credentials#33, as 0.12
- trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#691, as the next `trust-tasks-rs`
- OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1859, as the next `vta-sdk`

## What changes on the wire
| Flow | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| All DTG credentials | `firstperson.network/credentials/dtg/v1` context, no `issuerScope` | `registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1`, with a required `issuerScope` |
| Role grants / vetter eligibility | `EndorsementCredential` + `CommunityRole` | A community `AuthorityCredential`: `actions: ["role:<name>"]`, vetter = `role:vetter` |
| Vetting Statement | `EndorsementCredential`, `identity-vetting/0.1` | A `StatementCredential` with predicate `…/dtg/vsc/vetted/1`, the body in `object.value`, and `taskContext` + `taskDigestMultibase` |
| Witness | `WitnessCredential` | A `witnessed/1` statement, classified by predicate |
| Member VMC acknowledgement | `new_member_vmc` | `new_member_vmc_for`, `issuerScope: directed` |
| VRC | no scope | `pairwise` for a relationship DID, `directed` for the persona DID |

The scope rules live in one module, `openvtc-core/src/dtg.rs`.

## Stored state
Credentials already stored in pre-v1 shapes are non-conformant. They are dropped on load with a `warn!`; they are never kept and never allowed to fail the load. The member sees a notice:
- A membership's VMC, role credential or acknowledgement is listed as retired, with "ask the community to re-issue it".
- The Credentials panel shows the count of retired VRCs.
- The Vetting page lists the retired vetter grants and statements.

A conformant replacement clears the notice.

## Other changes
- **Vetting session:** the vetter now signs and keeps the `vetting/session` document it sends. The applicant refuses a statement that doesn't match its copy.
- **Hidden-vetting PCS fixture:** regenerated because `statementType` changed, which moved `requirementsDigest`. VTI carries the matching fixture.
- **Object-form `issuer`:** VICs and VMCs with an object-form `issuer` are now refused, because the spec's Base Structure makes `issuer` a string.
- **Docs:** `vetting-process.md`, `vetting-hidden-vetters-pcs.md` and `relationships-vrcs.md` describe the v1 shapes. §9.4 of `vetting-process.md` could use a careful read.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- There is no "renew membership" action in the TUI yet. The notice asks the community to re-issue.
- `did-git-sign` 0.5.2 still pulls `vta-sdk` 0.56 into the graph. That goes away with a VGI release on 0.57.
- On release, `dtg-credentials` is raised from `"0.11"` to `"0.12"`. It says 0.11 now only so the local patch matches.

## Checks
- `cargo fmt` is clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 1722 passed, 0 failed, built against the VTI branch at 32b2187b. `vta-sdk` is unchanged since 0c3c8c75.

title: feat!: DTG Credentials v1 — role VACs, vetted/1 and witnessed/1 statements, issuerScope (#397)
body:
feat!: DTG Credentials v1 — role VACs, vetted/1 and witnessed/1 statements, issuerScope (#397)

* feat(openvtc-core)!: hold every DTG credential to DTG Credentials v1

Every DTG credential the client issues, receives, verifies or stores now
carries the v1 context (https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1,
the pre-v1 context refused with no alias), a top-level issuerScope and
exactly one concrete type, on dtg-credentials 0.12, vta-sdk 0.57,
vta-service 0.46 and trust-tasks 0.24.8.

- openvtc_core::dtg: the scope each issued credential declares
  (MEMBER_IDENTIFIER_SCOPE = directed for the persona DID a membership
  names; relationship_issuer_scope: pairwise for a relationship DID,
  directed for the persona DID; PERSONA_ANNOTATION_SCOPE = directed),
  parse_conformant, community_roles, and predicate-based statement
  display with a fail-closed core accept list.
- Member acknowledgement: new_member_vmc_for with the signing persona,
  declaring directed; build_member_vmc takes the member DID.
- VIC validation parses through dtg-credentials: v1 context second,
  issuerScope public, one concrete type. join::DTG_CONTEXT re-exports
  DTG_CONTEXT_V1.
- CredentialKind::Role is a community role VAC (AuthorityCredential,
  authority.scope the community, role:<name> actions); from_credential
  classifies conformant credentials only.
- VRCs declare the scope of the identifier the relationship uses.
- personhood AssertReply::role_vec -> role_vac (wire roleVac).
- Stored credentials in a pre-v1 shape are set aside on load with a
  logged reason: CommunityRecord::retired_credentials (persisted, cleared
  by a conformant replacement), Vrcs::retired, dropped VRCIssued tasks,
  and RejectionReason::Nonconformant on a vault rebuild.

The patch block this builds against is its own commit.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(openvtc-core)!: vetting statements are vetted/1 VSCs; vetter roles are VACs

Follows vta-sdk 0.57 (vetting statements are vetted/1 VSCs; role
credentials are VACs).

- The vetter's Vetting Statement is a StatementCredential under
  https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/vetted/1, the body at
  object.value, issued directed, citing the vetting/session document by
  taskContext and taskDigestMultibase. The desk keeps the signed session
  document (VettingBook::record_session_document, DeskSession::document)
  and a session without one cannot be attested; the applicant keeps the
  one it received (OpenSession::document) and refuses a statement that
  does not cite it (check_against_session).
- Statements are claimed by predicate, never by type; manifests name the

title: vta-service-v0.47.0
body:
### Added

- **vta-service**: Retire superseded REST routes; pre-session auth moves to Trust Tasks ([#1858](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1858))

* feat(vta-service)!: retire superseded REST routes; auth family moves to Trust Tasks

  Deletes the ~56 REST routes `deprecation::SUPERSEDED` marked as superseded
  by a Trust Task (acl, audit, config, contexts, did_templates, keys, webvh
  servers/dids, POST /vta/restart, the /api/trust-tasks alt spelling) and the
  always-403 POST /attestation/mnemonic stub. The REST-route half of
  `deprecation.rs` (the SUPERSEDED table, mark_superseded middleware) is
  removed now that it's empty; the unrelated SUPERSEDED_TASKS (Trust-Task URI
  supersession) table is untouched.

  Pre-session auth (auth/challenge/0.1, auth/authenticate/{0.2,0.3},
  auth/refresh/0.2) moves onto `/trust-tasks`, dispatched by a new
  family-owned bypass (`trust_tasks::auth::owns`/`dispatch_pre_session`) that
  runs ahead of the ACL-gated pipeline on all three transports (REST,
  DIDComm, TSP) — mirroring affinidi-webvh-service's `trust_tasks_auth`
  pattern. The document's own proof (required on authenticate, absent on
  challenge/refresh) is the whole of the authority these four carry, so
  there is no session and no ACL pre-filter to apply. authenticate/refresh
  0.1 are retired outright (this is a test deployment); 0.2/0.3 add
  sessionKey and delegation fields this VTA declines with a typed refusal
  rather than silently ignoring.

  Kept as tested REST_EXCEPTIONS: POST /bootstrap/request, GET+POST
  /backup/blob/{bundle_id}, GET /openapi.json, GET /attestation/mnemonic,
  GET /metrics.

  Client-side (vta-sdk, vta-mobile-core) callers move onto the Trust-Task
  form; cnm-cli/pnm-cli/vta-mcp needed no changes (already Trust-Task only).

- DTG Credentials v1 — role VACs, vetted/1 and witnessed/1 statements, IDVCs, issuerScope ([#1859](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1859))

* feat(vta-sdk)!: vetting statements are vetted/1 VSCs; role credentials are VACs

  Conform the SDK's vetting artifacts to the DTG Credentials Core
  Specification (v1 context, `issuerScope`) and the DTG VSC predicate
  registry, following the regenerated vetting specifications
  (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf feat/dtg-vsc-conformance).

  Vetting Statement (vetting/session/0.1): no longer an
  EndorsementCredential. `sign_statement` builds a StatementCredential with
  `new_vetted_vsc` under `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/vetted/1`;
  the body is `credentialSubject.object.value`, with no `type` member.
  `taskContext` and `taskDigestMultibase` are both read from the
  `vetting/session` document, which `StatementDraft::session` now carries
  in place of `task_context`, and `StatementDraft::issuer_scope` is
  `directed` or `public` (pairwise is refused by the profile).
  `verify_statement` parses through `dtg-credentials`, so the v1 context,
  the one-subtype rule and the profile are checked by the code that issues
  them; `VerifiedVettingStatement::check_against_session` binds a statement
  to the session document by id and task digest.

  - `IdentityVettingEndorsement` -> `VettedObjectValue` (no `type`; digests
    and commitment must be base58btc, as the registry schema requires).
  - `IDENTITY_VETTING_ENDORSEMENT_TYPE` -> `VETTED_PREDICATE`.
  - `VerifiedVettingStatement::endorsement()` -> `value()`; new
    `issuer_scope()`, `task_digest_multibase()`.

  Vetter role credential (vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1, vetting/request/0.1):
  a community-issued VAC, `issuerScope` public, `authority` { scope:
  <community DID>, actions: ["role:vetter"], maxAttenuation: 0 }.
  `eligibility::community_role` -> `community_roles`, returning every
  `role:<name>` of a VAC the community issued in its own scope with no
  parent; `verify_eligibility_vp` parses the VAC strictly and refuses a
  non-public scope or an attenuation.

  - `COMMUNITY_ROLE_ENDORSEMENT_TYPE` removed; new `ROLE_ACTION_PREFIX`,
    `VETTER_ROLE_ACTION`, `role_action`, `role_of_action`.
  - `protocols::members::ENDORSEMENT_CREDENTIAL_TYPE` removed; new
    `AUTHORITY_CREDENTIAL_TYPE` and `STATEMENT_CREDENTIAL_TYPE`.
  - `VerdictWith::role_vec` -> `role_vac` (wire `roleVac`).



### Fixed

- **vta-service**: Passkey-only step-up once a subject has enrolled one ([#1854](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1854))

A subject with an enrolled passkey verification method must complete
  step-up with a WebAuthn assertion only: mint no longer offers the
  did-signed gate for such an approver, and handle_approve_response
  refuses a did-signed (or evidence-absent) approve-response for one
  with noGate, even if a stale client sends it anyway. A subject with no
  passkey keeps the original did-signed-or-webauthn offer.

  Passkey enrolment also clears any elevation the subject reached
  without a passkey, so a stepped-up session from before enrolment can't
  outlive the switch to passkey-only.

  Along the way, wires the webauthn step-up gate's credential-id lookup
  to the enrolled DID's local WebVH document instead of the
  still-stubbed generic resolver enumeration, which otherwise made every
  webauthn step-up approve-response fail closed.

- **vta-service, vta-backup**: Build when vta-config's tee feature is unified in ([#1853](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1853))

AppConfig.tee exists whenever vta-config/tee is on, which vta-tee turns
  on. vta-service and vta-backup gated their AppConfig literals on their
  own tee feature, so any build that unified vta-tee with a non-tee
  vta-service or vta-backup failed with a missing field. Always enable
  vta-config/tee in both (it only adds the field and its types) and set
  the field unconditionally; TEE behaviour stays behind each crate's own
  tee feature.
