title: ci(release): tag with RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN; the Actions token gets 403 on refs
body:
The #1861 release is half-published. `vta-sdk` 0.58.0, `vti-common` 0.31.0 and `vti-rooms` 0.3.0 are on crates.io. After each publish, `release-plz` failed to create the crate's tag:

```
failed to create ref refs/tags/vti-common-v0.31.0 …
"message": "Resource not accessible by integration", "status": "403"
```

That happens even though the job has `contents: write`. `release-plz` stops at the first error, so each of the three publishing passes published one crate. **17 crates are unpublished**, including `vta-service` 0.47.0, `vti-secrets`, `vta-vault`, `cnm-cli` and `pnm-cli`.

This PR makes the three `release-plz release` passes use `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN`, falling back to `GITHUB_TOKEN`. That's the same token the Release PR job in this file already prefers.

When this merges, the push to main runs the release again and publishes and tags the remaining crates. The three crates that published without tags are skipped as already published, so I'll create their tags at `946efedc` by hand afterwards.
author: stormer78

title: vtc-client-v0.10.0
body:
### Added

- **vta-service**: Retire superseded REST routes; pre-session auth moves to Trust Tasks ([#1858](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1858))

* feat(vta-service)!: retire superseded REST routes; auth family moves to Trust Tasks

  Deletes the ~56 REST routes `deprecation::SUPERSEDED` marked as superseded
  by a Trust Task (acl, audit, config, contexts, did_templates, keys, webvh
  servers/dids, POST /vta/restart, the /api/trust-tasks alt spelling) and the
  always-403 POST /attestation/mnemonic stub. The REST-route half of
  `deprecation.rs` (the SUPERSEDED table, mark_superseded middleware) is
  removed now that it's empty; the unrelated SUPERSEDED_TASKS (Trust-Task URI
  supersession) table is untouched.

  Pre-session auth (auth/challenge/0.1, auth/authenticate/{0.2,0.3},
  auth/refresh/0.2) moves onto `/trust-tasks`, dispatched by a new
  family-owned bypass (`trust_tasks::auth::owns`/`dispatch_pre_session`) that
  runs ahead of the ACL-gated pipeline on all three transports (REST,
  DIDComm, TSP) — mirroring affinidi-webvh-service's `trust_tasks_auth`
  pattern. The document's own proof (required on authenticate, absent on
  challenge/refresh) is the whole of the authority these four carry, so
  there is no session and no ACL pre-filter to apply. authenticate/refresh
  0.1 are retired outright (this is a test deployment); 0.2/0.3 add
  sessionKey and delegation fields this VTA declines with a typed refusal
  rather than silently ignoring.

  Kept as tested REST_EXCEPTIONS: POST /bootstrap/request, GET+POST
  /backup/blob/{bundle_id}, GET /openapi.json, GET /attestation/mnemonic,
  GET /metrics.

title: ci: faster test loop — no-fail-fast, one test binary per service, skip admin-ui in Rust-only jobs
body:
## Summary
- `--no-fail-fast` on every `cargo test` invocation in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that lacked it, so one CI run reports every failing test binary instead of stopping at the first.
- `vtc-service` (82 files) and `vta-service` (37 files) each get a single integration-test binary (`tests/it/main.rs`, one `mod` per file) instead of one binary per file — link time dominated these jobs. `autotests = false` + an explicit `[[test]] name = "it"` make it the only integration-test target; the two CI steps that named individual test binaries now use `--test it -- <module>::`.
- `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1` added to Check, MSRV, Clippy and the all-features lint job — none of them execute vtc-service's tests, so none need the real admin-ui npm build. `Test (VTC)` is left alone: `routing_modes.rs` asserts on the real baked bundle's content.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --test it --no-run` and `cargo test -p vta-service --test it --no-run` both succeed.
- Test counts match `origin/main` exactly (`cargo test -p <crate> --tests -- --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': test$'`): vtc-service 2460, vta-service 1817.
- A full `cargo test -p vtc-service --test it --no-fail-fast` run (846/848 passing locally; the 2 failures are `routing_modes` cases that need the real admin-ui bundle, which my local run skipped via `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1` — CI's `Test (VTC)` job builds the real bundle, unaffected by this PR).
- Before/after link-time numbers for the two consolidated binaries, and the equivalent full-suite run for vta-service, to follow as a PR comment.

Not merging; letting CI run.

title: ci: faster test loop — no-fail-fast, one test binary per service, skip admin-ui in Rust-only jobs (#1862)
body:
ci: faster test loop — no-fail-fast, one test binary per service, skip admin-ui in Rust-only jobs (#1862)

* ci: report every test failure per run, skip admin-ui build for Rust-only jobs

Add --no-fail-fast to every `cargo test` invocation that lacked it, so one
CI run surfaces every failing test binary instead of stopping at the first.

Set VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1 in Check, MSRV, Clippy and the all-features
lint job: none of them execute vtc-service's tests, so none of them need
the real admin-ui npm build — only routing_modes.rs (in Test (VTC)) reads
the baked bundle's actual content, and that job is left alone.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test: consolidate vtc-service and vta-service integration tests into one binary each

Every file under tests/ used to be its own integration-test binary, each one
linking the whole crate again — 82 binaries for vtc-service, 37 for
vta-service, almost all of that time spent relinking libvtc_service /
libvta_service rather than compiling anything new.

tests/it/main.rs pulls every file in as a `mod` of one binary instead.
Contents and test names are unchanged; each file's own
`#![cfg(feature = "...")]` keeps working unchanged, since an inner attribute
at the top of a file included via `mod foo;` applies to the `foo` module
itself. vtc-service's shared `tests/common/` helpers move to
`tests/it/common/` and are declared once; every file that referenced them
via `mod common;` + `common::...` now uses `crate::common::...` instead.

Two relative `include_str!`s that assumed their old tests/ location move
with them (console_signed_document.rs's fixture, vta-service's
app_state_single_construction.rs reading its own router.rs), and
vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs's `#[path]` into the old
tests/common/webauthn_harness.rs follows the move.

`autotests = false` plus an explicit `[[test]] name = "it"` is what makes
this the only integration-test target in each crate, and CI's two
mediator-backed steps that named individual test binaries now pass
`--test it -- <module>::`. Test counts are unchanged (vtc-service 2460,
vta-service 1817, both crates' default-feature `--tests -- --list` count),
and `cargo test -p vtc-service --test it --no-run` /
`cargo test -p vta-service --test it --no-run` both succeed.

Doc references to individual test file paths that moved are updated to
match (vtc-service/CLAUDE.md, docs/05-design-notes/*, docs/02-vta/approvals.md).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

## `vta-sdk`

## [0.58.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-sdk-v0.57.0...vta-sdk-v0.58.0) — 2026-09-30 ### Added - **vta-service**: Retire superseded REST routes; pre-session auth moves to Trust Tasks ([#1858](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1858)) * feat(vta-service)!: retire superseded REST routes; auth family moves to Trust Tasks Deletes the ~56 REST routes `deprecation::SUPERSEDED` marked as superseded by a Trust Task (acl, audit, config, contexts, did_templates, keys, webvh servers/dids, POST /vta/restart, the /api/trust-tasks alt spelling) and the always-403 POST /attestation/mnemonic stub. The REST-route half of `deprecation.rs` (the SUPERSEDED table, mark_superseded middleware) is removed now that it's empty; the unrelated SUPERSEDED_TASKS (Trust-Task URI supersession) table is untouched. Pre-session auth (auth/challenge/0.1, auth/authenticate/{0.2,0.3}, auth/refresh/0.2) moves onto `/trust-tasks`, dispatched by a new family-owned bypass (`trust_tasks::auth::owns`/`dispatch_pre_session`) that runs ahead of the ACL-gated pipeline on all three transports (REST, DIDComm, TSP) — mirroring affinidi-webvh-service's `trust_tasks_auth` pattern. The document's own proof (required on authenticate, absent on challenge/refresh) is the whole of the authority these four carry, so there is no session and no ACL pre-filter to apply. authenticate/refresh 0.1 are retired outright (this is a test deployment); 0.2/0.3 add sessionKey and delegation fields this VTA declines with a typed refusal rather than silently ignoring. Kept as tested REST_EXCEPTIONS: POST /bootstrap/request, GET+POST /backup/blob/{bundle_id}, GET /openapi.json, GET /attestation/mnemonic, GET /metrics. Client-side (vta-sdk, vta-mobile-core) callers move onto the Trust-Task form; cnm-cli/pnm-cli/vta-mcp needed no changes (already Trust-Task only). - DTG Credentials v1 — role VACs, vetted/1 and witnessed/1 statements, IDVCs, issuerScope ([#1859](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1859)) * feat(vta-sdk)!: vetting statements are vetted/1 VSCs; role credentials are VACs Conform the SDK's vetting artifacts to the DTG Credentials Core Specification (v1 context, `issuerScope`) and the DTG VSC predicate registry, following the regenerated vetting specifications (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf feat/dtg-vsc-conformance). Vetting Statement (vetting/session/0.1): no longer an EndorsementCredential. `sign_statement` builds a StatementCredential with `new_vetted_vsc` under `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/vetted/1`; the body is `credentialSubject.object.value`, with no `type` member. `taskContext` and `taskDigestMultibase` are both read from the `vetting/session` document, which `StatementDraft::session` now carries in place of `task_context`, and `StatementDraft::issuer_scope` is `directed` or `public` (pairwise is refused by the profile). `verify_statement` parses through `dtg-credentials`, so the v1 context, the one-subtype rule and the profile are checked by the code that issues them; `VerifiedVettingStatement::check_against_session` binds a statement to the session document by id and task digest. - `IdentityVettingEndorsement` -> `VettedObjectValue` (no `type`; digests and commitment must be base58btc, as the registry schema requires). - `IDENTITY_VETTING_ENDORSEMENT_TYPE` -> `VETTED_PREDICATE`. - `VerifiedVettingStatement::endorsement()` -> `value()`; new `issuer_scope()`, `task_digest_multibase()`. Vetter role credential (vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1, vetting/request/0.1): a community-issued VAC, `issuerScope` public, `authority` { scope: , actions: ["role:vetter"], maxAttenuation: 0 }. `eligibility::community_role` -> `community_roles`, returning every `role:` of a VAC the community issued in its own scope with no parent; `verify_eligibility_vp` parses the VAC strictly and refuses a non-public scope or an attenuation. - `COMMUNITY_ROLE_ENDORSEMENT_TYPE` removed; new `ROLE_ACTION_PREFIX`, `VETTER_ROLE_ACTION`, `role_action`, `role_of_action`. - `protocols::members::ENDORSEMENT_CREDENTIAL_TYPE` removed; new `AUTHORITY_CREDENTIAL_TYPE` and `STATEMENT_CREDENTIAL_TYPE`. - `VerdictWith::role_vec` -> `role_vac` (wire `roleVac`).

The console signs every policy call. Per-type document limits come from the specifications: size.rs reads the codegen'd maxDocumentBytes (schema_index::max_document_bytes_for) and keeps an interim entry only for policy/upsert and did/register, whose specs declare none yet. A raised limit applies to a served type only, and only when the claimed issuer holds a live ACL entry (or is a signing key delegated by one), looked up before verification. The HTTPS cap is the largest served limit; a refusal does not echo an oversized type. ### Fixed - **vta-service**: Passkey-only step-up once a subject has enrolled one ([#1854](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1854)) A subject with an enrolled passkey verification method must complete step-up with a WebAuthn assertion only: mint no longer offers the did-signed gate for such an approver, and handle_approve_response refuses a did-signed (or evidence-absent) approve-response for one with noGate, even if a stale client sends it anyway. A subject with no passkey keeps the original did-signed-or-webauthn offer. Passkey enrolment also clears any elevation the subject reached without a passkey, so a stepped-up session from before enrolment can't outlive the switch to passkey-only. Along the way, wires the webauthn step-up gate's credential-id lookup to the enrolled DID's local WebVH document instead of the still-stubbed generic resolver enumeration, which otherwise made every webauthn step-up approve-response fail closed.

title: ci: raise the Test (VTC), release-bump and Release-PR timeouts
body:
Three job timeouts that cancelled healthy work on 2026-09-30, raised with the measurements in the workflow comments.

| Job | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Test (VTC)` | 40 | **60** | Every successful run from 09-29 to 09-30 took 30–33 min, on main and on PRs. That left ~1.3× headroom, and a slow runner hit it on the Release PR (#1856). The comment's 11–16 min baseline is stale; the suite has grown. |
| `release bump is large enough` | 45 | **90** | This runs `cargo-semver-checks` over every bumped crate. On #1856, where `vta-sdk` and `vti-common` move to breaking versions and most of the workspace bumps, it timed out at 45. |
| `Release-plz PR` (publish.yml) | 60 | **120** | The run after #1859 was cancelled at 60 min doing semver-checks, and the Release PR had to be regenerated locally. |

A real hang still ends at the new limits. There are no other workflow changes.

  the Release PR had to be regenerated by hand.

title: feat(vta-service)!: retire superseded REST routes; pre-session auth moves to Trust Tasks
body:
## Summary

- **Deleted** the ~56 REST routes `deprecation::SUPERSEDED` marked as superseded by a Trust Task: `acl/*`, `audit/*`, `config`, `contexts/*`, `did-templates/*`, `keys/*`, `webvh/{servers,dids}/*` (management CRUD — the public `did.jsonl` read stays), `POST /vta/restart`, the `/api/trust-tasks` alt spelling, and the always-403 `POST /attestation/mnemonic` stub. The REST-route half of `deprecation.rs` (the `SUPERSEDED` table, `mark_superseded` middleware, its metric) is removed now that it's empty. `SUPERSEDED_TASKS` (Trust-Task URI supersession) is untouched.
- **Moved**: pre-session auth (`auth/challenge/0.1`, `auth/authenticate/{0.2,0.3}`, `auth/refresh/0.2`) onto `POST /trust-tasks`, dispatched by a new family-owned bypass (`trust_tasks::auth::owns` / `dispatch_pre_session`) that runs ahead of the ACL-gated pipeline on all three transports (REST, DIDComm, TSP) — mirroring `affinidi-webvh-service`'s `trust_tasks_auth` pattern. The document's own proof (required on authenticate, absent on challenge/refresh) is the whole of the authority these four carry, so there's no session and no ACL pre-filter to apply. `authenticate`/`refresh` `0.1` are retired outright (test deployment, no compat shims); `0.2`/`0.3` add `sessionKey` and delegation fields this VTA declines with a typed, spec-declared refusal (`sessionKeyUnsupported` / `delegationNotRecognized`) rather than silently ignoring them.
- **Kept**, as tested `REST_EXCEPTIONS`: `POST /bootstrap/request`, `GET`+`POST /backup/blob/{bundle_id}`, `GET /openapi.json`, `GET /attestation/mnemonic`, `GET /metrics` — one-line rationale each in `deprecation.rs`.
- Client-side callers (`vta-sdk`'s `auth_di`/`auth_light`/`session`/`provision_client`, `vta-mobile-core`) moved onto the new Trust-Task auth family and `/trust-tasks`. `cnm-cli`/`pnm-cli`/`vta-mcp` needed no changes — they already dispatched everything else as Trust Tasks.

## Deliberate deviation from spec

`vta_sdk::trust_tasks::REST_ROUTED_URIS` is **not emptied**: passkey-login (`vta/auth/passkey-login-{start,finish}/{0.1,0.2}`) stays in it unchanged, since passkey-login routes and their flat-JSON wire shape are explicitly out of scope ("passkey/WebAuthn routes... stay as they are"). The four pre-session auth URIs also stay listed there — its doc comment is updated to explain why (not reachable through the session-gated dispatcher, whichever REST route or family-owned bypass serves them) — since removing them would require inventing a new parity-harness bucket for no functional gain, and the SDK-level "operations excluded from the generic invoke-any-operation surface" semantics is exactly what still applies to them.

## Known gap — flagged for follow-up

`vta-service/tests/api_integration.rs` was almost entirely REST-route integration tests for the families deleted above (acl/keys/contexts/audit/did-templates/webvh CRUD). ~87 of ~113 tests exercised those routes directly and had to be removed rather than ported (no existing Trust-Task-dispatch equivalents elsewhere in the test suite for most of these families). The file is trimmed from ~4600 to ~1700 lines, keeping discovery/health/rate-limit/timeout/provision-integration/webvh-update-and-rotate tests (already Trust-Task based) plus `every_rest_exception_names_a_live_route`. **This is a real integration-coverage gap** for acl/keys/contexts/audit/did-templates/webvh-management business logic on the Trust-Task path — a follow-up should port the deleted scenarios to `/trust-tasks` dispatch form.

## Local checks

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all`: clean.
- Did **not** finish running `cargo test -p vta-service` (stopped early per "speed matters, open the PR now" instruction) — CI covers it. If it surfaces failures in the trimmed `api_integration.rs` or elsewhere, they're mine to fix in a follow-up push on this branch.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: full workspace build + clippy + test
- [ ] CI: vta-service census/conformance tests
- [ ] Manual: confirm `auth/challenge` → `auth/authenticate/0.2` → `auth/refresh/0.2` round-trips over REST, DIDComm and TSP

body:
feat(vta-service)!: retire superseded REST routes; pre-session auth moves to Trust Tasks (#1858)

* feat(vta-service)!: retire superseded REST routes; auth family moves to Trust Tasks

Deletes the ~56 REST routes `deprecation::SUPERSEDED` marked as superseded
by a Trust Task (acl, audit, config, contexts, did_templates, keys, webvh
servers/dids, POST /vta/restart, the /api/trust-tasks alt spelling) and the
always-403 POST /attestation/mnemonic stub. The REST-route half of
`deprecation.rs` (the SUPERSEDED table, mark_superseded middleware) is
removed now that it's empty; the unrelated SUPERSEDED_TASKS (Trust-Task URI
supersession) table is untouched.

Pre-session auth (auth/challenge/0.1, auth/authenticate/{0.2,0.3},
auth/refresh/0.2) moves onto `/trust-tasks`, dispatched by a new
family-owned bypass (`trust_tasks::auth::owns`/`dispatch_pre_session`) that
runs ahead of the ACL-gated pipeline on all three transports (REST,
DIDComm, TSP) — mirroring affinidi-webvh-service's `trust_tasks_auth`
pattern. The document's own proof (required on authenticate, absent on
challenge/refresh) is the whole of the authority these four carry, so
there is no session and no ACL pre-filter to apply. authenticate/refresh
0.1 are retired outright (this is a test deployment); 0.2/0.3 add
sessionKey and delegation fields this VTA declines with a typed refusal
rather than silently ignoring.

Kept as tested REST_EXCEPTIONS: POST /bootstrap/request, GET+POST
/backup/blob/{bundle_id}, GET /openapi.json, GET /attestation/mnemonic,
GET /metrics.

Client-side (vta-sdk, vta-mobile-core) callers move onto the Trust-Task
form; cnm-cli/pnm-cli/vta-mcp needed no changes (already Trust-Task only).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-service): retire header-gated REST for install, recognise, bootstrap, website, publish

Trust-Task-header-gated REST mounts for install/claim, admin/bootstrap,
auth/recognise, relationships/publish and the website management verbs
(files list/delete, generations list, rollback) had no caller left that
a signed document on POST /v1/trust-tasks doesn't already serve. Add
dispatch for auth/challenge, authenticate/0.2+0.3 and refresh/0.2
alongside the existing 0.1 REST mounts (trust_tasks::auth_tasks), move
the retired verbs' handlers to plain functions called from the spine
(trust_tasks::install_tasks, recognise_tasks, website_tasks), and
delete their REST routes. Update the admin-ui install/bootstrap flow
to sign Trust Task documents instead of raw REST calls, and regenerate
openapi.json/wire.ts.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc-service): serve auth/challenge+authenticate over /trust-tasks, retire vetting/branding REST

feat/vta-retire-rest (#1858) switched vta-sdk::auth_light (shared by the
VTA client and cnm vetting's bearer-session login) to signing
auth/challenge/0.1 and authenticate/0.2 documents against POST
/trust-tasks instead of the dedicated Trust-Task-header-gated REST
mounts. Delete those now-uncalled mounts on the VTC side (0.2/0.3
dispatch already existed) and update the affected tests and census
allowlists.

Also retire the remaining admin-only bearer REST for the vetter grant
listing, automatic-grant configuration, withdrawal notices, community
branding and requested attributes: their signed-document dispatch
already existed (trust_tasks::surface_tasks), and vtc-client/cnm-cli
were the only REST callers left. Move vtc-client onto signed documents
for these five verbs, force their response schemas into the OpenAPI
spec now that no REST route references them, and regenerate
openapi.json/wire.ts.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* build(deps): bump trust-tasks-rs to 0.24.9

Carries vta/metrics/show/0.1, vta/attestation/mnemonic-status/0.1 and
vtc/vetting/hidden/publish/0.1 — the last three REST-exception routes'
specs.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-service): serve metrics/show and mnemonic-status over trust-tasks

Retire the last two REST-exception routes: GET /metrics (admin only,
now vta/metrics/show/0.1) and GET /attestation/mnemonic (super-admin
only, now vta/attestation/mnemonic-status/0.1). Both reuse the REST
handlers' logic — the Prometheus recorder reshaped into the spec's
structured MetricsSnapshot, and the mnemonic guard's status read
unchanged — dispatched on /trust-tasks like every other verb.

Drops both REST_EXCEPTIONS rows and vta-service/src/routes/vta.rs.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-service): serve vetting/hidden/publish over trust-tasks

Retire POST /vetting/hidden behind the vetting-pcs feature: it is
vtc/vetting/hidden/publish/0.1 now, dispatched on /trust-tasks like the
suite's other four hidden-vetting verbs. The derivation itself moves to
a shared publish_hidden_vetting_core, so the retired REST handler and
the new trust task cannot drift.

Updates the conformance witness table, the dispatched-URI census, and
empties the openapi snapshot's vetting-pcs path/schema allowlist now
that the feature adds no REST surface at all.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc,vta-sdk): move tests off retired REST auth/vetting routes

#1858 retired the VTA's and VTC's REST auth family and the VTC's vetter
grants/auto-grant/revocations/branding/requested-attributes REST mounts
in favour of signed Trust Tasks. Move the affected tests onto the
surviving transport instead of the gone REST route:

- vta-sdk: classify the new vta/metrics/show and
  vta/attestation/mnemonic-status URIs as ReadOnly; fix the challenge
  429 test's expected URL (/trust-tasks, not /auth/challenge).
- vtc-service: use vtc/auth/recognise/challenge/0.1's generated
  response type instead of a hand-written duplicate.
- vtc-service tests: post auth/challenge, auth/authenticate and the
  vetting admin reads/writes as signed documents against
  /v1/trust-tasks (or /v1/wallet/auth/* for the DIDComm-authcrypt
  sender-binding and forged-plaintext regressions, whose transport
  stays there); keep every refusal assertion unweakened. Point the
  size-cap and rate-limit regression checks at /v1/auth/refresh, the
  REST mount that still exists.
- vtc-client: list_vetter_grants() now signs
  vtc/vetting/vetters/grants/list/0.1 instead of calling the retired
  GET /vetting/vetters; drop the now-dead bearer-REST helpers this was
  the last caller of.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-mcp): classify vta/attestation/mnemonic-status as a read

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-service): witness metrics/show and mnemonic-status; drop /metrics from the documented-path census

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-service): restore ACL/contexts/keys/audit/did-templates/webvh coverage over trust tasks

PR #1858 deleted the superseded VTA REST routes and cut most of
vta-service/tests/api_integration.rs with them, losing integration
coverage for ACL, keys, contexts, audit, DID templates and did:webvh
management. Port that coverage onto the signed Trust Task dispatcher
(POST /trust-tasks), the successor every one of those routes pointed
at.

- vta-service/tests/trust_task_admin.rs: ACL CRUD + step-up metadata,
  context CRUD + DID update/scoping, key lifecycle + role gates +
  context scoping, audit list/retention/scoping.
- vta-service/tests/trust_task_did_management.rs: global and
  context-scoped DID-template CRUD/render, did:webvh creation modes
  (path-mode, template-driven, server-managed validation) and
  context-template shadowing.
- Fix vta-service/tests/api_integration.rs's create_test_webvh_did
  helper, which still posted to the now-gone `/webvh/dids` REST route
  and so silently broke the 4 webvh update/rotate-keys tests it feeds;
  it now dispatches webvh/dids/create/1.0 like the rest of the file.

REST status codes are mapped onto the Trust Task error `code` per the
HTTPS binding's status table (malformedRequest->400,
permissionDenied->403, idConflict->409, everything else via
taskFailed/extended codes->422).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-service): the unauthenticated rate-limit tests meter anonymous auth/challenge at /trust-tasks

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc-service): count vetting/hidden/publish in the vetting-pcs census

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-service): sign in over /trust-tasks, and assert the retired auth entry points are gone

The retired /auth/* and /api/trust-tasks REST paths are gone; the tests
now drive auth/challenge 0.1, authenticate 0.2 and refresh 0.2 at
/trust-tasks. Tests that drove a raw DIDComm envelope into the retired
/auth/ route now assert that route is gone; the sender-binding property
stays covered by bind_authcrypt_sender's tests, vault unseal and the

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc-service): the unwitnessed baseline size counts hidden/publish under vetting-pcs

* style: cargo fmt

* test(vtc-service): read the publish refusal's code from the Trust Task error document

* fix(vta-sdk): build warning-free under every feature set; session_store's mock signs in with a spec-length challenge

title: feat!: DTG Credentials v1 — role VACs, vetted/1 and witnessed/1 statements, IDVCs, issuerScope
body:
This moves every DTG credential VTI issues, verifies or documents onto the DTG Credentials Core Specification (WD 0.6.0) and the DTG VSC predicate registry: `vta-sdk`, `vtc-service`, `vta-service` rooms, the local `trust-tasks/` specs and the docs. The DTGWG reviewed and agreed the migration plan.

**This is a draft only because it builds against unreleased crates.** The work is finished and tested. The last commit, `chore: DO NOT MERGE — patch …`, points `dtg-credentials` and `trust-tasks-*` at local worktrees. Once OpenVTC/dtg-credentials#33 (0.12) and trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#691 release, that commit is replaced with version bumps. The workspace `dtg-credentials` requirement then moves from `"0.11"` to `"0.12"`.

## Checks
- Workspace: 5262 passed, 0 failed.
- `vtc-service` lib: 1611 passed, and every integration binary passes. The environment kept killing long runs, so they ran in batches.
- The `vetting-pcs` feature tests pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` is clean, including with `vetting-pcs` and the three reduced-feature `vta-service` runs.
- `cargo fmt --check` is clean.
- admin-ui: `tsc` and vitest (498 tests) pass, and the openapi snapshot matches.
- The `wasm32` build for `vti-rooms-wasm` succeeds.

## Summary of the change
- **Roles:** role grants are community VACs (`actions: ["role:<name>"]`, vetter = `role:vetter`, `maxAttenuation: 0`), not `CommunityRole` endorsements. Vetter eligibility matches the action. `community_roles` now parses as strictly as `verify_eligibility_vp`.
- **Vetting statements** are `vetted/1` VSCs. The body is in `object.value` (`VettedObjectValue`, with no `type`). `statementType` is the predicate IRI.
- **Witness credentials** are `witnessed/1` VSCs, classified by predicate in the ceremony, join present and personhood paths.
- **Identity verification** is issued as a plain W3C IDVC, `[VerifiableCredential, IdentityVerificationCredential]`, which is not a DTG credential. The personhood policy reads that type.
- **Endorsement types** are the community's predicate accept list. `vtc/endorsements/issue` mints `StatementCredential`s and refuses member-only profiles such as `vetted/1`.
- **VIC and VMC** declare `issuerScope`. The member acknowledgement keeps the member's declared scope, and published VRCs and VPCs must carry one.
- **Room credentials** (`vta-service`, `vti-rooms-*`) declare `issuerScope` under the v1 context.
- **Clean-up:**
  - The unused `openvtc.org/contexts/dtg-*-v1.jsonld` constants are removed.
  - In the local `trust-tasks/` specs, the relationships `$id`s are aligned.
  - Also there, the rejected `Verifiable*Credential` names are dropped.
  - Also there, `MembershipAcknowledgement` is replaced with the member-issued VMC.

## Wire changes for clients
- **Join:**
  - `decide` returns `roleVac`: a role VAC with `actions: ["role:<VtcRole wire>"]` and `maxAttenuation: 0`.
  - `members/vmc` requires the v1 context and `issuerScope`, and binds only to a `public` grant.
  - A join presentation carrying a statement under a predicate the community doesn't accept is refused.
- **Vetting:**
  - Statements must be `vetted/1` VSCs carrying `taskContext` and `taskDigestMultibase`.
  - `statementType` is the predicate IRI.
  - The vetter grant is a VAC. Its `endorsementId` is unchanged and still revocable.
- **Relationships:** VRCs and VPCs must carry `issuerScope`. A `pairwise` VRC issued under the membership DID is refused.
- **Personhood:**
  - A VWC is a `witnessed/1` VSC, with a new binding state `subjectMismatch`.
  - The in-person evidence is an `IdentityVerificationCredential`.
- **Recognise:** the presentation must carry a VAC and a VMC. Custom Rego policies read `input.foreign_vac`, renamed from `foreign_vec`.
- **Endorsements:**
  - `issue` mints a VSC under the registered predicate and refuses `vetted`, `witnessed` and `presented` with `predicateNotIssuable`.
  - The reserved `typeUri` `IdentityVerificationCredential` mints the plain W3C IDVC.
  - Registration accepts predicate IRIs only.
  - The four core predicates are seeded at boot.
- **Storage:** stored rows keep reading `roleVecId`, `vecId` and `currentRoleVec` through serde aliases. The `VecIssued` audit envelope name is kept, because SIEM rules key on it.

## vta-sdk API changes (vs 0.56)
- **Removed:**
  - `COMMUNITY_ROLE_ENDORSEMENT_TYPE`
  - `IDENTITY_VETTING_ENDORSEMENT_TYPE`
  - `IdentityVettingEndorsement`
  - `ENDORSEMENT_CREDENTIAL_TYPE`
  - `eligibility::community_role`
- **Added:**
  - `VETTED_PREDICATE`
  - `VettedObjectValue`
  - `role_action()` and `role_of_action()`
  - `VETTER_ROLE_ACTION`
  - `AUTHORITY_CREDENTIAL_TYPE` and `STATEMENT_CREDENTIAL_TYPE`
  - `eligibility::community_roles`, which parses strictly
- **Changed:**
  - `StatementDraft` takes `value`, `session` and `issuer_scope`.
  - `VerifiedVettingStatement::endorsement()` is renamed `value()`.
  - `role_vec` is renamed `role_vac`. The same rename applies in `vtc-client`.

## Related
- trustoverip/dtgwg-vsc-registry#19: the `vetted/1` and `presented/1` predicates
- trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#70
- OpenVTC/openvtc#397: the client migration, built against this branch's `vta-sdk`

title: feat!: DTG Credentials v1 — role VACs, vetted/1 and witnessed/1 statements, IDVCs, issuerScope (#1859)
body:
feat!: DTG Credentials v1 — role VACs, vetted/1 and witnessed/1 statements, IDVCs, issuerScope (#1859)

* feat(vta-sdk)!: vetting statements are vetted/1 VSCs; role credentials are VACs

Conform the SDK's vetting artifacts to the DTG Credentials Core
Specification (v1 context, `issuerScope`) and the DTG VSC predicate
registry, following the regenerated vetting specifications
(dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf feat/dtg-vsc-conformance).

Vetting Statement (vetting/session/0.1): no longer an
EndorsementCredential. `sign_statement` builds a StatementCredential with
`new_vetted_vsc` under `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/vetted/1`;
the body is `credentialSubject.object.value`, with no `type` member.
`taskContext` and `taskDigestMultibase` are both read from the
`vetting/session` document, which `StatementDraft::session` now carries
in place of `task_context`, and `StatementDraft::issuer_scope` is
`directed` or `public` (pairwise is refused by the profile).
`verify_statement` parses through `dtg-credentials`, so the v1 context,
the one-subtype rule and the profile are checked by the code that issues
them; `VerifiedVettingStatement::check_against_session` binds a statement
to the session document by id and task digest.

- `IdentityVettingEndorsement` -> `VettedObjectValue` (no `type`; digests
  and commitment must be base58btc, as the registry schema requires).
- `IDENTITY_VETTING_ENDORSEMENT_TYPE` -> `VETTED_PREDICATE`.
- `VerifiedVettingStatement::endorsement()` -> `value()`; new
  `issuer_scope()`, `task_digest_multibase()`.

Vetter role credential (vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1, vetting/request/0.1):
a community-issued VAC, `issuerScope` public, `authority` { scope:
<community DID>, actions: ["role:vetter"], maxAttenuation: 0 }.
`eligibility::community_role` -> `community_roles`, returning every
`role:<name>` of a VAC the community issued in its own scope with no
parent; `verify_eligibility_vp` parses the VAC strictly and refuses a
non-public scope or an attenuation.

- `COMMUNITY_ROLE_ENDORSEMENT_TYPE` removed; new `ROLE_ACTION_PREFIX`,
  `VETTER_ROLE_ACTION`, `role_action`, `role_of_action`.
- `protocols::members::ENDORSEMENT_CREDENTIAL_TYPE` removed; new
  `AUTHORITY_CREDENTIAL_TYPE` and `STATEMENT_CREDENTIAL_TYPE`.
- `VerdictWith::role_vec` -> `role_vac` (wire `roleVac`).

vtc-client: `role_vec` -> `role_vac` on `DecideResult`, `MemberRenewal`,
`MemberRotated` and `PersonhoodRevocation`, matching the `roleVac`
rename in vtc/join-requests/decide, vtc/members/{renew,rotate} and
vtc/members/personhood/*.

vti-common: `MembershipRenewedData::role_vec_id` and
`DidRotatedData::role_vec_id` -> `role_vac_id` (wire `roleVacId`,
reading `roleVecId` on older rows). The `VecIssued` envelope keeps its
name, which SIEM rules key on; it now records role VACs and statement
VSCs, named by `credentialType`.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vta-service)!: room credentials declare issuerScope under the DTG v1 context

Adopt dtg-credentials 0.12 across the room surfaces — vta-service's
`rooms/owner/*` handlers and room oracle, vti-rooms-dtg and
vti-rooms-wasm. Every DTG credential they mint now carries the v1
context (`https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1`) and a
top-level `issuerScope`, chosen for what the identifier truthfully is:

- `public` where a room issues as itself — the invitation (VIC) from
  `rooms/owner/invite` and the root VAC from `rooms/owner/issue-authority`.
  The room's DID is the scope every verifier of a room credential
  already resolves.
- `directed` for every attenuation — a member narrowing a room grant to
  a presentation leaf (`room_oracle::present`, vti-rooms-wasm
  `MemberIdentity::present`). The member issues under the DID the room
  admitted: one identifier recognised by the room, its host and the
  agent, neither per-counterparty nor a public identity.

Attenuations pass `max_attenuation: None`, taking the library default
under the parent's bound.

No room code used the retired endorsement, witness or r-card types. Two
test fixtures carried the old endorsement type name as a plain string:
an SD-JWT `vct` in vta-vault (now `SkillEndorsement`) and an opaque vault
entry in vta-service's persona tests (now `StatementCredential`).

Wire change, no API change: a VIC or root VAC from `rooms/owner/*`, and a
presentation leaf from the room oracle or the browser, now carry
`issuerScope` and the v1 context, and 0.11 verifiers refuse them.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc-service)!: issue and verify DTG v1 credentials — role VACs, statement VSCs, IDVCs

Every DTG credential the VTC issues, verifies or documents now conforms to
the DTG Credentials Core Specification's v1 context and the DTG VSC
predicate registry, following the regenerated Trust Tasks
(dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf feat/dtg-vsc-conformance). Built on
dtg-credentials 0.12.

Common structure (credentials::ingress::classify_dtg): `@context` is
exactly `[credentials/v2, https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1]`
in that order (the firstperson.network context is refused, no alias),
`issuerScope` is REQUIRED, `type` carries exactly one concrete subtype
(the library's rule, so retired types are refused by name), and a
statement is held to its predicate profile. Everything the VTC mints is
built through the catalog and validated before signing; the community
always declares `issuerScope` `public`.

- VIC: `issuerScope: public`.
- VMC grant: `public` (fixed by the catalog). Member acknowledgement
  (members/inbound_vmc): any declared scope accepted; the stored grant it
  binds to must be `public`; the Working Draft 01 `digest` spelling is no
  longer read.
- Role grants (credentials::vac, was vec): a VAC from
  `new_community_role_vac` — `authority` { scope: community DID, actions:
  ["role:<VtcRole wire>"], maxAttenuation: 0 }. The vetter grant is
  `role:vetter` (vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1), recorded as an
  endorsement row of type `role:vetter` so vtc/endorsements/revoke keeps
  revoking it. `CommunityRole` is gone. Cross-community recognition
  (vtc/auth/recognise/0.2) takes a role VAC + VMC, requires scope ==
  issuer and no parent, reads the role from the first `role:` action, and
  hands `cross_community_roles.rego` `input.foreign_vac` (was
  `foreign_vec`).
- Vetting Statements: counted only as `vetted/1` VSCs verified by
  vta-sdk, picked by predicate, and only under a predicate the community
  accepts (new failure `predicate-not-accepted`); eligibility reads the
  `role:vetter` grant rows.
- Witness (credentials::witness): a VWC is a `witnessed/1` VSC,
  classified by predicate, digest read from `object.digestMultibase`;
  a digest naming an edge whose issuer is not the statement's subject is
  the new binding state `subjectMismatch`. `taskContext` requirement
  derives from the predicate profile (task_context::
  requirement_for_predicate). The ceremony `Credential` fact gains
  `predicate`, and DI credentials report their concrete subtype as
  `type` instead of `DTGCredential`.
- Identity verification (credentials::idvc): a plain W3C VC,
  `["VerifiableCredential", "IdentityVerificationCredential"]`, v2
  context only, issued by the community on its revocation list. Issued
  through vtc/endorsements/issue/0.1 with the reserved typeUri
  `IdentityVerificationCredential` — no registration — and revoked like
  any row. That reuse diverges from the task's "mints a VSC" text; it is
  recorded in docs/03-vtc/personhood-and-graph.md pending a dedicated
  task. personhood.rego accepts it when issuer is the community and the
  subject the applicant; its witness rule matches the `witnessed/1`
  predicate. A workspace-authored personhood default that refuses a
  bound v1 witness, or admits an unbound one, is upgraded at boot
  (policy::default::upgrade_stale_personhood_default).
- Endorsement types → predicate accept list: a registered `typeUri` must
  be a predicate IRI (`invalidUri` otherwise); `role:vetter` and the IDVC
  type are reserved. The four core registry predicates are seeded once at
  boot (a marker keeps deletions deleted). endorsement_types::accept_list
  builds a fail-closed `PredicateAcceptList`, applied to vetting
  statements, join presentations and personhood assertions.
  vtc/endorsements/issue/0.1 mints a VSC (predicate = typeUri,
  object.value = claim, validated against the claimSchema) and refuses a
  predicate whose profile needs `taskContext` with `predicateNotIssuable`.
  Schema-registry defaults are Membership/Authority/Statement/Invitation
  plus the IDVC.
- Relationships: VRCs and VPCs must declare `issuerScope`; the Rego
  `identifier_form` is read from it (pairwise → pairwise, directed |
  public → attributed) and the raw `issuer_scope` is passed too. A
  `pairwise` VRC under the caller's membership DID is refused.
- Renames on the wire and in storage: `roleVec` → `roleVac` (join
  decide, members renew/rotate/personhood, ceremony verdicts),
  `currentRoleVecId`/`currentRoleVec` → `currentRoleVacId`/
  `currentRoleVac`, endorsement row `vecId` → `credentialId`; stored rows
  keep reading under the old names.

Also: admin-ui (vetting predicate, `role:vetter` rows, a
`holds_trusted_statement` rule condition and `statement_trusted` helper,
openapi.json + wire.ts regenerated); `cnm member endorse` help;
vti-vetting-pcs fixture statementType; pseudonym extraction reads only
`credentialSubject.pseudonym`.

Wire break with no upgrade ordering: 0.11-era credentials are refused and
existing role grants, statements and vetter grants must be re-issued.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs: describe the DTG v1 credential shapes the VTI issues and verifies

Rewrite the operator and design docs, and the local trust-tasks folder,
for the conformance change: role credentials are VACs (`role:<name>`,
maxAttenuation 0), Vetting Statements are `vetted/1` VSCs, witnesses are
`witnessed/1` VSCs classified by predicate, the identity-verification
credential is a plain W3C VC issued through the reserved
`IdentityVerificationCredential` typeUri (recorded as a divergence from
vtc/endorsements/issue/0.1), endorsement types are the community's
fail-closed predicate accept list, and a VRC's `issuerScope` sets the
Rego `identifier_form` (pairwise → pairwise, directed | public →
attributed). The ceremony rule-IR docs and examples gain the `predicate`
fact and `statement_trusted(p)`.

trust-tasks/: recognise/1.0 describes the role VAC + VMC instead of the
`Verifiable`-prefixed names; join-requests/accept/1.0 replaces
`MembershipAcknowledgement` with the member-issued VMC; `roleVec` →
`roleVac`; relationships 1.0 `supersededBy` now names the 0.2 versions the
Rust serves.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-sdk): community_roles parses a role VAC as strictly as verify_eligibility_vp

`vetting::eligibility::community_roles` read the raw JSON while
`verify_eligibility_vp` parses through dtg-credentials, so a wallet
could pick a candidate the verifier then refused as malformed. It now
parses the credential with the same strict DTG parse (v1 context, one
subtype, declared issuerScope) before reading `authority`. Signature
unchanged; credentials that are not conformant DTG VACs now yield None.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc-service): join fixtures carry DTG v1 member VMCs and witnessed/1 statements

Member-issued VMC fixtures gain the v1 context, `DTGCredential` and
`issuerScope: directed`; the SD-JWT witness fixture is a `witnessed/1`
statement (vct `StatementCredential`, predicate + object claims); the
vetter-grant assertion checks the VAC authority. The vti-vetting-pcs
cross-repo fixture is the one OpenVTC regenerated for the vetted/1
statementType (its requirementsDigest moved with it).

* test(vtc-service): the last join fixture names StatementCredential

vtc/endorsements/issue/0.1 declares that refusal as claimSchemaViolation;
it was a generic validation error.

title: First tagged release, then move the two core profiles' authority into the registry
body:
## Summary

Nothing has been tagged yet: there are no tags, no GitHub Release, and every build reports `revision: unreleased`. GOVERNANCE §8 says a tagged release is what implementations bundle and what a verifier pins, so until one exists the accept-list's `revision` field has nothing to point at and the "signed release" half of the integrity story in [cred-spec #52](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/issues/52) is unexercised.

The first release is also the trigger for the second half of this issue. The [DTG Credentials Core Specification](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec) still carries the full normative text of the `dtg:endorses` and `dtg:witnessed` profiles and says, in its "where profiles live" editor's note, that "the two core profiles move there once it has a release." The registry already holds both as `endorses/1` and `witnessed/1` in `draft`; what moves is the authority for the profile text, after which the specification references the registry entries instead of restating them.

## What to do

1. Cut the first tagged release once `contexts/v1.jsonld` (now merged via #7) and the two predicates are the intended `v1` state, and confirm the release workflow attaches the archive, its digest and the provenance attestation as §8 describes.
2. Open the matching specification PR that replaces the two profile sections with references to `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/endorses/1` and `.../witnessed/1`, keeping the VEC and VWC names as the specification's names for those profiles.

## Meaning must not drift in the move

Each `<name>/<n>` is immutable once published, and a change of meaning is by definition a new `<name>/<n+1>` (GOVERNANCE §3). When the profile text moves, the normative members of `endorses/1` and `witnessed/1` (`establishes`, `doesNotEstablish`, `objectKind`, the subject–object relationship, `taskContextRequired`, `minimumIssuerScope`, the additional members) have to carry the specification's meaning across unchanged. Reviewers of that PR should diff the registry definition against the specification's profile section member by member, not just read the prose. Anything that reads as an improvement rather than a transcription is a candidate for `/2`, not an edit to `/1`. This is the one place in the current follow-up list where a version bump could slip in by accident.

Refs cred-spec #52 (sequencing step 4).

title: Refer to the registry for the two core profiles' definitions
body:
## Summary

The `dtg:endorses` and `dtg:witnessed` profile sections no longer restate the profiles' normative members; they say what each profile is and refer to its registry entry, `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/endorses/1` and `.../witnessed/1`, which is now the normative definition (trustoverip/dtgwg-vsc-registry#22). The VEC and VWC names, the two section headings and anchors, and both examples are unchanged. Nothing on the wire changes.

This is the second half of registry #14: the registry serves the two IRIs, which was the honest gate for the move; "once it has a release" was a proxy for that, and the registry is not tagged (registry #21).

## Changes

- **The two profile sections.** Each keeps its heading and a one-paragraph statement of the profile (what a VEC or VWC is, who may witness), then says the registry entry defines the profile's members and that a verifier configures against it per *Predicate Handling*. The VWC section keeps the two places where the profile engages this specification's own mechanisms: `taskContext` and `taskDigestMultibase` are required, so *Trust Task Context Binding* and *Outcome Interpretability* apply; and the object is a *Digest Encoding* digest, so the referenced edge credential must be to hand and SHOULD be made available. The "direction binding" editor's note is dropped: it explained a WD02-to-WD03 change, and its rationale lives in the registry entry's profile text.
- **Predicate Profiles.** "This specification defines the profiles for the predicates in the DTG context" becomes "The DTG VSC Predicate Registry defines the profiles for the predicates in the DTG namespace, including the two core profiles this specification names below."
- **"Where profiles live"** is now an informative note rather than an editor's note, stating the steady state: this specification defines the statement mechanism and the nine members a profile states; the profiles, including the two core ones, are defined in the registry. The "move there once it has a release" and "nothing on the wire changes when a profile's text moves" sentences are gone.
- **Related Specifications** says the registry holds every profile in the DTG namespace, including the VEC and the VWC.
- **CONTEXT.md**: the VEC and VWC entries name the registry IRIs as the normative definitions.

## Meaning must not drift

The registry entries were compared member by member against the sections this PR removes before the registry PR was opened; all match. What this PR removes is a restatement, not a requirement.

## Test plan

- [x] All 17 JSON examples parse; the two profile examples are byte-identical to before
- [x] No dangling in-document anchors; the two profile anchors still resolve (referenced from *DID Method Considerations* and the VSC editor's note)
- [x] No remaining "once it has a release"
- [ ] Spec-Up-T render checked on the preview

No Document Status bump: the change is editorial under *Compatibility Rules*, as #70 was.

Lands after trustoverip/dtgwg-vsc-registry#22, the same day.

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.25.0` → `0.25.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.25.0` → `0.25.1` | patch |

| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.25.0` → `0.25.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.25.0` → `0.25.1` | patch |

| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.22.0` → `0.22.1` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.4.1`) | `0.4.0` → `0.4.1` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.4.0` → `0.4.1` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: Make endorses/1 and witnessed/1 the normative core-profile definitions
body:
## Summary

Makes `endorses/1` and `witnessed/1` the normative definitions of the specification's two core profiles, the VEC and the VWC, as #14 (rescoped) calls for. The specification's two profile sections become references to these entries in the companion PR, trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#71. Nothing on the wire changes: the IRIs, the definitions' normative members and both examples are untouched, and both terms stay `/1` and `draft`.

Also folds in the three fork-only fixes from Glenn's review of #20, since this is the next PR touching the tooling.

## The profile move

Before this PR the two entries described themselves as transcriptions ("its normative text is the section this definition links under *Defined in*") and `definedIn` pointed at the specification's sections, with anchors that were already wrong (`#the-dtg%3Awitnessed-profile-(vwc)` where Spec-Up generates `#the-dtgwitnessed-profile-vwc`). Now:

- `definedIn` is `null` on both, as it is for `vetted/1` and `presented/1`: the definition format says `definedIn` is "where the profile's normative text lives, if outside this registry", and it no longer is.
- Each `profile.md` opens by saying the entry is the profile's normative definition and the specification refers here for its members. The stale closing bullet about the "placeholder namespace" and cred-spec #48 (resolved by cred-spec #64) is replaced by one line on the `dtg:` notation.
- `witnessed/1`'s "What this predicate is not" section now names `presented/1`, which exists since #19, as the predicate for presentation.
- README's status line records that the two entries are the normative definitions; PLAN.md §1.8 step 4 is marked done.

**Meaning must not drift.** Before making any edit I compared each entry against the specification's section member by member: definition, classification and `weighedBy`, object kind, subject–object rule, `witnessContext` and its three members, `taskContext` requirement, minimum issuer scope, issuer, `establishes`, and every item of `doesNotEstablish`. All match, and the prose obligations (one statement per direction, make the referenced credential available, the direction-binding rationale) are already in `profile.md`. No normative member changes in this PR; the `predicate.jsonld` diffs are the `definedIn` line only.

## Glenn's three points from #20

1. **Config collision.** `parseConfig` now refuses a `contextBase` or `metaBase` whose path is the parent of `namespace`, since that is where the home page is written and the build would silently overwrite the other index. Covered by a new test.
2. **Escaped comparison in `verify.mjs`.** The `/dtg` check compares `esc(config.siteName)` against the page, which renders it through `esc()`.
3. **The index heading comes from config.** New required value `indexName` (`VSC Predicate Registry` here, `Predicates` in the fixture), rendered at `/dtg/vsc` and added to the instance-values check, so nothing instance-specific is left in `render.mjs`. README and PLAN.md list it.

## Verification

`docker compose run --rm check` against `origin/main`: validator, immutability (4 draft, 0 frozen), instance-values scan (now also checking `"VSC Predicate Registry"`), 25 unit tests, build.

Refs #14 (the profile move) and #20 (review points 1–3).

title: spec(vtc/endorsements): IDVC issuance and reserved type values, matching VTI
body:
This follow-up to #691 carries one commit that missed that merge. It makes `vtc/endorsements/*`, `vtc/endorsement-types/*` and the personhood evidence text describe what VTI implements (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1859). All affected specs are draft and change in place.

## Changes
- **`vtc/endorsements/issue/0.1`:**
  - The reserved `typeUri` `IdentityVerificationCredential` mints the community's identity-verification credential instead of a statement. It is a plain W3C VC (an IDVC in the DTG spec's sense), deliberately not a DTGCredential:
    - `@context` is `["https://www.w3.org/ns/credentials/v2"]`.
    - `type` is `["VerifiableCredential", "IdentityVerificationCredential"]`.
    - The issuer is the community and the subject is `subjectDid`.
    - The `claim` members sit beside `id`.
    - It carries `validUntil`, and `credentialStatus` on the community status list, so `vtc/endorsements/revoke` withdraws it.
  - A `claim` naming `id` is `claimSchemaViolation`.
  - `role:vetter` is not issuable here; only `vtc/vetting/vetters/grant` issues it.
  - A worked example is added.
- **`vtc/endorsements/{list,show,revoke}` and `_shared/0.1/endorsement`:** a row's `typeUri` is one of:
  - a registered predicate IRI, for a statement
  - `IdentityVerificationCredential`, for an IDVC
  - `role:vetter`, for a vetter-role VAC
- **`vtc/endorsement-types/{register,list}` and `_shared/0.1/endorsement-type`:**
  - Only absolute predicate IRIs are registrable; anything else is `invalidUri`.
  - `IdentityVerificationCredential` and `role:vetter` are `reserved`.
  - The four core predicates (`endorses/1`, `witnessed/1`, `vetted/1`, `presented/1`) are seeded at community start, so registering one again is `exists`.
- **`vtc/members/personhood/assert/0.1` and `_shared/0.1/community` (`acceptedIdvps`):** a community that vets in person is its own identity-verification provider. It issues the evidence itself, as an `IdentityVerificationCredential`.

## Binding changes
None in any language. The regenerated bindings change only doc comments and embedded schema text.

## Checks
- Rebased onto the 0.25.0 release (#694).
- `npm run validate`: 640 specs.
- `check-bindings`: all four languages agree, and 1368 error codes match.
- On the original branch, the full Rust, TS, Go and Dart suites passed. That branch was identical apart from the release commit.

title: spec(vtc/endorsements): IDVC issuance and reserved type values, matching VTI (#695)
body:
spec(vtc/endorsements): IDVC issuance and reserved type values, matching VTI (#695)

Describe what the implementation (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1859)
does. All affected specs are `draft` and change in place.

vtc/endorsements/issue/0.1: the reserved `typeUri`
`IdentityVerificationCredential` mints the community's identity-verification
credential (IDVC) instead of a statement. It is deliberately not a
DTGCredential — the DTG Credentials Core Specification says IDVCs are not —
but a plain W3C VC: `@context` [credentials/v2] only, `type`
[VerifiableCredential, IdentityVerificationCredential], issuer = community,
`credentialSubject.id` = `subjectDid` with the `claim` members beside it
(`claim` MUST NOT carry `id`; refused with `claimSchemaViolation`),
`validUntil`, and a revocation `credentialStatus` on the community status list,
so vtc/endorsements/revoke withdraws it. The reserved value is recognised before
the registry lookup; `role:vetter` is not issuable here (typeNotRegistered). A
worked example is added.

vtc/endorsements/list, show, revoke and vtc/_shared/0.1/endorsement: a row's
`typeUri` is a registered predicate IRI (statement),
`IdentityVerificationCredential` (IDVC), or `role:vetter` (vetter role VAC from
vtc/vetting/vetters/grant); the list filter accepts all three.

vtc/endorsement-types/register (and list, vtc/_shared/0.1/endorsement-type):
only absolute predicate IRIs are registrable — anything else is `invalidUri`;
`IdentityVerificationCredential` and `role:vetter` are refused as `reserved`;
the four core predicates (endorses/1, witnessed/1, vetted/1, presented/1) are
seeded when the community starts, so registering one again is `exists`.

vtc/members/personhood/assert/0.1 and vtc/_shared/0.1/community
(`acceptedIdvps`): the personhood evidence is an IDVC, and a community that
vets in person issues it itself as an `IdentityVerificationCredential` through
vtc/endorsements/issue.

Bindings regenerated: documentation and embedded schema text only; no type,
field or error-code changes in any language.

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.24.9` → `0.25.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.24.9` → `0.25.0` | breaking |

| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.24.9` → `0.25.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.24.9` → `0.25.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.24.9` → `0.25.0` | breaking |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.24.9` → `0.25.0` | breaking |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.21.16` → `0.22.0` | breaking |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.4.0`) | `0.3.16` → `0.4.0` | breaking |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.3.16` → `0.4.0` | breaking |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: Implementation Guide: the explanatory chapters, extracted from the specification (WG-13)
body:
The companion **DTG ZKP Implementation Guide**: a navigation companion to the compressed specification. It explains where each construction record fits, how the records compose, and how to read their evidence. It defines nothing; the specification is authoritative. The explanatory chapters are extracted from the specification, as the chair's Round 1 position asked (spec PR #11, refine 2) and WG-13 records.

**Chapters**
- **Reading this guide:** three reading paths, how to read a record part by part, and an outcome-to-record index linked into the specification.
- **From a Trust-Graph Outcome to a Proof:** the six implementation steps.
- **Trust-Graph Operations:** the life cycle, ADR-001, and admission.
- **Construction walkthroughs:** every record family in plain terms (what it proves, how its clauses fit, where its limits lie), each entry linking to its record.
- **Reading the evidence:** formal models, circuit proofs, runtimes and policy enforcement kept apart; evidence states; formal blocks; proving routes as a map; reading a mapping to a paper.
- **Cryptographic Background**, and **Attribution and maintenance**.

Working-group notes, call narrative, dated research entries, the SIROS review pack and the verification worklist are **not** in the guide. The open decisions are tracked in the specification's appendix; the working material is kept in the evidence repository.

**Also in this PR:** `.github/workflows/guide.yml` renders and checks the guide on pull requests and uploads a preview artifact (it does not deploy Pages; publication is a maintainer decision), and `README.md` points to the guide.

**Merge order:** this first. [dtgwg-zkp-spec PR #12](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-zkp-spec/pull/12) replaces the moved chapters with pointers here.

Local check: 8 chapters, internal links resolved, render clean from a clean checkout; all 18 record links resolve against the rendered specification.

title: spec!: conform vetting, member and endorsement credentials to DTG VSC/VAC and the predicate registry
body:
This updates the vetting, witness, member and endorsement Trust Task specs so that every DTG credential they define conforms to the DTG Credentials Core Specification (WD 0.6.0) and the DTG VSC predicate registry.
- Every credential uses the `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1` context and carries `issuerScope`.
- The retired `EndorsementCredential` and `WitnessCredential` types are gone.

Every spec touched is `status: draft`, so the changes are in place (SPEC §5.2).

This is a **draft** so it lands together with its consumers: dtg-credentials 0.12 (OpenVTC/dtg-credentials#33), then the VTI and OpenVTC migrations. The DTGWG reviewed and agreed the migration plan.

## Credential shapes

| Where | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `vetting/session/0.1` (the Vetting Statement) | `EndorsementCredential`; `endorsement.type` = `https://firstperson.network/endorsements/identity-vetting/0.1` | `StatementCredential` with predicate `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/vetted/1`. The body is in `object.value` with no `type`, `issuerScope` is `directed`, and `taskDigestMultibase` is now MUST. |
| `vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1`, `vetting/request/0.1` (vetter eligibility) | `EndorsementCredential` with `CommunityRole` | A community-issued `AuthorityCredential`: `authority { scope: <community>, actions: ["role:vetter"], maxAttenuation: 0 }`, `issuerScope: "public"` |
| `vtc/join-requests/decide/0.1`, `vtc/members/{personhood/assert,personhood/revoke,renew,rotate}/0.1` | `roleVec`, a role endorsement | **`roleVac`**, a community-issued VAC with `actions: ["role:<name>"]` |
| `vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.2` | `statementType` = endorsement type URI | `statementType` = the predicate IRI. `eligibleVetters.role` is matched as `role:<role>` in a community VAC. The DCQL examples filter `StatementCredential` + `credentialSubject.predicate`. |
| `vtc/endorsements/*` | mints an `EndorsementCredential` | mints a `StatementCredential`: predicate = registered `typeUri`, `object.value` = the claim, `issuerScope: "public"`. New error code `predicateNotIssuable` for profiles only a member may issue, such as `vetted/1`. |
| `vtc/endorsement-types/*` | `CommunityRole` reserved | Entries are predicate IRIs, and verifiers fail closed on unlisted ones. Roles are never registered. |
| `witness/session/0.1`, `witness/session/submit/0.1` | VWC | `StatementCredential` with predicate `witnessed/1`: subject = issuer of the witnessed credential, `object.digestMultibase`, `issuerScope` at least `directed` |
| `vtc/members/credentials/0.1`, `vault/credentials/{get,receive,query}` examples | `VerifiableMembershipCredential` / no DTG context | Real DTG VMCs. The grant is `public`. The member acknowledgement is `directed`, with the real digest of the printed grant. |

All recomputed `requirementsDigest` and statement digests are reproducible from the printed documents.

## Binding changes (source-breaking)
- **Rust:**
  - `role_vec` becomes `role_vac` (the field, the builder setter and serde) in decide, personhood assert/revoke, renew and rotate.
  - `current_role_vec_id` becomes `current_role_vac_id` in members show/list/update.
  - New error code `PREDICATE_NOT_ISSUABLE`.
  - Everything else is doc comments, embedded schemas and fixtures.
- **TS / Go / Dart:** the same renames. The identity-vetting shared body type is renamed (`VettedObjectValue` / `IdentityVettingStatementValueSharedDefinition`), and it loses its `type` field.

## Checks
- `npm run validate`, `validate-ceremonies` and `test-ceremonies` pass.
- `check-bindings`: 637 specs agree across the four languages.
- Rust:
  - `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`: 1325 passed.
  - `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate`: 1614 passed.
  - `fmt` is clean.
- TS: `tsc`, 79/79 tests and smoke pass.
- Go: `build`, `vet` and `test` pass.
- Dart: `analyze --fatal-infos` and tests pass.

## Related
- trustoverip/dtgwg-vsc-registry#19 (`vetted/1`, `presented/1`)
- trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#70
- OpenVTC/dtg-credentials#33

title: spec!: conform vetting, member and endorsement credentials to DTG VSC/VAC and the predicate registry (#691)
body:
spec!: conform vetting, member and endorsement credentials to DTG VSC/VAC and the predicate registry (#691)

* spec(vetting)!: conform vetting credentials to DTG VSC/VAC and the predicate registry

The credentials the vetting family defines now follow the latest DTG
Credentials Core Specification and the DTG VSC predicate registry. All
affected specifications are `draft`, so they change in place (SPEC §5.2).

Vetting Statement (vetting/session, vtc/vetting/revoke-statement): no longer
an `EndorsementCredential`. It is a Verifiable Statement Credential —
`type` [VerifiableCredential, DTGCredential, StatementCredential], `@context`
[credentials/v2, https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1],
`issuerScope` directed or public, `taskContext` and `taskDigestMultibase`
both REQUIRED — with `credentialSubject.predicate`
https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/vetted/1 and the vetting body in
`credentialSubject.object.value`. The body's `type` member is gone; the
predicate carries the meaning. The example's statement digest is recomputed.

vetting/_shared/0.1/identity-vetting: `$defs.IdentityVettingEndorsement` is
renamed `VettedObjectValue` and mirrors the registry's vetted/1 object
schema: no `type`, and the three digests are base58btc (`z…`) only.

Vetter eligibility (vtc/vetting/vetters/grant, vetting/request): the vetter
role credential is a Verifiable Authority Credential, not a `CommunityRole`
endorsement — issued by the community with `issuerScope` public,
`credentialSubject.authority` { scope: <community DID>,
actions: ["role:vetter"], maxAttenuation: 0 }. `eligibilityVp` carries that
VAC, and the applicant's advisory check reads `authority.scope` and
`authority.actions`. Wire field names (`endorsementId`, `credentialId`) are
unchanged; revocation still goes through vtc/endorsements/revoke.

vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.2 and vtc/_shared/0.1/schema-registry:
`statementType` is now the predicate IRI a counted statement carries in
`credentialSubject.predicate`; `eligibleVetters.role` is matched as the VAC
action `role:<role>` at the community's scope. The example
presentation-definitions filter on `StatementCredential` plus a DCQL claim on
`credentialSubject.predicate`, and both `requirementsDigest` values (and the
one vetting/request cites) are recomputed. vtc/schemas/accepts examples use
the registry predicate.

Endorsement types (vtc/_shared/0.1/endorsement-type,
vtc/endorsement-types/register): a registered `typeUri` is a predicate IRI
the community accepts — a registry IRI or a community-namespace IRI in the
registry definition format — and verifiers fail closed on unlisted
predicates. `CommunityRole` is no longer reserved; the `reserved` code stays.

witness/session, witness/session/submit: the VWC is described as a VSC under
https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/witnessed/1 — subject is the issuer
of the witnessed credential, `object.digestMultibase`, `issuerScope`
directed or public. The identity-vetting ceremony's attest step is reworded.

The firstperson.network credentials context and endorsement-type IRI are
removed everywhere, with no alias.

Bindings regenerated. Rust: documentation, embedded schema text and example
fixtures only; no type or field changes. TypeScript
`IdentityVettingShared_v0_1.IdentityVettingEndorsementSharedDefinition` is
now `IdentityVettingStatementValueSharedDefinition`. Go
`vettingsharedidentityvettingv0_1.IdentityVettingEndorsement` and Dart
`IdentityVettingEndorsement` are now `VettedObjectValue`: the `Type` field is
removed, the digest fields are plain strings, and the `DigestMultibase` alias
is gone from that package/library. Validators generated from these schemas
now reject a vetting body carrying `type`, and a manifest or statement using
the old endorsement-type IRI no longer matches.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(vtc/members)!: role credentials are VACs; rename roleVec to roleVac

Roles are authority, not endorsements: granting one is a decision by the party
that governs the community, and the DTG Credentials Core Specification carries
such a decision only in a Verifiable Authority Credential. Every role
credential these draft specs return is now described as the community-issued
AuthorityCredential with `issuerScope` public and
`credentialSubject.authority` { scope: <community DID>,
actions: ["role:<name>"] } — the shape vtc/vetting/vetters/grant issues for
role:vetter. All affected specs are `draft` and change in place.

Breaking wire renames (coordinated cut):
- `roleVec` -> `roleVac` in the responses of vtc/join-requests/decide/0.1,
  vtc/members/personhood/assert/0.1, vtc/members/personhood/revoke/0.1,
  vtc/members/renew/0.1 and vtc/members/rotate/0.1.
- `currentRoleVecId` -> `currentRoleVacId` in vtc/_shared/0.1/member
  (MemberResponse, used by vtc/members/show, list and update).

vtc/auth/recognise/0.2 (description only): the presentation carries the
foreign community's role VAC and VMC; the `role:<name>` action is the foreign
role. The retired 0.1, whose `vec` member is frozen, is unchanged.

Bindings regenerated. Rust: `Response::role_vec` -> `role_vac` (field and
builder setter) in vtc::join_requests::decide::v0_1,
vtc::members::personhood::{assert,revoke}::v0_1, vtc::members::renew::v0_1 and
vtc::members::rotate::v0_1; `MemberResponse::current_role_vec_id` ->
`current_role_vac_id` in vtc::members::{show,list,update}::v0_1. TypeScript,
Go and Dart rename the same members (`roleVac` / `RoleVac`,
`currentRoleVacId` / `CurrentRoleVacID`).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(vtc/endorsements): issue statements as DTG StatementCredentials

The DTG Credentials Core Specification no longer has an
`EndorsementCredential` type: a statement's meaning is its predicate. What
vtc/endorsements/issue mints is now a Verifiable Statement Credential —
`@context` [credentials/v2, https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1],
`type` [VerifiableCredential, DTGCredential, StatementCredential], issued by
the community with `issuerScope` public, `credentialSubject.predicate` =
`typeUri` (a registered predicate IRI) and `credentialSubject.object.value` =
`claim`, validated against the registered claimSchema, with a revocation
`credentialStatus` at the allocated slot. Under
https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/endorses/1 it is a Verifiable
Endorsement Credential; a community may register predicates of its own. The
spec gains a worked example. All affected specs are `draft`.

New error code `vtc/endorsements/issue:predicateNotIssuable`: a registered
predicate whose profile requires `taskContext`, or names an issuer other than
the community (vetted/1, for one), cannot be issued through this task.

vtc/_shared/0.1/endorsement and the list/show/revoke specs are reworded to
match. vtc/endorsements/revoke also documents that it revokes the vetter role
VAC issued by vtc/vetting/vetters/grant, keyed by the same `endorsementId`.
Wire member names (`endorsementId`, `typeUri`, `claim`, `endorsement`,
`credential`) are unchanged; the legacy naming is noted where it appears.

Bindings regenerated. Rust adds
`vtc::endorsements::issue::v0_1::error_codes::PREDICATE_NOT_ISSUABLE` (also in
`ERROR_CODES`); everything else is documentation and embedded schema text.
TypeScript, Go and Dart: documentation only.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(vtc/members/credentials): make VMC examples real DTG MembershipCredentials

`VerifiableMembershipCredential` is a rejected legacy type name. The
vtc/members/credentials/0.1 examples now carry DTG VMCs: `@context`
[credentials/v2, https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1], `type`
[VerifiableCredential, DTGCredential, MembershipCredential], the
community-issued grant with `issuerScope` public, and the member-issued
acknowledgement with `issuerScope` directed and a
`credentialSubject.digestMultibase` that is the real digest of the printed
grant (proof excluded), so `memberVmcBound: true` holds as shown. The complete
edge example also carries a `roleCredential` VAC ({ scope: <community DID>,
actions: ["role:moderator"] }), and the prose states the VMC and role
credential shapes. The `roleCredential` description names the VAC.

vault/credentials/get/0.1 and receive/0.1: the stored MembershipCredential
examples gain the DTG context, `DTGCredential`, `issuerScope` public, and
drop the non-DTG `memberOf` claim; the `types` echoes in receive and
vault/credentials/query/0.1 match. All affected specs are `draft`.

Bindings regenerated: documentation and example fixtures only, no type or
field changes in any language.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat!: conform to the v1 context — issuerScope, StatementCredential, predicate acceptance
body:
This brings the crate into line with the current DTG Credentials Core Specification (Working Draft 0.6.0) and the frozen `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1` context. It is a clean break: a 0.12 verifier refuses every credential a 0.11 issuer emits, and the reverse. The spec treats credentials issued before the Implementers Draft as non-conformant, so there is no legacy alias.

It is a **draft** until the VTI and OpenVTC migrations build and pass against it. The release PR (0.12.0) follows once they do.

## What changes
- **Context:** `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1` replaces `firstperson.network/credentials/dtg/v1`.
- **`issuerScope` is required** on every credential, as `IssuerScope { Pairwise, Directed, Public }`.
  - Every constructor takes it.
  - The community-issued VMC is always `public`.
  - `new_member_vmc_for` refuses a grant that isn't `public`.
- **`StatementCredential` (VSC)** carries `predicate` and `object`, where the object is one of `id`, `digestMultibase` or `value`.
  - Profile helpers: `new_endorses_vsc`, `new_witnessed_vsc` (replaces `new_vwc_for_session`, with subject = issuer of the witnessed credential), `new_vetted_vsc` and `new_presented_vsc`.
  - Constants for the registry IRIs.
  - Each profile's object kind, `taskContext` requirement and minimum `issuerScope` are enforced.
- **`PredicateAcceptList`** is a fail-closed verifier helper. It matches predicates byte-exactly and loads from the registry's `accept-list.json`, filtered by status.
- **VAC:** `maxAttenuation` was missing; spec-conformant VACs failed to parse without it. It is now parsed and enforced along the chain.
  - `new_community_role_vac` builds a role grant as `authority.actions: ["role:<name>"]`, which replaces `CommunityRole` endorsements.
- **Removed:**
  - `EndorsementCredential`, `WitnessCredential` and `RCardCredential`. The r-card is a verifiable data structure, not a DTG credential.
  - `new_vec`, `new_vwc*`, `new_rcard`, the deprecated `new_member_vmc` and `new_delegate_vdc`, and `Default for DTGCommon`.

The CHANGELOG has a before/after migration table covering every call site change.

## Related
