body:
feat!: conform to the v1 context — issuerScope, StatementCredential, predicate acceptance (#33)

* feat!: conform to the v1 context — issuerScope, StatementCredential, predicate acceptance (0.12.0)

DTG Core Credentials (Working Draft 0.6.0) moves every credential onto the frozen
https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1, makes issuerScope REQUIRED, and
replaces the EndorsementCredential and WitnessCredential subtypes with one
StatementCredential whose meaning is its predicate. Credentials issued before the
Implementers Draft are not conformant, so this is a clean wire break with no
legacy alias.

- Context: the W3C context first and DTG_CONTEXT_V1 second, exact strings; the
  firstperson.network context is refused. `type` must hold VerifiableCredential,
  DTGCredential and exactly one concrete subtype (PersonhoodCredential only as a
  hint on a VMC). The WD01 `digest` alias is gone.
- IssuerScope { Pairwise, Directed, Public }: REQUIRED top-level member, taken by
  every constructor; the community-issued VMC is always `public`, enforced at
  parse and in validate().
- StatementCredential: CredentialSubjectStatement { id, predicate, object,
  witnessContext? }, StatementObject { Id, DigestMultibase, Value }, predicate IRI
  validation (absolute, no CURIEs, NFC). new_vsc plus profile constructors for
  endorses/1, witnessed/1 (ports new_vwc_for_session, reading the subject and
  digest from the edge credential), vetted/1 and presented/1; core profile
  constraints (object kind, taskContext + taskDigestMultibase, minimum
  issuerScope) enforced at parse, validate and sign; subject-object checks
  witnesses_issuance_of / witnesses_presentation_of.
- PredicateAcceptList: fail-closed exact-match acceptance, from IRIs or from the
  registry's accept-list.json with a status floor, applying entry constraints.
- VAC: authority.maxAttenuation (a spec-conformant VAC carrying it previously did
  not parse), enforced at attenuation and in verify_chain per link and per
  ancestor; new_community_role_vac for role grants as `role:<name>` actions.
- Removed: EndorsementCredential, WitnessCredential, RCardCredential and their
  constructors and subject structs; the deprecated new_member_vmc and
  new_delegate_vdc; Default for DTGCommon.
- validate() re-runs the parse checks, so a credential mutated out of shape is
  never signed.

The construction named for the Linux Plumbers integration is recorded as an option until its authors publish; the lab's Groth16 route is constructed (clause 7 not built there).
   - **DG-024-4, pending review:** clause 4 admits secret-derived serials (cap each vetter) or blind-issued transferable tokens (cap the vetter set), with a `doesNotEstablish` line for the per-vetter cap.
   - **023 amended:** no witness without a relationship credential; the single-use challenge; and a `doesNotEstablish` line: no clause excludes a self-vouch by an applicant who is already a member (010 excludes it at the leaf level, 024 by clause 7). Evidence for WG-16.
   - **001 and 006:** issuance requirements the formal models showed necessary (domain separation or fixed path depth; `rl_root` over strictly sorted handles).
   - **Formal parts on seventeen records**, each with a scope line naming the clauses its model covers. They are machine-checked properties of abstract models, not implementation correspondence; the Lean sources are local until an immutable evidence revision is cited.
   - **007:** Denys Popov's review recorded as *refined* (did:key has no space for the commitment; did:peer numalgo 2/4, did:web, did:webvh can carry one).

4. **Record 013 specified — mutual edge admissibility (cred-spec #25).** From `requested` to `specified`: each party learns the counterparty's committed half would be admitted under its own community's published policy, and neither half is revealed until both answers are yes. Composed from 022 (commit before either answer), 001 twice (the form in the counterparty's policy root; a claimed membership in the prover's root) and 003. The negative space names policy privacy (policies stay published, the request's step one), fairness (a party can learn the yes and walk away) and acceptance once published. With it, every record in the draft is at `specified` or beyond, and all eighteen carry a formal model.

title: Digest-valued binders are unsalted and enumerable; blinding is deferred from WD02
body:
## Summary

Every digest-valued binder in this specification — the VWC `digestMultibase`, the member-issued VMC `digestMultibase` (#12), and the VDC `delegation.parent` / `delegation.accepts` (#19) — is an unsalted JCS-SHA-256 digest over content that is often low-entropy. Where a verifier is shown the digest but not the referenced credential, an observer who knows the schema and the governing vocabulary can recover the referenced content by enumeration.

## Where this was raised

@stormer78's design note in [dtgwg-cred-tf#40](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-tf/discussions/40), edge case E3: a VTC publishes forty scope strings; a commitment to a `scope` array is matched by enumerating plausible subsets in milliseconds. The same shape applies to a VWC digest over a VRC whose two identifiers are known, and to a VMC acknowledgement digest over a grant whose fields are predictable. The ZKP task force took this as a work item ([dtgwg-cred-tf#39](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-tf/discussions/39), ScottJeezey, 25 August): salted commitments available now, PRF-derived per-context pseudonyms as the fuller construction.

## Why it is not in WD02

It is cross-cutting — it changes the hashed representation of three credential types at once — and the construction (a salt member in the hashed block, ACDC-style `u`; a SAID; or a ZK commitment) is a choice the ZKP task force is working through. #19 lands the encoding (Multibase/Multihash per VC Data Integrity §2.6, per #17) without changing what is hashed, so a blinding scheme can be added to the canonicalization step later without a second encoding migration.

## What this issue tracks

- Whether WD03 should add a salt to the hashed representation of every digest-valued binder, and where it lives.
- Whether the same construction serves the anchoring / revocation-status / registry-membership unification proposed in cred-tf#40 §5.
- Coordination with the ZKP task force's Q2 (blinded binder) work.

Related: #9 (common-control linkage, the other cross-TF dependency).

title: Carry the trust-task citation in committed form: taskContext and taskDigestMultibase are durable correlators (ZKP record 008)
body:
**What is asked.** A credential that cites the exchange it was issued in carries the citation in the clear: under [PR #56](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/pull/56), `taskContext` (the initiating document's `id`) and `taskDigestMultibase` (its task digest). Both are stable across every presentation of that credential, so a credential presented twice is linked by its citation even where everything else about it is proven in zero knowledge. The ZKP specification's [record 008](https://trustoverip.github.io/dtgwg-zkp-spec/#construction-008-blinded-binder-taskcontext-hiding-presentation-correlation-unresolved) (blinded binder) asks the credential layer for one member: a committed form of the citation that a holder can open, in proof, to the exchange a verifier already holds.

**The shape.** Route 1 of record 008: the issuer carries `C = commit(taskContext, taskDigestMultibase; u)` with a blinding value `u` the holder keeps; a verifier that holds the exchange checks the opening, or in a proof the holder shows that `C` opens to the exchange the verifier names. Route 2 — a per-context pseudonym derived by a PRF from the holder secret and a context descriptor — is the fuller construction and stays on the ZKP side. The record also states what neither route gives: a visible `C` still links presentations of the same credential; hiding `C` inside the proof is what removes that.

**What is this specification's to decide**, so the Credentials TF can schedule it:

- whether the committed form replaces the pair or sits beside it under a profile;
- the member name(s), and that the value is `digestMultibase`-encoded per §Digest Encoding so both layers agree on the encoding;
- generation, distribution and retention of `u` — never published beside a low-entropy plaintext;
- how §Outcome Interpretability pairs a committed citation with outcome evidence: the verifier that holds the outcome evidence already holds the plaintext, so the opening is against what it holds, and nothing is lost there.

**What stays with the ZKP TF:** the proof that `C` opens to the exchange, its composition into the enclosing records, the per-context pseudonym — record 008 on `main`, re-read against PR #56 in [dtgwg-zkp-spec PR #11](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-zkp-spec/pull/11).

**Relation to #38.** `taskDigestMultibase` is a digest over a document, so the enumeration concern of #38 reaches it; record 022 (PR #11) covers the digest-valued members and would cover this one on the same terms. This issue is the citation's committed form, not its salt.

Filed at the credential maintainer's request on the ZKP working draft review (16 September). [PR #18](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/pull/18) is parked and is not this issue.

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in

  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a

title: Drop registry release tags: pin the commit or the accept-list digest
body:
This is the cleanup #14 calls for, now that the editors have agreed not to tag registry releases. It is mechanical: no predicate, context or definition-format member changes.

**Why.** The registry's unit of immutability is each `<name>/<n>` and each `context/vN`. A credential names those IRIs and never a registry version, so a repo-wide tag would be a second version axis nothing needs. The specification's own release records which registry IRIs it depends on.

## Changes
- **GOVERNANCE §8:** implementations bundle, and verifiers pin, the `commit` in `accept-list.json` or the digest of the list they fetched. `release.json` and the `.sha256` sidecars already digest every published file on every build.
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`:** deleted. It fired only on `v*` tags.
- **`meta/accept-list.schema.json`:** `revision` is dropped from `required` and `properties`, and `commit` gains a description saying it is what to pin.
- **`scripts/lib/registry.mjs`:**
  - The `git describe` lookup is gone.
  - `accept-list.json` and `release.json` no longer carry `revision`.
  - The build log line and the page footer show the commit only, e.g. "Commit `0d30941`" in place of "Revision unreleased (0d30941)".
  - The `validate.yml` and `deploy.yml` comments no longer mention tags. `fetch-depth: 0` stays, because the build reads `git log` for per-predicate dates.
- **PLAN.md:** C7, the repository tree, the `release.json` and accept-list shapes, the integrity-layers paragraph, the `release.yml` description, §1.8 step 4, and §2.7 (the "land release.yml" step is removed and the handoff renumbered to step 4, with its two cross-references).

## Consumers
`dtg-credentials` 0.12's `PredicateAcceptList` read `revision`. OpenVTC/dtg-credentials#33 (9e1531d) no longer requires it and ignores unknown envelope metadata; predicate entries stay strict. That crate change and this PR can land in either order.

One side effect: a list built before this PR still carries `revision`. The new schema has `additionalProperties: false`, so such a list no longer validates against it. No tagged list was ever published, only transient `"unreleased"` builds, so nothing pinned depends on the old shape.

## Checks
- `npm run check` passes: 4 predicate versions and 1 context validate, all tests pass, and the build succeeds.

## Review
GOVERNANCE.md is registry content, so this needs two editor approvals (§6, §9). PR #20 also edits `scripts/lib/render.mjs` and `scripts/lib/registry.mjs`. The overlap is one footer line, so whichever PR lands second takes a trivial rebase.

Closes the cleanup part of #14.

title: ToIP follow-ups: deliverable type, account handoff, host root ownership
body:
## Summary

Carried over from [cred-spec #52](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/issues/52), which flagged it as a question for ToIP staff and never got an answer: which ToIP deliverable type a repo-driven registry is, and whether the CTWG glossary's process and tooling can be borrowed wholesale.

Why it matters: a ToIP specification moves Working Draft → Implementers Draft → Approved Deliverable under the JDF process, and this registry deliberately does not, because a vocabulary has to be able to add an entry the week a community needs it. But the registry's content is licensed under OWFa 1.0 (LICENSE.md) and contributions under the OWF CLA plus DCO (CONTRIBUTING.md), copied from the Trust Tasks registry, and it is published under a ToIP-controlled host. Someone at ToIP should confirm that a continuously published, PR-governed registry fits an existing deliverable category (the glossary is the precedent), or say what it should be called and what process applies.

## Ask

A short answer from ToIP staff, recorded here and then in README.md, on: the deliverable category; whether the IPR mode in LICENSE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md is the right one for that category; and whether anything about the release process (GOVERNANCE §8) needs to change to fit it.

title: Hosting handoff to a ToIP account, and whether this registry's home page moves to /dtg/vsc
body:
## Summary

Two questions about the host, raised separately, that belong to the same conversation with ToIP.

**1. Handoff of the deployment.** GOVERNANCE §4.3 gates every promotion past `draft` on `registry.trustoverip.org` being served from a Cloudflare account the Trust Over IP Foundation owns, with the custom domain resolving there, and records "Handoff completed: *not yet*." Until that happens no predicate can become `candidate`, whatever its adoption. This needs an owner on the ToIP side and a date.

**2. Where this registry's home page lives.** Drummond's question on the spec call: if `registry.trustoverip.org` is to be the home of all ToIP-defined registries (there will be others), should the home page of the VSC predicate registry be at `registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc` rather than at the host root? Today the root `index.html`, the `<title>`, the nav and `siteName`/`siteUrl` in `registry.config.json` all present the host as this one registry.

## What is already right

Every IRI this registry publishes is already under `/dtg/`: predicates at `/dtg/vsc/<name>/<n>`, contexts at `/dtg/context/vN`, the definition format at `/dtg/meta/v1/`, and `/dtg/vsc` already serves the human predicate index. Moving the home page changes no identifier, no credential and no specification text. It is a `site/` and `registry.config.json` change: `/dtg/vsc` becomes this registry's home (the introductory text now on `/` moves there, nav "Home" points at it, `siteUrl` becomes `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc`), and `/` becomes a minimal landing page listing the DTG Working Group's namespaces under a ToIP registries heading.

## What needs a decision first

Who owns the host root once a second registry exists: one umbrella repository deploying `/` with each registry a separate Cloudflare Pages project on a path route, or this repository continuing to deploy the root and growing an umbrella page. The worker's routing is already path-based, so splitting later is a routing change rather than a rebuild, but the decision is ToIP infrastructure rather than this working group's, and it is the same decision as the account handoff above.

Proposed sequence: settle 1 and the ownership question with ToIP, then do the site change in one PR.

title: Make /dtg the registry's home and / a landing page for the host
body:
## Summary

Makes `/dtg` this registry's home and `/` a landing page for the host, as agreed on #15 after the editors' call: `registry.trustoverip.org` is to be the home of ToIP-defined registries, and what this repository publishes is the DTG Working Group's registry, whose namespaces (`vsc/`, `context/`, `meta/`) are already siblings under `/dtg/`. The predicate index at `/dtg/vsc`, with its `application/ld+json` and `application/json` variants, is unchanged.

No IRI, credential or specification text changes. Nothing linked to `/` as this registry's home, so no redirect is needed. The worker's routing is untouched: `/dtg` lies outside the negotiated prefixes and is served as a plain page.

## Changes, by the numbered steps on #15

1. **`/dtg` is the registry's home.** `render.homePage` now lands at `<registryPath>.html`, carrying the introductory paragraph (widened by one clause to mention the contexts and the definition format, since the page is no longer only about predicates) and the resource list for `/dtg/vsc`, `/dtg/context` and `/dtg/meta/v1/`, plus the GOVERNANCE link. The "releases page" sentence moves as is; the #14 cleanup PR drops it.
2. **`/` is a minimal landing page.** `render.landingPage`: the host-level heading, one sentence, and the registries this deployment serves, which is one entry pointing at `/dtg`. No registry nav; the footer stays.
3. **Naming.** `siteName` is now `DTG Registry`; the predicate index at `/dtg/vsc` is headed "VSC Predicate Registry". The repository name stays.
4. **Nav and titles.** The site-name link points at `/dtg`; "Predicates", "Contexts" and "Definition format" are as before; a trailing "All registries" link points at `/`. Pages under `/dtg/` keep the `· DTG Registry` title suffix; the root page uses the host-level name. Breadcrumbs start at `/dtg`.
5. **Config.** One new required value, `hostName` (`Trust Over IP registries`), read like everything else and added to the instance-values check. `siteUrl` stays as it is, since `deploy.yml` and `infra/verify.mjs` use it as the origin. The registry's home path is derived in `config.mjs` as the parent segment of `namespace` (`registryPath`); a namespace directly under the host root makes `/` the home itself, with no landing page and no "All registries" link, so a fork keeps the same shape at its own host.
6. **Verification.** `verify.mjs`'s root check now also asserts the page links to `/dtg`, and a new check asserts `/dtg` is HTML and carries `siteName`. The worker test gains a case for `/` and `/dtg` (plain pages, `/dtg/` redirects to `/dtg`); the build test asserts the root-level fixture shape and gains a nested-namespace case (`/community/vocab/`) covering the landing page, the home, the nav and the breadcrumbs.
7. **Docs.** README's "How the registry is served" table gains rows for `/` and `/dtg`, "Running your own registry" gains `hostName` and a sentence on the site's shape, the "Published registry" bullet points at `/dtg`, and PLAN.md §1.7's tree and §1.9's one-config-file bullet match.

## Verification

`docker compose run --rm check` against `origin/main`: validator, immutability, instance-values scan (now also checking `"Trust Over IP registries"`), 24 unit tests, build. The generated `index.html`, `dtg.html` and `dtg/vsc.html` were read back and match the description above.

Refs #15 (question 2). Question 1, the account handoff, stays open on #15 as gated by GOVERNANCE §4.3.

title: Add the vetted and presented predicates as draft
body:
## New predicates

**IRIs:**
- `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/vetted/1`
- `https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/presented/1`

Closes #16.

## Summary

**`vetted/1`.** The spec's identity-vetting worked example, moved into the DTG namespace. A member records that it checked an applicant's claimed identity, by a stated method, against stated document classes, for one community. The community weighs several such statements when it decides admission.

The `object.value` shape is now fixed in `vetting.schema.json`, not delegated. The registry entry is the normative definition (`definedIn` is `null`), and the spec's worked example is informative. Two differences from the spec's example:

- **camelCase values.** Enumerated values are `inPerson`, `priorAcquaintance`, `communityColleague`, `sameEmployer`, `otherPersonal` and `nationalId`. That is the convention VC Data Model 2.0 and Data Integrity use for their own values, for example `proofPurpose: "assertionMethod"`. It is also what OpenVTC and VTI already emit. The spec's example uses kebab-case.
- **`taskDigestMultibase` added.** The profile requires `taskContext`, and with it `taskDigestMultibase`. The spec's example omits the latter, and this registry's validator rejects an example without it.

trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#70 aligns the worked example on both points.

**`presented/1`.** The presentation/custody predicate drafted in cred-spec #52 and pointed to by `witnessed/1`'s *What this predicate is not*. The observed party is the holder: `credentialSubject.id` MUST be the `credentialSubject.id` of the credential that `object.digestMultibase` names. No implementation issues it yet. It enters as `draft` so the identifier exists, and it stays `draft` until something uses it.

One wording change from the #52 draft. "The presented credential… was issued to the subject" is no longer in `doesNotEstablish`, because the subject–object rule does establish that the credential names the subject. What the statement still doesn't establish is proof of control of that identifier. The entry now says exactly that.

## Admission checklist (GOVERNANCE.md §5)

- [x] 1. Complete against `meta/predicate.schema.json`. `npm run check` passes: 4 predicate versions, both new examples validated, including `object.value` against `vetting.schema.json`.
- [x] 2. On the **attests** side. `vetted` is explicitly not admission, and the profile says so. `presented` is not authority or task completion.
- [x] 3. **Unilateral**: each is signed by the issuer alone.
- [x] 4. Meaningful outside the exchange. Both cite it through `taskContext`, but both stay true afterwards.
- [x] 5. **No existing term with the same meaning.** Near misses:
  - For `vetted`: `endorses/1` would say the vetter endorses the applicant, which is not what they did. `witnessed/1` names a credential, and a vetting statement names none.
  - For `presented`: `witnessed/1` binds the subject to the referenced credential's *issuer*. `presented` binds it to its *subject*.
- [x] 6. IRIs in §2.1 form, with English label and definition.
- [ ] 7. **Editors' decision needed; the basis is stated here rather than ticked.**
  - `vetted`: this relies on "**credibly about to be** in use", not on "needed by a DTG specification". The spec's worked example is informative and uses a community namespace. Today the only implementer is one stack, OpenVTC with VTI, and its migration to this IRI is in progress, not yet public: `dtg-credentials` 0.11.0 and `vta-sdk` 0.56.0 still emit the WD02 endorsement shape. Whether one stack meets "more than one community" is for the editors to decide.
  - `presented`: no consumer exists. Its only basis is the review request on cred-spec #47 and the pointer in `witnessed/1`. The risk of admitting it early is real: if the meaning needs to change once a consumer appears, that burns `/1` and the fix becomes `/2`. If the editors would rather not reserve the name, I'll split `presented/1` into its own PR and leave it open until something issues it.

## Naming (GOVERNANCE.md §2.3)

- [x] Simple past for a completed act in both.

## Example

- [x] `vetted/1/examples/video-vetting.json` and `presented/1/examples/presented-vmc.json`.

## Notes for reviewers

`vetted/1` stays `draft` while cred-spec #38 (blinding digest-valued binders) and #58 (committed task citation) could change how its three digest members and its task citation are carried.

## Review

Two approving reviews from the `predicates/` owners in CODEOWNERS.

[cred-spec #52](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/issues/52) named two first entries beyond the core profiles, and neither is in the registry yet; only `endorses/1` and `witnessed/1` exist.

**`presented`** — the presentation/custody predicate a reviewer asked for on cred-spec #47: the issuer observed the subject *present* the credential the object names, where the subject is the holder rather than the credential's issuer. A full draft definition is in the body of cred-spec #52 (`objectKind: ["digestMultibase"]`, `taskContextRequired: true`, `minimumIssuerScope: "directed"`, subject–object rule "`credentialSubject.id` MUST be the `credentialSubject.id` of the credential `object.digestMultibase` names"). **`vetted`** — the identity vetting predicate. Cred-spec #50 landed it as the specification's single worked example under *Community-Defined Predicates*, under an illustrative community namespace, which is fine for the specification; #52 intended it to be the registry's first entry as well. Whether it enters the DTG namespace is an admission question under GOVERNANCE §5, criterion 7 in particular (needed by a DTG specification, or in use, or credibly about to be, by more than one community). The name follows §2.3 (simple past for a completed act).

## Notes

- Neither predicate adds a member beside `object` in `credentialSubject`, so neither needs a context term; `v1` stays as it is (GOVERNANCE §3.1). The vetting payload lives entirely inside `object.value`, which the context types as `@json`.

title: Align the identity-vetting worked example with the registry's vetted/1
body:
This is an editorial change to the informative worked example under *Community-Defined Predicates*. No normative text changes.

It companions trustoverip/dtgwg-vsc-registry#19, which publishes this profile as `dtg:vetted` (`https://registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/vsc/vetted/1`).

## Changes

- **Registry pointer.** The example keeps its illustrative `vtc.example` IRI, because the section is about how a community defines its own predicate. It now adds that the registry publishes the same profile, and that a community running peer vetting uses the registry IRI rather than minting a second one.
- **camelCase values.** `in-person`, `prior-acquaintance`, `community-colleague` and `same-employer` become `inPerson`, `priorAcquaintance`, `communityColleague` and `sameEmployer`. That is the convention VC Data Model 2.0 and Data Integrity use for their own values, for example `proofPurpose: "assertionMethod"`. It is also what the OpenVTC and VTI implementations already emit, so the registry entry, the spec and the code now agree.
- **`taskDigestMultibase` added to the example JSON.** Base Structure makes it REQUIRED wherever `taskContext` is REQUIRED, and this profile requires `taskContext`. The registry's validator rejected the example without it.
- **`attestationTextDigest` marked optional.** A community that shows the vetter no attestation text has nothing to digest. This matches the registry schema and the implementation.

## Context

The DTG credential flows between OpenVTC and the VTC/VTA are being migrated to this spec: `StatementCredential` with registry predicates, `issuerScope`, and the `registry.trustoverip.org/dtg/context/v1` context. The editors reviewed the migration plan. This PR is the spec-side piece of it.

title: feat(social-recovery): add the social-recovery task family (4 specs)
body:
This is the `social-recovery` family, split out per your review of #672 — one PR for the
categories, then one PR per family with its schemas. **CODEOWNERS routes this to the
`social-recovery` reviewers only.**

## What is here

- **4 specs**, each with a `payload.schema.json`.
- Categories used: **`key-management`** — all of them already in your enum. **This family
  does not depend on #672**, so it can be reviewed and merged independently of the
  category discussion.
- Additions only. The assembler stages the diff and **refuses to run if anything
  outside `specs/social-recovery/` changed, or if any path already exists upstream** — the
  clash check is exercised against a planted file each run, so a silent pass cannot
  be mistaken for a clean one.

## Validation

**596 specs validate against your own `spec.meta.schema.json`** — your
existing corpus plus these 4 — using **your unpatched 17-category schema**,
not a version of it we edited. 0 failures. Every spec declares `errorCodes`.

Payload schemas are draft 2020-12, `$id` on `https://trusttasks.org/spec/<slug>/<version>`,
`additionalProperties: false`, and reference `$defs/Ext` from
`_framework/0.2/framework.schema.json` — your convention, not one we invented.

## Why this family first

It is small, and it is one of only three of our families that is already
**lowerCamelCase-clean**, so it does not carry the §4.10 casing work we owe you on
the rest. **Please treat it as a shape template**: if the file layout, the spec
structure, the schema conventions or the commit/PR format are wrong, correcting them
here costs you one review instead of twenty-eight. We will not open the remaining
families until you have had a chance to say.

## Known-open, stated rather than hidden

- 🟡 **Worked examples are not yet round-trip verified against our implementation.**
  We tested this and the honest result is that some examples describe an intended
  API rather than the one our code accepts today. Where that is true of a spec in
  this family we would rather fix the example than quietly ship it — tell us if you
  want those corrected before merge or tracked separately.
- 🟡 **`ext` passthrough is declared but not universally implemented** on our side.
  The schemas model it per your `$defs/Ext`; our runtime honours it for some
  operations and not yet all.
- The `Security & Privacy` sections follow your house structure. Our earlier
  submission cited internal `src/...` paths in some spec bodies; **0 of your 592 do
  that**, so they are removed here.

## Casing

On your `sourceClass` point: **your conclusion was right and we are conforming.**
§4.10 items 3 and 4 govern it (your citation of §8.3 was the error-code table), and
we confirmed you hold your own corpus to it — zero unexplained snake_case enum values
across your 592 payload schemas. This family needed no changes. The rest is measured
and in flight; see the discussion on #672.

## Open questions for maintainer review

The `🟡 NEEDS-REVIEW:` convention this description promised is now actually in the
specs, under an **Open Questions for Registry Review** heading in each. Thank you for
catching that it was missing — it should have been there from the start.

It was missing for a reason on our side, now fixed: our own validator treated any spec
containing the marker as a failure, so the convention could not be used without turning
our own gate red. That encoded the wrong reading of our rule. A `NEEDS-REVIEW` marker
does not mean "we did not finish it" — it means "complete as far as we can take it, and
flagged for the reviewer who has to decide."

- **`social-recovery/buddies/list`** — in our reference implementation this is a
  same-device, owner-local read: a Settings-screen listing of the operator's own recovery
  buddies, not a request one party sends about another party's data. We documented it as
  the code behaves, but whether it belongs in a peer-facing registry at all is a call we'd
  like your judgment on.
- **`social-recovery/status/get`** — declares a `deviceNotFound` error code our
  implementation never emits (`localDeviceDid` is only checked for list membership, never
  looked up against an owner record). Flagged rather than silently resolved either way.
- **`social-recovery/buddies/add`** — same pattern: declares a `selfEnrollment` code our
  implementation never emits; nothing compares the buddy DID to the requester's own.

A fourth candidate was deliberately **not** marked: `buddies/list` publishing each buddy's
`publicKeyHex` is an intentional disclosure whose rationale is already in the spec text.
It is a decision, not an open question, and padding this list would cost you attention
rather than save it.

## Still red, and named rather than left to look handled

`bindings match specs`, both drift checks and `cargo test` are failing because no
generated client binding (Rust/TypeScript/Go/Dart) declares these four operations'
TYPE_URIs — codegen has not been run for this family. That is a generator run, not a
spec change. We are running it; this note is here so the red is not mistaken for a
spec defect.

## Summary

VTC batch 3, part 4 (stacked on #1836). Website content moves off the raw-byte routes and onto the Trust Task spine (`trust_tasks::website_tasks`, trust-tasks #682):

- `vtc/website/upload/{begin,chunk,commit,abort}/0.1`: a chunked upload.
  - **Hashes are committed in `begin`.** It records the target (a file at a path, with an optional `ifMatch`, or a whole-site bundle), the total size, the whole-content SHA-256 and every chunk's digest before any byte moves.
  - **Each `chunk` is checked against its committed digest and length on arrival.** Chunks are at most **256 KiB**, and the spec's floor is 16 KiB.
  - **`commit` verifies the reassembled SHA-256 before anything is written.** On a mismatch the upload is discarded (`digestMismatch`). `commit` then writes a file target atomically, re-checking the path, the deploy mode and `ifMatch`, or stages a bundle (`stagedUntil`).
- `vtc/website/deploy/0.1` publishes a staged bundle and consumes it. It re-checks the staged bytes' hash, and a bundle the site refuses gets `bundleRefused` with the site unchanged.
- `vtc/website/files/show/0.1` does ranged reads of up to 256 KiB. Each read reports the whole-file `etag` and the served `contentType`, and supports `ifMatch` (`changed`).
- **Upload state is bounded per identity and expires.** The transfer reuses `vti_common::backup_transfer::chunked`, the machinery behind `backup/*`: staging, manifest checks, the per-DID chunk rate limiter and the sweeper. A slot lives 5 minutes from its last chunk and never more than an hour, and an identity holds at most 3 open at once. An upload belongs to its beginner, and anyone else's id gets `notFound`. `vti-common` gains owner-based `initiate_import_for`/`put_chunk_for`/`finalize_precheck_for`, because the website's authority is `Admin` (the old routes' `AdminAuth`), not the unrestricted admin the backup wrappers still require.
- **Size**: `begin`, `chunk` and the `files/show` response declare `maxDocumentBytes` (256/352/352 KiB). #1834's codegen'd limits admit a full-size chunk document from a signer with standing.
- **Audit**: file writes and deploys are now audited against the signing administrator, where the old routes recorded the literal `"admin"`.
- Every declared code is witnessed in `tests/website_spine.rs`, except `upload/chunk:alreadyStored`. That one is baselined (UNWITNESSED 9→10) because different bytes at a stored index fail the committed digest first (`chunkMismatch`).

The console has no website screen, so there is no console change.

## Routes

Removed: `GET /v1/website/files/{path}`, `PUT /v1/website/files/{path}`, `POST /v1/website/deploy`.

Kept, and out of this batch because they carry no bytes and were not in scope: `GET /v1/website/files`, `DELETE /v1/website/files/{path}`, `GET /v1/website/generations`, `POST /v1/website/rollback/{gen}`. `vtc-client` and `cnm` call none of the website routes.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`, fmt
- [x] new/changed targets: `website_spine` (new, 11), `website_task_gating`, `trust_task_manifest`, `trust_task_size`; lib `spine_proof_tests` (94), `error_code_census`, `trust_tasks::{tests,size,backup_tasks}`; `vti-common` `backup_transfer`
- [x] openapi snapshot and `wire.ts` regenerated; admin-ui lint
- [ ] CI

title: ci(release): retry the publishing pass on a fresh crates.io token
body:
The #1821 release published 29 crates and then failed on `vta-tee` with `403 Forbidden: Invalid authentication token`, exactly 30 minutes after the Trusted Publishing exchange. A Trusted Publishing token lives 30 minutes, and release-plz publishes the whole workspace in one pass on one token.

- The release job now runs up to three passes, each after a fresh `crates-io-auth-action` exchange. Attempts 1 and 2 use `continue-on-error`, and each later pass runs only if the one before it failed.
- release-plz skips crates already on crates.io, so a retry resumes where the last token ran out. A non-token failure, such as an ordering or build error, fails every pass the same way and still fails the job.
- `timeout-minutes` goes from 60 to 110: three 30-minute passes plus setup.
- The single-crate recovery path (`workflow_dispatch` with `package`) is unchanged.
- `docs/05-design-notes/trusted-publishing.md` explains the lifetime and the retry.

title: feat(vtc-service)!: console signing keys are auth/signing-key Trust Tasks
body:
## Summary

VTC batch 3, part 3 (stacked on #1835). The console's signing keys move from `/v1/admin/console-keys` to `auth/signing-key/{enroll,list,revoke}/0.1` (trust-tasks #680) on the Trust Task spine (`trust_tasks::signing_key_tasks`). All of enroll's normative items 4–8 are implemented:

- **4. The approval digest covers the whole document.** No delegation is written without a passkey gesture of `identityDid` bound by `bound_step_up::operation_digest` to the type and the **whole** payload (`signingKeyDid`, `identityDid`, `scope`, `deviceLabel`, `expiresAt`), recomputed over the document as received. A changed label or another key finds no gesture (tested).
- **5. Step-up only on the requester's authenticator; standing is not an oracle.** The gesture is asked for inline, only of the requester (`bound_step_up::request_for_enrolment`). It offers every registered console passkey, as an unauthenticated passkey login already does, so the first answer is the same for an administrator and for a DID nobody has heard of (tested). Nothing reaches the identity's devices. Standing (a live `Admin` row) is checked after the gesture, and only a passkey registered to `identityDid` can record it.
- **6. Capped expiry.** Every delegation has an expiry, at most 30 days away. A requested `expiresAt` is capped, and absent means 30 days. `ConsoleKeyDelegation.expires_at` is no longer optional.
- **7. Console-only scope, never accepted for `assertionMethod`.** The stored delegation carries `scope: console`. The spine refuses any approval type (`auth/step-up/approve-response`, `task-consent/decision`) whose proof is by a key a delegation names, whatever the delegation's state. The console now answers bound step-ups **unsigned** with `evidence.kind = webauthn` (approve-response 0.4 allows this), with the passkey as the only gate. An unsigned answer is heard only when it is an approval carrying a *console session passkey* of the subject. It is checked before the pending step-up is touched. A member's step-up passkey is still only accepted beside the member's own signature, and a denial always needs one.
- **8. Per-identity cap and rate limits.** At most 5 active keys per identity (`tooManyKeys` with `details.maxActiveKeys`). Enrolment attempts are limited per identity (10), per enrolling key (5) and overall (120) in each 10-minute window, answered `unavailable` with `retryAfter`. Per-source-address limiting is the HTTPS door's governor.
- Also item 1 (`keyNotIssuer`), item 2 (the key rules before anything about the identity: `selfDelegation`, `keyHoldsStanding`, `alreadyEnrolled`, `keyRevoked`, `expiryInPast`), item 9 (the key rules are re-checked, the cap checked, the gesture spent and the row written under one lock), and item 12 (audited against the identity, naming the key).
- **Revoke** is accepted from the key itself, from its identity, or from an unrestricted admin. A context-scoped admin revoking a peer's key, like an unknown key, gets `notFound`. A repeat revocation reports the original `revokedAt`. **List** returns the signer's identity's own keys (its own row, or the identity an active delegation names).
- **Console**: enrolment signs with the new browser key, runs the bound gesture (`postSignedWithStepUp`), and re-sends the identical document. List and revoke are signed by this browser's key. `answerStepUp` sends unsigned.

## Routes

Removed: `POST /v1/admin/console-keys`, `GET /v1/admin/console-keys`, `DELETE /v1/admin/console-keys/{console_did}`. None kept; `vtc-client` and `cnm` never called them.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`, fmt
- [x] changed targets: `signed_step_up` (enrolment, capped lifetime, oracle parity, digest binding, key-rule codes, cap, revoke authority, list, routes gone, console key cannot sign an approval), `unrestricted_admin_consent`, `trust_task_manifest`, `openapi_schema_names`; lib `spine_proof_tests` (89), `step_up_passkey_tasks`, `signing_key_tasks` (rate limits), `acl::`, `git_ns::tests`
- [x] openapi snapshot and `wire.ts` regenerated; admin-ui lint; vitest 495/495
- [ ] CI

title: fix(vta-service): passkey-only step-up once a subject has enrolled one
body:
## Summary

Security change: once a subject (step-up approver) has an enrolled passkey verification method, step-up MUST be satisfied by a passkey (WebAuthn) assertion only.

- `mint_pending_step_up` no longer advertises `did-signed` in `acceptableEvidence` once the approver has an enrolled passkey (checked via a new `subject_has_passkey`).
- `handle_approve_response` now checks the submitted evidence kind against the pending step-up's own `acceptable_evidence` and refuses with `auth/step-up/approve-response:noGate` when the kind was not offered — which is what makes a did-signed (or evidence-absent) response fail closed for a passkey holder, even from a client that ignores the mint-time offer.
- A subject with no enrolled passkey is unaffected: both gates are still offered and accepted.
- `operations::passkey_vms::finish_enrollment` (passkey VM enrolment) now also clears any live step-up elevation the subject reached *without* a passkey (`Session::clear_non_passkey_elevation`, `clear_non_passkey_elevation_for_did`), so a session already stepped up before enrolment can't outlive the switch to passkey-only.
- Along the way: the webauthn step-up gate's credential-id → verification-method lookup is now read from the subject's local WebVH document (`operations::passkey_vms::find_passkey_vm_by_credential_id`) rather than the generic DID resolver's `enumerate_passkey_vms`, which is a pre-existing stub that always returns no verification methods (documented there as deferred "Phase 3 hardening"). Without this, webauthn step-up approve-responses could never actually succeed for any subject — that gate was silently dead before this change.
- Checked `messaging/auth.rs` and `routes/auth.rs` for any other non-passkey route to `aal2` for a passkey-holding subject: `routes/auth.rs`'s `passkey_login_finish` is itself the passkey route (fine), and there is no other route that elevates a session's `acr` outside `trust_tasks::step_up`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy -p vta-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p vti-common --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo check -p vta-service --no-default-features --features rest,didcomm` (webvh off)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p vta-service --no-default-features --features rest --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt`
- [x] New unit tests: a passkey holder's did-signed approve-response is refused (`noGate`) and a webauthn approve-response over the same enrolled passkey is accepted end-to-end (real WebAuthn assertion, verified through the real gate); a subject with no passkey keeps did-signed; enrolling a passkey clears a prior non-passkey elevation (session-level and DID-level)
- [x] Existing `trust_tasks::step_up`, `operations::passkey_vms`, `vti_common::auth::session`, `messaging::auth`, `routes::auth` unit tests, plus the `mock_vta` `webvh_family_response_shapes` integration test (full enroll-challenge/enroll-submit/revoke ceremony) — all green

title: fix(vta-service): passkey-only step-up once a subject has enrolled one (#1854)
body:
fix(vta-service): passkey-only step-up once a subject has enrolled one (#1854)

A subject with an enrolled passkey verification method must complete
step-up with a WebAuthn assertion only: mint no longer offers the
did-signed gate for such an approver, and handle_approve_response
refuses a did-signed (or evidence-absent) approve-response for one
with noGate, even if a stale client sends it anyway. A subject with no
passkey keeps the original did-signed-or-webauthn offer.

Passkey enrolment also clears any elevation the subject reached
without a passkey, so a stepped-up session from before enrolment can't
outlive the switch to passkey-only.

Along the way, wires the webauthn step-up gate's credential-id lookup
to the enrolled DID's local WebVH document instead of the
still-stubbed generic resolver enumeration, which otherwise made every
webauthn step-up approve-response fail closed.

title: fix(vtc-service): sign operational Trust Tasks with one proof, not one per held key
body:
A VTC holding a second (post-quantum) key emitted a proof array on every operational document. A Trust Task's `proof` is a single object (`trust_tasks_rs::Document`), so the registry client's reparse failed locally with `invalid type: sequence, expected struct Proof`. The boot health probe, membership sync and the hook relay all failed as a `Transient` error that never cleared, leaving `registry_status=degraded`.

`sign_operational` now signs with the primary key only. Credentials are unchanged and still carry a proof set from every key.

Test: `a_hybrid_signer_signs_a_trust_task_with_one_proof` signs with a two-key signer and round-trips through `TrustTask`.

Not run: the full workspace / CI-equivalent suites.

title: security(vtc-service): a step-up passkey, once enrolled, is the only gesture that counts
body:
## Summary
- Once a subject holds a dedicated step-up passkey, the operation-bound step-up gate (`acl/grant`, `acl/change-role`, git break-glass, ...) accepts a gesture only from that passkey — their ordinary session/console passkey stops counting for them.
- Wallet-signed (`didSigned`) evidence on `auth/step-up/approve-response` was, and remains, refused unconditionally on this door (`noGate`), whether or not a step-up passkey is enrolled.
- A subject with no step-up passkey keeps today's route (any of their registered passkeys), so nobody already relying on it is locked out.
- Enrolling a step-up passkey now also revokes (not merely waits out) any session elevation the subject already holds, since that elevation was granted through a route that stops counting for them the moment a step-up passkey exists.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt -p vtc-service` (no diff)

title: feat(spec-meta): add 10 category values for domains the taxonomy has no home for
body:
## What this changes

Two files, and they have to move together:

1. `specs/spec.meta.schema.json` — ten values added to `#/properties/category/enum` (17 → 27).
2. `website/assets/data.js` — the matching ten `window.TT_CATEGORIES` entries.

Nothing else. No specs, no bindings, no version bumps, no CHANGELOG entry.

This is the first of the split series you asked for. The families and their specs
follow as one PR per family, so `CODEOWNERS` can route each one by slug.

## Why both files

`scripts/build-registry.mjs::checkCategoryTaxonomy()` fails the build on any enum
value with no `TT_CATEGORIES` entry — *"its specs would render without a
name/color and crash the spec page"* — and warns on the reverse. So the enum
patch alone would break `main`, and the `data.js` entries alone would be dead
weight. `CLAUDE.md` in this repo records this shipping for real once, when
`chat/message/1.0` went out broken on the live site.

We reproduced that check locally against a clean clone before opening this, in
four arms: pristine/pristine silent, patched-enum + unpatched-`data.js` failing on
exactly these ten, patched/patched clean, and unpatched-enum + patched-`data.js`
warning rather than failing. The third arm alone would not have told us whether
the check discriminates.

We also assert something the build does not: every `color` we set resolves to a
`--tt-<color>` token `tokens.css` actually defines, because `catColor()` emits
`var(--tt-${cat.color})` and an undefined token renders nothing rather than
failing. All ten use the existing six-token palette.

## The ten values

| Value | Family it serves | Why no existing value fits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `temporal-coordination` | `calendar` | Negotiating *when*, between parties |
| `automation` | `scheduler` | Scheduled or triggered execution with no human in the loop |
| `media` | `media` | Custody and delivery of recorded audio/video/image/book assets |
| `communications` | `call` | Real-time synchronous session setup — offer/answer, participants |
| `collaboration` | `canvas` | Concurrent multi-party editing of shared state |
| `matchmaking` | `matchmaking` | Mutual-interest discovery and introduction |
| `privacy` | `data-subject` | Data-subject rights against a controller |
| `storage` | `files` | Document custody on behalf of another party |
| `task-management` | `todo` | Human work tracking and assignment |
| `prediction` | `forecast` | A claim about the future plus the record that settles it |

**`privacy`** has a regulatory anchor (GDPR data-subject rights) the registry has
no home for today. `consent` covers a subject *granting* permission; it cannot
express a subject compelling a controller who would rather not comply.

**`prediction`** is the only temporally-directional value here. `reputation`
scores the past and `provenance` records it; neither can hold the claim half.

## Where we think you are right

You flagged `communications`, `matchmaking` and `media` as overlapping the
existing `chat`, `messaging` and `data-exchange`. We would rather discuss those
three than defend them, and we are happy to drop or merge any of them. If you
want the smallest possible first step, `privacy` and `prediction` are the two you
said make a good case, and this PR is easy to reduce to just those.

Separately, and this one is ours to fix rather than yours: all 36 `bridge/*`
specs we proposed declare `category: messaging`, and you are right that this
repo's `messaging` means operator-facing control of a mediator or relay, not an
application-level protocol bridge. That is a genuine misclassification on our
side. We will pick a better category for `bridge` in its own PR rather than
smuggle it through this one.

## Provenance

These ten values are not a taxonomy proposal in the abstract. Each one is the
category a family needed while implementing the Trust Task framework against this
registry, and every one of them is declared by specs we are submitting in the
follow-up PRs. If a value ends up with no family behind it, it should not land —
`checkCategoryTaxonomy()` would warn about it as dead weight, correctly.

title: fix(vta): build when vta-config's tee feature is unified in
body:
`cargo check -p vta-service -p vta-tee` failed with `missing field tee in initializer of AppConfig`.

`AppConfig.tee` exists whenever `vta-config/tee` is on, and `vta-tee` turns it on. `vta-service` and `vta-backup` gated their `AppConfig` literals on their *own* `tee` feature. So any build that unified `vta-tee` with a non-tee `vta-service` or `vta-backup` broke, because features must be additive.

The fix always enables `vta-config/tee` in both crates (it adds only the field and its plain config types, with no dependencies) and sets the field unconditionally. TEE behaviour stays behind each crate's own `tee` feature.

Checked: `cargo check --all-targets` for `-p vta-service`, `-p vta-service -p vta-tee`, `-p vta-service --features tee`, `-p vta-backup` and `-p vta-backup -p vta-tee`, plus clippy `-D warnings` and fmt.

title: Decide whether the registry also holds VDC scope, VAC actions and endorsement vocabularies
body:
## Summary

An open question carried over from [cred-spec #52](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/issues/52): whether this repository should also hold the other value vocabularies the DTG credentials already depend on, which have the same publication gap as predicates did.

- VDC `delegation.scope` entries (the acts a delegate may perform), which the specification says are "opaque strings compared for exact equality" whose vocabulary "is defined by the governing VTC or VTN".
- VAC `authority.actions` entries, likewise governed-party-defined, compared as exact case-sensitive strings.
- The VEC endorsement vocabulary carried in `object.value` (`SkillEndorsement` and friends).

GOVERNANCE §2.5 already reserves the shape of the answer: "a new vocabulary under `/dtg/` gets its own sibling of `vsc/` and its own definition format." What is not decided is whether the working group wants to curate a shared default set for any of these, or leave them entirely to communities.

## Constraints

- These are value vocabularies, not JSON-LD terms. `contexts/v1.jsonld` already types `scope` and `actions` as sets of plain strings and the endorsement payload as `@json`, so publishing allowed values under a sibling namespace does not touch the context.
- The one thing that would force a new context version is deciding the values should be IRIs (`"@type": "@id"`) rather than opaque strings. That is a design change to the specification, not something this issue proposes.
- The registry's name and `siteName` say "VSC Predicate Registry". If it grows to hold these, the "DTG Vocabularies" name floated in #52 becomes the better one, and that interacts with the home-page question.

No action proposed yet; this issue exists so the question has a home the registry's reviewers see.

title: vta-service-v0.46.0
body:
### Added

- **vta**: Vta contexts update --clear-did, offline ([#1830](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1830))

The offline binary's `contexts update` could set a DID but not clear one,
  the one CLI left behind by #1828. `--clear-did` conflicts with `--did`
  and clears through update_context_did(None), as pnm's does.

- **vta**: Clear a context's DID with vta/contexts/update-did/1.1 ([#1828](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1828))

* feat(vta): clear a context's DID with vta/contexts/update-did/1.1

  Once a context had a DID it could be replaced but never removed:
  update-did/1.0 requires a non-empty `did`, and contexts/update only sets
  one. `webvh/dids/delete` refuses a DID a context still acts as and says
  "reassign it first", so a context's last DID could not be retired short
  of assigning another the operator did not want.

  Serve update-did/1.1 (trust-tasks `feat(vta/contexts/update-did): 1.1`)
  beside 1.0 through one handler. `did: null` clears — the record comes
  back with `did` absent, and clearing a context with no DID succeeds. A
  string `did` must be a DID; 1.1 is parsed into the generated
  `update_did::v1_1::Payload`, whose `PayloadDid` holds the pattern, and
  1.0 keeps its original body. 1.0 is listed as superseded by 1.1, and the
  legacy `PUT /contexts/{id}/did` now names 1.1 as its successor.

  - vta-sdk: `TASK_CONTEXTS_UPDATE_DID_1_1` (retry-safe);
    `update_context_did` sends 1.1; new `clear_context_did`.
  - pnm / cnm: `contexts update-did <id> --clear`, and
    `contexts update <id> --clear-did` (conflicts with `--did`), both on
    update-did so a context admin can do it.
  - The delete blocker offers both fixes and names update-did rather than
    contexts/update (super-admin only); its text also carried a run of
    literal spaces from an unjoined line wrap.

  Needs a trust-tasks-rs release carrying update_did::v1_1; see the TODO
  on the floor in Cargo.toml.

- **trust-tasks**: Advertise the acceptance window over trust-task-discovery 0.3 (VTI-TRN-047) ([#1817](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1817))

Both VTI node types refuse a document more than ten minutes (plus 60 s of
  skew) past its issuedAt (VTI-OPS-024). A sender holding a document before
  delivery has to know that window to decide when to issue a new attempt
  instead, and until now the only way to know it was to share the constant.
  trust-task-discovery/0.3 (trust-tasks #677, trust-tasks-rs 0.24.4) lets a
  responder state it.

  - Raise the trust-tasks-rs floor to 0.24.4, the first release carrying
    discovery 0.3, and trust-tasks-capability-client with it. Only those two
    lockfile entries move.
  - vti-common: `trust_task::acceptance::AcceptanceWindow` and
    `VTI_ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW` (ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW + DEFAULT_SKEW). This is the one
    value the consumers apply (`freshness_policy()`), the responders advertise
    (`advertised()`, rounded down so it is never wider, VTI-TRN-047), and the
    push engine judges staleness by (`past_max_age`, `refuses`).
    `trust_task::discovery` has the pattern grammar and the 0.1/0.3 response
    builders, so both nodes answer the same way.
  - VTA: serves trust-task-discovery/0.3 next to 0.1, answering each in the
    version it was asked. The window goes at response level, since the VTA
    applies one window to everything it dispatches. The 0.1 frameworkVersion was
    "0.2", a stale copy of the framework crate's default. It is now "0.6",
    the MAJOR.MINOR of the 0.6.0 that 0.3 writes, so one responder no longer
    names two framework releases.
  - VTC: serves trust-task-discovery/0.3 for the first time. It answers
    identified callers only, as the VTA does, and lists the routing table itself
    (DISPATCHED_URIS plus the rooms and git-ns registrations).
  - Registrations: TASK_TRUST_TASK_DISCOVERY_0_3 in vta_sdk::trust_tasks and
    its task list, ReadOnly in retry_safety, the VTA dispatch table and its
    conformance witness (built from the real builder, not a literal), and the
    VTC DISPATCHED_URIS and its declared-URI census.
  - Push engine (VTI-TRN-045): its two staleness predicates now read
    VTI_ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW, the same value the nodes advertise, where before
    they combined two separate constants. It still reads no advertised window.
    A lookup would be a request/reply exchange, and every push is one-way.
    None of the recipients (approvers' devices, wallets, requesters) serves
    discovery. The window only matters when the recipient cannot answer. The
    engine never sees an `expired` refusal, so 0.3's "re-ask after an
    unexpected refusal" would have no trigger. The module docs and
    docs/05-design-notes/retry-and-idempotency.md say so. What remains of the
    spec's divergence F.3 is the producer side only.



### Fixed

- **vta**: Provision mediator ACL during DIDComm enable and update ([#1843](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1843))

title: fix(release): vta-tee 0.7.0 and vta-webvh 0.4.0, not patch bumps
body:
The #1821 release stopped at `vta-tee` (crates.io 403, Invalid authentication token, at the 30-minute mark), leaving `vta-tee`, `vta-webvh`, `vta-service` and the rest unpublished.

Before it is re-run, `scripts/check-release-bump-sizes.py` flags two of the unpublished crates. Each moved its `vta-sdk` / `vti-common` requirement to the new compatibility range, but only as a patch bump. That would let a caret dependent resolve a second copy of `vta-sdk` or `vti-common`, the #1795 failure.

- `vta-tee` 0.6.1 → 0.7.0 (`vta-service` and `vta-enclave` requirements updated)
- `vta-webvh` 0.3.1 → 0.4.0 (`vta-service` requirement updated)

`vta-service` is already 0.46.0, a breaking bump, and `vta-enclave` is `publish = false`, so nothing further cascades.

Both guards pass locally: `check-release-bump-sizes.py` (23 published members) and `check-workspace-version-reqs.py` (32 members). `cargo check` is clean.

Already published by the partial run with the same patch-bump problem: `vti-rooms-dtg` 0.4.4 and `vti-secrets` 0.4.9. These can only be yanked and superseded, which is a maintainer decision.

title: vti-common-v0.30.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc-service**: The administrator's operational verbs are signed Trust Tasks ([#1824](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1824))

The trust-registry reconciler, the audit log, the runtime configuration,
  admin invites and the auth service's sessions are served by the spine
  (trust_tasks::admin_tasks) on every transport, with the signer's ACL row
  as authority: the role and scope questions the bearer extractors asked,
  and an invite's step-up bound to the document.

  auth/sessions/list/0.1 answers { sessions: [Session] } under the
  revocation's authority (caller_covers_target); auth/revoke-session/0.2
  is served on the spine, and a refused revocation by subject is audited
  (SessionRevocationRefused). The console's drift read moves to
  git-ns/view/0.5.

  The bearer routes are removed, except GET /v1/audit/verify, which
  vtc-client still calls.

- **trust-tasks**: Advertise the acceptance window over trust-task-discovery 0.3 (VTI-TRN-047) ([#1817](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1817))

Both VTI node types refuse a document more than ten minutes (plus 60 s of
  skew) past its issuedAt (VTI-OPS-024). A sender holding a document before
  delivery has to know that window to decide when to issue a new attempt
  instead, and until now the only way to know it was to share the constant.
  trust-task-discovery/0.3 (trust-tasks #677, trust-tasks-rs 0.24.4) lets a
  responder state it.

  - Raise the trust-tasks-rs floor to 0.24.4, the first release carrying
    discovery 0.3, and trust-tasks-capability-client with it. Only those two
    lockfile entries move.
  - vti-common: `trust_task::acceptance::AcceptanceWindow` and
    `VTI_ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW` (ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW + DEFAULT_SKEW). This is the one
    value the consumers apply (`freshness_policy()`), the responders advertise
    (`advertised()`, rounded down so it is never wider, VTI-TRN-047), and the
    push engine judges staleness by (`past_max_age`, `refuses`).
    `trust_task::discovery` has the pattern grammar and the 0.1/0.3 response
    builders, so both nodes answer the same way.
  - VTA: serves trust-task-discovery/0.3 next to 0.1, answering each in the
    version it was asked. The window goes at response level, since the VTA
    applies one window to everything it dispatches. The 0.1 frameworkVersion was
    "0.2", a stale copy of the framework crate's default. It is now "0.6",
    the MAJOR.MINOR of the 0.6.0 that 0.3 writes, so one responder no longer
    names two framework releases.
  - VTC: serves trust-task-discovery/0.3 for the first time. It answers
    identified callers only, as the VTA does, and lists the routing table itself
    (DISPATCHED_URIS plus the rooms and git-ns registrations).
  - Registrations: TASK_TRUST_TASK_DISCOVERY_0_3 in vta_sdk::trust_tasks and
    its task list, ReadOnly in retry_safety, the VTA dispatch table and its
    conformance witness (built from the real builder, not a literal), and the
    VTC DISPATCHED_URIS and its declared-URI census.
  - Push engine (VTI-TRN-045): its two staleness predicates now read
    VTI_ACCEPTANCE_WINDOW, the same value the nodes advertise, where before
    they combined two separate constants. It still reads no advertised window.
    A lookup would be a request/reply exchange, and every push is one-way.
    None of the recipients (approvers' devices, wallets, requesters) serves
    discovery. The window only matters when the recipient cannot answer. The
    engine never sees an `expired` refusal, so 0.3's "re-ask after an
    unexpected refusal" would have no trigger. The module docs and
    docs/05-design-notes/retry-and-idempotency.md say so. What remains of the
    spec's divergence F.3 is the producer side only.



### Fixed

- **vti-common**: Step-up gate reads the session's level, not the token's ([#1842](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1842))

A step-up (`auth/passkey/login/finish/0.2`, `purpose: stepUp`) elevates the
  session row and mints no new token; the spec has the caller's existing tokens
  pick the elevation up at introspection. `check_fresh_step_up` nonetheless
  required `claims.acr == "aal2"` from the JWT, so a session that signed in at
  aal1 (SIOPv2, DID-signed authenticate) kept an aal1 token for its whole life
  and could never satisfy any StepUpAuth / `elevation::verified` gate. In the VTC
  console that surfaced as "passkey verification did not complete" on enabling
  console signing, after the passkey ceremony had succeeded.

  The gate now checks the row's `acr` and the live elevation window. The window
  remains the authority: only a step-up writes it.

title: feat(pnm)!: context ids are paths; --parent removed
body:
`pnm contexts provision --id vtc/trust-registry` failed with "context id must contain only lowercase alphanumeric characters and hyphens": only `create` could nest (via `--parent`); `provision` and `bootstrap` took a bare slug.

`create`, `bootstrap` and `provision` (pnm and cnm) now take a context path in `--id`. A shared helper in `vta-cli-common` validates it with `vta_sdk::context_path::validate_context_path` and splits it into the wire request's `parent` + leaf `id`. Wire format and server are unchanged; authorization is unchanged (admin of the parent to nest, super-admin for top-level).

**Breaking:** `--parent X --id Y` becomes `--id X/Y`.

Tested: unit tests for the splitter; clippy `-D warnings` on pnm-cli, cnm-cli, vta-cli-common. Not run against a live VTA; full workspace suite not run.

title: feat(vtc): last member-facing REST routes retire to signed Trust Tasks
body:
## Summary

trust-tasks-rs 0.24.8 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#689) publishes the two specs that closed the last member-facing VTC REST gaps. Both new task versions are served, their REST doors deleted, and callers moved.

## Route → task table

| REST route (deleted) | Trust Task | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `DELETE /v1/relationships/{id}` | `vtc/relationships/revoke/0.2` | `0.2` adds `pop`, a `VrcRevokeAuthorization` bound to the document's own `id` and to the edge (`relationship`) instead of a REST session. Three routes, checked in spec order: issuer (document signer == `rel.issuerDid`), admin, pairwise (via `pop`) — all failures collapse to `notFound`. `0.1` (attributed/admin only) stays served, unretired. |
| `POST /v1/vetting/vetters/{memberDid}/resend` | `vtc/vetting/vetters/resend/0.2` | `0.2` adds `memberDid`, gated on the community-administrator capability (`admin_signer`, including console-key delegation) so an admin can resend another member's grant. `0.1` (self-resend, empty payload) stays served. |
| `GET /v1/credentials/endorsements` | `vtc/endorsements/list/0.1` | Already served on the spine (#1809 era); REST route had no caller left once the console and `cnm` moved onto the signed door. |
| `GET /v1/credentials/endorsements/{id}` | `vtc/endorsements/show/0.1` | Same. |
| `DELETE /v1/credentials/endorsements/{id}` | `vtc/endorsements/revoke/0.1` | Same. |

## What moved

- **vtc-client**: `revoke_relationship` now signs `relationships/revoke/0.2` and takes an optional `pop`.
- **cnm-cli**: `member relationships revoke` gains `--pop-file`, mirroring `publish`'s `--pop-file`.
- **admin-ui**: `resendGrant` and `revokeGrant` (vetting panel), and the members plugin's grant list/revoke, sign documents instead of hitting REST. `openapi.json` and the generated `wire.ts` are regenerated (`UPDATE_OPENAPI=1 cargo test --test openapi_snapshot` + `npm run wire:generate`).
- **Census**: `routes::openapi_tests` (route lists), `trust_tasks::conformance` (two new witnesses: `revoke/0.2` with `pop`, `resend/0.2` with `memberDid`), `tests/trust_task_manifest` (`SPINE_DOCUMENT_TYPES`, admin-UI-task-is-enforced check).
- **Integration tests**: `tests/relationships.rs`'s revoke suite and the pairwise `revocation` module move onto `POST /v1/trust-tasks` directly; `tests/endorsements.rs` moves onto a `signed_task` helper; `tests/vetting_journey.rs` and `tests/join_requests.rs` move onto `common::signed`/`common::legacy` (new `translate()` entries for the three retired routes), following `tests/members_crud.rs`'s established pattern.

## Security note

A PR comment covers the `pop` verification's security properties (binding, replay resistance, anti-probing).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service -p vtc-client -p cnm-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` clean
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib -- openapi_tests conformance error_code_census` green
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --test trust_task_manifest --test openapi_snapshot` green
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --test relationships --test endorsements --test vetting_journey --test join_requests --test vtc_client_live --test members_crud` green (208+ tests across the touched binaries)
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-client -p cnm-cli` green
- [x] admin-ui: `npm run wire:check`, `npx tsc -b --noEmit`, `npx vitest run` (498 tests) all green

body:
feat(vtc): last member-facing REST routes retire to signed Trust Tasks (#1846)

* feat(vtc): last member-facing REST routes retire to signed Trust Tasks

Bumps trust-tasks-rs/trust-tasks-capability-client to 0.24.8
(trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#689), which adds:

- vtc/relationships/revoke/0.2: an optional pop, a VrcRevokeAuthorization
  proof of possession by the relationship's issuerDid, bound to the
  document's own id and to the edge (relationship) rather than to a REST
  session. Reuses the REST handler's DI-proof verification path
  (verify_di_proof); the three authorization routes (issuer, admin,
  pairwise-via-pop) are checked in the order the spec requires, collapsing
  to the same notFound for all three failure modes. The bearer-less REST
  route is deleted; vtc-client's revoke_relationship and cnm's
  `relationships revoke` gain an optional --pop-file.
- vtc/vetting/vetters/resend/0.2: an optional memberDid, gated on the
  community-administrator capability (admin_signer, including console-key
  delegation), for an admin resending another member's grant. The
  admin-only REST route is deleted; the admin console signs 0.2 instead.

vtc/endorsements/{list,show,revoke}/0.1 were already served on the spine;
their REST routes had no caller left once the console and cnm moved onto
the signed door, and are deleted too.

Census tests (openapi_tests, conformance witnesses, trust_task_manifest,
error_code_census), the checked-in admin-ui/openapi.json and its generated
wire.ts are all updated to match. Integration tests move onto the signed
door via tests/common/signed.rs and tests/common/legacy.rs's translate(),
following tests/members_crud.rs's established pattern.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc-service): the dispatch census counts relationships/revoke 0.2 and vetters/resend 0.2

title: feat(pnm): up to ~20× faster commands on a distant VTA (ssh-style ControlMaster)
body:
> **Draft / WIP** — the feature works and is measured, but see *Not done yet* at the bottom.

## Why

Every `pnm` invocation is a fresh process. Each one re-resolves the VTA and mediator DIDs,
opens a TLS connection per host, authenticates to the mediator and upgrades a WebSocket —
and only then sends the command. None of that survives the process, so the next command
pays for all of it again.

On a local stack that is invisible: a round trip costs microseconds, so the setup is free
and every command looks instant. Against a VTA in another region it is the whole story.

Counted off the reverse proxy's access log, one `pnm acl list` over DIDComm is **12–17 HTTPS
requests**: 6 `did.jsonl` fetches, a mediator challenge and authenticate, a WebSocket
upgrade, an inbox drain, the actual outbound/inbound pair, and several cleanup `DELETE`s.
Because each fresh connection also pays TCP and TLS on top of its request, that is **~23
serialised round trips** — for a command whose useful work is one.

## What it costs today, and with this change

`pnm acl list`, three runs per cell, median. Both arms are the same binary and the same
`docker exec` into one long-lived container, so process startup is in neither number; the
~103 ms exec floor is subtracted. Latency injected with a delaying relay in front of the
stack, so these are propagation delay only — no jitter or loss, which makes them floors.

| RTT | one-shot (`--control-master no`) | multiplexed | removed | **ratio** |
|-----:|-----:|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| 0 ms | 64 ms | 41 ms | 23 ms | **1.6×** |
| 50 ms | 1 378 ms | 107 ms | 1 271 ms | **12.9×** |
| 150 ms | 3 646 ms | 215 ms | 3 431 ms | **17.0×** |
| 300 ms | 6 892 ms | 360 ms | 6 532 ms | **19.1×** |

Both sides are linear in RTT, which is the useful form:

```
one-shot     ≈ 22.8 × RTT
multiplexed  ≈  1.06 × RTT
```

The ratio therefore climbs with distance and approaches **~21×** (22.8 / 1.06) as the
fixed local cost stops mattering: 19.1× is what was measured at 300 ms, not a ceiling.

A multiplexed command costs **one application round trip** — the same thing a trust ping
measures. So the rule needs no RTT estimate at all: **the multiplexed number is your trust
ping**, and everything above it is setup the one-shot CLI redoes every time.

| your trust ping | multiplexed | one-shot today |
|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| 50 ms | 50 ms | ~1.2 s |
| 150 ms | 150 ms | ~3.5 s |
| 300 ms | 300 ms | ~7.0 s |

At 300 ms RTT a twenty-command script goes from over two minutes to about seven seconds.

### Starting the master is ~free

The first command has no master to talk to, so it starts one and then delegates. That costs
about what running the command directly would have, because the master does the setup the
command needed anyway:

| RTT | first command (starts master) | one-shot |
|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| 0 ms | 168 ms | 64 ms |
| 50 ms | 1 432 ms | 1 378 ms |
| 150 ms | 3 638 ms | 3 646 ms |
| 300 ms | 7 044 ms | 6 892 ms |

Which is why the default can be `auto`: nobody has to think about it, and nobody pays to
find out.

## What this adds

```
--control-master no|auto|yes|ask    (default: auto)
--control-persist no|yes|10m|600    (default: 10m)
--control-path <PATH>               (default: per-VTA socket in a private dir)

pnm sidecar serve | status | stop   (ssh -M / -O check / -O exit)
```

Names and semantics follow `ssh_config(5)` so the behaviour transfers. Rarely typed:
`auto` starts a master on demand, the way nobody types `ssh -M`.

The client hands the master its own stdin/stdout/stderr over `SCM_RIGHTS`, so a delegated
command's output is indistinguishable from a direct one — same terminal, same `isatty`,
same colours, same redirection.

## Why it is safe to default on

A master that is missing, stale, wrong-version or unusable is **never an error**. Every
such path falls back to the ordinary one-shot command, so the worst case is exactly
today's behaviour. Verified by killing a master with `SIGKILL` and running the next
command: the stale socket is detected, unlinked, replaced, and the command succeeds.

## Security

The master holds the only copy of the operator's admin private key in memory and will run
any command handed to it, so the socket is the privilege boundary:

- control directory forced to `0700` and ownership-checked; socket `0600`
- a symlinked or foreign-owned control path is refused, which closes the path-swap race
- **peer uid verified on every connection** (`SO_PEERCRED` / `getpeereid`) rather than
  trusting file permissions alone, with no exemption for root
- protocol version checked, so a master left running across an upgrade is refused rather
  than guessed at
- `--control-persist 10m` bounds how long the key stays resident — a security control, not
  just resource hygiene
- `ask` confirms before a master is used or created

## Two details taken from the OpenSSH implementation, not its documentation

1. **The socket is claimed atomically.** Binding a temp path and `link()`ing it into place
   means a second master loses with `EEXIST`. The obvious `unlink()`-then-`bind()` would
   remove a live master's socket, leaving that master running but unreachable while every
   later client silently started another. There is a regression test for this.
2. **Stale sockets are removed by the client, on `ECONNREFUSED` only**, and not at all when
   multiplexing is disabled.

Deliberate divergences from ssh are documented in `control/client.rs`: we spawn a child
rather than forking a thread-bearing tokio process; we confirm on the client's terminal so
`ask` works headless (ssh's askpass silently denies with no `DISPLAY`); we vet the control
path, which ssh does not; we do not exempt root from the peer check; and `yes` means "never
silently fall back" rather than ssh's "be the master".

No OpenSSH code is used — the design is reimplemented in Rust.

## Testing

`cargo test -p pnm-cli` — 104 pass, including the socket race, socket mode, path
sanitisation, symlink refusal and the `ControlPersist` time vocabulary. `clippy` and `fmt`
clean.

Against a live stack: idle timeout evicts the master, `sidecar stop` exits it, a
`SIGKILL`ed master is recovered from, `--control-master no` still runs direct, and the
control socket is `0600` inside a `0700` directory on both macOS and Linux.

## Not done yet

- [ ] `-O stop` (stop-listening) as distinct from `-O exit` — matters less here, where a
      session is one short command rather than a shell
- [ ] config-file keys to match the flags, so a default can be set per VTA
- [ ] review of whether `auto` should be the shipped default or opt-in for a release or two
- [ ] the `ask` prompt is per master, not per command — worth deciding which is wanted

## Summary
- `cnm consent approve`/`deny` authenticated to the VTC with a bearer-token REST session (`vtc::connect`), the one hard-coded-transport holdout among cnm's Trust Task verbs.
