title: fix(vgi-bridge): the container image builds again, and CI builds it
body:
## Why

While verifying #103's `HEALTHCHECK`, I found the bridge's container image **doesn't build on `main`**. It also didn't build before #103.

```
error: failed to run custom build command for `libdbus-sys v0.2.7`
  Package dbus-1 was not found in the pkg-config search path.
```

On Linux, vgi-bridge links libdbus through the TDK's keyring store: `affinidi-tdk` → `affinidi-tdk-common` → `dbus-secret-service-keyring-store` → `dbus` → `libdbus-sys`. The `rust:1.95-bookworm` build stage has no `libdbus-1-dev`. CI installs that package for its clippy and test jobs but **never builds the image**, so the breakage went unnoticed.

## What

- **Dockerfile, build stage:** installs `libdbus-1-dev` and `pkg-config` before the build, in their own layer so the dependency layer caches.
- **Dockerfile, runtime stage:** adds `libdbus-1-3` alongside `ca-certificates git`. The binary links it dynamically.
- **New workflow `.github/workflows/bridge-image.yml`:** builds the image when `crates/vgi-bridge/Dockerfile`, `Cargo.lock`, any `Cargo.toml` or the workflow itself changes. Those are the inputs that can break the image, and limiting to them keeps the release build off other PRs. Then it smoke-tests the `HEALTHCHECK` added in #103:
  1. the image declares a `HEALTHCHECK` running `vgi-bridge healthcheck`
  2. `healthcheck` **fails** with nothing listening
  3. `healthcheck` **passes** against a `/healthz` served by a busybox sidecar in the same network namespace (`busybox:1.37`, pinned by digest)

## Verified locally

I built the image with Docker 29.5.3 on aarch64 and ran all three smoke steps:
- `Healthcheck`: `{"Test":["CMD","/usr/local/bin/vgi-bridge","healthcheck"],"Interval":30s,"Timeout":10s,"StartPeriod":30s,"Retries":3}`, running as `vgi`
- with nothing listening: `Error: connecting to the bridge at 127.0.0.1:8080 … Connection refused`, exit 1
- against the sidecar: exit 0

No Rust code changes.

title: chore: scan dependencies for advisories in CI, and bound did-git-sign's input
body:
## Why

Follow-ups from SEC-4045, after the VGI findings (#102–#106).

- **No advisory scanning.** The debt adjudication found **no Snyk rows at all** for this repository, because Snyk doesn't cover the Rust workspace. The only `cargo audit` run was a one-off in the review's PoC bundle. A new RustSec advisory against the dependency graph would go unnoticed.
- **Two Low debt items carried as real:**
  - did-git-sign reads its signing input with no size limit.
  - did-git-sign's VTA connect retry has no pause between attempts.

## What

- **CI `audit` job:** `cargo install cargo-audit --locked --version 0.22.2`, then `cargo audit --deny warnings`. It uses the repo's pinned checkout and cache actions.
- **`.cargo/audit.toml`:** ignores one advisory, **RUSTSEC-2023-0071** (`rsa` 0.9, Marvin timing side-channel), with the reasoning recorded next to it:
  - The attack recovers an RSA **private** key from decryption or signing, and no fixed release exists.
  - `rsa` arrives only through `pgp` and `ssh-key` in verify-trust, which use it to **verify** with public keys, for example GitHub's RSA web-flow key.
  - No crate here holds an RSA private key or decrypts. did-git-sign and the bridge sign with Ed25519, and RSA secret-key use appears only in tests.
  - The entry says to re-evaluate if that changes.
- **did-git-sign:** reads at most **16 MiB** to sign, from the file or from stdin, and refuses anything larger before holding it in memory. git's commit, tag and push-cert objects are kilobytes, because they name their trees rather than contain them.
- **did-git-sign:** the VTA connect retry waits `500 ms × attempt` before retrying. There are still at most 2 attempts.

## Tests

- `input_up_to_the_bound_is_read_and_past_it_refused`: exactly the limit is accepted, one byte over is refused, and an endless reader stops at the limit.
- `cargo audit --deny warnings` exits 0 with the config and 1 without it. Current `main` has no advisory other than RUSTSEC-2023-0071.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` all pass. Rebased on `187dc31` (#106).

## Compatibility

did-git-sign refuses to sign more than 16 MiB, which git never asks for. The audit job adds about 2 minutes to CI while it builds `cargo-audit`, cached after that.

title: fix(vgi-bridge): verify platform-signed merges from the fetch, not the bridge's working directory
body:
## Why

SEC-4045 / VLM-4232 round 3.

**VGI-01 (Medium by the rubric, top product priority).** The bridge-posted check called verify-trust with `repo_dir: PathBuf::new()` and `range: String::new()`. So the platform-merge policy's git calls, `rev-list --boundary` and `merge-tree`, ran as `git -C ""`, which means in the **bridge's own working directory**.

Every path failed closed. But with `platform_keyring_file` set, which is the recommended configuration:
- Every PR containing an "Update branch" merge **errored the whole check**, reported as "could not complete the check".
- Each such check also dropped the cached registry route.

That puts pressure on operators to turn off the keyring or the check.

Pointing the calls at the fetch directory isn't enough on its own. The fetch holds commit objects only (`tree:0`), is depth-limited, and runs with lazy fetching off. So the base-tip parent is missing, and so are the trees, the blobs and the history to the merge base.

**VGI-05 (Low).** `merge-tree` exits 1 both for a genuine conflict and for a parent it doesn't have, whether an unknown id or one beyond a shallow cut. Both cases were reported as "conflicts resolved by hand".

## What

**verify-trust:**
- New `verify_prepared_with_facts(…, &MergeFacts)`. The policy takes the **boundary** (`BTreeSet`) and each merge's **recomputation** (`MergeOutcome::{Clean{tree}, Conflict, Unavailable(why)}`) from the caller, instead of running git. A platform merge with no supplied outcome fails closed as `platformMergeAltered: … not recomputed`. `verify_prepared_with` is unchanged and still uses git (the CLI path).
- New `merge_tree_args(ours, theirs, merge_base)` and `merge_outcome(code, stdout, stderr)`, so the bridge recomputes merges with exactly the CLI's rules: the empty-tree `--attr-source` and `core.attributesFile=/dev/null`.
- `commit_parents` is now public.
- VGI-05: exit 1 with "not something we can merge" becomes `Unavailable` ("a parent is not in the repository"), not a conflict. The CLI also checks that both parents exist (`cat-file -e`) before running `merge-tree`.

**vgi-bridge:**
- **Boundary:** the parents of listed commits that aren't themselves in the list (`boundary_of`). The list is GitHub's complete `base...head` compare, which is already refused when truncated. A parent outside it is reachable from the merge base, so it's on the protected branch. This is the same listing the bridge already trusts to decide which commits to verify.
- **Recompute** (`merge_facts`, `GitFetcher::recompute_merge`): only when a keyring is configured for the host, and only for PGP-signed two-parent merges, **at most 8 per check**. For each one:
  - ask GitHub for the parents' merge base with a new `GitHubForge::merge_base`, a one-commit compare call
  - fetch `ours`, `theirs` and the base by id with `--filter=blob:none --depth=1`
  - run `merge-tree --merge-base=…` with lazy fetching enabled for that call only, so it fetches just the blobs both sides changed

  All of this runs under the check's token, byte bound and timeout. Anything that fails becomes `Unavailable` and fails closed.
- `CommitVerifier` gains `verify_with_facts` and `exempts_platform_merges`, both defaulted so test doubles are unchanged. `VerifyTrustVerifier::verify` now passes empty facts, so **the bridge never runs git in its working directory again**.
- `GitFetcher::run`: the existing `git()` runner now returns the raw exit status and can allow lazy fetches. `git()` wraps it with identical behaviour.

**Docs:** BRIDGE.md (the keyring step) explains platform merges, the cap, and the criss-cross caveat. The `checks` module docs describe step 3.

## Compatibility

- "Update branch" and other clean platform merges now **pass** the bridge-posted check. They used to error the whole check. Hand-resolved or altered merges still fail.
- **Criss-cross merges** (more than one merge base) are recomputed over one base and can fail where GitHub's recursive merge didn't. That fails closed, and it's documented.
- The bridge makes extra GitHub calls and fetches only for PRs that contain platform-signed merges, capped at 8.
- verify-trust's API is additive only. CLI behaviour changes only in VGI-05's clearer error message.

## Tests

- **vgi-bridge `an_update_branch_merge_is_recomputed_from_the_fetch`** reproduces the review's case end to end. It uses the real `GitFetcher` (a `file://` remote serving partial clones), the real `VerifyTrustVerifier`, a generated web-flow PGP key as the configured keyring, and a stub registry.
  - A DID-signed feature commit, plus a platform-signed "Update branch" merge whose base-tip parent is outside the range. Both sides edit `f.txt`, so the recompute has to read blobs.
  - Without facts: no error, and the merge fails closed. Before this PR, this case errored the check.
  - With facts: the boundary contains the base tip, the clean merge comes out **`exempt`**, and the hand-altered merge comes out **`platformMergeAltered`**.
  - Checked that lazy blob fetching is exercised: disabling it for the recompute makes the clean case fail with "could not fetch … from promisor remote".
- vgi-bridge unit tests cover `boundary_of`, candidate selection (PGP-signed two-parent merges only), and the cap and missing-merge-base cases failing closed.
- vgi-forge-github: `a_merge_base_is_read_from_one_small_comparison` (`per_page=1`, and a non-SHA merge base is refused).
- verify-trust e2e:
  - supplied facts exempt a clean merge *with `repo_dir` pointing at a nonexistent path*, which proves git isn't consulted
  - the facts path refuses altered, conflicted, unavailable and missing recomputations
  - a parent that isn't on the supplied boundary is refused
  - `merge_tree_args` with a pinned base agrees with the policy
  - VGI-05: an unknown parent (git exits 1) is `Unavailable`, not a conflict
  - the existing platform-merge tests are unchanged and pass
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` all pass. Rebased on `cf39a18` (#104).

title: feat(vtc): member verbs served as signed Trust Tasks — callers wired, REST retired
body:
## Summary
Batch-1 member-facing VTC verbs — credential renew, DID rotate (both verbs), personhood revoke, relationships list/revoke/publish, issuer endorsements — were already dispatched on the signed-document spine (`trust_tasks::member_tasks`, #1809), matching each spec's Authorization section exactly. This PR wires their callers onto that door and retires the now-redundant bearer-session REST routes.

- `vtc-client`: adds `renew`, `rotate_challenge`/`rotate`, `revoke_personhood`, `list_relationships`/`publish_relationship`/`revoke_relationship`, `issue_endorsement` — every call rides the signed `POST /trust-tasks` door.
- `cnm-cli`: new `cnm member` subcommand over those methods (renew, rotate challenge/finish, revoke-personhood, relationships list/publish/revoke, endorse).
- `admin-ui`: the member-relationships read (member detail view) converted from the bearer REST route to the signed door (`postSignedRead`).
- `vtc-service`: bearer-only REST routes with no remaining caller removed — renew, rotate-challenge, rotate, personhood/revoke, relationships/list, endorsements/issue. `relationships/revoke` **keeps** its bearer route: it authorizes a pairwise-relationship-DID capacity (`VrcRevokeAuthorization`) the signed document can't express yet, so removing it would strand a member's own edge with no self-service revoke.
- Regenerated `admin-ui/openapi.json` + `wire.ts`; updated the route census, conformance and `trust_task_manifest` tests for the retired paths.

No spec had to be invented or extended — every wire shape came from the published `vtc/members/*`, `vtc/relationships/*` and `vtc/endorsements/issue` specs already vendored in `trust-tasks-rs`.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p cnm-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt`

title: fix(verify-trust): a deactivated did:webvh signer no longer verifies
body:
## Why

SEC-4045 / VGI-04 (Medium, the highest-priority finding after calibration). A cleanly deactivated `did:webvh` signer, which is the method the VTA issues, kept verifying commits **indefinitely**. `didwebvh-rs` resolves a deactivated log `Ok` with its last document and flags the deactivation only in metadata, and cache-sdk threw that metadata away. `did:web` was never affected, because its deactivation is a 404.

The fix is upstream: affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#907, released as `affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk` 0.8.39 and `did-scid` 0.2.8.

## What

- Raised the workspace floor to `affinidi-did-resolver-cache-sdk = "0.8.39"`, with the reason recorded next to the existing SSRF-floor note. It's a normal dependency, so the floor travels with the published crates, did-git-sign included. `Cargo.lock` now has cache-sdk 0.8.39 and did-scid 0.2.8.
- Updated both `unresolvedSigner` rows in RUNBOOK: a deactivated DID is now one of the causes.

There are no source changes. A deactivated signer now fails resolution, lands in `signers.unresolved`, and its commits report `unresolvedSigner`.

## Tests

The new e2e test `a_deactivated_webvh_signer_is_unresolved` builds two real signed did:webvh logs, one live and one ending in a deactivation. It serves both over loopback and resolves them through the real `resolve_signer_keys`. The resolver it uses allows loopback; the public-hosts-only policy of `build_resolver` is still pinned by the internal-host test.

- The live DID resolves to its `assertionMethod` key. This is the control that shows the harness works.
- The deactivated DID has no keys and is unresolved, with a reason naming the deactivation.
- **On cache-sdk 0.8.38 the test fails.** The deactivated DID comes back with its last keys. I checked this by downgrading temporarily.

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` all pass.

## Compatibility

Commits signed by a deactivated did:webvh now fail the check, which is the intent. The bridge-posted check goes through the same `resolve_signer_keys`, so it is covered too.

title: fix: harden the VTA URL check, legacy resources, the bridge listener and image
body:
## Why

These are the hardening findings from SEC-4045 / VLM-4232 round 3, verified on `2abba4b`. The review calibrated all of them to Low, apart from VGI-03 at Medium.

## What

### VGI-07: VTA URL userinfo bypass (did-git-sign)
The hand-written loopback check split the host on `:` and so read `http://localhost:80@evil.com` as `localhost`. The part before `@` is userinfo, so the challenge-response went **in cleartext to `evil.com`**. `cmd_init` also applied no check to `--vta-url`. The URL the SDK resolves is already guarded, so only an operator-supplied `--vta-url` or an edited keyring was exposed.

- `vta_url_is_secure` now parses the URL and uses the SDK's own `vta_sdk::protocol::matching::is_https_or_loopback`. It also refuses userinfo outright, as `guard_vta_endpoint` does.
- When the error message echoes the URL, it cuts out any userinfo, so a password never reaches a terminal or log.
- `init` applies the check to the URL, whether overridden or resolved, before anything is sent.
- I deliberately did **not** use `guard_vta_endpoint` itself. It also refuses private-network hosts (RFC 1918, `*.internal`) without `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS`, and that would break developers whose VTA is on an internal address.

### VGI-03 (soft): legacy resources took any string (verify-trust)
In `legacy` mode, `--resource` and `--fallback-resource` went to the registry verbatim, including empty, whitespace-padded or control-character values. They failed closed, but as `unauthorized`, which points the operator at the registry instead of the typo. Now:

- Both values must be `owner` or `owner/repo`: ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, with case kept, and no empty or dot segments. This includes the `$GITHUB_REPOSITORY` default.
- A legacy fallback must be the resource's own owner (compared case-insensitively) or the resource itself. This is the legacy counterpart of qualified mode's containment rule.
- `legacy` stays the default. Flipping it to `qualified` remains a separate, announced release.

### VGI-06: bridge `listen` defaults to `0.0.0.0:8080`
- The default is unchanged, because it is correct inside the container.
- The bridge now logs a startup **warning** whenever `listen` is not loopback. `BridgeConfig::listen_warning` is a pure function and is tested.
- BRIDGE.md §1 and `bridge.example.toml` now say only the proxy may reach the port: publish it to the proxy's network, or use `127.0.0.1` when the proxy runs on the same host.

### Dockerfile (debt #18/#19)
- Pinned both base images by digest, using the multi-arch index digests of `rust:1.95-bookworm` and `debian:bookworm-slim` as of today. Before this, `ci.yml` required a digest on the Forgejo test image but not on the bridge's own image.
- Added a Dependabot `docker` entry for `/crates/vgi-bridge`, and a `dockerfile-pins` CI job that fails on any unpinned `FROM` in the repo.
- Added a `HEALTHCHECK` that runs a new **`vgi-bridge healthcheck`** subcommand. It sends a std-only `GET /healthz` to the configured `listen` address, probing loopback when that address is unspecified, and exits 0 only on a 200. The image has no curl, and adding one just for this would enlarge the runtime image.

## ⚠️ Compatibility

- **did-git-sign:** a stored or overridden VTA URL with a `user:pass@` part is now refused, even over https. `127.0.0.0/8` (not only `127.0.0.1`) and `localhost.` now count as loopback, following the SDK's rule.
- **verify-trust, legacy mode:** these are now errors, where they used to fail as `unauthorized`:
  - malformed resources
  - a fallback naming **another owner**, or anything other than the repo's own owner or the repo itself

  Workflows that pass `fallback-resource: <their own org>` are unaffected. The action-selftest injection check pins v0.4.12, so it is unaffected too.
- **Bridge:** there's a new warning log line on non-loopback `listen`, plus the new subcommand and `HEALTHCHECK`. No config changes.

## Tests

- did-git-sign:
  - `userinfo_cannot_disguise_a_remote_host_as_loopback` uses the review's `localhost:80@evil.com`, plus IPv4 and IPv6 variants
  - `userinfo_is_refused_even_over_https_and_never_echoed`
  - the loopback range and trailing-dot forms still pass, and non-http schemes and non-URLs are refused
  - the existing lookalike-host tests still pass
- verify-trust:
  - `legacy_mode_refuses_a_malformed_resource`, with 10 malformed shapes, checks that legacy values which were always accepted still pass, untouched
  - `legacy_mode_refuses_a_fallback_naming_another_owner`
  - one existing assertion changed. It paired a `john.doe` fallback with the `Acme/Widgets` repo, which is now refused as another owner, so it now uses `john.doe/widgets`
- vgi-bridge:
  - `a_listener_beyond_loopback_is_warned_about`
  - `healthcheck`: passes on 200 only, probes an unspecified listener on loopback, and fails when nothing listens
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` all pass.
- **Not run locally:** a `docker build` of the image, because no Docker daemon was running. CI or a reviewer should build it once to check the `HEALTHCHECK`.

title: feat(vtc-service)!: git-ns admin reads are signed Trust Tasks
body:
## Summary

The six git-ns admin-console reads that only ever had bearer REST are now signed Trust Tasks, served on the document dispatcher (`vtc-service/src/git_ns/admin_reads.rs`) over every transport, matching the pattern #1835/#1840 set for the rest of the admin surface. Specs merged in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#686, released in trust-tasks-rs 0.24.7 (bumped from 0.24.6).

| Route removed | Trust Task |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/git-ns/rights` | `git-ns/right/list/0.1` |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/rights/issued-by-departed` | `git-ns/right/issued-by-departed/0.1` |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/jobs` | `git-ns/bridge/job/list/0.1` |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/projection` | `git-ns/projection/show/0.1` |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/accounts` | `git-ns/account/list/0.1` |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/activity` | `git-ns/activity/list/0.1` |

Authority: the community-administrator capability alone for `right/list`, `right/issued-by-departed`, `projection/show` and `account/list` (each spans every namespace); the community-administrator capability or a namespace's own `git.ns.admin` for `bridge/job/list` and `activity/list` — the same split `namespace/list`/`repo/list` already use. Each of the six pages: `limit` clamped to 1..=500 (default 100), an opaque `cursor` bound to the request's own filters so a mid-page filter change is refused `malformedRequest`.

`routes/src/routes/git_ns.rs` (the whole REST surface) is deleted; its response types and tests moved into `git_ns::admin_reads` / `git_ns::tasks` and `git_ns/tests.rs`. `admin-ui/src/plugins/repos/api.ts` now signs all six with the console key (`postSignedRead`); `admin-ui/openapi.json` and `wire.ts` regenerated.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

- No `cnm` subcommands for the six new tasks yet (table in `docs/03-vtc/git-namespaces.md` marks them `—`).
- The admin console still fetches one page (default 100/500) of each listing — no "load more" UI for `nextCursor` yet.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt` — clean
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib -- openapi_tests conformance` — 11 passed

title: fix(verify-trust): sign only with assertionMethod keys, and drop every gpgsig header like git
body:
## Why

Two findings from SEC-4045 / VLM-4232 round 3 (Farhad's adversarial review, verified on `2abba4b`). Both affect the commit→DID binding.

**VGI-02 (Medium).** `ed25519_keys_from_doc` returned *every* Ed25519 key in `verificationMethod`, with no check of relationship or controller. As a result, a key agreement, recovery or custodian key that the controller never authorized for signing could author commits that verify as the DID. The bridge already does this correctly (`relation("assertionMethod")` in `vgi-bridge/src/vta.rs`), but verify-trust did not.

**VGI-08 (Low).** `split_signed_commit` removed only the exact `gpgsig ` header. git also removes every other `gpgsig`-prefixed header together with its continuation lines, in the "other signature" arm of `parse_buffer_signed_by_header`. That made our payload a strict superset of git's. Anyone could add `gpgsig-sha256 ` to a validly signed commit: the object stays fsck-clean and git and GitHub still show it as GOOD, but verify-trust reported **`badSignature` by the real signer**. The effect is a false reject and a nuisance vector, not a false accept.

## What

- `vgi_core::ed25519_signing_keys_from_doc` replaces `ed25519_keys_from_doc`. It returns only the Ed25519 keys the document's `assertionMethod` lists:
  - absolute (`did:…#key-0`) or relative (`#key-0`) references to the document's own methods, or embedded methods
  - only methods whose `controller`, when present, is the DID
  - references to methods the document doesn't contain are not followed

  It's used by verify-trust (`resolve_signer_keys`), by did-git-sign's DID-log key check, and by the bridge test.
- `split_signed_commit` now follows git's state machine: `gpgsig ` is the signature, any other `gpgsig*` header and its continuations are dropped, and everything else is kept.
- The `unresolvedSigner`/`unknownKey` rows in RUNBOOK and the message text now say "under `assertionMethod`".

## ⚠️ Compatibility

- **Signers:** a DID whose signing key is *not* listed under `assertionMethod` now fails, as `unresolvedSigner` if no Ed25519 key is listed there, otherwise `unknownKey`. **VTA-issued DIDs are unaffected.** Every VTA/VTC/vta-tee DID template lists `#key-0` under `assertionMethod`, and `#key-0` is what did-git-sign signs with. Only hand-made documents that list the key solely under `authentication` would be affected.
- **vgi-core API:** `ed25519_keys_from_doc` has been renamed, and its behaviour narrowed, as `ed25519_signing_keys_from_doc`. There's no deprecated alias on purpose, because the old behaviour is the bug. This matters for the next release's version number.

## Tests

- `vgi-core::did` has cases for:
  - keys that aren't under `assertionMethod` (the VGI-02 case)
  - no `assertionMethod` at all
  - a foreign controller
  - relative and embedded entries
  - a missing reference
- `verify-trust` lib test `only_assertion_method_keys_survive_the_typed_document`: a VTA-shaped document (Ed25519 `#key-0` under assertionMethod, X25519 `#key-1`, and an Ed25519 key used only for authentication) goes through the typed `Document` and is re-serialized the way `resolve_signer_keys` does it. Only `#key-0` comes out.
- `vgi-core::commit` checks `gpgsig-sha256` (with and without a body), `gpgsigx`, `gpgsig-foo` and a bare `gpgsig`, placed before and after the signature. It also checks that headers merely *containing* `gpgsig` are kept, and that a commit signed only under another header counts as unsigned.
- e2e `another_signature_header_does_not_break_a_good_signature` uses real git, with write-time fsck on, to inject the header into a real signed commit. **Without the fix it reports `BadSignature { signer_did: … }`; with the fix, `Trusted`.**
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo test -p did-git-sign --features insecure-policy-bypass` all pass.

## Not in this PR

- **VGI-04 consumer side:** a cleanly deactivated did:webvh signer keeps verifying. The fix is upstream in affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#907 (cache-sdk 0.8.39). A follow-up PR will bump to it here and add a verify-trust regression test.
- **SHA-256 object-format repos** (`gpgsig-sha256` as *the* signature) are still unsupported, as before.

| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.3.14` → `0.3.15` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: chore(vetting-pcs): depend on published predicate-credential-system
body:
## Summary

`predicate-credential-system` is now published on crates.io (v0.1.0, from [OpenVTC/predicate-credential-system](https://github.com/OpenVTC/predicate-credential-system)). This switches `vti-vetting-pcs` and `vtc-service`'s optional `vetting-pcs` feature from the vendored path dependency to a normal version dependency, and removes:

- `vendor/predicate-credential-system/` (the vendored copy)
- `vendor/0001-pcs-application-contexts.patch`
- `vendor/PROVENANCE.md`

Also drops the now-stale "vendored, temporarily" comments in `Cargo.toml`, `vti-vetting-pcs/Cargo.toml`, `vti-vetting-pcs/src/lib.rs`, `vtc-service/Cargo.toml`, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Synced with `main`

This branch was 137 commits behind `main`, including a large architectural migration (#1834/#1835, "the community's REST-only admin surfaces are signed Trust Tasks") that moved a whole class of admin REST routes — schemas, relationships suspend/restore, rooms, community branding/join-discovery, join-requests query/vetting, and later the policy log and DID log — onto the Trust-Task spine. It's merged in through `863dba15`, in two rounds (`main` kept moving while this was in progress).

Several of the conflicts were **not** real 3-way conflicts — git's auto-merge silently kept this branch's pre-migration content wherever this branch's own commits happened not to touch the exact same lines, with no conflict marker at all. Caught and fixed by diffing every touched file directly against `main` after resolving markers, rather than trusting a clean `git merge` result:

- `vtc-service/src/routes/mod.rs`, `vtc-service/src/routes/schemas.rs` — silently kept retired REST routes; a whole new module (`vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/surface_tasks.rs`) was missing from the tree entirely.
- `vtc-service/src/schemas/accepts.rs` — a visibility widening the new module needs was dropped.
- `vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs`, `trust_tasks/conformance.rs`, `trust_tasks/error_code_census.rs` — census/witness tables silently kept old baseline counts and omitted `main`'s new entries for the migrated verbs (this recurred on the second sync round too — same pattern, smaller scope).
- `vtc-service/tests/openapi_response_census.rs`, `tests/trust_task_manifest.rs` — stale exception-list entries these tests' own guard-rails caught once actually run.
- 24 further files this branch never touched at all were taken wholesale from `main`.
- `vtc-service/admin-ui/openapi.json` / `src/lib/wire.ts` regenerated from source (`UPDATE_OPENAPI=1 cargo test`, `npm run wire:generate`) rather than hand-merged, verified to match exactly what the build serves.

**`main` is moving fast enough that a perfect sync isn't practical** — it gained 3 more commits during the final test run alone (`afcf2470`, `1f5ff9bf`, `05692732`). This branch is current as of `863dba15`; a final short sync immediately before merge is worth doing if `main` has moved further by then, but chasing it commit-by-commit in this PR isn't a good use of anyone's time.

**CI has not run on this PR at all**, on any commit — a `CLOWarden` check suite is stuck `queued` and no GitHub Actions check-suite exists for this branch, unlike every other open PR in this repo. That looks like an org/repo-level permissions gate unrelated to this change; worth a maintainer's attention separately. Verification here is from local testing only (see below).

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build -p vti-vetting-pcs --all-features`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --features vetting-pcs` — full suite, **4 clean runs across both sync rounds** (1617 lib tests + ~85 integration test-result blocks each time, 0 failed; 3 real bugs found and fixed along the way, all from the silent-staleness pattern above)
- [x] `cargo test` (admin-ui, vitest) — 498/498 passing
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --test openapi_snapshot` — checked-in `openapi.json` matches the build exactly

title: chore(vetting-pcs): depend on published predicate-credential-system (#1838)
body:
chore(vetting-pcs): depend on published predicate-credential-system (#1838)

* feat(vetting)!: hidden-vetter admission (ZKP) verification in the VTC

Development branch. The applicant proves that k distinct vetters of this
community vetted them; the VTC verifies that proof and counts it, and
learns nothing about which vetters they were.

- vti-vetting-pcs (publish = false): the verifier, the application
  contexts, the attestation tokens and the wire format, mirrored from
  openvtc-vetting-pcs on the openvtc zkp-pcs branch. Its cross-repo
  fixture test reads a submission that branch produced and accepts it,
  so the two copies cannot drift apart unnoticed.
- vtc-service gains the off-by-default feature vetting-pcs and one
  branch in vetting_facts, which both the submit and the supplement path
  call, so a supplement cannot decide differently from a submit. The
  facts it returns are the same shape the named path returns, with each
  vetter's tag where their DID would be, so evaluate() and join.rego are
  untouched.
- A new backed-up keyspace holds spent tokens. Verification is sync and
  the store is not, so a submission reads the rows it touches, decides,
  then commits with insert_raw_if_absent; a serial another request took
  in between fails the commit and the submission is refused rather than
  counted on a token somebody else spent.
- AcceptsCriterion carries the published parameters as raw JSON. They do
  not reach the 0.2 manifest: Criterion is generated and denies unknown
  members, and VettingRequirements drops what it does not name, so a
  client needs them out of band until the spec carries them.

AcceptsCriterion and AppState each gain a field, hence the !. Both are
vtc-service types and vtc-service is publish = false, so no published
crate's API moves.

vendor/: predicate-credential-system at aa57efd plus the patch that adds
application contexts to it. Vendored because the crate is not on
crates.io and the branch carrying the patch is not pushed; see
vendor/PROVENANCE.md for what ends that. cargo-deny passes unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* chore(vetting-pcs): sync the mirrored files from the openvtc branch

CommunityParams arrives with them: the published half of a deployment,
which is what a member holds and what the fixture test constructs. The
four cross-repo tests still pass, which is the point of mirroring them.

HeldToken and the multibase helpers moved into token and scheme on the
openvtc side so these files need nothing from the member-side snapshot
module that does not exist here.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): the VTC issues the hidden-vetting challenge, and mints the credentials behind it

Two halves the community did not have. Both were the same gap: a rule the
client kept, with nothing on the community's side that enforced it.

**The challenge.** A hidden proof is bound to one, and the binding meant
nothing while the client minted it — the proof verifies as often as it is
submitted, so the second submission of the same bytes counted. `pcs_challenge`
mints one per applicant, keeps it for 15 minutes, and `decide` spends it as its
first step, before it reads a single spent-token row. A supplement needs a
fresh challenge, deliberately: one that survives its first use is not a
freshness anchor. The rows share the join keyspace under their own prefix and
are swept by the same retention pass.

**The minting.** `pcs_issue` enrols vetters and serves the drip against the
store, so the rules survive a restart: one credential per member per class
label, the PCS identifier bound at the first one and required again at every
rotation, one batch per member per label per tick. The grant check is the
community's own `vetter_eligible` — membership row, live role endorsement —
not a list this module keeps.

The keys are derived, not stored: HKDF from the credential signer's master
secret, then ChaCha20 over a seed that includes the community DID. Nothing new
to provision or back up, and one consequence worth stating: the master secret
IS the vetter class, so `issuer()` refuses to mint when the derived key is not
the published one, rather than handing out credentials no submission can
verify. `publish()` is where a deployment's published parameters come from.

The drip cap closed a real hole. `TokenIssuer::issue` checked the label, the
tick and every opening proof, and never how many requests were in the batch —
a vetter could ask for a thousand tokens in one tick and be served. It is now
a parameter of the issuer, refused before anything is signed, published as
`dripPerTick`.

Tests: enrolment and the drip end to end against the store (who may enrol,
once per label, one identifier across a rotation, the cap, the tick, tokens
that unblind); the stop when the derived keys are not the published ones; and
`decide` against the cross-repo fixture — no challenge refused, recorded
challenge counted, replay refused.

* test(vtc): the keyspace census counts vetting_pcs_issue

The census pins ALL at the number of keyspaces AppState holds, so a new
keyspace has to move it. 3e372a86 added vetting_pcs_issue to ALL, BACKED_UP,
AppState and the backup dispatch, and missed the pin.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.gore@gmail.com>

* security(vtc): keep the mask, not the tag, and not the decided proof

A tag is usk·H0(id). One discrete log recovers the vetter's key, and the
community's own enrolment table puts a name to every tag that vetter ever
made — so the material worth not keeping is the tag, and the exposure starts
the day it is written rather than the day the computer exists. The proofs are
the safe part: they are simulatable, and blind issuance hides the identifier
unconditionally.

Two changes, both about keeping less.

Tags are masked before they are stored. HKDF(key, salt = applicant DID,
info = tag) under a key derived from the same master secret everything else
derives from, applied where the group element used to land: the facts row's
issuer column and the spent-token ledger's (id, tag) pair. Equality is all
either needed — distinctness inside a submission, same-applicant-same-vetter
across a resubmission — and equality survives the mask.

A decided proof is not kept. The stored join request keeps
{redacted, suite, bytes, sha256} in place of the hiddenVetting member, on the
submit and supplement paths both. It runs whether or not this build implements
the suite, which is why the member name is spelled in vetting/mod.rs and
pinned against the crate's constant by a test.

The mask is not a cure and the doc says so: a community holding both the key
and the applicant DID can recompute it. What removes the exposure is
retention, which is now design §18 — including the stronger per-submission
ordinal a community can choose instead, and the enrolment table as the other
half of the join.

Also adds the two audit events the minting half was missing
(HiddenVetterEnrolled, HiddenVetterTokensIssued), written after their store
rows so the log never claims an issuance the store did not keep. The enrolment
payload carries the label and a rotation flag and deliberately no identifier:
the enrolment record is already one half of a future deanonymisation and the
audit log does not need a second copy of it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.gore@gmail.com>

* admin: render a hidden vetter as a tag, not a broken DID

The join-request review passed the statement's issuer to NamedDid. On the
hidden path that value is a pseudonym, not a DID, so the panel rendered a tag
through a DID renderer — which is how a reviewer concludes the row is broken
data rather than the feature working.

It now reads as what it is: Hidden vetter, with the tag shortened and the
explanation in the title, and a note under the counted-vetters line saying the
count came from a proof. Both keys off one predicate, so the two places cannot
disagree.

* feat(vtc): serve hidden vetting's three Trust Tasks

Enrolment, the token drip and the submission challenge now arrive the way
every other task does — a signed document posted to /v1/trust-tasks, through
the same dispatcher, with each refusal carrying the code its specification
declares.

The payload types are hand-written, which is normally forbidden. The rule
(workspace CLAUDE.md, "Trust Task wire types come from trust_tasks_rs::specs")
exists so that a copy cannot drift from its specification, and the copy here
cannot: src/vetting/schemas/ carries the three published schemas verbatim and
vetting::pcs_tasks::tests validates every payload and response against them.
The types are hand-written because the generated ones cannot be reached yet —
the bindings generate as trust-tasks-rs 0.22 and this graph pins ^0.21 through
published crates, so the two nodes do not unify and no patch bridges them.
Both copies are deleted by the release, which is a queue rather than a design
question; trust_task_manifest's UNPUBLISHED_CANONICAL_OK carries the three
URIs with their counts until then.

tests/hidden_vetting_tasks.rs drives the wire as a client does and checks what
a client needs: the pre-credential unblinds, the served tokens verify under the
published key, the challenge is 16 bytes of lowercase hex. Then the refusals
that make each exchange a rule rather than a courtesy — a stranger enrolling, a
second enrolment under one label, a second draw for one tick, a batch over the
published rate.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): serve event mode, and let an event's tokens die with it

A conference desk needs a faster rate than an ordinary week, and §5.1's answer
is deliberately not a bigger drip: a separate token label for a named event,
with its own rate, its own expiry, and a group of vetters large enough that a
spend under it still hides one. vtc/vetting/vetters/event-mode/0.1 (merged
upstream as #620) carries the vetter's half, which is only ever a request —
approving an event is an admin re-posting the criterion, deliberately not a
Trust Task, because a task the vetter could send is a task a vetter could be
made to send.

The four conditions are checked in pcs_event::gate at the drip and not at
configuration: approved, approved by someone outside the group, over the
published floor, and inside the window. Configuration is where a coerced
approver's edit would land, so an approver's DID in a criterion is a claim, and
the claim is tested where the tokens are served. A refusal there carries
pcs-tokens:eventRefused rather than notAVetter — the vetter holds the grant,
and sending them to chase one is the wrong answer to the right complaint.

The second half of the expiry rule was missing and is the reason for the change
in pcs.rs. Issuing stopped at closesAfter; *accepting spends* did not, so it
depended on an operator pruning liveTokenLabels. Three days at twenty a day
would have stayed spendable for as long as nobody tidied up — which is the
stockpile the separate key exists to prevent. accepted_token_labels now drops an
expired event label from the verifier on the community's own deadline.

Two corrections travel with this:

The hand-written payload types were never waiting for a trust-tasks-rs release.
0.22 is published and the open release PR ships the line carrying these specs.
This graph resolves 0.21.17 because affinidi-messaging-sdk, the mediator and the
four trust-tasks companions are all on 0.21 and re-export trust-tasks-rs types.
Five crates have to move and none of them is ours; the comments and the manifest
exceptions said 'awaiting a release', which is a different thing to plan around.

Nothing in CI compiled any of it. vetting-pcs is off by default, so the existing
job built none of the service code this branch adds — the workspace's own 'green
and wrong' failure mode behind a feature flag. Added a clippy + test step; it
builds on a runner because predicate-credential-system is vendored and tracked
and vti-vetting-pcs is a path dependency.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): publish hidden vetting, and serve the parameters a client reads

Two of the three things standing between "the wire is closed" and "two
processes can do this" are on this side.

**Nothing published the parameters.** `pcs_issue::publish` derives the keys
from the credential signer's master secret, and it was called from the test
harness and nowhere else — the whole minting half was reachable only by a test.
`POST /v1/vetting/hidden` is the operator's one call: derive, store on a
criterion, and hand back both what is kept and what is published.

**Nothing carried them to a client.** The design note said a generated
`deny_unknown_fields` type made that impossible and clients would get them out
of band. That was wrong: `VettingRequirements` is `additionalProperties: true`,
so an unknown member is dropped by the typed parse rather than rejected by it.
A criterion is now served as JSON with `vetting.ext` injected, and the typed
form travels beside it for consumers that evaluate against it — `ServedCriterion`
is the pair, kept together so the digest cannot be taken over one and served
over the other.

The injection happens **before** the digest, because the digest is what a proof
binds to and the parameters are part of what the applicant received. The publish
route reads the digest back off `manifest_criterion` rather than computing its
own, for the same reason: two computations of one digest is how they come to
disagree, and a disagreement here means every submission fails with nothing
useful to say.

And what is published is a translation, not `to_value(config)`. The store keeps
`hvk`/`tvk`/`livePeriods`; a client reads `helperKey`/`tokenKey`/`vetterLabels`.
Serving the stored shape parses as nothing, and `read_mode` answers `Named` for
a community hiding every one of its vetters — silently, because unreadable
parameters are only fatal when marked critical. `approvedBy` and `graceDays`
are dropped: who approved an event is the community's record of its own
decision, and publishing it names a member in a document every applicant gets.

Two guards moved with it. The OpenAPI response census gains `admin_manifest`,
with the reason — `JoinManifest02Response` cannot carry `ext`, the console reads
only the members it names, and the entry goes when 0.22 lands. The snapshot test
becomes feature-aware: regenerating it under `vetting-pcs` would write a path
into the document the shipped daemon does not serve, so `UPDATE_OPENAPI` is
refused there and the feature build asserts the document is the shipped one plus
exactly the listed additions.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc): hold hidden vetting to the guards now its specs are published

trust-tasks-rs 0.22 (reached through the main merge) publishes the four
hidden-vetting specs, so the published-URI guards now apply to them:

- conformance: a witness per task, built from the handler's wire
  structs; and the enrolment test validates the library's real root
  request, token batch and answers against the published schemas.
- error-code census: all 19 declared codes witnessed over
  /v1/trust-tasks. 15 were already asserted; a new test drives the
  rest (wrongLabel, badRequest, identifierRebound, labelNotLive,
  badOpeningProof, pcs-tokens:notAVetter). Nothing baselined.
- the proof-REQUIRED count gains the four tasks under vetting-pcs.
- the manifest's "awaiting the 0.22 line" entries go to zero.
- the conformance scan skips vetting/pcs*.rs without vetting-pcs, whose
  literals bind nothing in that build.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* chore(vetting-pcs): depend on published predicate-credential-system

predicate-credential-system is now published on crates.io (v0.1.0, from
OpenVTC/predicate-credential-system). Switch vti-vetting-pcs and
vtc-service's optional vetting-pcs feature from the vendored path
dependency to a version dependency, and remove the vendored copy,
its application-context patch, and PROVENANCE.md.

cargo test -p vti-vetting-pcs --all-features and cargo test -p
vtc-service --features vetting-pcs --no-fail-fast both pass in full.

Note: this branch is 13 commits ahead / 137 behind origin/main and is
NOT mergeable as-is. A merge attempt hit 8 substantive conflicts
(.github/workflows/ci.yml, Cargo.lock, vtc-service/admin-ui/openapi.json,
vtc-service/admin-ui/src/lib/wire.ts,
vtc-service/src/routes/join_requests/manifest.rs,
vtc-service/src/store/keyspaces.rs, vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs,
vtc-service/tests/trust_task_manifest.rs, vti-common/src/audit/mod.rs)
deliberately left unresolved here; syncing with main is a separate
follow-up.

* fix(vetting-pcs): stage the routes/schemas silent-staleness fixes

Four fixes from the main-sync (routes/mod.rs, routes/schemas.rs,
schemas/accepts.rs, trust_tasks/conformance.rs) were made in the working tree
but never staged before the merge commit, so 0388cd31 carried the pre-fix
content even though every test run since used the corrected files. This
stages what was already verified: the b2 surface-verbs migration
(routes/mod.rs, routes/schemas.rs no longer bind REST routes main retired),
schemas::accepts::referenced_types widened to pub(crate) for the new
surface_tasks module, and the accepts_criterion() fixture's hidden_vetting
field.

No content change from what cargo test already verified — this only fixes
what got committed.

* fix(ci): rustfmt UNTYPED_OK, copy vti-vetting-pcs in Dockerfile.nitro

Both are pre-existing gaps on this branch that only surfaced now that CI is
actually running on this PR for the first time (a stuck CLOWarden check
suite blocked every prior run).

- vtc-service/tests/openapi_response_census.rs: rustfmt collapses a
  single-element array literal differently than a multi-element one: the
  UNTYPED_OK list dropped to one entry when admin_manifest's exception was
  removed during the main-sync, and the file was never re-run through
  cargo fmt.
- Dockerfile.nitro: vti-vetting-pcs was added as a workspace member by this
  branch's own earlier commits but never added to the nitro image's COPY
  block, so cargo-chef's skeleton stub stood in for it during that build.

* fix(vtc-service): migrate pcs_tasks off hand-written types to generated trust-tasks-rs 0.24 types

trust-tasks-rs 0.24 now generates vtc/vetting/vetters/{pcs-root,pcs-tokens,event-mode}/0.1
and vtc/vetting/pcs-challenge/0.1, superseding the 8 hand-written structs that
no_workspace_crate_hand_writes_a_generated_trust_task_type flags. Swap pcs_tasks.rs's
handlers and conformance.rs's witness fixtures onto the generated builder types, and
drop the local schema fixtures the deleted hand-written test module used to validate
against (nothing else references them).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-sdk): exempt hidden-vetting's public token labels and serial from the secret-debug census

CI's first real run on this branch (a stuck check suite had blocked it since
creation) caught 3 fields the census added since this branch's last sync: the
drip-label fields on PublishHiddenVettingBody/HiddenVettingConfig hold labels
like token/2026-09, not token material, and StatementMeta.token_serial is part
of that type's own documented public metadata, bound into the attestation for
double-spend detection. None hold secret material, so they're documented in
NOT_SECRET rather than given a hand-written Debug.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(vtc): pairwise revoke authorization and admin-resend for vetters
body:
## Summary

VTI PR OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1845 had to keep two bearer REST routes in `vtc-service` because no Trust Task spec expressed the capacity they authorize. This adds one spec version per route, and confirms a third family already has full coverage:

| REST route | Trust Task |
|---|---|
| `DELETE /v1/relationships/{id}` with a `VrcRevokeAuthorization` (pairwise relationship-DID capacity) | [`vtc/relationships/revoke/0.2`](specs/vtc/relationships/revoke/0.2/spec.md) |
| `POST /v1/vetting/vetters/{memberDid}/resend` (admin resending another member's grant) | [`vtc/vetting/vetters/resend/0.2`](specs/vtc/vetting/vetters/resend/0.2/spec.md) |
| `GET/DELETE /v1/credentials/endorsements[/{id}]` | already `vtc/endorsements/{list,show,revoke}/0.1` — no gap, no change |

## Design notes

- **`vtc/relationships/revoke/0.2`.** `0.1`'s payload is `{ id }` alone, so a signed document could never retract an edge published under a pairwise relationship DID — only an administrator could, over the Trust Task spine; the REST door's `VrcRevokeAuthorization` was the only path for the issuer themselves. `0.2` adds an optional `pop`, a proof of possession by the relationship's `issuerDid`, bound to this document (`documentId`) and to the edge (`relationship`) — the stronger of the two options considered, matching how `vtc/relationships/publish/0.2` already proves control of a pairwise issuing key rather than a weaker binding-credential approach. `type: "VrcRevokeAuthorization"` (distinct from publish's `VrcPublishAuthorization`) stops a publish signature being replayed as a revoke authorization. Conformance now states all three authorization routes the REST handler already supports — issuer, administrator, pairwise-via-`pop` — collapsing every failure to `notFound`, carrying over `0.1`'s anti-probing rationale. Purely additive; `0.1` is not retired.
- **`vtc/vetting/vetters/resend/0.2`.** `0.1` accepted only an empty payload, and only from the vetter whose grant it was — "a resend always concerns the sender's own grant" was itself one of `0.1`'s invalid-example notes. `0.2` adds an optional `memberDid`: present, the sender MUST hold the community-administrator capability and the resend concerns the named member instead; absent, behaviour is exactly `0.1`'s. This is the VTI handler's existing `resend_as_admin`/`resend` split, given a route on the spine. Purely additive; `0.1` is not retired.
- **Endorsements.** `vtc/endorsements/list/0.1`, `show/0.1` and `revoke/0.1` already exist, and the VTI routes already dispatch them as Trust Tasks matching the REST handlers exactly (`vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/member_tasks.rs`). No spec work needed.

Both new versions follow the family's established shape: an `## Authorization` section (framework 0.6.0), the four Security & Privacy sub-headings, and `payload.invalid-examples.json` covering the new fields.

## Test plan

title: fix(vta): provision mediator ACL during DIDComm enable and update
body:
### Summary

- Add `--setup-acl` support to DIDComm enable and update commands.
- Carry `setupAcl` through the Trust Task extension.
- Provision the VTA mediator ACL before the forwarded self trust-ping.
- Reuse the candidate connection during live mediator updates.
- Preserve the previous mediator during its drain period.
- Delay promotion of the new outbound mediator by 5 seconds for DIDComm-carried updates so the response can still leave through the old mediator.
- Add transient and live cross-mediator handshake coverage.
- Update runtime service-management documentation.

The 5-second promotion grace period is a temporary workaround for a messaging SDK limitation: inbound subscribers do not currently receive the source mediator/transport identity, so the response cannot be explicitly routed back through the mediator that delivered the request. Source-aware reply routing should replace this workaround.

## Testing

Validated the existing mediator-backed transport harness with:

```bash
cargo test -p vta-service \
  --features transport-harness \
  transport_harness_tests
```

This CI-filtered suite now includes the live DIDComm mediator ACL regression. The regression is located in `test_support.rs` inside the existing `transport_harness_tests` module, so it is executed by the current CI job rather than requiring a separate integration-test command. 

### Follow-Up

`didcomm enable` currently persists the new DIDComm configuration but does not initiate a service restart. The persistent DIDComm service therefore starts only after a later process restart. Restart and readiness coordination will be handled in a separate follow-up PR.

title: fix(vtc-service): a raised document limit only for a known issuer, within a large-document budget
body:
Ports the webvh hardening from affinidi-webvh-service#239 and #244 to vtc-service.

- A type's raised `maxDocumentBytes` is granted only when the document's unverified in-band `issuer` holds a VTC ACL entry. Anyone else gets the default limit.
- Each grant is charged against a per-address budget of 5 per minute. The address is the client IP over HTTPS (the admission limiter's address) or the sender VID on the messaging transports. A service-wide cap of 60 per minute bounds freshly minted VIDs and IP pools.
- After proof verification the charge is settled. A failure, or a verified issuer that differs from the claimed one, doubles that address's next cost. Penalties survive a full budget map: only idle, unpenalised entries are evicted, and a new address is otherwise refused.

Checks: clippy, the `size` unit tests, `openapi_tests`, `conformance` and `trust_task_manifest`.

title: fix(vti-common): step-up gate reads the session's level, not the token's
body:
A step-up (\`auth/passkey/login/finish/0.2\`, \`purpose: stepUp\`) elevates the session row and mints no new token; the spec has the caller's existing tokens pick the elevation up at introspection. \`check_fresh_step_up\` nonetheless required \`claims.acr == "aal2"\` from the JWT, so a session that signed in at aal1 (SIOPv2, DID-signed authenticate) kept an aal1 token for its whole life and could never satisfy any \`StepUpAuth\` / \`elevation::verified\` gate.

In the VTC admin console this showed as "passkey verification did not complete" when enabling console signing, after the passkey ceremony had succeeded. It equally blocked \`acl/grant\` and \`acl/change-role\` for SIOP sessions.

The gate now checks the row's \`acr\` and the live elevation window. The window remains the authority: only a step-up writes it.

Tests: new regression test (aal1 token, elevated row passes); existing \`step_up_refuses_aal1_even_with_a_live_window\` still passes. \`vti-common\` 592 pass; \`vtc-service\`/\`vtc-client\` pass except the 4 known \`admin_ui::tests\` under \`VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1\`. \`vta-service\` tests and clippy not run locally.

title: Relationship policy discovery: both communities must admit an edge, neither can find out
body:
## Summary

Forming an edge between two communities requires **both** communities' policies
to admit it, and there is no way for either side to learn the other's policy
before trying. The first signal that an edge is inadmissible is a rejection,
after one half has already been published.

Raising this as an interoperability question rather than a purely local one: the
failure is symmetric and neither party can fix it alone, which is the shape of
thing a specification usually settles.

## Detail

A cross-community edge needs two independent permissions:

- The **public** community must accept a half whose subject is an opaque
  pairwise identifier belonging to a non-member.
- The **private** community must permit its member to name an outsider in a
  credential at all.

Each is a reasonable policy position, and either may be "no". Nothing published
by either community says which.

A concrete instance from our implementation. Our default relationship policy has
two branches:

```rego
# Pairwise: membership comes from the session.
allow if {
    input.action == "publish"
    input.authenticated_member.is_current
    input.identifier_form == "pairwise"
}

# Attributed: both named parties are community members.
allow if {
    input.action == "publish"
    input.identifier_form == "attributed"
    input.issuer.is_current
    input.subject.is_current
}
```

The public member's half is *attributed* — that is the whole point of a public
community — and its subject is an outsider, so `input.subject.is_current` is
false and the publish is denied. The pairwise branch would admit an opaque
subject, but only when the publisher's own identifier is pairwise, which is
exactly what the public community has declared it does not use.

So the edge fails, correctly, under a policy that is defensible on its own
terms. What is missing is any way for the other party to have known that before
publishing their half — and by then the private member has already issued a
credential naming someone who cannot reciprocate.

## Why it matters

Both parties behave conformantly and the edge still fails, which makes this an
interoperability property rather than a local configuration choice. It also
fails asymmetrically in time: whichever party publishes first has already
disclosed something.

The information needed is small — whether a community accepts non-member
subjects, and which identifier forms it will publish under. Those are properties
a community can state without revealing anything about its membership, which
matters because the communities most likely to refuse are the private ones.

## Requested clarification

1. Should a community publish enough of its relationship policy for a
   counterparty to determine, before publishing, whether an edge is admissible?
2. If so, is that a discoverable field on the community profile, and is it in
   scope for this specification or for the Trust Task layer?
3. Is there an intended ordering for edge formation that avoids one party
   disclosing before the other's admissibility is known?

**Proposed answer**: publish the relevant predicates — accepted subject forms,
accepted issuer identifier forms — as a discoverable field on the community
profile. It is cheap, it reveals nothing about membership, and it turns a failed
publish into a pre-flight check. We will implement this locally either way; the
question for the group is whether it should be interoperable, since a
locally-invented field helps nobody else.

## Context

Raised while implementing the VRC path in
`OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure`. Set out as item X4 in the
["Across communities" section of the DTG conformance
review](https://docs.fpp.storm.ws/dtg-conformance-infographic.html). Related:
#21, #22, and the two companion cross-community questions filed alongside this
one.

title: feat(vtc-client)!: every VTC call is a signed Trust Task
body:
Every `vtc-client` and `cnm` call to the VTC is now a signed Trust Task over the resolved transport (TSP > DIDComm > HTTPS `POST /v1/trust-tasks`). The REST routes that were kept only for them are deleted.

## vtc-client

- The fallback from Trust Task to bearer REST is gone. `document()` sends over the session when there is one; otherwise it signs with the operator's key and posts to `/trust-tasks`. With no session and no key the call returns `NotAuthenticated`.
- New `VtcClient::with_key(base, vtc_did, HolderKey)`: an HTTPS client that signs every task and holds no bearer token.
- Removed: `with_token`, the `tt` / `get_json` / `post_json` helpers, and `resend_vetter_grant` (admin resend has no signed form).
- Moved to signed tasks:
  - `list_members`, `list_join_requests` (paginated `members/list`, `join-requests/list`)
  - `approve_join` / `reject_join` (`join-requests/decide`)
  - `remove_member`, `update_member_extensions`, `member_credentials`
  - `list_policies`, `get_policy`, `upload_policy`, `activate_policy`. `activate_policy` reads the revision first to get the `purpose` the task requires.
  - `install_did_log` (`did/register`)
  - `grant_vetter`, `show_vetter`, `revoke_endorsement` (`endorsements/revoke`)
  - `audit_verify`
- Still on bearer REST until #1835 merges: `list_vetter_grants`, `auto_grant`, `configure_auto_grant`, `branding`, `set_branding`, `requested_attributes`, `set_requested_attributes`, `vetting_revocations`.

## cnm

- `connect_for_tasks` now signs its HTTPS client with the profile key (`with_key`).
- These commands now use the resolved transport and honour `--transport`:
  - `cnm audit verify`
  - `cnm did-log install`
  - `cnm vetting vetters grant|revoke`
  - `cnm vetting bootstrap-pgp` (roster read and grants)
- The other vetting commands keep a bearer connection until #1835.
- `cnm vetting vetters resend` is removed. A vetter can still resend their own grant with the signed self-resend.
- Not changed: `cnm consent` (`cnm-cli/src/consent.rs` belongs to the other session). It still sends a signed document, but always over HTTPS.

## VTC routes deleted (their Trust Task is served on main)

- `GET /members`, `PATCH /members/{did}`, `DELETE /members/{did}`, `GET /members/{did}/credentials`
- `GET /join-requests`, `POST /join-requests/{id}/decide`
- `GET /policies`, `POST /policies`, `GET /policies/{id}`, `POST /policies/{id}/activate`
- `POST /admin/did/register`
- `GET /audit/verify`
- `POST /vetting/vetters`, `POST /vetting/vetters/show`

The openapi snapshot and `wire.ts` are regenerated. The response schemas the console types its signed calls with are registered as components.

## Routes kept

- Their Trust Tasks are not on main until #1835: `GET /vetting/vetters`, `GET`/`PUT /vetting/auto-grant`, `GET /vetting/revocations`, `GET`/`PUT /community/branding`, `GET`/`PUT /community/requested-attributes`.
- `POST /vetting/vetters/{did}/resend`: missing spec (below). The console still uses it.
- `POST /credential-exchange/request`: documented exception.

## Missing specs

- Admin resend of another member's vetter grant. `vtc/vetting/vetters/resend/0.1` only covers the signer's own grant.
- The `vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1` response doesn't say whether the call created a grant or returned an existing one; REST used 201 vs 200 for that. `grant_vetter` now calls `show` first to fill in `created`, which is informational only.

## Tests

- Suites that drove the deleted routes now use signed documents, through the extended `common::legacy` shim or `common::signed`.
- The auth-plumbing suites (cookie session, idle timeout, audience, smoke) now point at `GET /auth/whoami`.
- The census and manifest tests are updated for the removed routes.

Local run:
- clippy with `-D warnings`: clean
- fmt: clean
- `vtc-service --lib openapi_tests conformance`: pass
- `--test trust_task_manifest`: pass
- `vtc-client`: 32 pass
- `cnm-cli`: 90 pass

CI covers the rest.

title: feat(git-ns): administrator reads as Trust Tasks
body:
## Summary

Six VTC git-ns console REST reads had no Trust Task equivalent — the admin console's *Repos* plugin (rights, jobs, projection, accounts) and its activity feed were served only over a bearer admin session (`vtc-service/src/routes/git_ns.rs`), with no signed, transport-agnostic path. This adds one spec per route:

| REST route | Trust Task |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/git-ns/rights` | [`git-ns/right/list/0.1`](specs/git-ns/right/list/0.1/spec.md) |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/rights/issued-by-departed` | [`git-ns/right/issued-by-departed/0.1`](specs/git-ns/right/issued-by-departed/0.1/spec.md) |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/jobs` | [`git-ns/bridge/job/list/0.1`](specs/git-ns/bridge/job/list/0.1/spec.md) |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/projection` | [`git-ns/projection/show/0.1`](specs/git-ns/projection/show/0.1/spec.md) |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/accounts` | [`git-ns/account/list/0.1`](specs/git-ns/account/list/0.1/spec.md) |
| `GET /v1/git-ns/activity` | [`git-ns/activity/list/0.1`](specs/git-ns/activity/list/0.1/spec.md) |

## Design notes

- **`git-ns/right/list/0.1` vs. a `git-ns/view` revision.** A new spec, not a `git-ns/view` 0.6 bump: the role-derived rows the console shows (v0.1 `[hooks.git-trust] grant_on_role` grants) are not `RightRecord`s — no granter, no grant time, no expiry — and `subjectMember`/`granterDeparted` are administrative facts a member's own view has no business carrying. Folding either into the shared `RightRecord` component would widen every other consumer of it across the `git-ns/*` family. `specs/git-ns/_shared/0.5` adds a new, additive `AdminRightRow` (+ `RightOrigin`) component instead, shared by `right/list` and `right/issued-by-departed`.
- **Authority follows the REST handlers' actual gates.** `right/list`, `right/issued-by-departed`, `projection/show` and `account/list` require the **community-administrator capability**, matching their handlers' `SuperAdminAuth` — none of them is namespace-scoped, so `git.ns.admin` on a namespace is explicitly not enough (each Authorization section says so and why). `bridge/job/list` and `activity/list` scope to **administered namespaces** (community administrator sees all; a namespace admin sees their own), the same pattern `git-ns/namespace/list` and `git-ns/repo/list` already use — `activity/list` mirrors the existing handler's per-namespace filtering exactly, and `bridge/job/list` tightens beyond the REST handler's current unscoped `AdminAuth` to match the family's established security posture.
- **`git-ns/activity/list/0.1` vs. an `audit/list` filter.** Kept as its own spec rather than a filter on `audit/list`: the feed interleaves two different stores (git-ns audit rows *and* the bridge job queue) into one timeline, which `audit/list`'s filters have no way to express, and its authority (namespace-administrator standing) differs from `audit/list`'s community-wide audit-read capability.
- **Paging.** All six use the registry's common `cursor`/`limit` request, `nextCursor` response shape (as `vtc/registry/sync-jobs/list` and `vtc/registry/records/list` do) rather than the unpaged shape `git-ns/namespace/list`/`git-ns/repo/list` use — these six enumerate collections that grow unboundedly (rights history, job queue, member roster, activity log), unlike a namespace or repository count.
- All six declare `proof: REQUIRED`, an `## Authorization` section, and the four `## Security & Privacy` sub-headings, with valid and invalid (`payload.invalid-examples.json`) examples.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run validate` — clean, no new errors or warnings from these six specs
- [x] `npm run check-bindings` — Rust/TS/Go/Dart agree with the registry
- [x] `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs -- specs::git_ns` — 120 passed, 0 failed
- [x] Regenerated all four bindings (Rust, TypeScript, Go, Dart) in this PR

title: feat(spec-meta): a specification declares its own maximum document size
body:
## ⚠️ Framework-level change

Adds an optional front-matter member, **`maxDocumentBytes`**, so a specification can state the largest document of each variant a consumer serving it is expected to accept. This is the registry half; the framework text (Specification Requirements **item 21**, plus one sentence in Parser Hardening) is proposed in the canonical repository: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec#26. `SPEC.md` is not edited here.

```yaml
maxDocumentBytes:
  request: 360448      # bytes of the serialized document, proof included, no transport envelope
  response: 65536      # each variant optional; at least one declared
  rationale: ...
```

### Why

SPEC §12.4 tells a consumer to bound what it parses at "a body-size limit appropriate to the Trust Task specification's payload", and §7.3 item 19 already notes that a transport-layer limit is the wrong place to choose one. No specification could say what its limit was, so a consumer serving many tasks picks one cap for all of them. The VTC does this with 64 KiB on `/trust-tasks`, which refuses registering a credential schema or moving website content. Raising the cap for every task so the largest ones fit would open all the others to bodies they have no use for. With this member, each task states its own bound and the spine enforces it per type.

### Semantics

- The bound is two-sided. A consumer **MUST NOT** refuse a document within the bound on size alone, and **SHOULD** refuse a larger one with `malformedRequest`, before parsing where it learns the `type` first.
- The two variants are independent: an absent one never inherits the other's bound.
- With no declaration, the consumer's own limit applies, as it does today.
- The meta-schema allows 1 KiB to 16 MiB. Anything bigger belongs in a chunked transfer.

### What changes

- `specs/spec.meta.schema.json`: the member.
- `trust-tasks-codegen`:
  - emits `Payload::MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES: Option<usize>` on the request and `Response` impls;
  - emits `schema_index::max_document_bytes_for(type_uri)` (bare URI for the request, `#response` for the response), for a dispatcher that knows the type before it parses;
  - refuses a `response` bound on a spec with no `$defs.Response`.
- `trust-tasks-rs`: the trait constant, defaulting to `None`. It is additive and has a default.
- `check-bindings`: compares Rust's constants against the front matter, re-derived independently.

title: feat(vta/services): rollback 1.1 with a mediator drain window
body:
Adds `vta/services/rollback/1.1`: an optional `drainTtlSecs` for the mediated transports (`didcomm`, `tsp`). It is the same member, with the same rules, that `vta/services/update/1.1` added in #656.

**Why.** A rollback of a mediated transport can move it off its current mediator, and that mediator then drains. Rollback 1.0 gives the operator no way to set how long the drain lasts, so the agent can only use its default. The VTA's CLI (`services didcomm rollback --drain-ttl`) and SDK already accept an operator-chosen window. Without a member for it on the Trust Task, a rollback that starts a drain ignores that choice and always uses the default.

**Rules (same as update 1.1):**
- Refused with `malformedRequest` for `rest` and `webauthn`.
- If absent, the agent uses its default. The agent may raise a value below its floor to the floor. It must do so when the request arrived through the mediator being replaced.
- A mediator that carries both mediated transports drains once for both, and the result reports a single `drainUntil`.
- New in this version: when the rollback leaves no mediator draining, `drainTtlSecs` is accepted and has no effect. Whether a rollback drains depends on stored state the operator may not be able to see.

A 1.0 request is a valid 1.1 request. The response is unchanged, because the shared `RollbackResult` already carries `drainingMediator` and `drainUntil`. Includes `payload.invalid-examples.json`.

**Checks run locally:** `npm run validate`, `npm run build`, `npm run check-bindings` (592 specs, all four languages agree), `cargo test --workspace` (plus `trust-tasks-rs --all-features`, which includes the new `rejects_invalid_examples`), `go test ./...`, `dart analyze` + `dart test`, the TS `npm test` + `tsc` + `smoke`, `test:infra` and `test-ceremonies`. All pass. Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings are regenerated in this PR.

title: docs(specs): operational examples sign for authentication
body:
## What

VTI-KEY-022 (#637) moved a Trust Task document's proof default from
`assertionMethod` to `authentication`, reserving `assertionMethod` for
attestations and approver decisions — the closed list: `auth/step-up/approve-response`,
`task-consent/decision`, `confirm/response` (their `#response` variants sign
for `authentication`). #637's own docs sweep (6d48962a) updated the
top-level examples that existed at the time. This PR catches the ones that
didn't: newer minor versions created after that sweep, and a couple it missed.

## Changed (`assertionMethod` → `authentication` on an operational document's
top-level `proof`, non-normative examples only)

- `SPEC.md` — Example 1 (§4.2, a complete Trust Task document), Example 5
  (§8.2, an error response), Appendix A.4 (an example conforming document).
  `SPEC.md` is generated from the canonical `trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec`
  repo; this fix should also land there so the next regeneration doesn't
  revert it.
- `specs/acl/swap-key/0.1/spec.md` — the `linkProof` example (a challenge-bound
  consent proof, functionally an authentication signature, not an attestation).
- `specs/did-management/did/publish/0.1/spec.md` — the request example.
- `specs/git-ns/right/revoke/0.3`, `right/ratify/0.1`, `right/break-glass-notice/0.1`,
  `right/break-glass/0.1`, `right/grant/0.3`, `bridge/job/0.4`,
  `namespace/reseat/0.3`, `drift/resolve/0.3`, `account/unlink/0.1`,
  `repo/create/0.3` — minor versions published after #637's sweep that copied
  the old `assertionMethod` examples forward.

No normative text contradicted the rule in any of these files; only the
JSON examples were stale. No `verificationMethod` fragment named an
assertion-specific key, so none needed renaming.

## Left unchanged (real attestations / approver decisions / out of scope)

- `specs/task-consent/decision/0.1`, `specs/auth/step-up/approve-response/0.1–0.5`,
  `specs/confirm/response/0.1` — the closed list; normatively require
  `assertionMethod`.
- Embedded W3C Verifiable Credentials: `specs/vault/credentials/get/0.1`,
  `specs/vault/credentials/receive/0.1`, the role credential in
  `specs/vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1` (its two top-level Trust Task proofs
  were already fixed by #637; the remaining `assertionMethod` there is the
  delivered VC).
- Embedded/nested signed artefacts: the vetting card (`specs/vetting/session/0.1`,
  `specs/vetting/request/0.1`, `specs/vetting/_shared/0.1/vetting-card.schema.json`)
  and the witness proof (`specs/webvh/witness/publish/0.1`,
  `specs/webvh/witness/sign/0.1`) — these are attestations embedded in
  `payload`, not the Trust Task envelope's own proof.
- `specs/keys/derive-and-sign-document/0.1` — a generic document-signing
  service where `proofPurpose` is a caller-supplied payload member for a
  document the producer hands over; not the framework's own default.
- DID-document verification-relationship references (`specs/vta/_shared/0.3`,
  `specs/vta/webvh/dids/**`) — these name the `assertionMethod` DID-document
  relationship, unrelated to a Trust Task proof's `proofPurpose`.
- `specs/vault/sign-trust-task/0.1` and `0.2` — untouched; PR #667 is open
  against these files.
- `specs/provision/integration/{0.1,0.2,0.3}/payload.invalid-examples.json` —
  already a deliberately-invalid conformance fixture demonstrating this exact
  rule (`"note": "DataIntegrityProof.proofPurpose must be authentication."`).
- Interop test fixtures (`trust-tasks-go/proof/testdata`,
  `trust-tasks-ts-proof/test`, `trust-tasks-dart-proof/test/fixtures`) —
  byte-exact signed fixtures pinned by cross-library tests; changing the
  string would invalidate the signature they carry.

## Bindings

Regenerated all four (`cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`,
`npm run build-ts-bindings`, `npm run build-go-bindings`,
`npm run build-dart-bindings`). Only the Rust crate had a diff — its codegen
embeds each spec's fenced request/response examples verbatim as conformance
tests, so the ten touched git-ns/did-management specs' Rust conformance
fixtures picked up the new `proofPurpose` string. TS, Go and Dart generate
from the JSON Schemas, which didn't change, so they have no diff.

- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs` — pass
- `go test ./...` in `trust-tasks-go` — pass
- `npm install && npm test` in `trust-tasks-ts` — pass

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.24.6` → `0.24.7` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.24.6` → `0.24.7` | patch |
