title: feat(vtc): Trust Tasks for the community's REST-only admin surfaces
body:
Builds on #679 (merged: the `maxDocumentBytes` front-matter member and the `"variant": "response"` invalid-example fixtures). Rebased directly onto `main`; this PR is no longer stacked, and its diff is only its own commits.

This PR specifies the VTC surfaces that today exist only as REST routes (inventory class b2). The rule it follows: every remote API is a sender-bound signed Trust Task over TSP, DIDComm or HTTPS. Each spec describes the current handler in `vtc-service/src/routes/**` (fields, roles, bounds, errors), and calls out where the signed form has to behave differently.

## New Type URIs (all `0.1`, draft, framework 0.6.0)

| URI | Replaces |
|---|---|
| `auth/signing-key/enroll` · `list` · `revoke` | `/admin/console-keys` POST · GET · DELETE |
| `vtc/community/branding/{show,update}` | `/community/branding` |
| `vtc/community/requested-attributes/{show,update}` | `/community/requested-attributes` |
| `vtc/community/join-discovery/{show,update}` | `/community/join-discovery` |
| `vtc/schemas/{register,list,show,delete}` | `/schemas` |
| `vtc/schemas/accepts/{register,list,show,delete}` | `/schemas/accepts` |
| `vtc/vetting/vetters/grants/list` | `GET /vetting/vetters` |
| `vtc/vetting/auto-grant/{show,update}` | `/vetting/auto-grant` |
| `vtc/vetting/revocations/list` | `GET /vetting/revocations` |
| `vtc/relationships/{suspend,restore}` | `/relationships/{id}/{suspend,restore}` |
| `vtc/join-requests/vetting/show` | `GET /join-requests/{id}/vetting` |
| `vtc/join-requests/query` | `POST /join-requests/query` |
| `vtc/rooms/list` | `GET /rooms` |

New shared components:

- `auth/_shared/0.1/signing-key`
- `vtc/_shared/0.1/{community-presentation, schema-registry, vetting-auto-grant, relationship-lifecycle}`

Each spec ships request **and** `"variant": "response"` invalid-example fixtures.

## Design decisions for review

1. **`auth/signing-key/enroll` is signed by the key being enrolled.** The `issuer` is `signingKeyDid`, so the proof doubles as proof of possession. The identity the key will act for is a payload member, `identityDid`. The console can't hold the admin's key, so this is the only signer it can produce for its first key.
   - Control of `identityDid` comes from separate evidence, not from the key's signature. In the reference design that evidence is the VTC's operation-bound passkey step-up, bound to the enrolment digest: a refusal with `permissionDenied` + `details.stepUpRequest` (approve-request/0.3 inline delivery), then `approve-response/0.4`, then the same document re-sent.
   - This is written descriptively, because §7.3 item 13 forbids a spec from requiring step-up.
   - The consumer **SHOULD** issue the step-up before checking standing, so the refusal doesn't reveal who is an administrator.
   - REST takes the admin from the cookie session. This is the largest REST-to-Trust-Task change in the set.
2. **Size bounds.** `vtc/schemas/register` declares 256 KiB for the request and 320 KiB for the response. `vtc/schemas/show` declares 320 KiB for the response only. Both are sized to the ~352 KiB document that `backup/put-chunk` derives as surviving a 1 MiB mediator message. Today's REST route accepts up to the global 1 MiB. No other task here declares a bound.
3. **`vtc/schemas/list` returns summaries.** It returns `hasCredentialSchema` instead of the schema bodies, and it is paged. REST returns every full entry unpaged. `show` returns the body.
4. **Update payloads wrap their value.** `{ branding }`, `{ requestedAttributes }` and `{ joinDiscovery }` replace the bare REST bodies, because a payload has to be an object. Updates are full replacements, matching the handlers.
5. **`CommunityBranding`, `RequestedAttribute` and `VettingRequirements` are copied into `_shared` from `vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.2`.** There is no cross-task `$ref` precedent to use instead. Re-pinning the manifest to them is left as an editorial follow-up, because it renames generated types that VTI consumes.
6. **Relationships suspend/restore drop the REST `pop` authorization.** The edge's issuer, including a pairwise relationship DID, signs the document itself, so the proof already shows control. Refusals for "not yours" collapse to `notFound`, as `vtc/relationships/revoke` does. REST returns 403 there. `reason` is bounded at 500 characters; REST doesn't bound it.
7. **`vtc/join-requests/query` is its own task, not a `credential-exchange/*` one.** An administrator instructing the verifier to start an exchange is neither party of that exchange. Also, only the verifier can build the query: the nonce is a challenge bound to the VTC's own DID and thread. The holder still receives a `credential-exchange/query/0.1`, and the response carries its payload for relay.
8. **`vtc/rooms/list` sits under `vtc/`, not `rooms/`.** Invariant I5 says room authorization never uses host ACLs, and this list is authorized by host admin standing across owners. Timestamps are unix seconds, matching the handler.
9. **`vtc/join-requests/vetting/show` is a `vetting/show` sub-slug.** The alternative was a new member on `join-requests/show`, which would be a breaking change to that task. The facts also have a different audience and name third parties.
10. **Paging added to the admin lists.** Grants, revocations, schemas, accepts and rooms gain `cursor`/`limit`. REST is unpaged for all of them.
11. **`vtc/schemas/delete:inUse` is a SHOULD.** The handler doesn't check references today. Deletes are classed `destructive`, following `endorsement-types/delete`.

## VGI review of `auth/signing-key/*`, folded in

Each item below is written as a condition on the consumer *accepting an enrolment*, not as a required step-up mechanism, so the spec still complies with SPEC §7.3 item 13, which forbids a specification from requiring step-up.

1. **The approval binds this exact enrolment** (enroll Conformance item 4). The consumer MUST NOT accept evidence of control over `identityDid` unless it is bound to a digest of the whole enrol document: its `type` and full payload, including `signingKeyDid`, `identityDid`, `scope` and `expiresAt`. The consumer MUST recompute that digest over the document it is about to enrol.
2. **No push-based step-up before standing is known** (item 5). Evidence requested before standing is checked MUST be completed by the requester on its own authenticator, and nothing may reach the identity's devices. A consumer that pushes prompts to the identity MUST check standing first and MUST rate-limit the prompts. There is a new `### Approval fatigue` subsection under Security & Privacy.
3. **Lifetime and scope:**
   - `scope` (enum `console`) is now required on the request and on the stored record.
   - `expiresAt` is now required on the record returned by both enroll and list. The consumer sets it and caps it (SHOULD be at most 30 days), and the request's `expiresAt` is only a request (item 6).
   - A delegated key is accepted only within its scope, and MUST NOT be accepted wherever an `assertionMethod` attestation is required (approve-response, task-consent/decision, confirm/response). This mirrors authenticate/0.2's `sessionKey` rule (item 7).
   - `revoke` MUST accept a request signed by the identity *or* by the delegated key itself, so a console can revoke its own key on logout.
4. **Abuse limits** (item 8). The consumer SHOULD cap active keys per identity, using the new error code `enroll:tooManyKeys`, and SHOULD rate-limit enrolment attempts (`unavailable` + `retryAfter`).

**Schema and fixture changes:** a new `SigningKeyScope` def, `scope` and `expiresAt` required as above, and updated examples. New invalid fixtures cover: `scope` missing, `scope: approver`, a record missing `expiresAt` (enroll and list), and a record missing `scope`.

**Differences from today's VTI handler:** it takes no scope, allows an unbounded lifetime, and applies no cap on keys per identity or rate limit.

## Out of scope

- `vtc/relationships/persona` attach/detach: blocked on dtgwg-cred-spec#9.
- git-ns console reads: being folded into `git-ns/view` and the list tasks in another PR.
- Website content: #682.

## Checks run locally (this branch)

All green: `npm run build`, `check-bindings`, `check-dart-packages`; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets` (includes every new `rejects_invalid_examples` / `rejects_invalid_response_examples`), `cargo doc --all-features`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` (default + `--all-features`); TS `tsc --noEmit` / `npm test` / `npm run smoke` (no `X1` duplicate types — descriptions sit on `$defs`, never beside a `$ref`); Go `build` / `vet` / `test` / `gofmt`; Dart `analyze --fatal-infos` / `test`.

* feat(vtc): Trust Tasks for the community's REST-only admin surfaces

Specifies, at 0.1, the VTC operations that existed only as REST routes, so each can be served as a sender-bound signed Trust Task over TSP, DIDComm or HTTPS:

- auth/signing-key/{enroll,list,revoke} — delegated signing keys (the admin console's non-extractable browser key). Enrolment is signed by the key being enrolled (proof of possession) and names the identity it acts for; control of that identity is established by separate authority evidence, which the reference implementation takes as an operation-bound passkey step-up.
- vtc/community/{branding,requested-attributes,join-discovery}/{show,update}
- vtc/schemas/{register,list,show,delete} and vtc/schemas/accepts/{register,list,show,delete} — register and show declare maxDocumentBytes, since a credential schema exceeds the 64 KiB default.
- vtc/vetting/vetters/grants/list, vtc/vetting/auto-grant/{show,update}, vtc/vetting/revocations/list
- vtc/relationships/{suspend,restore} — the edge issuer's own proof replaces the REST pop authorization.
- vtc/join-requests/vetting/show, and vtc/join-requests/query — its own task rather than credential-exchange/*, because an administrator instructs the verifier, which alone can author the query's challenge.
- vtc/rooms/list — under vtc/, not rooms/, because it is authorized by host ACL and rooms invariant I5 forbids that for any rooms/* task.

* spec(auth/signing-key): bind the approval to the enrolment, scope and cap the key

Folds in VGI's review of auth/signing-key/*, each written as a condition on the consumer accepting an enrolment rather than a mandated step-up (SPEC §7.3 item 13):

- Consumers should cap active keys per identity (new enroll:tooManyKeys) and rate-limit enrolment attempts.

Delete is the D5 eviction's `forget`. `--all` also removes half-formed records, which D9's enumeration cannot see, and only reports without `--yes`. The keyspace is opened through `CliStore`, so it decrypts under hardened configuration. `reset` and `delete` are refused on a sealed VTA; `list` is not. Built only with the `tsp` feature. All reads and writes go through the SDK's `PersistentRelationshipStore`. ### Fixed - **provision**: A setup DID granted without a hand-off is told to re-grant, not to shorten an expiry ([#1813](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1813)) Online `vtc setup` (and any setup whose ephemeral is the authenticated caller) rolls the setup DID over to a permanent long-term admin. That rollover is allowed only through the granter's one-time hand-off marker (VTI-ACL-054, `--admin-handoff` / `--handoff`), and every printed setup command carries it. When the entry was granted without it, provision-integration fell through to an ordinary grant and #1738's VTI-ACL-053 bound refused it with "your entry expires at …, so you cannot write a permanent one — give it an expiry no later than yours". That points the operator at the wrong remedy: the successor must be permanent, and what is missing is the marker, which can only be set when the entry is created (VTI-ACL-055). The refusal is now specific: it names the missing hand-off and prints the re-grant (`pnm acl delete --did ` then `pnm acl create … --expires 1h --handoff`, with the entry's own scope derived through `act_scope`). It refuses exactly what VTI-ACL-053 already refused, before anything is minted; nothing is newly allowed. - **pnm**: The persona-holder hint prints a pnm acl update that runs ([#1811](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1811)) The persona refusal and `pnm persona --help` both told operators to run `pnm acl update --did --capabilities persona-holder`. `acl update` takes the entry's DID as a positional argument and has no `--did` flag, so the command offered as the fix failed to parse. Both now print `pnm acl update --capabilities persona-holder`. A new test parses that form and checks that the `--did` form is rejected, so a change to the arguments fails in CI rather than for an operator.

title: Decide the home of the DTG namespace before the Implementers Draft
body:
## Summary

#47 makes VSC predicates absolute IRIs on the wire, so the core predicates are now written out in full. The PR writes them under the existing context URL plus `#`:

```
https://firstperson.network/credentials/dtg/v1#endorses
https://firstperson.network/credentials/dtg/v1#witnessed
```

That is a default inherited from the `@context` requirement in Base Structure, not a decision anyone has made. The namespace is where every predicate this WG defines will live, it is the prefix communities will copy when they define their own vocabularies, and it is what the planned DTG Predicate Vocabulary specification will be published under. It needs an owner.

## Why it has to be decided early

Changing the namespace later is a find-and-replace in the spec but a migration for every credential issued under it: a predicate IRI is compared byte-exact (Predicate Handling in #47), so a credential issued under the old namespace does not match a verifier configured for the new one. That cost is zero today and grows with every issued credential. **This should be settled as soon as possible, and at the latest before the specification bumps to an Implementers Draft**, since that is the point at which implementations start issuing credentials that have to keep verifying.

The same question applies to the `@context` IRI itself, which Base Structure already requires and which is not yet published either; the two should be decided together.

## Options

1. **Keep `https://firstperson.network/credentials/dtg/v1#`.** No change to the spec. The vocabulary — and the context — are then hosted and controlled by First Person, and the DTG Predicate Vocabulary spec, if it becomes a ToIP deliverable, would define terms under a namespace ToIP does not control.
2. **Move to a ToIP-controlled IRI.** For example under `https://trustoverip.org/...` or another origin the Foundation administers. The context and vocabulary are then governed with the specification. Requires ToIP to agree to host and maintain the resources, and a find-and-replace in the spec before any credential is issued.

## What the decision needs to cover

- The namespace IRI for DTG-defined predicates.
- The `@context` IRI (currently `https://firstperson.network/credentials/dtg/v1`), and whether the namespace is that URL plus `#` or a separate IRI.
- Who administers the origin, and the commitment that published context and vocabulary versions are immutable (a requirement in #47).
- Versioning: whether `v1` in the path is the context version, the vocabulary version, or both.

## Proposed resolution

Decide at the next editors' call, record the answer here, and apply it to #47 before merge or in a follow-up PR before the Implementers Draft.

Refs #45, #47.

title: fix(provision-client): setup's authorization hint is a scoped grant, with the hand-off when setup rolls over
body:
Follow-up to #1813, prompted by VGI's review of the online `vtc setup` VTI-ACL-053 report.

## What was wrong
- **Authorization diagnostic** (`provision_client::authz`). When the setup DID isn't granted on the VTA, it told the operator to run `pnm acl create --did <setup-did> --role admin`:
  - **no `--contexts`**, which makes the setup DID an **unrestricted admin**;
  - **no expiry or hand-off**, so an operator adding a time box by hand, without `--handoff`, gets the last-step VTI-ACL-053 refusal the user hit.
- **Phase-1 guidance** (`provision_client::driver`). Under the correctly printed `pnm contexts create … --admin-expires 1h --admin-handoff`, it said `--admin-handoff` "lets" the hand-off, which reads as optional.

## Change
- `verify_authorization` takes the target context. A new `grant_hint` prints the scoped grant for that context:
  - `--contexts <ctx> --expires 1h --handoff` when setup rolls the setup DID over to a minted admin (AdminRotated / FullSetup, VTI-ACL-054);
  - a scoped grant with no expiry for AdminOnly, where the setup DID stays the admin.
  - It never prints an unscoped `--role admin`. A unit test pins both forms.
- The phase-1 text now says to keep `--admin-handoff`, that setup's last step is refused without it, and that it can't be added afterwards.

## Answers to VGI's questions
- **Plain `pnm contexts create --admin-did X`** writes a *permanent* entry, which VTI-ACL-053 never refuses. Only an expiring grant without the marker fails, and `--admin-handoff` requires `--admin-expires`.
- **`vtc setup` and the other setup wizards** (mediator, webvh) have printed `--admin-expires 1h --admin-handoff` since #1738, the same PR that added the bound. From May to #1738, the VTC wizard printed `--admin-expires 1h` *without* the marker. So an older `vtc` binary run against a current VTA reproduces the report exactly. The expiry in the report (10:28:41 UTC) is consistent with that 1h grant.

## Checks
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p vta-sdk --all-features --lib provision_client`: 83 passed.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib setup`: 49 passed.

title: feat(vta): re-invite an idle TSP relationship alongside the request, and stamp activity on every reply
body:
## Summary

The sender only learns that a peer lost its half of a TSP relationship when its reply window expires. §7.2.2 drops silently, and C2 rules out any signal back. So the first request after such a loss always cost a full 30s before D6 recovered it. Reproduced end to end: reset the DID hosting service's half, then create a DID. Hosting logs `Failed to unpack TSP frame … no relationship` at 11:31:20, and the VTA's recovery lands at 11:31:50. A caller whose budget is near 30s (the browser wallet) reports a failure for a create that succeeded.

**D10: re-invite an idle relationship before trusting it.** In `TspSender::first_attempt`, when our half is `Bidirectional` but the pair has had no successful round trip for an hour (`TSP_IDLE_REESTABLISH_MS`), or was never stamped, the VTA resets our half and sends the request with a fresh invite (`send_reestablishing`, the D6 resend's path).
- A peer that kept its half re-accepts (D2) and answers.
- One that lost it admits the request on the invite.
- Nothing is signalled back, so C2 holds.
- A timeout still goes on to D6 exactly as before.

Details:
- **Activity is stamped now.** Every correlated reply calls `touch` (D5). Nothing did before, so the idle-eviction sweep, which only sweeps stamped pairs, could never evict anything, and `vta tsp-relationships list` always said "never recorded".
- **`AppState.tsp_relationships`:** the durable store, built in `build_app_state` over the encrypted keyspace and shared with the startup sweep. The ATM keeps its own instance over the same keyspace; neither caches.
- **Single-flight** (`AppState.tsp_idle_reinvites`, `IdleReinvites`): one re-invite per peer at a time, and a concurrent send goes out the ordinary way. Deliberately **not** the D6 `RecoveryCoordinator`, whose D8 metrics would otherwise count a proactive re-invite as a recovery (R6).
- **Direct, not nested,** for a cross-mediator peer, like the D6 resend. That's at most once per idle hour per peer.
- **Upgrade:** existing relationships carry no stamp, so the first send to each peer after this ships carries one extra invite.
- Documented as D10 in `docs/05-design-notes/tsp-relationship-recovery.md`.

Companion wallet change: OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#287 gives relayed tasks the 80s `vta_sdk::budget` floor, so the wallet waits long enough even when a recovery does happen.

## Test plan

- [x] `an_idle_relationship_is_reinvited_with_the_request_and_restamped` (transport harness: real mediator, answering peer). An aged relationship takes the re-invite path, the peer answers, the reply re-stamps it, the next send is ordinary, and D6 metrics stay at 0 attempts.
- [x] `one_idle_reinvite_per_peer_at_a_time_and_released_on_drop` (unit)
- [x] Existing D6 harness tests: pass
- [ ] Full `cargo test -p vta-service --features transport-harness --lib`, clippy `-D warnings`, and a build without `tsp`: running; I'll update this PR with the results

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): none
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): the single-flight is a `std::sync::Mutex` held only to insert or remove; the claim guard holds no lock across the send
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the reset of our half precedes the invite, the same order as D6; a crash between them leaves `None`, which the next send re-invites from
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retry added. The request is sent once, with an invite; D6's retry-safety gate still governs any resend
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no wire types; the invite is the existing control message
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): an unreadable stamp falls back to the ordinary send
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): the stamp is written only on a correlated reply, and proactive re-invites are kept out of D8's recovery metrics
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): see R2.1 above; a lost stamp costs one extra invite
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: fix(core): give a task the VTA relays onward longer than the VTA can spend on it
body:
## Why

Creating a DID from the manager reported a timeout while the DID was in fact created. The VTA relays the create to the DID hosting server. When that server has lost its half of the TSP relationship, the VTA's first send is dropped silently (Rev 3 §7.2.2), and the VTA only re-forms the relationship and resends after its own 30s reply window. The wallet waited 30s, so it gave up at 30.00s and the VTA's answer came at 30.07s.

`vta_sdk::budget` already fixes this for Rust clients with an 80s floor for tasks the VTA relays onward. The wallet didn't mirror it.

## What

- **`vta/budget.ts`**, a port of `vta_sdk::budget`: `clientBudgetMs(type, requested)` raises a relayed task to `minRelayBudgetMs()` (80s = two 30s TSP windows + re-form + client headroom). It never lowers a budget, and tasks the VTA serves itself keep theirs. `RELAYS_ONWARD` imports each `TYPE_URI` from `@openvtc/trust-tasks`, so a renamed task fails to compile. It is the Rust list less the three tasks this wallet never sends (`vault/proxy-login/0.1`, `vta/services/update/1.1`, `rooms/owner/anchor/0.1`), which `task-surface` holds it to. The two console-only services tasks that relay (`vta/services/enable`, `update`) are budgeted at their own call sites in `admin/services.ts` instead. `budget.ts` ships in every wallet surface, and the build's admin-surface guard rightly rejects an admin task URI outside `manager.js`.
- **All three channels apply it:** TSP, DIDComm and REST.
- **`RestChannel` honours `timeoutMs`.** Its 20s fetch deadline was fixed at construction, so a per-request timeout was silently ignored. It is now applied per request (still 20s when none is given).

Companion VTA change (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1816): the VTA re-invites an idle relationship alongside the request, so the silent 30s mostly goes away as well. This PR makes the wallet correct even when it doesn't.

## Tests

`tests/vta.budget.mjs`, 7 new tests: the arithmetic (80s, above the VTA's worst case), every relayed task raised whatever it asked for, the clamp never shortening a budget or touching local tasks, and a `TspChannel` handing its transport 80s for `dids/create`, 30s for a local task, and a longer configured budget unchanged. Core: 725 pass; extension: 866 pass. `npm run build` plus the admin-surface guard run locally: no admin URI outside `manager.js`.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): every REST request still gets a finite deadline, now per request
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added; the wait is longer, not repeated
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6)
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): none
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): a relayed task no longer reports a timeout for work that succeeded
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): n/a
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: spec(webvh/witness/sign): let a witness sign the entry that deactivates a DID
body:
## What

`webvh/witness/sign/0.1` refused any log entry carrying `parameters.deactivated:
true` with `deactivated`, unconditionally. did:webvh deactivation is itself a
log entry, and per did:webvh witnessing is not exempt for it — so a DID that
ever had witnesses could never be deactivated: its deactivating entry could
never be witnessed. This fixes the rule.

A witness now:

- signs the entry that **first** sets `parameters.deactivated: true`, exactly
  as it signs any other entry that is the log's last entry, is authorised by
  the DID's current update keys, and names this identity in the witness
  parameter in force for it;
- refuses every entry **after** the deactivating entry with `deactivated`.

## did:webvh citation

[did:webvh specification](https://didwebvh.info/latest/specification/),
"DID Witnesses" > "Witness Lists":

> After the first `witness` parameter has been set to other than `{}` (empty
> object) in a DID log entry, and while there are active witnesses, a
> threshold of the active witnesses must provide valid proofs associated with
> each DID log entry before the DID log entry can be published.

and the `witness` parameter's own definition, for the case where an entry
both deactivates the DID and turns witnessing off in the same entry:

> If witnesses are active when the `witness` parameter is set to `{}`, that
> log entry MUST be witnessed.

No exception is carved out for the entry that sets `"deactivated": true`
("Deactivate (Revoke)"). `Verifying Witness Proofs During Resolution` confirms
the resolver side: a threshold of approving witnesses is required for every
entry with an active witness set.

## Why in place, not a new version (0.2)

Per [SPEC §5.2](https://trusttasks.org/SPEC.md#52-compatibility-rules), a
`draft` artifact's schema and prose *MAY* change without notice. This change
is additionally backwards-compatible on the wire: every document a witness
accepted before is still accepted, one previously-refused class (witnessing a
DID's deactivating entry) is now accepted, `payload.schema.json` is
unchanged, and nothing consumes `webvh/witness/sign` yet. So there is no
predecessor behaviour a new version would need to preserve. Status of this
Document now says so explicitly.

## Changes

- `specs/webvh/witness/sign/0.1/spec.md`: Conformance item 4 rewritten, a
  non-normative "Witnessing the entry that deactivates the DID" subsection
  citing did:webvh, a `Deactivating entry` definition, the `deactivated`
  error code's `meaning` updated, and two new examples (witnessing the
  deactivating entry; refusing an entry after it, paired with the
  `trust-task-error` response).
- Regenerated Rust/TS/Go/Dart bindings — only the `deactivated` doc comment
  and the two new example round-trip tests changed (Rust); `check-bindings`
  confirms all four agree.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run validate`
- [x] `npm run check-bindings`
- [x] `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs` (934 passed)
- [x] `go test ./...` in `trust-tasks-go` (ok)
- [x] `npm install && npm test` in `trust-tasks-ts` (79 passed)

carrying `deactivated: true` outright, so a DID that ever had witnesses could

per SPEC §5.2): a witness now signs the entry that first sets
`parameters.deactivated: true` exactly as it signs any other entry that
clears invalidLog/versionNotLast/notListed, and refuses every entry after it
with `deactivated`. Add an example of witnessing the deactivating entry and
an example of refusing an entry after it, and cite the did:webvh sections
this follows.

title: feat(spec-meta): a specification declares its own maximum document size (#679)
body:
feat(spec-meta): a specification declares its own maximum document size (#679)

Adds an optional front-matter member, maxDocumentBytes { request?, response?, rationale }, stating the largest serialized Trust Task document (proof included, transport envelope excluded) of each variant that a consumer serving the task must not refuse on grounds of size alone, and should refuse beyond with malformedRequest.

SPEC §12.4 already tells a consumer to bound what it parses at "a body-size limit appropriate to the Trust Task specification's payload", and §7.3 item 19 notes that a transport-layer limit is the wrong place to pick the number; until now no specification could say what it was. A consumer serving many tasks therefore applied one blanket cap sized for the small ones, and a task that legitimately carries a JSON Schema or a chunk of a file was refused. This lets the bound be stated, and enforced, per type.

- specs/spec.meta.schema.json: the member (at least one variant, 1 KiB to 16 MiB; larger content belongs in a chunked transfer).
- trust-tasks-codegen: reads it and emits Payload::MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES on the request and response impls, plus schema_index::max_document_bytes_for(type_uri) for a dispatcher that learns the type before parsing. An absent variant never inherits the other's bound.
- trust-tasks-rs: the trait constant, defaulting to None.
- check-bindings: holds Rust's constants to the front matter, re-derived independently.
- CONTRIBUTING-SPECS: when and how to declare it.

Rust only for now, like ERROR_CODES; the TypeScript, Go and Dart generators do not emit it yet. The framework text (a §7.3 item) is proposed in the canonical specification repository; this is the registry's half.

title: fix(provision): a setup DID granted without a hand-off is told to re-grant, not to shorten an expiry
body:
Reported by a user via VGI. Online `vtc setup` failed at its last step with:

> provision-integration call failed: forbidden: … your entry expires at 1790591321, so you cannot write a permanent one — give it an expiry no later than yours (VTI-ACL-053)

## Diagnosis
The online flow authenticates as the ephemeral setup DID, which rolls itself over to a permanent long-term admin. #1738 allows that rollover only through the granter's **one-time hand-off marker** (VTI-ACL-054–058, `--admin-handoff` / `--handoff`):
- The successor is bounded by the granter's recorded authority.
- The setup DID's entry is consumed atomically, under `HANDOFF_LOCK`.

Every setup command we print carries the marker, and so does `docs/03-vtc/non-interactive-setup.md`. This entry was granted without it; the expiry in the error is ~10h out rather than the printed `1h`, which points to a hand-written grant. `register_admin` then fell through to an ordinary grant, and VTI-ACL-053 refused it. The refusal was correct. The **message** wasn't: it told the operator to shorten an expiry, which can't help, because the successor must be permanent.

## Change
- `register_admin` refuses an ephemeral that rolls itself over with an expiring, unmarked entry, using a specific error. It names the missing hand-off and prints the re-grant: `pnm acl delete --did <setup-did>`, then `pnm acl create --did <setup-did> --role admin --contexts <its scope> --expires 1h --handoff`. The marker can't be added by update (VTI-ACL-055).
- The scope in the printed command comes from `act_scope()`, not `allowed_contexts.is_empty()`.
- It refuses exactly what VTI-ACL-053 already refused, at the same point and before anything is minted. Nothing is newly allowed, and no spec note is needed.
- `an_expiring_ephemeral_cannot_roll_over_to_a_permanent_successor` now pins the message. The hand-off success path (`a_marked_ephemeral_rolls_over_once`) is unchanged.
- The VTC setup guide describes the error and the re-grant.

## User workaround (today, no upgrade)
```
pnm acl delete --did <setup-did>
pnm acl create --did <setup-did> --role admin --contexts <ctx> --expires 1h --handoff
vtc setup --from <setup.toml>
```

## Checks
- `cargo test -p vta-service --lib provision_integration`: 67 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p vta-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt`: clean.

body:
fix(provision): a setup DID granted without a hand-off is told to re-grant, not to shorten an expiry (#1813)

Online `vtc setup` (and any setup whose ephemeral is the authenticated
caller) rolls the setup DID over to a permanent long-term admin. That rollover
is allowed only through the granter's one-time hand-off marker (VTI-ACL-054,
`--admin-handoff` / `--handoff`), and every printed setup command carries it.
When the entry was granted without it, provision-integration fell through to
an ordinary grant and #1738's VTI-ACL-053 bound refused it with "your entry
expires at …, so you cannot write a permanent one — give it an expiry no later
than yours". That points the operator at the wrong remedy: the successor must
be permanent, and what is missing is the marker, which can only be set when
the entry is created (VTI-ACL-055).

The refusal is now specific: it names the missing hand-off and prints the
re-grant (`pnm acl delete --did <setup-did>` then `pnm acl create … --expires
1h --handoff`, with the entry's own scope derived through `act_scope`). It
refuses exactly what VTI-ACL-053 already refused, before anything is minted;
nothing is newly allowed.

title: fix(deps): take affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.30.1, so an already-deleted message stops logging a warning
body:
## Summary

Takes the fix from affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#904 (published): `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.30.0 → **0.30.1** and `affinidi-messaging-mediator-common` 0.17.0 → 0.17.1, **lock-only**.

A Fjall or in-memory mediator answers the redundant delete of a redelivered message with `NOT_FOUND: message_hash (…)`. SDK 0.30.0 didn't recognise that as "already gone", so each one logged `WARN deletion_handler: the mediator refused some ids … deleted=0 failed=1`. 0.30.1 logs it at debug and remembers the id.

The workspace requirement stays `"0.30"`, following the floors-in-comments convention on that line, so no published crate's requirement changes. `fuzz/Cargo.lock` doesn't include the SDK.

- [x] `cargo test -p vta-service --bin vta tsp_relationships`: 5 passed

- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)

title: ci: run Mobile build and the semver report only where they can find something
body:
Over the last 30 PR runs, the two slowest jobs caught nothing a faster job didn't:

| Job | Ran | Avg | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mobile build | 22/30 | 22–40 min | 16 pass, 6 cancelled, **0 failures** |
| semver report | 30/30 | 33 min | 22 red (by design, never blocks), 8 cancelled |

## Mobile build — gated on its own sources

It was gated on vta-mobile-core's dependency closure, which includes `vta-sdk`, and most PRs touch `vta-sdk`. A change to vta-sdk's *source* cannot cause what only this job sees: a phone-target link failure, a deployment-target regression, or UniFFI binding generation. Those arrive through a dependency or the toolchain.

- **When it runs on a PR:** when `vta-mobile-core/` changes, or any global file does (`Cargo.lock`, a root manifest, the toolchain, `.github/`, `scripts/`). That's why it still runs on this PR.
- **Pushes to main and nightly:** always run it.
- **Host coverage:** `Test (workspace)` and clippy still build and test vta-mobile-core on every PR.
- **Implementation:** `ci-affects.sh --own` / `ci-closure.py --own` tag only the named packages. Every other job keeps the closure.
- **Timeout:** 45 → 60 minutes. A warm run on main takes ~40, and #1807's run hit 45 on a busy runner and was cancelled.

Verified by replaying the filter on a vta-sdk-only commit (`--own` skips, the closure runs) and on a vta-mobile-core commit (runs).

## semver report — opt-in

It now runs only on a PR labelled `semver-report` (the label now exists). `release bump is large enough` already runs the same check in enforcing mode on every Release PR, which is where an unmarked breaking change must be caught before publishing. `bash scripts/semver-report.sh` gives the answer locally. CLAUDE.md and RELEASING.md are updated to match.

## Not changed

`Feature combos` (29 min, 30/30 runs) is the one job that catches reduced-feature `#[cfg]` breaks nothing else compiles, so it stays on every PR. Its filter never skips, because its scope spans both vta-service and vtc-service. Narrowing that is a separate change.

title: fix(console): clear a pane's list when the context changes
body:
## Why

Switching context in the console left the previous context's DIDs on screen under the new context's heading until the agent replied. It looked like the console had answered the wrong question.

## What

`useAsync` (used by 19 console panes) kept its last answer until the next one arrived, for a reload and a context switch alike. That's right for a reload (after a delete, the list shouldn't jump) and wrong when the question itself changes.

The hook now tags its state with the question it answers:
- **Context switch:** the list clears and "Reading DIDs…" shows in the same render, then the new list fills in.
- **Reload:** the current list stays while it re-fetches, as before.
- **Failed listing for a new context:** no longer leaves the old context's rows on screen next to the error.

Keys and the other context-scoped panes get the same fix.

## Tests

`dids-context-switch.render.test.mts` covers the switch (old rows gone, loading shown, new rows after the reply) and the failed-listing case. Both fail against the old hook. `tsc -b` clean; extension 861 pass.

- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): n/a

title: fix(onboard): grant persona-holder in the setup command, and read it back
body:
## Why

Since verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1673, no role reaches the holder's attribute pool, not even an admin with no context restriction. The agent admits a caller only on an ACL entry granted `persona-holder` by name. The setup command we print never asked for it, so a newly set-up console had its persona pane refused on every task. The console's persona caution also stayed silent for an unrestricted admin, which is now the credential most likely to be refused.

## What

**The setup command (`grant-command.ts`, `onboard-view.tsx`)**
- **Manage the whole agent:** `pnm acl create --did <eph> --role admin --capabilities persona-holder --expires 1h --handoff`. Always included.
- **Work inside one context:** a new *"Also manage your own identity"* checkbox. When ticked, the command gets `--capabilities persona-holder` and the screen warns that someone with the whole agent must run it. The VTA refuses this capability from a context-scoped operator (`validate_additive_capability_grant`).
- Checked against the VTA source:
  - `persona-holder` is additive, so it doesn't narrow the admin role. It is the only capability the command ever names.
  - The VTA carries it across the hand-off rollover to the permanent admin (#1573).
- The flag goes from the onboarding page through the background to the offscreen document (`personaHolder` on the prepare request).

**The persona caution (`holder-gate.ts`, `whoAmI`)**
- `whoAmI` in `@openvtc/pnm-core` now returns `auth/whoami`'s effective `capabilities`. It is the only member that shows a capability granted by name.
- `isUnscopedHolder` is replaced by `holdsPersonaHolder`. With the grant there's no caution, whatever the scope. Without it the caution shows, including for an unrestricted admin.
- The caution no longer suggests a wider credential as a way in. It prints the fix with the wallet's own DID: `pnm acl update <holder DID> --capabilities persona-holder`. `acl update` takes the DID positionally. The VTA's own hint said `--did`, fixed in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1811.
- Behaviour note: the persona buttons that already disabled on this caution (e.g. *New world*, a world's *Delete*) now disable only when the agent actually reports the capability missing.

**CLAUDE.md:** the grant-command section now covers the capability. The persona section said the agent gates on `require_super_admin`; it now describes the capability gate.

## Tests

- `grant-command.test.mts`: whole-agent grant always names it; one-context grant only when asked; `persona-holder` is the only `--capabilities` value; the super-admin operator warning follows it.
- `manager-holder-gate.test.mts`: rewritten around the capability, including the unrestricted-admin-without-grant case the old gate missed and the positional command syntax.
- `admin.policy-sessions.mjs`: `whoAmI` returns `capabilities`.
- `tsc -b` clean; extension 864 pass, core 718 pass.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new network calls
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): n/a
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): inbound path untouched
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no new wire type. Reads `capabilities`, already declared in `auth/whoami/0.1` and served by the VTA. Internal bridge message gains an optional `personaHolder`.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): a missing `capabilities` reads as none held, so the caution shows. The agent decides either way.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): the caution now reflects what the agent reports rather than a role guess
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): no mutation touched
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

title: fix(pnm): the persona-holder hint prints a pnm acl update that runs
body:
## What

The persona refusal (`vta-service/src/trust_tasks/persona.rs`) and `pnm persona --help` (`pnm-cli/src/cli.rs`) both told operators to run:

```
pnm acl update --did <did> --capabilities persona-holder
```

`pnm acl update` takes the entry's DID as a **positional** argument and has no `--did` flag, so the command offered as the fix fails to parse. Both places now print:

```
pnm acl update <did> --capabilities persona-holder
```

## Test

`acl_update_hint_tests` in `pnm-cli/src/cli.rs` parses the printed form and checks that the `--did` form is rejected. It follows the same pattern as `config_update_flag_tests`, so a change to `acl update`'s arguments fails in CI rather than for an operator.

- `cargo test -p pnm-cli --bins acl_update_hint`: pass
- `cargo test -p vta-service --test persona_trust_task`: 41 passed
- `cargo fmt -p pnm-cli -- --check`: clean

## Not changed

The `vta-service` and `pnm-cli` CHANGELOG entries for #1673 also say `--did`. They are released history generated by git-cliff, so I left them alone. This commit's message carries the correction into the next release's notes.

Found while fixing the same hint in the browser plugin's console, which now prints the positional form.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): n/a, text only
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): n/a
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): n/a

title: feat(vta): list, reset and delete TSP relationships offline
body:
## Summary

Each endpoint keeps its own half of every TSP relationship, and the mediator holds none. So restarting the VTA or wiping the mediator never resets a pairing, and there was no way to clear the VTA's half by hand. Adds an offline command group:

```
vta tsp-relationships list                                  # established pairs + last active
vta tsp-relationships reset  --peer <did> [--our <vid>]     # D4 stale-half reset; next send re-invites
vta tsp-relationships delete --peer <did> [--our <vid>]     # D5 forget: every facet
vta tsp-relationships delete --all [--yes]                  # every record, half-formed too; dry run without --yes
```

- `vta-service/src/tsp_relationships_cli.rs`, split like `approvals_cli`: thin `run_*` openers plus `_on` functions that the tests drive directly.
- Opens the `relationships` keyspace through `CliStore`, so it decrypts under hardened configuration. The tests seed an encrypted keyspace.
- `reset`/`delete` go through `check_seal`; `list` is read-only. Gated on the `tsp` feature, as the relationship store is.
- Uses the SDK's `PersistentRelationshipStore` API only; no key layout is re-derived.
- A peer with no established relationship is an error, not a silent no-op. A half-formed pair needs `--our` because the store only enumerates established ones.
- Adds an "Operator tooling" paragraph to `docs/05-design-notes/tsp-relationship-recovery.md`.

The companion DID-hosting command is `tsp-relationship-*` (affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#233). A clean first-contact repro needs both halves cleared.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p vta-service --bin vta tsp_relationships`: 5 new tests (list through the encrypted keyspace, reset scope, unknown-peer refusal, half-formed delete via `--our`, `--all` dry run and real)
- [x] Argument rules checked by hand (`--our` conflicts with `--all`, and so on)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p vta-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt`
- [ ] Manual: against a stopped VTA, `list` shows the DID hosting pairing and `delete --all --yes` clears it

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): none
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): offline, no network
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): local-only state; the peer re-forms the relationship on the next invite (D2)
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): no wire changes
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): the fjall lock refuses to open while the daemon runs; writes are sealed; `--all` is a dry run unless `--yes` is given
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): the output reports what was written
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): each record delete is independent and idempotent; a partial `--all` is finished by re-running it; `persist` runs after the writes
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none

feat(vta): list, reset and delete TSP relationships offline (#1812)

TSP relationship state is per endpoint and persisted in the encrypted
`relationships` keyspace, so neither restarting the VTA nor wiping the mediator
clears it, and there was no way to clear this VTA's half. Adds:

  vta tsp-relationships list
  vta tsp-relationships reset  --peer <did> [--our <vid>]
  vta tsp-relationships delete --peer <did> [--our <vid>] | --all [--yes]

Reset is the D4 stale-half reset (`None` plus cleared thread digests; the
capability cache is kept), so the next send re-invites. Delete is the D5
eviction's `forget`. `--all` also removes half-formed records, which D9's
enumeration cannot see, and only reports without `--yes`. The keyspace is
opened through `CliStore`, so it decrypts under hardened configuration. `reset`
and `delete` are refused on a sealed VTA; `list` is not. Built only with the
`tsp` feature. All reads and writes go through the SDK's
`PersistentRelationshipStore`.

title: feat(vtc): member verbs are Trust Tasks on the spine (renew, rotate, personhood, relationships, endorsements)
body:
## What

Eleven VTC tasks were bound to published specs (trust-tasks-rs 0.24.2) but served only on HTTPS REST. They are now dispatched by the Trust Task spine (`vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/member_tasks.rs`), so TSP, DIDComm and HTTPS `/trust-tasks` all reach them:

| Task | Authority (the verified proof signer's current ACL row) |
|---|---|
| `vtc/members/renew/0.1` | signer renews own membership (no ACL/member row: declared `notMember`) |
| `vtc/members/rotate-challenge/0.1` | signer opens a rotation of own DID |
| `vtc/members/rotate/0.1` | signer == `oldDid`; both in-payload signatures authorize the swap |
| `vtc/members/personhood/revoke/0.1` | the subject, or an administrator |
| `vtc/relationships/list/0.2` | any current member or administrator |
| `vtc/relationships/publish/0.2` | signer, via the same `publish_inner` as the bearer-less REST route |
| `vtc/relationships/revoke/0.1` | the edge's issuer or an admin; any other member gets declared `notFound` (spec anti-probing) |
| `vtc/endorsements/{issue,list,show,revoke}/0.1` | `Admin` or `Issuer` row |

An expired row refuses. A console-key delegation (`admin_signer`) is honoured only for administrative capacities, never for the self verbs.

Each arm calls the operation its REST route calls. The route bodies were factored into shared inner functions. **REST routes are unchanged and stay mounted.** `admin-ui`, the session/auth surface and the admin verbs are untouched.

## Worth reviewing

- **Authority vs the bearer routes.** A VTC bearer session is minted only for an Admin row (`map_vtc_role_to_auth_role`), so in a deployment the REST routes were in practice admin-only. This door admits the member or issuer that the specs (`renew`: "the authenticated caller … acting on their own membership", `endorsements/*`: "community-admin or issuer capability against the live ACL") and the handlers' own checks name. That is the same stance `members/personhood/challenge` already takes on the spine. No arm admits a party its handler would refuse.
- **Wire shapes.** Payloads are parsed through the generated types. Replies are read back through the generated `#response` type and schema-validated before sending, so this door fails as `internalError` rather than answering in an unpublished shape. `relationships/list` maps stored edges to the six published fields (the stored row also carries persona/lifecycle).
- **`endorsements/list` filters.** `subjectDid` / `typeUri` / `includeRevoked` are applied before pagination (`list_endorsements_matching`), as the spec's Conformance requires. The REST route passes no filter, so its behaviour is unchanged.
- **Publish rate limit.** The limiter refusal is `unavailable` with `limiter` + `retryAfterSecs`.

## Known limits (in the design note)

- A pairwise edge can still be retracted only on the bearer route. Its `VrcRevokeAuthorization` binds to a REST session, and `revoke/0.1` has no authorization member.
- `endorsements/revoke`'s `reason` is accepted but not persisted, because `CustomEndorsementRevoked` has no field for it and adding one is a breaking change to `vti-common`.

## Tests

`trust_tasks::member_tasks::tests` has 28 tests, named by task. Every task succeeds on REST, DIDComm and TSP contexts and conforms to its `#response` schema. Each authorization refusal is held: non-member, expired row, wrong party, missing issuer role, and unsigned proof-optional reads. The proof-REQUIRED dispatched-set count moves from 52 to 60.

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes
- `cargo test -p vta-sdk --test generated_wire_types_census` passes
- `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1 cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast` passes, except the flag's known 4 `admin_ui::tests` + 2 `path_mode_admin_*` failures
- No shared crate was touched, so the workspace job is unaffected.

Since VTI #1673 no role reaches the holder's attribute pool, not even an

  restriction", which after #1673 passed the credential the agent
  refuses. The caution prints the fix:
  pnm acl update <holder DID> --capabilities persona-holder.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.24.4
body:
### Added

- **trust-task-discovery**: Publish 0.3, a responder advertises its acceptance window ([#677](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/677))

A consumer refuses a document whose issuedAt lies outside its acceptance
  window (SPEC §7.2 item 13), and the framework leaves that window to the
  consumer's policy. A producer that holds a document before delivering it
  (store-and-forward, retry, escalation, a queue replayed after a restart)
  cannot tell a document the consumer will still accept from one it will
  refuse as expired. So it cannot tell when to issue a new attempt (SPEC
  §8.4) instead. The only alternative is a constant both ends share.

  - specs/trust-task-discovery/0.3: the response gains an optional
    acceptanceWindow { maxAgeSeconds, clockSkewSeconds }, in whole seconds.
    It appears at the response level, and on an expanded supportedTypes
    entry, where the entry's value takes precedence.
    - Responder: MUST NOT state a window wider than it applies, and is not
      bound by what it advertised.
    - Discoverer: authenticated responses only. SHOULD NOT send after
      issuedAt + maxAge, and MUST NOT after issuedAt + maxAge + skew. It
      issues a new attempt instead (fresh id and issuedAt, same thread,
      new proof), and never re-stamps under the original id (idConflict).
      It does not issue a new attempt of a consequential task unless a
      repeat is harmless or recognizable. It never backdates to fit a
      window, bounds its new attempts, and treats a refusal as the answer.
    - Absent: the discoverer has learnt nothing. It falls back to the
      window the task's specification states (item 17) or its own, with
      the typical skew tolerance of at most 60 s. Absence is never read as
      "no window".
    - The response is closed, so a 0.2 discoverer that validates would
      reject the member. §5.2 makes an added optional member a MINOR
      increment, hence 0.3 rather than an edit to 0.2.
    - Response-side invalid examples: a missing member, a zero max age,
      negative skew, fractional or string values, an unknown member, and
      a malformed entry-level window.
  - trust-tasks-codegen: a payload.invalid-examples.json fixture may carry
    "variant": "response". It is checked against Response and its
    sub-schema by a separate rejects_invalid_response_examples test. It is
    refused in a spec with no response. Existing fixtures, and every other
    generated module, are unchanged.
  - CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md documents the variant.
  - Bindings regenerated (Rust, TS, Go, Dart).

  The framework text (SPEC §10) still names 0.2 as the current version.
  That is a change to the canonical repository and follows separately.

  Proposed from OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1799, where both
  ends currently share a constant window.

| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.3.10` → `0.3.11` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: ci: refuse a release that would break a published crate or halt partway
body:
Guards the two ways #1795's release went wrong. That release stopped at vta-backup and left vta-service 0.44.0 unbuildable from a fresh resolve; openvtc had to stay on 0.43.0 until three runs later.

`scripts/check-release-bump-sizes.py` runs beside the existing whole-tree manifest guards (the lockfile self-pin job).

**Rule 1 (every PR): a published crate's dev-only dependency on a sibling has no version.**
- A versioned one makes `cargo publish` require the sibling on crates.io, and the release publishes in normal-dependency order. That's how vta-backup went before vta-webvh 0.3 and halted the run (fixed in #1805).
- A sibling that is also a normal dependency is already ordered first, so it's allowed. vta-service's `vta-sdk` and `vti-rooms-dtg` test-feature entries are exactly this case.

**Rule 2 (does real work on Release PRs): moving a sibling's compatibility range needs a breaking bump.**
- vta-audit 0.3.26 and vta-support 0.5.7 moved vti-common from `^0.27` to `^0.29` as *patch* releases. vta-service 0.44.0 requires `vta-audit = "^0.3"`, so a fresh resolve picked them up along with a second vti-common.
- release-plz derives a patch here, and cargo-semver-checks can't see it. The check compares each unpublished version with its newest published predecessor's requirements on crates.io. On a feature PR every version is already published, so it does nothing.

**Proof**
- On current main: passes (23 published members).
- Rule 1: with vta-backup's `version = "0.3"` dev-dependency restored, it fails and names the fix.
- Rule 2: replayed against a crates.io stand-in for the state before #1795 (vta-audit 0.3.25 on vti-common `^0.27` / vta-sdk `^0.54`), it fails on both moved requirements and tells you to raise vta-audit to its next breaking version.

**RELEASING.md**
- New: read the release job's log after every Release PR merge. A re-run only resumes once the cause is fixed.
- The two causes that halted #1795.
- The breaking-bump rule, with how to fix a Release PR that trips it.

   Versioned, `cargo publish` must find it on crates.io, and the release
   publishes in normal-dependency order — so vta-backup went before vta-webvh
   0.3 existed and the run halted (#1805 fixed that one). A sibling that is also
   a normal dependency is already ordered by that edge and is allowed.
2. Moving a sibling's compatibility range is a breaking bump. vta-audit 0.3.26

   see it. The check compares each unpublished version against its newest
   published predecessor's requirements on crates.io, so it only has work on a
   Release PR.

title: feat(trust-task-discovery): publish 0.3, a responder advertises its acceptance window
body:
A consumer refuses a document whose `issuedAt` falls outside its acceptance window (SPEC §7.2 item 13). The framework leaves that window to the consumer's policy.

A producer that holds a document before delivering it needs to know that window. Holding happens in store-and-forward delivery, retry with backoff, escalation to another transport, and a queue replayed after a restart. Without the window, the producer cannot tell a document the consumer will still accept from one it will refuse as `expired`. So it cannot tell when to issue a new attempt (SPEC §8.4) instead.

The only alternative is a constant both ends share. That is how OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1799 works today, and it breaks for the first consumer configured differently.

## Change

**`specs/trust-task-discovery/0.3`** adds an optional response member, `acceptanceWindow { maxAgeSeconds, clockSkewSeconds }`, in whole seconds, with both members required inside it:

- **Where it goes.** It can appear at the response level, or on an expanded `supportedTypes` entry. An entry's value takes precedence over the response-level one.
- **What it means.** The consumer refuses a document when `now > issuedAt + maxAge + skew`, and when `issuedAt > now + skew`. `expiresAt` is honoured independently and is never extended.
- **Responder rules.** A responder MUST NOT state a window wider than the one it applies. A narrower one only costs producers new attempts they did not need. The responder is not bound by what it advertised.
- **Discoverer rules.**
  - Act only on an authenticated response, as already required.
  - SHOULD NOT send a document after `issuedAt + maxAge`. MUST NOT send one after `issuedAt + maxAge + skew`.
  - Issue a new attempt in its place: fresh `id` and `issuedAt`, same thread, new proof.
  - Never re-stamp under the original `id`; the consumer rejects that as `idConflict`.
  - MUST NOT issue a new attempt of a consequential task unless a repeat is harmless, or the consumer will recognise it (for example through an idempotency mechanism).
  - Never backdate or post-date a document to fit a window.
  - Bound the number of new attempts.
  - Treat a refusal as the answer, and re-ask discovery after an unexpected `expired`.
- **When the member is absent.** The discoverer has learnt nothing, and MUST NOT read absence as "no window". It falls back to the window the task's own specification states (§7.3 item 17), or its own configured one. For skew, it uses the typical tolerance of at most 60 s from §4.2. The framework defines no default maximum age.
- **Examples.** A response example with a top-level window and a per-entry override, plus a worked timeline.
- **Security & Privacy.** Data carried, correlation (the window is a deployment fingerprint, and a responder MAY omit it), retention, and purpose are updated.

**Why 0.3 rather than an edit to 0.2.** The response is closed (`additionalProperties: false`), so a 0.2 discoverer that validates the response would reject one carrying the new member. SPEC §5.2 also makes an added optional member a MINOR increment. This follows the same reasoning 0.2 gave for leaving 0.1 unchanged.

**`trust-tasks-codegen`.** Fixtures in `payload.invalid-examples.json` could only test the *request* payload, which left the new member with no negative tests. A fixture may now carry `"variant": "response"`:
- It is checked against `Response` and its `$anchor: "response"` sub-schema by a separate `rejects_invalid_response_examples` test.
- A `"response"` fixture in a spec with no response is refused.
- Existing fixtures, and every other generated module, are byte-identical after regeneration.
- `CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md` documents the new variant.

0.3 carries seven response-side fixtures: a missing member, a zero max age, negative skew, a fractional value, a duration string, an unknown member, and a malformed entry-level window.

Bindings are regenerated for all four languages.

## For review

- **Units are whole seconds, not an ISO 8601 duration.** The value is only used for arithmetic, and a duration admits months.
- **Both members are required inside the object.** An absent skew would otherwise be ambiguous between zero and the typical 60 s.
- **There are two bounds for the discoverer.** SHOULD NOT after `maxAge`, MUST NOT after `maxAge + skew`. Between the two, delivery is uncertain.
- **The per-entry override** exists because §7.3 item 17 lets each task specification state its own expected window.
- **Rule 4 is the one with safety weight.** It stops a new attempt from being a silent second execution of a consequential task.

## Not in this PR

- **SPEC §10** still names discovery 0.2 as the current version. That text is generated from trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec and changes there.
- **Runtime support** (`DiscoveryRegistry::respond_to_v0_3` in `trust-tasks-rs`, and answering 0.3 in the HTTPS servers) is a follow-up. A discoverer falls back to 0.2 until then, as the spec allows.

## Checks

- `npm run build`: 594 specs validated, framework links checked, and 0.3 carries all four Security & Privacy sub-headings. Every warning printed is on an unrelated spec.
- `npm run check-bindings`: TypeScript, Rust, Go and Dart all agree.
- `npm run check-dart-packages` and `npm run test-ceremonies` pass.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets` pass, including the new `rejects_invalid_response_examples`.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` with `-D warnings`, with and without `--all-features`, is clean.
- `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features` produces no warnings.
- `trust-tasks-ts`: `tsc --noEmit` passes, `npm test` passes 79/79, and `npm run smoke` passes.
- `trust-tasks-go`: `go build`, `go vet` and `go test ./...` pass, and `gofmt -l` is clean.
- `trust-tasks-dart`: `dart analyze` finds no issues, and `dart test` passes.

title: Do not count a copy collected after its acceptance window as delivered (VTI-TRN-044 – 047)
body:
VTI-TRN-040 counts transport evidence that the recipient collected a message as delivery. A store-and-forward delivery can outlive the document it carries. A copy a mediator holds while the recipient is offline, a hop refused for longer than the window, or an escalation under VTI-TRN-042 can reach the recipient after the acceptance window of VTI-OPS-024 has closed. The recipient then refuses it as `expired`. A sender that recorded the collection as delivery has closed the one obligation, VTI-TRN-042's, that would have delivered the operation, and nothing tells it otherwise.

## Changes

**Transports, messaging and delivery.** A new subsection, *Delivery and the acceptance window*:

- It defines the **latest acceptable instant** of a document at a recipient: the time of issue plus the recipient's maximum age and skew tolerance, or the document's expiry where that is earlier.
- **VTI-TRN-044** (new): evidence of the first or third class does not count as delivery where the message arrived after that instant. The arrival is placed at the time the evidence states, or at the time the sender received the evidence. The operation stays undelivered and VTI-TRN-042 still applies. A protocol reply is not affected: it carries the recipient's disposition, and an `expired` refusal is handled as a refusal.
- **VTI-TRN-045** (new): the sender takes the recipient's window from an authenticated discovery response (VTI-OPS-046) where the recipient advertises one. Failing that, it uses the operation definition's stated window. Failing both, it uses a documented window it applies to every such recipient.
- **VTI-TRN-046** (new): the sender does not send a document past its latest acceptable instant, and SHOULD NOT send one past time of issue plus maximum age. Where delivery continues, the operation goes as a **new document**: a new identifier, a new time of issue and a new proof, with the original's thread and every other member unchanged, including the idempotency key (VTI-OPS-064). The sender MUST NOT re-stamp the original under its identifier, which VTI-OPS-026 refuses as a conflicting document. It MUST NOT issue a new document for an unkeyed operation of the third class, or once the original's expiry or the delivery window has passed. It MUST bound the number of new documents per delivery and surface the failure when the bound is reached.
- **VTI-TRN-047** (new): a node SHOULD advertise its window in discovery, and MUST NOT advertise one longer than it applies.
- **VTI-TRN-040 / VTI-TRN-041**: class 1 and class 3 now point to VTI-TRN-044. Evidence the sender declines to count is recorded as not counted.
- Each new requirement has a rationale.

**Introduction.** The cross-specification note records a pending minimum [TRUST-TASKS] Document Status for an advertised window. Until then, the fallback in VTI-TRN-045 applies to every recipient.

**Appendix F.**
- F.3 gets a new *observed* entry against VTI-TRN-045 and VTI-TRN-047. The push engine applies one constant, 10 min maximum age and 60 s skew, to every recipient. That is its own consumers' window, and a documented, uniform fallback. It reads no advertised window, and neither node type advertises one.
- F.7 gets a closed entry, *observed, never listed*, against VTI-TRN-044 and VTI-TRN-046, closed by OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1799. It records what remains open: a sealed copy a mediator already holds cannot be recalled.

## Design points for review

- **Class 1 is covered as well as class 3.** A receipt from the recipient's delivery layer can acknowledge arrival below the point where the window is applied, so it has the same defect. Class 2 is exempt, because a reply is the recipient's disposition.
- **The bound is the latest acceptable instant, which includes skew, not the maximum age alone.** A copy the recipient might still accept is therefore not recorded as lost. A copy refused inside the skew tolerance comes back as a refusal and is handled under VTI-TRN-046. Proactive re-issue, by contrast, is keyed to maximum age as a SHOULD.
- **VTI-TRN-046 item 2** makes the idempotency key a precondition for re-issuing a third-class operation. Without a key, a second delivery is a second execution.
- **VTI-TRN-045 is a MUST where a window is advertised.** The reference implementation's gap is recorded as a divergence, not accommodated by weakening the requirement.

Drafted from OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1799, whose "Spec follow-up" item 1 this is. Item 2, the discovery member, is proposed separately to dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf.

## Checks

`npm run render` completes with no warnings or errors, and `docs/index.html` carries VTI-TRN-044 to VTI-TRN-047.

title: chore(deps): take vta-service 0.45 and refresh the lockfile onto one stack
body:
Closes the last residual from the VTI/TDK 0.56 move.

- **vta-service 0.43.0 → 0.45.0.** 0.45.0 is the republished family on vta-sdk ^0.56 / vti-common ^0.29. 0.44.0 is skipped for good: it came from a half-published VTI release whose subcrates disagreed on `vti-common`, so it never builds on a fresh resolve. The `openvtc-core/Cargo.toml` note is rewritten to match.
- **Full `cargo update`.** A targeted update left the lock holding older vta-* subcrates (vta-audit 0.3.23, vta-config 0.7, and so on) still on vta-sdk 0.53 / vti-common 0.26 / TDK 0.18 / messaging-sdk 0.28 / trust-tasks 0.23. After the refresh, `cargo tree -d` shows one copy each of vta-sdk, vti-common, trust-tasks-rs, affinidi-tdk and affinidi-messaging-sdk, and the lock is 185 lines smaller. That also halves the compile, which should stop the benchmarks runner being shut down mid-build as it was on #393.

Checks (local): `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked` and `cargo bench --workspace --no-run --locked`.
